sessions.title: Registration & Check-In
Think Like a CTO: The Durable Engineering Skill in the Agentic Era
sessions.description:
Point ten agents at your codebase and you don't get 10x output; you get merge collisions, drifting context, confident slop. The gains are real, if you design the system that steers them. That's the system a CTO builds.

I've scaled orgs of hundreds at Google and led the team behind Firebase; now I'm a hands-on startup builder, running fleets of agents. Harnessing agentic intelligence takes the same evergreen skills as channeling human intelligence.

1. The architecture: decomposing problems so teams/agents can parallelize without colliding.
2. The vision and org: defining an outcome clear enough to align a thousand decisions, docs that ramp a new agent/human mid-task, staffing each problem to the right model or person.
3. The playbook: establishing feedback loops that turn bugs, metrics, and retros into a system that improves itself, and making judgment calls on where to push and where to cut.

In the agentic era, we all need to think like CTOs, and build the system that builds.

sessions.title: Community in the AI Era: Obsolete or Essential?
sessions.description:
AI is changing how we write code, search for information, and learn new technologies. As more of these tasks become automated, what keeps developer communities relevant? What do we still need each other for?

For years, the Android ecosystem has grown because developers learned from one another. We asked questions, challenged ideas, shared experiments, and collectively figured out what worked. But what happens when our first question is no longer asked to another developer? What happens when we're all getting answers from the same place?

This keynote explores what community means in the AI era. If AI changes how we learn, who creates the next best practices? If knowledge becomes a commodity, what makes a community valuable? And if Android was built by its community, what role will that community play in shaping what's next?

sessions.title: AI Makes It Easy to Migrate. Flutter Makes It Easy to Scale.
sessions.description:
AI agents can port an app to multiple native codebases on Day 1—but who maintains these codebase that are will imminently diverge on Day 2,000? Learn why verification speed—not code generation—is the true bottleneck of agentic development, and how Flutter's sub-200ms feedback loop, and Impeller engine power six surfaces from one source of truth.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

sessions.title: Give Your Agent Eyes
sessions.description: Agents write code in seconds, then call it done with total confidence, often, they get it wrong. Expo Simulators and Workflows close that gap: agents that check their work on a device, test with E2E flows, and ship through a pipeline a human approves. The tightest loop wins,

sessions.title: Software as Art: Crafting Apps in the Age of AI
sessions.description:
Like art, great products are made of lived human experience, strong opinions, and all the decisions along the way. AI tools are increasingly shaping the way we do design, engineering, testing, and everything in between. They can help accelerate many manual tasks. But what if you truly care about quality, user experience, and the art of storytelling in software?

In this talk, we will explore the novel challenges AI tools present for designing a quality app. We’ll discuss our evolving role as engineers and technical leaders, why craft still matters, and how we can prevent our ideas from turning into slop.

Whether you are an engineer working on a Swift codebase, a product manager, or a technical leader, you will leave with practical techniques to help you focus on what really matters: delivering delightful apps and experiences to your users.

sessions.title: XR Meets AI: A Practical Framework for What's Next
sessions.description:
The convergence of XR and AI is reshaping how digital experiences are created, experienced, and scaled. Too often, XR and AI are bundled together as part of the latest technology buzzword bingo, with little clarity about where the real synergies exist.

In this keynote, Gabriele Romagnoli introduces a practical framework for understanding where XR and AI genuinely complement one another. Through tangible examples, emerging tools, and real-world use cases, he explores how generative AI is becoming part of 3D workflows, immersive experiences, and the next generation of mobile platforms.

A practical and informed session designed to help audiences move beyond the buzzwords and understand the real opportunities at the intersection of XR and AI.

sessions.title: Mobile Application Security - Welcome to masCon
sessions.description: Join OWASP Mobile Application Security Project Lead, Carlos Holguera to kick off three days of talks on MAS!

sessions.title: Speed Networking (All Communities)
sessions.description:
Location: Activity & Networking Area Level 2

This is a chance to quickly get to make connections with other developers from various communities.

sessions.title: Break
Beyond SaaS: How software companies can thrive in the Autonomous AI era
sessions.description: In a single week of February 2026, the software sector lost roughly a trillion dollars in market cap — not because a better competitor showed up, but because autonomous agents started dissolving the jobs traditionally done by SaaS vendors, and getting closer to the user while doing it. This session gives organization that builds software for a living a different mental model for the agentic era, and one diagnostic to run on their own business. We'll walk through the six surfaces where coding agents now decide whether your product gets used, then look at the new business models emerging on the horizon for autonomous AI — and the challenges that come with them, from security and distribution to monetization. We'll wrap with the emerging patterns of how the teams that build all of this are starting to look.

sessions.title: Building AI apps with the Google ecosystem
sessions.description:
The way we build software has changed. Today, the most successful developers aren't just writing code, they are orchestrating AI tools and agents to build better and faster. This hands-on session is a deep dive into this modern "Builder Stack”, where you will learn how to build with a variety of tools in the Google ecosystem.

Come to this session if you want to spend less time configuring and more time creating. We’ll guide you through a complete development lifecycle, from prototyping an idea, to generating a beautiful UI, building AI features, and integrating a secure, scalable backend.

sessions.title: Is the "Mobile Developer" Dead? Being a software developer in the AI age
sessions.description:
The world of software engineering is undergoing a drastic and rapid transformation. 
And many developers are asking themselves if they will become obsolete very soon.

This presentation tries to answer this a bit differently by asking: Do we still need the traditional split of specializations—like frontend, mobile, and backend developer?
To understand that, it is worth explaining why this split happened in the first place. It will give us a clearer picture of the current situation and what skill sets are needed going forward.

As Grady Booch recently noted, we have entered the 3rd Golden Age of Software Development. Join us to discuss how we got here and where we can go in this new era, focusing on why human-centric skills, such as system architecture and ethical judgment, are more critical than ever.

Let's talk about how we got here and where we can go from here in the new era.

sessions.title: Degrease your Android app: stripping bloat for low-end devices
sessions.description:
Low-end Android devices expose performance problems that flagship phones often hide. Small inefficiencies in startup, memory usage, caching, or background work can quickly turn into ANRs and a frustrating user experience at scale.

In this talk, I’ll walk through how we approached a performance overhaul at Super, from local profiling to production telemetry. We’ll use memory dumps, Perfetto traces, flamegraphs, Macrobenchmark, and microbenchmarks to identify CPU and memory bottlenecks, then look at the trade-offs behind architectural choices such as on-disk caching, in-memory caching, and memory-efficient data structures. We’ll also cover how to ship risky performance changes safely using feature flags, and how to validate their real-world impact with production observability.

By the end, you’ll have a practical blueprint for finding Android performance bloat, reducing ANRs on constrained devices, and proving that your optimizations actually work in production.

sessions.title: Recreating 80s Amiga chiptunes in modern Android
sessions.description:
Remember the magic of turning on your console to hear the electronic chiptune melodies of Tetris, Super Mario, or Pac-Man? Long before MP3s, games didn't just play back audio files, they synthesised music on the fly, crafting sound waves out of thin air.

In Android, reconstructing this vintage environment is a fun dive into low-level media pipelines and precise concurrency. Working with OS audio architecture, we’ll generate real-time sound from scratch, maintain jitter-free timing using coroutines, and build a playback loop to survive Android 17’s strict background audio hardening.

Learn how to:
- Use android.media.AudioTrack to stream raw audio directly to hardware.

- Generate retro square waves and use bitwise math to create a gritty 80s chiptune sound.

- Use Coroutines to feed the audio buffer asynchronously without causing audio stuttering or frame drops.

- Use foreground services to work under Android 17's strict background rules

sessions.title: Making sense of Compose performance
sessions.description:
While Compose has greatly simplified UI development, it requires a change in the way we think about performance. The declarative paradigm fundamentally changes how UIs are constructed and, consequently, where performance bottlenecks occur.

In this talk, we will explore how to understand and optimize your app’s Compose usages. We will start with the state of Compose Performance and then dive deep into the life of a Compose frame by breaking it down into its core phases: Composition, Layout, and Draw. Using realistic scenarios and diving into Perfetto trace analysis, we will show you how to get your bearings and identify performance problems from a trace.

Along our performance journey, we will look at common pitfalls (such as unnecessary recompositions or inefficient custom design system setups), how to recognize them from traces and how you can avoid them. Oh, and we’ll share tooling recommendations to help you optimize your apps!

sessions.title: Atomic Design, Enforced: Scaling Mobile Design Systems
sessions.description:
Design systems are easy to start but hard to scale. As your codebase and team grow, an unstructured design system can become a bottleneck when building new features. Components get duplicated, styling decisions leak into the UI layer, and inconsistencies spread across the app, degrading the user experience.

This raises a few questions every mobile team has to answer: How do you organize your design system into layers of reusable components? How do you decide when a component belongs in the UI layer versus the design system? And how do you prevent AI agents from re-creating existing UI components?

In this session, we will show how we adapted Atomic Design in our production Android apps using Jetpack Compose. You will learn how to organize your design system into primitives, tokens, atoms, molecules, organisms, and templates, enforce clear boundaries with lint rules, and create workflows for AI agents to implement consistent UI that follows your design system rules.

sessions.title: Edge to Cloud: Running AI Models and Architecting Durable Memory Across Devices
sessions.description: Building a distributed AI application requires determining where models execute—on local devices or in the cloud—and how they share context and memories. This session details an architecture that balances execution: running lightweight models on client hardware for speed and privacy, while offloading complex reasoning to cloud infrastructure. We will show how you can architect a pipeline that runs from device to cloud, and uses online and offline analysis to create durable memories that AI can use. We will also show how AI coding tools help design these systems.

sessions.title: Beyond the Chat Bubble: Mastering Generative UI in Flutter
sessions.description:
Quick - name the first generative AI interface that pops to your head. Was it an input field and chat bubbles? I thought so.

As AI models get smarter and context windows grow, limiting our apps to just text feels outdated. Why settle for a paragraph of text when you could render a clickable carousel, a live chart, or a custom-built form? Generative UI (GenUI) allows us to move beyond simple chat and generate entire interactive experiences on the fly.

In this talk, we’ll explore the Flutter GenUI SDK to learn how you can use orchestration layers and widget catalogs to transform AI intent into rich, interactive Flutter experiences.

sessions.title: Building a Real-Time Multiplayer Space Game with Flame and Supabase
sessions.description:
Building real-time multiplayer games traditionally meant setting up dedicated game servers, orchestrating complex WebSocket states, and dealing with massive infrastructure overhead. But what if you could manage a global game loop using only Flutter and serverless primitives?

Led by a core maintainer of Flame and a Supabase SDK engineer, this hands-on workshop walks you through building a fast-paced multiplayer space shooter from scratch. We’ll skip the backend infrastructure headaches and leverage Supabase Realtime to power our netcode. You will learn how to initialize a high-performance 2D canvas with the Flame engine, bind player inputs to ship physics, and synchronize positions at 60 FPS across clients using Supabase Broadcast events. Furthermore, we’ll use Supabase Presence to build dynamic game lobbies and handle abrupt player disconnections cleanly. Stop dreaming about your multiplayer game idea and come build it, run it locally, and deploy it globally in a single session.

sessions.title: Jaspr in Production: How we rebuilt Dart and Flutter's Web Presence
sessions.description:
Over the past year, we’ve migrated all of flutter.dev, docs.flutter.dev and dart.dev to Jaspr, the open-source framework for building websites with Dart. In this talk, we share the full story of the migration, and see if Jaspr stood up to the task of powering documentation for millions of Flutter developers.

We will look at:
- The challenges we faced while migrating each website.
- What benefits and drawbacks we ended up with.
- How dogfooding Jaspr at scale shaped the framework itself.

You will also get an early look at new and upcoming features in Jaspr — many of them driven by real-world needs from this migration — focused on improving developer experience, performance, and full-stack capabilities.


Whether you’re building apps, websites, or both, this talk will show how Jaspr fills a crucial gap in the Flutter ecosystem. By the end, you’ll know of where Jaspr is today, how it holds up in production, and whether it’s something you can confidently bring into your own stack.

sessions.title: From Vibe-Coded Viral MVP to Launchable Product in 90 Days
sessions.description:
What happens when a viral, AI-vibe-coded Flutter app has to become a real, shippable product fast?

This is the story of Divine, a decentralized reboot of Vine backed by Jack Dorsey. Its CEO built an exciting MVP with vibe coding, but turning that into a stable, production-grade Flutter app was another challenge entirely. That's where Very Good Ventures came in. Together, Divine and VGV will share how we went from 500+ open issues and no CI/CD to a live product on Zapstore in 90 days.

Key Takeaways:

- Assess and stabilize AI-generated codebases.
- Agentic Flutter engineering: embedding AI agents like Claude Code as co-developers and reviewers
- Building on NOSTR: Flutter meets decentralized social

sessions.title: Developing better games with AI without drowning in slop and technical debt
sessions.description:
In game development, quality and shipping velocity are everything, but developing new features and improving existing ones takes time you often feel you don't have, so you end up not implementing them.
But what if you could leverage AI-assisted workflows to make more stable and content-rich commercial games faster?
In this talk, I'll show you some practical uses of AI tools that can help your team ship better games, faster, without losing their identity, drowning in AI slop or technical debt.

Target audience: Senior/Mid game developers; Creative directors

Takeaways:
- What AI is good at, risks of using it and misconceptions
- What tools to use to implement AI-assisted workflows to both write code and create visual assets
- How to multiply the output of your team with AI workflows
- Debugging with AI so you don't have to go through logs manually
- How to use AI to create automated tests and do code reviews pass
- Preventing AI slop and technical debt

sessions.title: The Runtime Strikes Back
sessions.description:
Dynamic instrumentation is one of the most powerful techniques in mobile app reversing, but modern apps are no longer passive targets. Through RASP, anti-tamper checks, environmental detection, integrity monitoring, and runtime self-defence, apps are increasingly aware of when they are being observed.

This talk explores the cat-and-mouse game between mobile analysts and applications that actively resist inspection. We will look at the broad categories of anti-instrumentation techniques used in real-world iOS and Android apps, how they affect the reversing workflow, and how analysts can adapt without relying on brittle one-off bypasses.

We will also discuss the role of newer tooling, lower-level visibility, custom instrumentation strategies, and LLMs in helping triage noisy traces, explain unfamiliar code paths, identify suspicious patterns, and accelerate the loop between observation and hypothesis.

sessions.title: AI can write the code, but it cannot ship the app
sessions.description:
We can now one-shot a decent app prototype with a single prompt. But it does not scale well. Codebases quickly become unmaintainable when agents keep suggesting new features that have no good product reason to exist. Task boards can fill with agent-generated activity: hypothetical bugs that were never reproduced in simulators, and features that crash the app because native APIs were used incorrectly.

This talk is about building Expo apps that get better with agents. We’ll look at how to keep agents grounded with current SDK documentation, how to use them to run real QA flows with simulator-control tooling, and how to decide which tasks to delegate to save time and which require human product taste.

sessions.title: Building a Figma to React Native AI Factory
sessions.description:
Ask enough React Native devs about the Figma MCP and you'll hear the same verdict: it's useless for React Native.

On a recent project, we set out to automate a chunk of our SDLC: generate production-ready RN screens directly from Figma designs. The Figma MCP sat at the core of this pipeline, and its "s*** for RN" reputation preceded it. So we dug in and realised that the MCP was doing its job. The failures were coming from everything around it: how the designs were structured, how web-shaped output got mapped onto React Native, and the fact that the agent had no reliable way to see what it had actually built.

You'll leave knowing:
- Why frame structure, layer naming, and a disciplined design system have the biggest impact on output quality.
- How to translate web-oriented MCP output into high-quality React Native.
- How to close the agent's feedback loop, giving it both the rendered screen and the component tree so it can see what it built, diff it against the design, and fix itself.

sessions.title: Prove Your Flows: Mapping Every Screen with Statecharts
sessions.description:
Every mobile app is already a state machine. Your routes, screens, auth gates, and multi-step flows are states & transitions, whether you modeled them that way or not. However, code under-specifies the behavior, making it hard to easily tell which screens are reachable, which flows are dead, or which edge cases you never handled.

This talk shows how to derive a framework-agnostic state machine from an existing codebase, whatever navigation library you use, then automatically walk every reachable path through it (with graph algorithms, not AI!). Instead of guessing at coverage, you get a map of every state your app can reach, the exact actions that get there, and the flows that should exist but don't.

sessions.title: Swift Export: Where We Stand
sessions.description:
Swift Export, the much-anticipated project from the JetBrains team, has been in progress for some time and is currently in the Experimental state. The project’s goal is to make calling shared Kotlin code from Swift more intuitive and idiomatic for Swift developers (and dare I say, even fun?).

In this talk, we will see exactly what the current state of Swift Export is, with some live coding demonstrating how to go from the old “Objective-C bridge” way to the new “Swift Export” way. We will discuss the currently supported features and any subtleties we encountered while mapping Kotlin to Swift. We will also discuss what still needs further work and refinement, and how the community can get involved.

By the end of the session, you’ll be able to assess for yourself whether Swift Export is ready to adopt for your team and use case, based on some guidelines from the Swift Export team. More idiomatic Swift, happier team!

sessions.title: Faster iOS Builds: Measuring Performance and Uncovering Hidden Compiler Costs
sessions.description:
Slow builds impact more than developer experience—they reduce productivity, slow feedback cycles, and increase CI infrastructure costs. As iOS codebases grow, even small increases in compile time can result in thousands of lost engineering hours.

The most expensive build-time bottlenecks are often the least obvious. Many originate from Swift compiler behavior, language features, and everyday coding patterns rather than the build system alone.

This session demonstrates how to measure and analyze iOS build performance using Xcode, compiler diagnostics, and build analysis tools. Through real-world examples, we'll uncover hidden compiler costs, explore practical optimization techniques, and discuss how AI can help engineers interpret build data, identify bottlenecks, and accelerate performance investigations.

sessions.title: AI Made Coding Faster. Why Aren’t We Shipping Faster?
sessions.description:
AI can now generate code, tests, documentation, and pull requests in a fraction of the time. Yet many teams are not shipping meaningfully faster.

The reason is simple: implementation was only one part of a complex system. As coding accelerates, the bottleneck moves downstream to architectural review, pull request fatigue, QA pipelines, release coordination, and the human attention required to understand machine-generated changes. What happens when machine-speed output enters an engineering system designed around human-speed production?

Drawing on practical leadership experience with agentic development and mobile delivery, this talk examines a systemic trap: local productivity gains can increase review queues, expand work in progress, and create new pressure across the delivery process. Attendees will learn how to identify where their bottleneck has moved, reduce downstream pressure, and redesign engineering workflows for faster, safer delivery in an AI-assisted organization.

sessions.title: Is Flutter a Smart Bet in an AI-Driven Job Market?
sessions.description:
Artificial intelligence is rapidly changing the job market, and many students and professionals are asking difficult questions: What skills will still matter tomorrow? Which technologies are worth investing time in? How do we avoid becoming obsolete as AI continues to reshape the industry?

This roundtable opens a discussion around the role of Flutter in this changing landscape. As entry-level roles evolve and traditional career paths become less predictable, choosing the right tools and technologies is no longer just a technical decision, it’s a strategic one.

Together, we’ll explore whether Flutter’s cross-platform approach, versatility, and broad application across mobile, web, desktop, and emerging experiences can make it a valuable foundation for an uncertain future. 

Expect an informal conversation with different perspectives, experiences, and practical insights rather than a one-way presentation.

sessions.title: Building Playable 3D Worlds with Three.js and AI-Assisted Blender Workflows
sessions.description: AI tools can generate impressive 3D assets quickly, but turning those assets into a playable browser experience still requires a real production pipeline. In this session, I’ll demonstrate an end-to-end workflow for taking AI-assisted 3D assets into Blender, cleaning and optimizing them, exporting them for the web, and assembling an interactive world in Three.js. We’ll cover topology, scale, pivots, textures, materials, collision geometry, GLB export, loading performance, and the foundations of first-person controls, with a look at what changes for third-person experiences. Attendees will leave with a repeatable workflow for moving from experimental assets to efficient, interactive 3D worlds that run reliably in the browser.

sessions.title: AI & Android Gathering
sessions.description:
Location: Activity & Networking Area Level 2

All Android-related community members come together for meet & greet

sessions.title: Break
"You Got This": Why Simple Agents Win
sessions.description:
The more dynamic the environment, the more boring your orchestration should be...
In the AWS AI League London finals, the winning edge was not an elaborate prompt stack or a swarm of agents. It was a simple architecture: explicit state, narrow tools, reactive logic, and orchestration simple enough that failures were obvious. This talk argues that the KISS principle is not anti-agent; it is how you build agents that survive real environments. I’ll show where LLM reasoning helps, where deterministic software should take over, and how to recognise when added complexity is actually justified.

sessions.title: When Emojis Break: A Cross-Platform Rendering Challenge
sessions.description:
Emoji rendering is deceptively complex in cross-platform applications. While Kotlin Multiplatform (KMP) and Compose Multiplatform enable shared UI across Android, iOS, JavaScript, and WebAssembly, visual consistency remains challenging due to platform-specific font rendering systems.

This talk explores a real-world issue where emojis rendered correctly on Android and iOS but failed on web targets. Despite sharing the same UI code, differences in browser and WebAssembly font support resulted in an inconsistent user experience.

To address this, we adopted a unified typography strategy using the Noto Color Emoji TrueType font as a shared application asset. Rather than relying on platform-provided emoji support, emoji rendering became an application-managed concern, ensuring consistent behavior across all targets.

By treating emojis as first-class typography assets rather than platform-dependent artefacts, we achieved a more predictable and consistent cross-platform UI experience.

sessions.title: Can You Trust a Non-Deterministic Agent to Test Your App?
sessions.description:
Computer use agents can drive any interface a human can, from head units to mobile HMIs to companion apps, without per-platform test code. But they're non-deterministic: the same instruction can take a different path each run. The catch is that the system under test is non-deterministic too. New releases shift the UI, ops pushes environment changes, data drifts, and most test failures come from state nobody controls. So how do you trust an agent in a CI pipeline where a flaky test is worse than no test?
This talk walks through the engineering patterns that make agent-driven test automation reliable enough to gate releases. We'll cover why both the agent and the application carry non-deterministic state, how to write intent-based tests that absorb that state instead of breaking on it, and how to harness and guardrail agent runs so the output is structured, auditable evidence rather than a noisy log.

sessions.title: Supercharged WebView Observability: Or what happens when Android and Frontend engineers talk
sessions.description:
For too long, WebViews have remained a "black box" where standard observability tools go dark. This session explores the technical (and interpersonal) breakthrough that occurs when Android and Frontend engineers collaborate to fix this blind spot using modern web techniques.

Learn the practical implementation details for capturing critical performance metrics (LCP, INP, CLS) using Google Chrome Web Vitals, monitoring granular user activity like "rage clicks," and gaining deep diagnostic visibility. We’ll show you how to funnel console output, resource errors, and promise rejections directly into the native platform layer for a unified source of truth.

sessions.title: All Answers, AIs? What Three Years of AI-Assisted Mobile Development Actually Delivered
sessions.description:
We now have an AI for every answer. Increasingly, one AI writes the code, another reviews it, and a third tries to break it.

With good steering, domain knowledge, and human judgment, these tools are valuable. But using them across the whole mobile lifecycle creates a dangerous illusion that faster generation means the hard parts of engineering have disappeared. They have not.

This talk looks at how mobile development changed from 2023 to 2026, beyond the demos and social media claims. We compare AI security detectors against established analysis, count the false positives, and show real Android code that was AI generated, AI reviewed, AI scanned, and still shipped with exploitable bugs.

The same acceleration is reaching reverse engineering, from Frida instrumentation to obfuscated code. Speed is not mastery.

AI made many parts of the process faster. Quality, stability, maintainability, and security still require real work.

sessions.title: Your Design System Has Two Codebases. Let's Fix That.
sessions.description:
Figma is where your Design System lives. Jetpack Compose is how it's built. But when developers open Figma Dev mode, they see generic Jetpack Compose scaffolding - not your actual components. So they search, guess, or roll their own. Design drift happens silently.

In this talk, I'll show how Figma Code Connect bridges that gap: developers see real Design System snippets directly in Figma, with the right Composable and the right parameters. We'll also cover pairing Code Connect with Figma MCP, so your AI coding assistant speaks your Design System's language instead of vanilla Compose.

Plus: how we scaled Code Connect across a large component library using Claude Code - the prompts that worked and the mistakes we made.

sessions.title: Full-Stack Dart with HTMX
sessions.description:
What if building interactive web applications did not require a separate frontend, JSON API, client-side router, and state-management layer?

In this session, we will look at the web as a hypermedia system, starting from HTML, HTTP, links, and forms, and see how Single Page Applications changed that model.

We will then explore how htmx extends HTML, allowing elements to make HTTP requests, receive HTML fragments, and update parts of the page without a full reload.

Finally, we will see how this approach works with Dart, when hypermedia-driven applications are a good fit, when a client-heavy architecture makes more sense, and why simplicity still matters.

sessions.title: Bridging the Gap: Incremental Navigation & UI Migration in Flutter Apps
sessions.description: Migrating a large Flutter app from a legacy setup to a modern, accessible architecture cannot happen overnight. But how do you keep your app fully functional when half of it is on an old navigation system (like GetX) and the other half uses modern patterns on Web and Mobile? This fast-paced session breaks down the technical details of managing a hybrid state during step-by-step refactoring. We’ll explore how to use Hexagonal Architecture to isolate legacy code, maintain design system consistency, and ensure accessibility (a11y) standards remain unbroken while transitioning your codebase package by package.

sessions.title: Beyond DevTools: What is Flutter doing on my GPU?
sessions.description:
Build, layout, paint, composite, rasterize: every Flutter frame runs this gauntlet, but most performance advice only covers the first half. DevTools shows your widgets rebuilding. It doesn't show what happens once your layer tree crosses to the raster thread and becomes real GPU work. In the era of liquid glass, that's where the cost hides: backdrop blurs, saveLayer, custom shaders, overdraw. Your phone warms up and you don't know why. (Did you know a spinning progress indicator can keep the whole pipeline awake every vsync and overheat your app?)

We follow one slow frame from build to burn: separate the UI thread from the raster thread, drop into Xcode's Metal frame capture to see the real GPU draw calls, then cover concrete ways to cut that cost. The pipeline and the fixes are platform agnostic; we demo on iOS and explain how the same investigation maps to Android. We close with an AI-assisted Claude Code skill that reads a trace and explains it.

sessions.title: Evolving the Loop: What Idle Games Taught Us About the Shift to Hybrid Idle
sessions.description: The classic 'tap-and-wait' idle loop is no longer enough to satisfy modern mobile players. Across the industry, player fatigue has driven a massive shift toward hybrid mechanics, arcade-idle loops, and active meta-layers. But how do you evolve a proven game without alienating core fans or destroying your UI? In this fast-paced 20-minute lightning talk, we explore the macro trends reshaping the idle genre through the lens of our own studio's journey. We’ll break down the design and UX lessons learned from transitioning our flagship games from pure idle toward active hybrid gameplay.

sessions.title: Don’t Let Attackers Hijack Your App’s Task
sessions.description:
Task hijacking is when a malicious app launches its Activity into the task of another. The trivial counter to the simplest form is to set an empty task affinity for your Activity. That's not all, as the more serious Strandhogg 2.0 exploit doesn't rely on Manifest-based configuration and can dynamically target multiple applications. There is also the fact that the system still allows background apps to launch their Activity on top of others in certain circumstances.

There are mitigations for most attacks on newer Android versions, but if your app needs to be backward compatible, it is entirely on you to apply defense in depth, and I'll show you how, including a quick demo.

sessions.title: Automating Mobile QA with Cloud Agents
sessions.description:
Modern mobile QA can move beyond scripts and CI pipelines into autonomous, cloud-executed agents. Traditional QA approaches struggle with flakiness, limited coverage, slow feedback loops, and not leveraging powerful mechanisms such as React Native's split between JS and native bundles. Teams need more reliable, automated ways to validate real user flows before code reaches production. Agent-based QA provides a scalable way to continuously verify app behavior on real devices and reduce risk in fast-moving codebases.

This talk shows how to design and operate QA agents that run against real iOS and Android devices hosted remotely. We’ll cover the architecture of a reliable agent, connecting Linux-based infrastructure to mobile devices running on macOS, and integrating outputs like screenshots, recordings, and logs directly into pull requests.

sessions.title: Building a multi-agent tabletop game master with TypeScript
sessions.description:
I built a tabletop RPG game master powered by multiple AI agents that talk to each other. One agent builds the world and generates characters. Another runs the campaign according to your rules. The whole thing is orchestrated in TypeScript and rendered in a React app.

In this session, you will watch me go from a single agent responding to prompts to a full multi-agent system with coordinated roles. You will see how agents communicate and streams responses in real-time, and how the game session stays alive across turns and how I connect it all to frontend.

You'll walk away knowing how to wire multiple AI agents together in TypeScript and plug them into a React app without turning your codebase into spaghetti.

sessions.title: True native RecyclerView & UICollectionView in react native, the challenge of sync rendering
sessions.description:
The never-ending quest for the fastest list library in react-native just got a new combatant: react-native-list.
It's a novel approach where the underlying list is a true native RecyclerView on android and a UICollectionView on iOS, promising the "most native" experience possible. This requires synchronous rendering of react(-native) views on another thread, which is a very interesting technical challenge.
This talk will be about react & react-native rendering internals to understand how such a library can be made possible, educate about the new react-native-worklets bundle mode and in general dwell on the challenges of list rendering in react-native.

sessions.title: Coding as a Creative Tool
sessions.description:
Creative coding has always lived at the intersection of art, design, and technology. But within the Swift community, it's still an emerging practice.
This talk is about how creative coding can feel less like learning a tool and more like a way of expressing yourself. I'll share my journey of discovering creative coding through SwiftUI, and how that exploration led to building a node-based app for creating generative visuals with Swift and SwiftUI.
We'll look at what creative coding actually is, how it works in practice with Swift, and how an app grew out of asking one simple question: what if Swift could be your creative tool?

sessions.title: Where Do the Bytes Go? Making iOS App Growth Observable at Scale
sessions.description:
App size is one of the few product metrics that directly affects App Store conversion, yet most iOS teams can only see it as a single opaque number. 

In this talk, I’ll show how we made app size understandable and actionable in a large-scale iOS codebase. 

We built Caliper, an open-source Swift CLI tool that analyzes IPA files, LinkMap output, and asset catalogs to break app size down into modules, dependencies, and resources. It turns build artifacts into structured reports that make growth visible and attributable. 

At CHECK24 Profis, this approach helped reduce our app size from 95 MB to 21.62 MB by exposing hidden contributors and making ownership of changes explicit across teams. 

I’ll walk through how iOS app size is actually composed, how we extract meaningful signals from build outputs, and how we integrated this into CI to prevent regressions.

sessions.title: Beyond the Crash: From 46-Hour Detection to Real-Time Recovery
sessions.description:
What's scarier than a mobile app crash? A silent failure. A broken payment flow, a black map screen, or a wallet that won't load. These "silent killers" don't trigger crash reports and can go undetected for hours, silently destroying revenue and operations.

In a 2024 analysis, our average time to detect a critical mobile incident was a staggering 46.21 hours. This delay represents a massive, unmeasured cost. This talk tackles this mobile "blind spot." We will explore a framework for "Critical Observability"—a strategy to proactively identify, monitor, and alarm on the core functions of your app, so you can stop an incident in minutes, not days.

sessions.title: AI workways for a happy brain
sessions.description:
AI tricks and tools change by the hour, but our biology, our brains, do not. How do we work in this new way, with these changing tools, without depleting ourselves. What can we do to improve our energy so we don't feel completely exhausted and overwhelmed at the end of the day working with AI. The lens we take is that of a developer shipping features or clearing tech debt. 70 Android engineers, 500k+ lines of code, 1k+ modules

We will briefly look at the different ways AI work depletes us so we can understand how to tackle each. We will get a quick overview of how our brain works. The bulk of the talk we will dig into adjustments we can make in the way we work to stay healthy and energised while we are surrounded by multiple agents and orchestrators. What known advice can we adjust to the AI workflows?

Looking after ourselves will help us to achieve some of the productivity gains AI promises without burning our brains to a crisp.

sessions.title: From Pixels to Spatial Intelligence: Building Next-Gen Apps with Android XR and Edge AI
sessions.description:
Modern Android XR applications go beyond static visualization by using interactive 3D models that respond to user context. This session covers how to build and optimize 3D assets for Android XR and explores runtime techniques like object recognition, spatial anchoring, and gesture interactions to guide users through workflows such as assembly, maintenance, and training scenarios. 
The second part focuses on integrating AI into these XR environments. We’ll look at how to build or adapt AI models and feed them with domain-specific content like manuals or training data. This enables systems that assist users in real time—answering questions, providing step-by-step guidance, and adapting to user actions using multimodal inputs like voice and gestures. 
Finally, we’ll connect these concepts to real-world use cases and architecture. From industrial training to immersive education, combining XR with AI creates scalable and practical solutions.

sessions.title: Break
401 Unauthorized? Auth & Communication Protocols for Agents Made Easy
sessions.description:
Struggling with agent security? Who acts as the OAuth server when an MCP client connects? When one agent calls another via A2A, does it authenticate as itself or on behalf of the user? And how do you propagate tokens across an agent chain without creating a confused deputy?

As agents move from demos to production, these questions become blockers. This session cuts through the complexity of MCP Auth, A2A, OAuth 2.1, and OIDC — clarifying what each protocol solves, where trust boundaries live, and how token exchange, scopes, and agent identity actually fit together.

Walk away with a clear mental model for securing agent communication and a plan to implement it in your own stack.

sessions.title: Close the Loop: Building a Reliable Workflow with AI Coding Agents
sessions.description:
AI coding agents can write code fast, but in real projects they still get lost, miss hidden constraints, and return confident wrong answers. This talk is about closing the engineering loop: collect requirements, change the code, validate the result, compare it with what “done” means, and repeat until it is ready for review.

I’ll show how to give agents the right context, create validation cycles with tests, logs, screenshots, UI state, and reports, and scale the workflow with running apps, parallel sessions, cloud emulators, and orchestration.

Attendees will leave with a practical workflow for using agents with less babysitting and more confidence.

sessions.title: I know where you are...
sessions.description:
Delivering seamless location-based experiences seems really simple, until your user steps into a concrete subway or an urban canyon and their blue dot completely vanishes. In this session, we’ll strip away the mystery behind the modern location stack, breaking down how everything from satellite positioning (GPS/GNSS), GeoIP, WiFi, Bluetooth beacons, and Ultra-Wideband (UWB) actually works under the hood. We will also look at what future positioning technologies are on the horizon, and when we can expect them to land on iOS and Android devices.

Tailored for all mobile frameworks, PMs, and designers alike, this talk tackles the trade-offs between pinpoint accuracy, battery life, user experience, and privacy, alongside the messy realities of indoor positioning. You’ll walk away knowing which technology to leverage for your specific use case, how to design a robust solution, and how to build location-aware apps that delight users.

sessions.title: Native Mobile and AI
sessions.description:
Native mobile development means building the same app twice, once per platform. Historically, teams faced a tradeoff: two native codebases for the best experience, or a cross-platform framework and its compromises. Frontier LLMs change that equation. Modern models and agents can now analyze and translate app code between platforms—turning what was a costly duplication into an engineering problem.
This talk explores what that shift means for native mobile. We've all heard the AI takes, from "pure hype" to "devs are obsolete." This isn't that talk, though we'll touch on it. Instead, we'll focus on why native mobile is uniquely positioned: it's critical to most products, dominated by two platforms, and usually delivered natively for the best user experience.
How does cross-platform translation actually work? What does it mean for how we build apps? I gave an intro to this a year ago, but so much has changed—and no domain will be impacted more.

sessions.title: An SDK Is Not an App
sessions.description:
Every Android engineer consumes SDKs in their app. Far fewer devs had to build an SDK by tearing apart an app that was never designed to be one. Expect war stories with the receipts from our journey of abstracting an app to an SDK. A type definition in the public API that silently collided with the consumer's types. A manifest entry that quietly blocked Play Store installs. A service locator that failed unpredictably in the host app.  

Building an Android SDK is not just extracting a feature module—it is a fundamental shift in constraints. We'll dissect the failures we encountered while turning an app into a reusable Android SDK, why they happened, and how to prevent them from happening again. Whether you plan to ship an AAR or considering it in the future or just want to stop guessing why a third-party SDK is misbehaving, you'll leave able to understand SDKs from both sides of the boundary.

sessions.title: Going Multiplatform with Your Android App
sessions.description:
Existing Android apps are in a great position to expand into Kotlin Multiplatform: you might already be using patterns, libraries, and APIs that work on more platforms than just Android. With Compose Multiplatform, you can build an app with a fully shared Kotlin codebase, targeting iOS, desktop, and even the web!

In this talk, we’ll look at how you can migrate an existing Android app to multiplatform. As this can be a significant engineering effort for an existing, well-established app, we’ll also discuss how to plan and organize the required changes, and how to adopt KMP incrementally across your codebase without disrupting day-to-day development.

sessions.title: Navigation 3 & Adaptive Layouts: A Real Migration Story
sessions.description:
I migrated a production Compose app from a third-party navigation library to Navigation 3. The app compiled. Then every detail screen crashed on launch.

This talk is the story of that migration: the paradigm shift of owning your back stack as plain Compose state, the runtime crash caused by a mismatch between Navigation 3's destination model and standard ViewModel argument passing, and the injection pattern that fixed it.

The second half covers adaptive layouts: a two-layer approach where navigation chrome adapts independently from content layout, connected by a single line of reactive state. I'll also cover the edge cases documentation doesn't prepare you for: landscape phone quirks, per-screen layout branching, and a transition animation fix that took surprisingly long to find.

Every example is from a production app on the Play Store. Every pitfall is one I actually hit.

sessions.title: Extending Productivity: Building Your Own Android Studio Plugins
sessions.description:
Android Studio is powerful - but your real productivity gains come from bending it to your workflow. In this talk, you'll see how to build custom plugins that eliminate repetitive tasks, enforce team conventions, and automate what your team does every single day.
Through real examples from production, you'll learn:

How the IntelliJ platform works under the hood and where to hook into it
How to spot automation opportunities in your daily workflow
The minimal steps to go from idea to working plugin
How to distribute your plugin to teammates with zero friction

No prior plugin experience needed. You'll leave with a clear mental model and the confidence to ship your first plugin.

1. Attendees will understand that building Android Studio plugins is more approachable than it looks — the barrier to entry is low with the right mental model
2. Attendees will be able to identify real automation opportunities in their own daily workflow and translate them into plugin ideas
3. Attendees will leave with a practical, end-to-end understanding of the plugin development lifecycle: from idea to distribution

sessions.title: Gemini in your Flutter app with Firebase AI Logic
sessions.description: What if you could add gen AI to your Flutter app today, calling Gemini directly from your Dart code with no backend to build or maintain? Firebase AI Logic makes this possible, already trusted by thousands of apps in the App Store and Play Store, serving millions of requests. In this session, you will go from zero to a working AI feature in minutes: generate text, images, and structured output, stream live conversations, and call tools, all from the client. Then we will make it production-ready: protect your app with App Check, update prompts instantly with Server Prompt Templates, and understand usage with AI Monitoring. Be ready to ship AI features your users will love.

sessions.title: Write Once, Map Everywhere: Cross-Platform Location Apps with Flutter + Mapbox
sessions.description:
If you've got a Flutter app already up and running and you're thinking about adding a map or some location smarts to it, this session is for you. We'll take an app and drop a map right into it, live, on a mobile emulator: get the map on screen, style it up, add some annotations, wire up interaction, and make it feel native to the rest of the UI. While we're at it, we'll toss in location search too, just to show how little extra effort it takes.

Once we've got that feature solid on mobile, we're going to do something fun: run that exact same code in a browser, no changes needed. The Mapbox Maps SDK for Flutter now supports web in public preview, and we'll wrap up talking about what that means if your app needs to live on more than just mobile.

Come see how quickly maps and location can go from "not in the app yet" to shipped, and leave with a good sense of where Flutter and Mapbox are headed next.

sessions.title: Run Dart everywhere with WebAssembly
sessions.description:
As Dart developers, we mainly know WebAssembly as a faster target for our Flutter web apps. But did you know that WebAssembly can run outside of the web too? Its portability, fast startup times and builtin sandboxing makes it a great target for serverless runtimes, IoT and even embedded systems.

Starting with Dart 3.13, it's possible to compile apps to WebAssembly without requiring JavaScript or any web APIs. This talk explores the landscape of WebAssembly outside of the web and answers the most important question of them all: How do I run Dart on that?

sessions.title: One Core, Two Shells: Flutter from Mobile to Embedded
sessions.description:
We made a bet that should have scared us more than it did: tear the UI framework out of our embedded product and rebuild the interface in Flutter.

These are precision measurement devices, not screens with a computer behind them. We already ran Flutter on mobile. The embedded front end was something else entirely. Betting our product experience on one shared core and two platform shells was either going to make us faster or set us back a year.

This is the story of that bet: the decision, the seam, the parts we had to build ourselves, and what we would tell anyone standing where we stood. The win was real. So was the work it took to get there.

Whether you run a Flutter mobile team or just wonder if Flutter belongs on hardware, come find out what it actually takes.

sessions.title: Showcasing Unity games with WebGPU: Lessons from the real world
sessions.description:
Is WebGPU ready for primetime? We share real-world lessons from publishing a preview of World of Us, our Unity based open world game for children aged 8-10, directly in the browser. Learn what worked, what surprised us, and what we’d do differently as we rethought the first-time user experience from traditional client download to instant web experience server. 

We’ll cover Unity template export, Terraform web architecture, localization strategies, Grafana analytics, and marketing integrations such as email capture. Whether you are a game developer, XR creator, or part of a DevOps team, you’ll leave with practical insights, pitfalls to avoid, and what it takes to ship a future-ready Unity experience on the Web without being afraid of a little MarTech.

sessions.title: Universally (Un)Reliable Frida Instrumentation
sessions.description:
Traditional Frida workflows often rely on assumptions that don't hold across all modern mobile applications. This talk explores experimental instrumentation techniques for investigating applications when conventional approaches fail, with the goal of understanding application behaviour rather than simply bypassing protections.

Topics include bypassing certificate pinning by replacing strings in memory, locating X509 certificate structures by working backwards from trusted CA names, and introducing Frimon - a tool built on Frida's eBPF tracer that adapts ideas from Procmon to complement frida-discover and frida-trace. The talk also explores instrumenting application UIs and WebViews, and discusses the challenges posed by frameworks such as Flutter and React Native/Hermes. Each technique is introduced from first principles before a technical deep dive, a (hopefully live) demonstration, and a discussion of its applicability and drawbacks.

sessions.title: Fullstack web apps on AWS without a PhD in cloud
sessions.description:
You built your frontend application and your app works well in the browser with local data. What do you do when you need a backend? There are many options and even choosing between them can take longer than learning and building the backend.

In this talk, you will learn how to extend an app into the cloud. You will bring your standard JavaScript web server, the same one you run on your laptop to the cloud through serverless cloud functions. It will handle HTTPS, scaling up when people arrive and back to zero when they leave, and keep latency low for users wherever they are. On top of it, you will add database and AI using the code you already write to expand your app's functionality even further. Join us to learn how you can turn your app building skills into full-stack apps on AWS without learning the internals of how cloud compute works.

sessions.title: Visual Editor for Reanimated
sessions.description:
React Native Reanimated is expressive and powerful, but animation is a visual medium being authored as text. The feedback loop is slow: write a timing value, reload, tweak by 50ms, reload again. The gap between what you imagine and what ships is wide, and it stays wide for the entire life of the feature.

Keyframer is a browser-based keyframe editor built specifically for React Native. It borrows its design philosophy from the tools that motion and compositing professionals use, After Effects, DaVinci Resolve's Fusion, Blender's node graph, not to abstract away Reanimated, but to give it a visual surface. Draw keyframes on a timeline. Wire gestures and animations through a node graph. Watch it move in real time on a canvas running the actual Reanimated v4 worklet engine. Then export the code, idiomatic, production-ready, the kind you'd be proud to commit.

Visual tooling doesn't replace Reanimated knowledge, it gives it a faster surface to work on.

sessions.title: Leveraging React Native Web And Custom CLIs: A Debugging Superpower For Coding Agents
sessions.description:
Your coding agent can build a lot of React Native code, but verification still falls heavily on the developer. This talk shows a technique that closes that loop: leverage the fact that Expo can build to web, expose stable test IDs and helper APIs, and create a custom CLI that uses Chrome CDP so the agent can work with the web version of the app while it codes. The agent can inspect state, query the DOM, emulate mobile viewports, capture screenshots, check network logs, and run real product workflows without waiting for a human to describe the problem. 

Attendees will learn how to create app-specific debug CLIs that let agents verify frontend behavior, application state, backend state, and React performance reports, then use those checks to debug and optimize the app.

sessions.title: Swift for Game Development: The Wins, The Walls, The Gaps
sessions.description:
iOS developer by day, game engine developer by night. I love Swift, so I wondered: could my favourite language actually work for games? It has the performance, value types, modern syntax, and a growing story beyond Apple's walled garden. So why is almost no one doing it?
So I tried. 

This talk is the result of that experiment, a dive into the corners of Swift most of us rarely touch.

Part one covers the features that shape game performance: memory layout, struct packing, raw memory, what C/C++ interop really feels like (and where Swift/C++ overpromises), the missing primitive of runtime reflection, Swift on Windows in 2026, and where the language's safety defaults fight you.

Part two is a live demo: building a small physics sandbox on stage with Swift, Raylib, and Box2D. Enough to see the pieces work, and the rough edges too.
Familiarity with Swift and C/C++ basics helps, but no game engine experience needed. 

An honest look at Swift outside Apple's ecosystem.

sessions.title: From Speech to Search: Understanding User Intent with Apple Foundation Models
sessions.description:
What if users could simply say what they want and your app understood their intent?

In this talk, I'll walk through how I built a voice-driven search experience that turns natural language requests such as “vegan pizza under 10€” into structured search queries and filters. Using Apple's Speech framework and Foundation Models, we'll go beyond speech-to-text and explore how on-device AI can understand what users actually mean.

We'll follow the entire journey from spoken input to search results: transcribing speech, extracting product intent, matching dynamic backend filters, and composing a final search request. Along the way, I'll share architectural decisions, implementation details, prompt-design lessons, and practical tradeoffs around privacy, latency, reliability, and cost.

This is a real-world case study in using Apple Foundation Models to build an intelligent product feature, moving beyond chatbots and into user-facing experiences that solve actual problems.

sessions.title: Swift Charts Supercharged: Programming advanced interactive charts
sessions.description:
Swift Charts is a new framework aiming to simplify creating a wide variety of charts and graphs making data visualization easy. However, Apple's own examples are never going beyond the basics: setting up the data source and showing the data. In this talk we'll take a look at probably one of the most complex Swift Charts implementation in details, involving interactive elements, axis auto-scaling, custom formatting and many more customizations to make the experience perfect. We will also go thru the common framework bugs, how to fix them and how Apple works around these bugs with their own apps.


Swift Charts simplifies creating charts, but Apple’s examples cover only basics. This talk explores a complex Swift Charts implementation with interactive elements, auto-scaling, custom formatting, bug fixes, and how Apple handles these issues in apps.

sessions.title: Measuring AI Without Fooling Ourselves
sessions.description:
Most AI coding tools show usage numbers: active users, tokens, and acceptance rates. These help track rollout, but rarely tell leadership whether review, delivery, and quality actually improved.

The harder question is what changed in the workflow: how much AI-assisted code reaches merged PRs, what happens to cycle and review time, whether defects stay under control, and how to measure it without handing vendors broad repo access. That shifts focus from tool usage to the coding harness around the model: permissions, repo access, hooks, logs, and PR flow. It matters more when teams switch between Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, or Copilot.

You will leave knowing:
- how to estimate AI-assisted code in merged PRs without broad vendor access
- which signals beat provider dashboards: cycle time, review time, defects
- where measurement gets risky: privacy, access rights, vendor-only metrics
- how to keep metrics useful when the tool or its pricing change

sessions.title: Crossing the Stack: How Backend Insights Made Me a Stronger Mobile Developer
sessions.description:
As Android developers, we are masters of a deeply specialized craft. But that specialization can sometimes feel like a gilded cage. While our backend counterparts often roam across various domains and languages, mobile engineers can find themselves disconnected from the broader software ecosystem.

This discussion is for those who want to break the "vertical niche" and explore how venturing into the world of TypeScript, API design, and backend architecture can actually make us better mobile engineers. We’ll move beyond the code to discuss how "thinking like a full-stack dev" changes the way we handle errors, collaborate with teammates, and future-proof our careers in an evolving industry.

What we’ll explore together:

The "API Empathy" Shift: How knowing how the sausage is made (the backend) changes how we consume it (the frontend).

The T-Shaped Developer: Balancing deep Android expertise with the broad skills needed to stay relevant in a shifting job market.

sessions.title: RodCone: Building the Universal Infrastructure for Smart Glasses Apps
sessions.description: Meta shipped millions of Ray-Ban smart glasses. Google, Samsung, and Apple are next. But building apps for AI glasses today means wrestling with raw device toolkits, native-only APIs, and custom media pipelines — for each OEM. We started building smart glasses apps two years ago, and quickly realized we were rebuilding the same infrastructure every time: camera access, real-time video relay, audio routing, AI processing. So we built RodCone — a cross-platform SDK and managed cloud that abstracts hardware complexity into a single multi-platform component. Drop in a view, select "glasses" as your source, and start handling multimodal AI events. This talk covers the architecture behind RodCone: how we designed a hardware abstraction layer that works across Meta (and soon Google) glasses, the managed Intelligence Cloud for video ingestion and AI processing, and the lessons learned going from agency project to developer platform.

sessions.title: Lunch
Don't let convenience quietly erode skill
sessions.description:
Engineers can generate working code in seconds, but understanding that code is more important than ever. As the copy-paste solution becomes even easier to reach for, teams need to be confident with analysing AI generated code and, as ever, maintain a good understanding of new tools and technologies.

This talk explores what learning in software engineering looks like in the age of AI, with a focus on mobile teams. Drawing from hands-on experience as a team lead and from building my own personal mobile apps, this talk will cover the skills teams should prioritise, how mobile engineers can build their technical knowledge while using AI tools and my top tips for training up junior colleagues in 2026.

sessions.title: Architecting Agentic Systems
sessions.description:
Most AI applications today are little more than interfaces built on top of large language models. The next generation of intelligent software, however, relies on agentic systems capable of planning, reasoning, collaborating, using tools, and executing complete business workflows autonomously.

This session explores how Software Architects can design production-ready agentic platforms using modern AI models, memory systems, tool calling, MCP integrations, workflow orchestration, observability, and human-in-the-loop controls.

Through a real-world architecture and live demonstrations, attendees will learn how multiple specialized agents can work together to automate complex processes such as customer support, order management, service coordination, and enterprise operations while maintaining security, governance, and scalability.

sessions.title: Develop Smarter, Not Harder: Shipping Peacock's Live NBA Features with AI in the Loop
sessions.description:
How do you build and test a live NBA experience when there's no live game to test against — and how much faster can you go once AI agents join in? At Sky's Prague team we ship Peacock Courtside Live, driven by a feed we don't control: score, clock and game state changing second by second, from backends we don't own, flawless across markets, devices and networks.

This session starts with two habits that make that manageable — if you repeat it, automate it; if you wait for it, mock it — then goes further with AI. You'll learn to automate repetitive API work with an API client (variables, environments, scripting), mock and reshape what you can't control with a proxy tool (map local, modify live data, simulate errors), connect these tools to AI agents via MCP, use AI to speed up problem analysis by pointing you at the failing call, and have AI generate the rules and scripts for you from a plain-English description. You'll leave with a concrete, modern API workflow.

sessions.title: Jetpack Compose Mechanisms
sessions.description:
Nowadays, Jetpack Compose is widely used to build modern Android and multiplatform applications, and it has become much more than just a UI toolkit.

Have you ever wondered how the “magic” behind the `@Composable` function actually works?

In this session, we’ll explore the internal mechanisms of Jetpack Compose, from its three foundational layers: the Compose Compiler, Compose Runtime, and Compose UI. We’ll look at how composable functions are transformed, how state changes trigger recomposition, how UI is measured and laid out, and how these concepts impact performance in real-world applications.

sessions.title: RemoteCompose: From Static SDUI to 60fps Animations Over the Wire
sessions.description:
Server-driven UI always starts small: a bit of JSON, a renderer, done. Then design asks for one more component, the schema gets a version number, and everyone is waiting on an app release again. Then someone asks for an animation.

This talk takes a screen every app has, the full-screen promo that usually ends up in a WebView, and builds it three times.
First the classic way, with everything hardcoded in the app.
Then with a well-built JSON SDUI engine, which goes fine right up until that animation request.
Then with RemoteCompose, where the server sends the UI itself, animation included, and the app just plays it.

Expect live demos, a live vote, and an honest look at what an alpha library can and can't do yet.

sessions.title: The Hitchhiker's Guide to Gradle Troubleshooting
sessions.description:
Just want to focus on writing your app, but something with your build is amiss? Don't panic!
We'll do a deep-dive into how Gradle works under the hood: how do up-to-date-checks, build cache, remote build cache and configuration cache actually work? What's the Gradle daemon for, and why will it launch multiple daemons sometimes, eating up precious memory? Why will parallel builds work beautifully, until they don't? And in particular: what are some nice debugging skills we can use to find the root cause, and some special tips we can use to fix things?
And if that was not enough, we'll do it all live on stage!

Buckle up, and don't forget to bring your towels - it's going to be quite a ride!

sessions.title: AI Doesn't Fix Accessibility. It Amplifies the Problems.
sessions.description:
AI learns from existing code. And existing code is, by and large, not accessible. That means AI doesn't just fail to solve the accessibility problems - it amplifies them.

In this talk, I'll use findings from my test series, generating the same app with four different AI tools and testing each for accessibility, as a starting point. From there, we'll look at what this means in a world where vibe coders and AI agents are shipping apps at scale, tackle the "just prompt it better" argument, and cover concrete steps you can take to your own projects.

The barrier to building apps is lower than ever. The need for understanding accessibility has never been higher.
Key takeaways:

- Why AI amplifies existing accessibility problems rather than solves them
- What vibe coding and AI agents mean for accessibility at scale
- Why asking AI to "just make it accessible" can do more harm than good
- Concrete steps to take to your own projects, with or without AI

sessions.title: Spin at the Gate Until Green: Engineering Primitives for Self-Driving Android Codebases
sessions.description:
Most AI-assisted development fails the same way: the AI produces output, the human checks it manually, finds a problem, re-prompts, and repeats. This loop doesn't scale.

On Android, we have a better option. Gradle tells you if it breaks. The Kotlin compiler tells you if types don't match. Paparazzi tells you if the UI drifted. These are binary gates — and if you have a binary gate, you can remove the human from the loop entirely. The AI submits, the gate checks, it adjusts and resubmits. Spin at the gate until green.

This talk covers the engineering primitives that make this possible: personas, skills, worklogs, postmortems, and spec-driven development. The culmination is a flag lifecycle agent — triggered by a cron job, cleaning up stale feature flags, verified by compile + test + lint. No human in the loop. Working prototype, proven in practice.

sessions.title: Building Flitz: How We Modified the Flutter Engine So Your Team Could Iterate Faster
sessions.description:
Your designer wants to review the latest app changes, but they cannot simply run flutter run. Your product manager wants to tap through a feature before it is merged, and QA wants to validate a flow on a real device without waiting for a full release pipeline. Flutter Go was built to solve this exact collaboration problem: build the app, share a QR code, and let teammates instantly open and test it on their own devices.

In this talk, I will show what it took to make that workflow possible. We will look at why standard Flutter tooling was not enough, what assumptions the Flutter engine makes about building and running apps, and how we modified parts of the engine and worked with the Dart VM to create a faster iteration loop for the whole team.

sessions.title: Turn Your Flutter Side Project into a Real Product
sessions.description:
The story often starts the same way: you have a great app idea, you spend weekends and evenings building it, and at some point, the main feature works.

But then comes the hard part: turning it into a product people can actually find, understand, use, pay for, and give feedback on.

In this talk, we will look at what comes after the core Flutter functionality: onboarding, paywalls, App Store screenshots, user feedback, rating prompts, analytics, support flows, app updates, and other practical details that make an app ready to ship.

We will discuss how to approach these parts without getting overwhelmed, what tools and libraries can help, and what is worth thinking about before launch versus after real users arrive.

By the end of this talk, you will leave with plenty of inspiration, but more importantly, with a practical plan for turning that motivation into action.

Let’s build some cool apps… and actually ship them!

sessions.title: Flutter GenUI: How to build AI-powered experiences users can actually interact with
sessions.description:
See how the GenUI SDK for Flutter is changing how AI-powered apps are built. Instead of forcing users to scroll through walls of text, the GenUI SDK allows AI agents to dynamically generate interactive widgets that match your app's look and feel. 

We will explore the developer benefits of a system that can display custom UI and how to manage state between components to deliver a cohesive developer experience.

In this session, you'll learn how to get started building engaging, context-aware user experiences that go above and beyond a typical chat experience.

sessions.title: LEGO Architecture for Enterprise-Scale Flutter Applications
sessions.description:
As mobile applications grow into large, long-lived systems, maintaining a clear and scalable codebase becomes increasingly challenging. This talk explores a production-proven architectural approach for large-scale Flutter applications, successfully used for several years in a product with millions of users and a multi-million-line codebase, developed by a team of 100+ mobile engineers.
Built around a LEGO concept, where the application is composed of highly modular, interchangeable, self-contained building blocks, this architecture enables teams to develop and deliver features in isolation, while keeping the overall system consistent and maintainable. We’ll cover key aspects such as code organization, state management, navigation, dependency injection, configuration, testing, and more, along with the principles that guided these choices.
You’ll leave with practical recommendations for structuring large codebases and scaling development without sacrificing efficiency or maintainability.

sessions.title: Beyond the Hype: How AI Is Really Used in Game UI/UX
sessions.description:
Figma killers, instant icon generators, automatic layouts, we've all seen the headlines. But what actually happens when these AI tools enter real game production?

This panel brings together four experienced UI/UX designers with completely different approaches to AI. From using AI as a simple day-to-day assistant to building highly automated creative and marketing pipelines, each panelist represents a different point on the AI adoption spectrum. Instead of debating AI's future, we'll compare what actually works today, where the tools still fall short, and why different teams have arrived at very different workflows.


Take away:
-Understand the real spectrum: See how AI adoption actually looks in active game UI/UX production.

-Identify the sweet spots: Learn which design tasks benefit from AI today, and which still strictly require human expertise.

-Get a realistic outlook: Gain a practical perspective on how AI is reshaping design tools, workflows, and long-term careers.

sessions.title: You Are Already Compromised: Why Attestation Is the Foundation of Mobile Security
sessions.description:
Do you have hardcoded API keys in your app? You're already compromised - but not for the reason you think.

Your app can have certificate pinning, encrypted storage, biometric authentication, and runtime integrity checks - and still be completely compromised. Why? Because all of these controls share a silent assumption: that the environment running your app can be trusted. Without attestation, that assumption is never verified.

This talk explores device and app attestation on Android and iOS – what it is, how it works under the hood, and why it forms the root of a secure chain of trust. We'll look at how attackers bypass security controls when attestation is absent or misconfigured, and how to implement it correctly using platform-native mechanisms (Android Key Attestation, Play Integrity API, Apple DeviceCheck and App Attest). It's the one that makes all the others meaningful — presented by the OWASP MAS Author behind the attestation Best Practices, Tests, Demos, and Knowledge base.

sessions.title: Future of React Native: AI, agents, and what comes next
sessions.description: The React Native ecosystem is changing fast, and AI is now influencing everything from code generation and testing to debugging, tooling, and app architecture. This panel brings together voices from across the community to ask what that shift really means for everyday RN developers: which AI and agent workflows are already useful, where the hype still outpaces the reality, and what skills will matter most in the next wave of mobile development. Expect a candid conversation about productivity, code quality, maintainability, and the practical changes teams will need to make as AI becomes part of the React Native workflow.

sessions.title: Dreams and reality of a single codebase
sessions.description:
React Native is well established for building cross-platform native mobile applications, using a declarative paradigm that feels immediately familiar to web developers. This familiarity inevitably raises an obvious question: why not use the exact same React codebase for the web as well?

In this talk, we examine the current state of universal React and what it takes to share components across web and native in production. We share our experience at Zalando adopting React Strict DOM as part of our ongoing migration to React Native and our longer-term vision for a single codebase. Finally, we share the learnings and pain points we encountered while exploring the gap between native-only development and a truly universal codebase.

sessions.title: Divide and Compile: Modular iOS Architecture at Scale
sessions.description:
As an iOS app grows beyond a single team, a monolithic codebase stops being an asset and starts being a liability - merge conflicts multiply, build times balloon, and nobody is quite sure who owns what.
