Splitting into modules is the obvious answer, but the decisions you make early about where to draw boundaries, how to wire dependencies, and what architecture pattern to put inside each module have compounding effects that are very hard to undo at 3,000 files.

This talk walks through the real architectural decisions behind a production banking app split across 45 Swift modules and 3,800 files — what we got right, what we got wrong, and the specific patterns that let a growing team ship features independently without stepping on each other. 

I will cover the Router–Interactor–Builder pattern we use in place of MVVM or TCA, how we enforce module boundaries and prevent circular imports, and the honest impact modular architecture has had on build times and developer experience.

sessions.title: Don’t call us - we’ll call you: Modern SwiftUI callbacks using AsyncStream
sessions.description:
Mobile apps have to permanently deal with asynchronous events - notifications, network status, database updates, user input, and more. The way how we have dealt with asynchronous events has changed significantly over time - from callback delegates to closures, and now AsyncSequence.

In this talk, we will take a deep dive into how AsyncStream works, how to use it in your apps, and how to use it to build ergonomic APIs. We will also take a trip down memory lane to understand where we’re coming from, and how asynchronous APIs have evolved over the years.

I will provide real-world examples to explain the underlying concepts, and we’ll take a look at how the Firebase team implemented asynchronous APIs over the span of almost a decade and several iterations of Objective-C and Swift.

sessions.title: Scaling SwiftData: Performance Lessons from Production Apps
sessions.description:
SwiftData makes it incredibly easy to get started with persistence in SwiftUI applications. The real challenges often appear later as datasets grow, imports become larger, CloudKit synchronization is introduced, and performance issues begin to surface.

In this session, you'll learn how to identify and diagnose SwiftData performance bottlenecks, understand the tradeoffs behind common architectural decisions, and apply practical techniques for building responsive and scalable applications. We'll also explore debugging tools and workflows that can help uncover what SwiftData is doing behind the scenes when performance isn't what you expect.

The lessons shared in this session come from building and shipping four App Store applications powered by SwiftData, including the successes, mistakes, and hard-earned insights gained while maintaining them in production.

sessions.title: Scrum Was a Workaround
sessions.description:
Sprints, story points, and daily standups are now considered essential parts of software development, but they actually started as workarounds. Agile methods were created to address slow, expensive, and unpredictable software projects. When long-term plans kept falling apart as new challenges came up, teams moved to more flexible, step-by-step approaches.

AI has changed development. Now, teams can launch production apps in weeks instead of months. This shift makes upfront planning matter again. I think AI-assisted development is bringing back Waterfall ideas, even though they used to get a bad rap. My team built a production Android app in about a month, and we did it without Scrum, sprints, story points, or retros. I'll go through Scrum's six big promises: predictable delivery, early feedback, adaptability, risk reduction, visibility, and sustainable pace. I'll talk about whether we lost these by skipping process, got them anyway by working fast, or never needed them at this speed.

sessions.title: Intentionally design your career in tech
sessions.description:
Are you a woman/non-binary person in tech (or even tech-adjacent)? This session is especially for you! 

Maia and Pamela have spent many, many years in the tech industry. We will discuss how to design your career thoughtfully, what kind of support (mentorship/sponsorship) is available and how to ask for it, how and what to learn next, and why your voice is needed and important in the field of computer science and beyond. 

Join this session to be encouraged and leave with practical steps on career design and growth!

sessions.title: Authenticating Glasses: How to authenticate with your Android AI Glasses
sessions.description:
Ever wanted to just touch your glasses to log in? Never find your Yubikey, or your phone, but you have your Google AI Glasses always on your nose?

Then you are in luck: In this talk I'll show you how to build an app for your glasses that can authenticate you in your favorite MFA / Passkey applications.

Expect Android Kotlin code, just like you would use for your classical Android app, some XR extensions to give your security the pop it needs, and a bit of security discussions and implications.

This will be a nice mix between the cutting edge technologies of glasses, cybersecurity, Android and authenticators.

sessions.title: AI Gathering
sessions.description:
Location: Activity & Networking Area Level 2

Anyone interested in talking about AI is welcome to come by for a meet and greet.

sessions.title: Break
Supercharging the frontline: Injecting AI skills into frontline workflows
sessions.description:
Much of the AI buzz centers around knowledge workers; however, 80% of the global workforce operates on the frontline. At Zebra, we are obsessed with empowering these frontline workers to perform their day-to-day tasks efficiently and safely.
We concentrate on identifying the micro-moments in workflows that can be vastly improved by AI. But even with great models and capabilities, a massive challenge remains: how do you build and deploy these rapidly at scale so they can be seamlessly "snapped" into both legacy and new workflows.
This talk provides an under-the-hood look into the approach and architecture Zebra has created to solve this integration problem on our Android devices, making agentic AI consumption a reality for enterprise customers.

sessions.title: Beyond Building Agents: Why Harness Design and Optimisation Matter
sessions.description:
Building an AI agent is only the first step. A real agent needs a strong harness around it — the system that controls how the agent thinks, uses tools, manages memory, handles errors, tracks cost, and responds safely.

Without a good harness, even a powerful model can become expensive, slow, unreliable, or difficult to debug. This is why agent optimisation is so important.

In this session, we will explore how to design agents that are not just smart, but also practical for real-world use. We will look at how to reduce token usage, choose the right model for the right task, improve tool calling, manage context, add evaluation checks, and monitor cost before deploying agents into production.

The goal is to help developers move from “I built an agent” to “I built an agent that is reliable, efficient, and ready to use.”

sessions.title: Native Mobile Development with... PHP?
sessions.description:
Yes. Yes, you read that correctly.

"Your scientists were so preoccupied with whether they could, they didn't stop to think if they should", utters Dr. Ian Malcolm. But, when thinking about this, why not? This session concerns the NativePHP framework, which now lets you take an existing Laravel application and compile it, bundled with a PHP runtime, to iOS or Android. With full access to device APIs. All through magical C extensions.

Welcome to Mobile App Development with PHP. In this session, we're going to explore the mad science behind it and see a demo app in action.

sessions.title: The state of AI
sessions.description:
In the early 1950s, Tavistock Institute researchers studied British coal mines. As mines grew more technically efficient through specialized, assembly-line-like work, productivity and morale fell. Mines that reverted to older ways performed better. This gave rise to socio-technical systems: a framework reminding us a workplace is both social and technical, embedded in organization and society. The two breathe together — neglect one and you harm the other.
Eighty years later, AI arrives full of promises: faster, cheaper everything. There are claims whole professions will vanish by end of 2026 — humans optional.
But what lies beyond the hype? The lessons of Tavistock, taught again at scale. People are laid off or fear they're next. CTOs cast coding as assembly-line work while engineers eye carpentry. Communities fight data centers over drinking water. Microsoft "rented" a nuclear plant for 20 years — now a "clean energy center."
This talk looks beyond boomers and doomers.

sessions.title: Coroutines vs. Threads: The True Cost of a Context Switch
sessions.description:
We've all been told that coroutines are "lightweight" and threads are "expensive." But what does this really mean at the OS and hardware level? This talk goes beyond the Kotlin APIs to explore the anatomy of a context switch.

We'll visualize the expensive journey of a blocked thread: the syscall, the kernel trap, the OS scheduler saving registers, and the resulting CPU cache invalidation. Then, we'll contrast it with the elegant, user-space dance of a suspending coroutine, which simply saves its state to a small object on the heap and returns control to its dispatcher.

This session connects high-level code to low-level mechanics. We'll prove this theory in a live demo, using the Android Studio Profiler to watch an app crash under the weight of a few hundred threads, only to then launch 100,000 coroutines with ease. Understanding why this happens will empower you to write, debug, and maintain truly efficient, performant, and scalable Android applications.

sessions.title: BFF4EAE: Your Backend's New Best Friend Forever
sessions.description:
Look, we've all been there. You ship a mobile app. Marketing wants a new flow yesterday. The backend team is three sprints deep in a service mesh refactor. Product is asking why the iOS team is "blocked" again. And somewhere in the middle of all this, somebody — probably you — is duct-taping seventeen REST calls together in a ViewModel and praying the network layer doesn't notice.

Enter the BFF. Backend for Frontend. The pattern your architecture diagrams promised would save you. Except… it didn't. Because we built BFFs that just shuffled JSON around and called it a day. We took "frontend-shaped backend" and made it mean "the same backend, but with worse pagination."

**It's time to do better. It's time for BFF4EAE.**

Backend For Frontend, but For Extending All Endpoints — and by "endpoints" I don't just mean HTTP routes. I mean *intent*. UI state. Actions. Side effects. Feature flags. The whole janky pile of "things the client has to coordinate." A BFF4EAE doesn't just give your mobile app a tailored payload — it gives your mobile app a tailored *brain*, one that knows what to do, when to do it, and (critically) how to stop doing the thing when the thing is no longer the thing.

We're going to talk about building BFFs that are self-controlling — services that own their own state machines, decide their own retries, manage their own degradation, and don't require your mobile client to be the orchestration layer for the entire company. Topics include:

- **Action-shaped APIs** — why `POST /do-the-thing` beats six chained GETs and a prayer, and how to design endpoints that ship *behavior*, not just data
- **The Self-Controlling BFF** — circuit breakers, adaptive backoff, and graceful degradation that lives on the server where it belongs, not smeared across three platforms in slightly incompatible ways
- **UI-as-Contract** — server-driven UI without falling into the "we built a worse React on the wire" trap
- **Action Manifests** — declarative descriptions of what the client *can* do right now, generated by the BFF based on user state, feature flags, and whether the downstream service is having a moment
- **Killing the Coordination Layer** — moving retry logic, dependency resolution, and "wait for these three things then do this fourth thing" out of your mobile codebase and into a place that can actually be tested
- **Versioning without crying** — how to evolve a BFF that controls UI *and* actions without bricking the v3.2.1 app some user refuses to update

A working mental model for treating your BFF as a *product*, not a passthrough. Concrete patterns you can steal on Monday. War stories from shipping this in production at scale, including the parts that went badly because — spoiler — some of it went badly. Honest tradeoffs about when this pattern is overkill and when not using it is malpractice.

Also: opinions. So many opinions. You will not agree with all of them. That's fine. Bring your own.

sessions.title: TestBalloon: Android testing is easier (and more fun) than you think
sessions.description:
You've always wanted an easier way to write tests? Parameterize tests in plain Kotlin? Reuse a series of tests? Easily extend own your test setup? Free yourself from JUnit restrictions while retaining first-class support on Android (and KMP as well)? Not least: Having 50% less code to review?

TestBalloon is a new test framework that brings the power and conciseness of Kotlin to your Android test setup. With a small-surface API, a hierarchical test structure and an extensible DSL, TestBalloon makes Android testing easier than ever.

Takeaways:

* Modern testing patterns with zero boilerplate and easy customization.
* Practical examples from simple unit tests to advanced testing with coroutines and generated data.
* Speeding up test runs with deep parallelization.
* How full Android integration works (host-based and instrumented tests, JUnit rules, Robolectric, Roborazzi).
* How TestBalloon compares to classic frameworks (JUnit 4/5, Kotest).

sessions.title: From prototype to production: shipping AI features in your Android app
sessions.description: Getting Gemini working in your Android app takes an afternoon. Getting it ready for real users is where things get serious: exposed API keys, abusive clients burning through your quota, prompts frozen inside a released APK, and no visibility into what your AI feature is actually doing in the wild. This session tackles the production gap. Using Firebase AI Logic, you will call Gemini directly from Kotlin with no backend to build, then harden it for launch: block unauthorized clients with App Check, update prompts and model configuration server-side without shipping a new APK using Server Prompt Templates, and track usage, latency, and cost with AI Monitoring. Finally, we will look ahead to hybrid inference: how the same API prepares your app to run Gemini Nano on-device, so your AI features can work offline, respond faster, and cost less. Ship AI features you can trust in production, and be ready for what comes next.

sessions.title: Flutteristas Panel: Does Your Partner Use AI Like You Do? The Next Gender Gap Is AI Fluency
sessions.description:
You use AI to write code, automate boring tasks, research faster, plan a trip, or test a business idea. Then you look at your partner, parents, or friends and realize they may use it in a completely different way. Or barely at all. Could that difference matter five years from now?

Early research already points to gaps in how people across genders and ages adopt and experiment with AI. Social media may widen them by feeding people different ideas, tools, and opportunities. AI itself can also reinforce old stereotypes, associating software and technology more strongly with some genders and care, beauty, or lifestyle with others. If AI fluency becomes a career advantage, a small difference in how we use these tools today can turn into a much bigger gap tomorrow.

This panel brings Flutteristas together to challenge that idea. Is the gap real? Where does it come from? Are algorithms making it worse? And what can we do before AI skills become another advantage that is unevenly distributed?

sessions.title: Build an agentic full-stack tabletop game master application
sessions.description:
I've run AI-powered tabletop game master sessions at conferences where the audience became the adventuring party and an AI ran the game. Audiences loved it. Now it is time you build the whole thing yourself.

In this workshop, you'll start with a pre-built UI and mock data for a tabletop role-playing game. Over the next few hours, you'll turn that static shell into a working full-stack application with real-time multiplayer sync and an AI game master that narrates encounters, controls enemies, and responds to player actions.

You will build:
- Authentication so players can sign in and own their characters
- Persistent game state for characters, inventory, and encounter history
- Real-time multiplayer sync so all players see the action as it happens
- An agentic game master with memory that tracks the story across turns
- File storage for character portraits and map assets

and have a running application where players can join a session, take actions, and have an AI game master.

sessions.title: Your router doesn't work here: navigation in add-to-app Flutter
sessions.description:
go_router, auto_route, and Navigator 2.0 all quietly assume one thing: Flutter owns the whole app. In add-to-app, it doesn't. The back stack is split across two runtimes, a deep link can start in native code and end in Flutter, and "pop" can mean six different things depending on who's on screen. Most teams reach for their favorite router, fight it for three sprints, and end up with a thousand-line workaround.
This talk is about what a router actually needs to do when Flutter is a guest in someone else's app. We'll tear down why mainstream routers break at the seam, work through the requirements a real add-to-app router has to meet, and walk through a design that keeps navigation sane on both sides. For anyone shipping Flutter modules inside an existing native app — or about to start.

sessions.title: Dependency Injection in Enterprise Flutter Applications
sessions.description:
Dependency injection (DI) is a crucial pattern for ensuring application maintainability and testability. These aspects are especially important in enterprise applications, where DI can become significantly more complex to implement effectively. In modular applications developed by multiple teams, DI requires additional consideration to ensure loose coupling and clear dependency definitions while avoiding cumbersome boilerplate.

In this talk, we will explore:
- DI challenges in enterprise Flutter applications
- DI solutions used in a couple of enterprise Flutter projects
- The benefits and drawbacks of each approach

sessions.title: Assembling the Party: Leveling Up Game Dev with AI Agents
sessions.description:
Over the past months I built an entire AI workflow around our Unity codebase - a custom persona, a stack of skills, several agents, full multi-agent pipelines and then deleted most of it. What survived made me faster than all of it combined.

This is the story of that workflow: what it actually takes to go from writing every line yourself to directing the work, on a real Unity/C# production codebase at Starberry. The result isn't a magic robot that replaces you - it's a "party" of prompts, skills, and agents you assemble around your own needs, letting you ship like a bigger team and spend your judgment on what to build instead of grinding out every line of how.
No hype, no perfect demos - including the parts where I over-built it and had to cut back.

sessions.title: Hooking Swift (the hard way)
sessions.description:
Hooking Swift code on iOS using Frida can be done in multiple ways, we'll focus on the hardest one: just treat Swift as compiled native code and use low level Frida capabilities without the help of higher level bridges.

That's what we've been doing for years, and it's the most flexible and fail-safe way to deal with Swift. Understanding the challenges at this level allows for building targeted tools, or even higher level bridges tailored for specific use cases.

The talk will go through real-life examples in form of live demos, to understand some of the building blocks necessary for hooking and interacting with Swift code and data.

sessions.title: Build AI Agents on the Edge. Are we there yet?
sessions.description:
Edge AI models are nothing new, but for a long time their capabilities fell short of expectations. They could chat just fine, but often lost track of instructions or couldn't use tools properly. That perception still keeps a lot of developers from taking edge deployment seriously. Recent releases like LFM2.5 or Gemma 4 families change the picture significantly. They bring proper agentic capabilities, while being less resource-hungry than older models. And all of that on device - this means no server, no per-token bill, no user data leaving the phone.

After this talk you will be able to:
1. Judge whether your use-case suits models capabilities.
2. Build a real on-device agent loop - model, tool calls, and structured output working together reliably.
3. Understand various tradeoffs and concerns when integrating edge LLM to your product.
4. Know when edge isn't the answer, so you reach for it makes sense.
5. Add it to a React Native app with react-native-executorch.

sessions.title: A React Compiler horror story
sessions.description:
This talk is based on a true story.
Once upon a time, there was a hook called useMemo that devs used to fine-tune the performance of their apps. It was hell to work with, but at least we were the ones harming ourselves.

Then the React Compiler was released with the promise to solve performance issues once and for all. No more useMemo, no more useCallback.

However, there was an evil hidden in the depths, waiting to trap innocent developers.
 
This fall, learn how to fix bailouts and avoid nasty crashes when using the React Compiler.

sessions.title: React Navigation 8: Building a modern navigation library - the hard parts
sessions.description:
In this talk, I'll showcase React Navigation 8 and cover various considerations and challenges of building it for a modern audience, including:

- Decisions behind building the Static API
- Choosing native vs custom primitives
- Building a type-safe API that works with complex navigation trees
- Working with React features - startTransition, Activity, etc.
- Differences in concepts when working on cross-platform code

Combining a good developer experience, cross-platform support, and modern features is a lot to take on. The talk will provide a glimpse into these challenges.

sessions.title: Mobile Security Fundamentals: Build Apps That Fight Back
sessions.description:
Building secure mobile apps is no longer optional—it’s expected by users, businesses, and the ecosystem. This talk offers a practical, beginner-friendly introduction to mobile security for iOS developers who want to improve their apps without getting lost in theory.

We’ll cover essential tools for analyzing app behavior, including network proxies and IPA inspection, and explain how code signing and entitlements define trust boundaries. We’ll also explore secure data storage with Keychain and file encryption, followed by key networking protections like certificate pinning and device attestation.

Attendees will gain a clear understanding of the mobile threat landscape, see real-world pitfalls, and learn actionable techniques they can apply immediately. The goal is to help developers make informed, security-first decisions and build resilient apps by design.

sessions.title: Feel Core Image: Live Image Processing
sessions.description:
Every iPhone ships with a fully GPU-accelerated image processing framework that most developers never use. Core Image can do far more! And in this hands-on session you will see exactly how far.

What you will learn:
- Build real filter pipelines with CIImage, CIFilter and CIContext
- Write your own kernels: a per-pixel color kernel, a coordinate-remapping warp kernel, and a sampling general kernel
- Combine Core Image with Vision to detect face landmarks and build complex beauty effects: mask-based lip tinting and distortion eye reshaping

sessions.title: Arts and Crafts
sessions.description:
A lot of us who have been developers for a long time have learned to think of ourselves as craftspeople. Now, the thing that we've spent all our time and effort honing our skills on is changing wildly, as quickly as week to week. 

So how does this compare to other evolutions in other arts and crafts? I'll look at writing code through the lens of my hobbies of woodworking, laser cutting, and 3D printing to talk about the evolution of art into craft, and craft into art. 

You'll walk away with some new ways to think about producing code, and I hope a way to make sense of some of the chaos around us.

sessions.title: The Manager in the era of AI: Decision-Making Without Delegation
sessions.description:
Every manager's role has three parts: strategist, leader, people manager. For the last decade, much of each was information work — gathering data, synthesizing reports, building the case for a decision. AI collapses the cost of that work to near-zero. But that's not where your job ends. That's where it changes.
This is a practitioner's report from someone who went from iOS dev to C-level of a 300-person company, and now applies AI across an 80–100-person engineering org. Three concrete shifts: Strategy — modeling five or six realistic scenarios instead of one or two gut reads, and building a verification ritual for when AI analysis nearly derails you. Leadership — why your span of control transforms rather than shrinks, and the line you never cross. People management — new hiring filters, the junior problem, quiet non-adopters, and the security blind spot most managers miss.
Closing question: once AI handles the information logistics, what is the manager's job for?

sessions.title: Kotlin by JetBrains, present and future
sessions.description:
Have a chat with Developer Advocates from JetBrains about anything Kotlin related that's on your mind. This is your chance to get answers straight from the source!

Let's talk about the evolution of the language, the tooling, development practices, or perhaps Kotlin Multiplatform and Compose Multiplatform... We're here for all of it!

Report issues, ask us for recommendations, tell us about your experiences of building apps with KMP, or perhaps just ask us what our favourite recent language feature is.

sessions.title: When Fiction Is the Interface: Designing Natural UI/UX in VR film Nana Lou
sessions.description:
Nana Lou is an award-winning VR animated interactive tale where you play a spirit accompanying a grandmother through her final moments, an experience built on nurse training for end-of-life care and grief psychology. 
I'll walk through how we built gesture, pacing, and presence into the role-play, and how we translated delicate psychological research into moments the player actually lives. 
This talk shows what a piece of immersive interactive fiction can teach for UI and UX practices : how storyworld logic and emotional storytelling produce a transformative user journey and interfaces that feel intuitive and rewarding.
What you will learn : 
- Transferable techniques from role-play and presence design to create diegetic interface 
- Reframed UX methodology to design a user journey combining performative pacing and story arc
- How to use world building to control narrative pacing
- Detailed VR use case for embodied UI using head and hand tracking and animated character interactions

sessions.title: Story Circle 'Worst Production Bug'
sessions.description:
Location: Activity & Networking Area Level 2

Story Circle 'Worst Production Bug' whilst building and programming a robot together – each person adds a story about an escalating bug.

sessions.title: Break
Better Debugging Context for Coding Agent
sessions.description:
When AI coding agents arrived in Android development, they made writing code faster. They didn't make debugging faster - because debugging Android isn't a code problem, it's a visibility problem. An agent reading your source files has no idea your network call is returning a 304, your Compose tree has a stale state holder, or your WebView is silently failing on a missing cookie.
DTA closes that gap. It's an open-source MCP server that gives coding agents direct access to a running Android app: real UI hierarchy with Compose and WebView nodes, live network and WebSocket traffic, navigation state, and database contents.
This talk shows what changes in practice. We'll walk through real debugging sessions - a network bug, a state bug, a WebView bug - comparing how an agent handles them with and without runtime access. The goal isn't to convince you AI is the future. It's to show you what AI debugging looks like when it actually works.

https://github.com/yamsergey/dta

sessions.title: The Mobile Engineer AI Won't Replace
sessions.description:
AI changed mobile engineering faster than career advice caught up. A working first draft now takes seconds. The job moved to everything around it: deciding what's worth building, catching the bugs the model introduced, and owning the code once it ships.

Product sense, spec quality, release confidence, review discipline, business impact. These always mattered. Today they are what decides who keeps growing as an engineer and who stalls out.

I made the jump from Android engineer to EM, and these are the things I weigh in hiring and promotion calls. This talk is what I see from that seat.

You'll leave knowing:

- where to put your energy now that AI handles the first draft
- how to get the spec and product thinking right before you open IDE
- how to tie feature work to metrics you can actually point to
- how to review AI-assisted PRs and stay accountable for what ships
- what a promotion case looks for when a clean first draft is table stakes

sessions.title: The Last Software Platform to Move to the Cloud: Why Mobile Devs and AI Agents Need Previews
sessions.description:
Format: Lightning Talk
Track: Engineering Leadership / Developer Experience / Technical Strategy
Presenter: Weiyin He, CTO at Appetize.io
LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/weiyinhe

Every major shift in software development has been driven by infrastructure moving to the cloud, and each time it happened, the way teams write and collaborate around code changed with it. Git, GitHub, CI/CD, AI coding assistants, and now agentic development have each pulled more of the development lifecycle online and unlocked new ways of working. Mobile development is lagging in this transformation. While web teams have been previewing pull requests in live browser environments for years, mobile teams are still passing around APKs to install onto physical devices. This talk makes the case that running apps in the cloud is the infrastructure shift mobile needs, and walks through what it concretely enables for teams and AI agents.

sessions.title: Vector Search on Android — Finding What You Mean, Not What You Type
sessions.description:
Keyword search is great until the user searches "red shoes" and your database returns everything tagged "red" or "shoe" sorted by nothing. Vector search fixes that by finding things by meaning, not by string matching. And the best part is that it runs entirely on-device, reducing latency, preserving user data privacy and making it an offline capable solution.

This talk covers the three ingredients you need and nothing more:
1. An embedding model
2. A vector database
3. Chunking

We'll walk through concrete use cases: semantic search in notes taking app, textual lookups in images ("find products that look have red shoes"). Code snippets, and links to guides can be referenced, instead of slides full of math. We will also talk about some of the caveats, such as bundling with your artifact or downloading a model into your app storage and memory to perform the embedding work.

sessions.title: Edge AI in Action: Building Real-Time Vision Solutions for Enterprise Android Devices
sessions.description:
Cloud-based AI is powerful, but for enterprise Android developers building solutions to find a specific package in the back of a dark delivery truck, inventory retail store shelves, or digitize complex delivery documents, the cloud is often too slow, too expensive, does not ensure privacy, and completely dependent on perfect Wi-Fi. The solution is moving vision AI directly to the edge—utilizing tailored, frontline-specific models designed to process and digitize environments in real-time.
In this session, we will dive deep into the architecture of building real-time, on-device computer vision workflows using an AI Data Capture SDK. We will bypass high-level AI hype and focus strictly on the developer journey—showing you how to combine modular AI Enablers (the building blocks) with adaptable AI Blueprints (the workflow orchestrators) to build robust, offline-first Android solutions.

sessions.title: Securing App Secrets: Hardware-Backed Cryptography and the Android Keystore
sessions.description: Your app may encrypt sensitive user data, but if the decryption keys are not securely stored, attackers can extract them directly from memory. While Android has offered secure, hardware-backed Keystore cryptography since API 24, software-based encryption remains the default, meaning developers may adopt it without further consideration. In this session, we will demonstrate how attackers use tools like Frida to extract keys from memory, and how the Android Keystore prevents it.You will learn about the performance overhead of Keystore operations and practical techniques to mitigate it. We will also share insights from real-world devices showing that Keystore operations are prone to unexpected failures, emphasizing the need to handle exceptions gracefully and designing recovery mechanisms to ensure app stability. Finally, we cover additional ways to secure your keys, such as requiring biometric authentication, and verifying hardware backing via key attestation.

sessions.title: Flutter on Foldables: How hard could it be?
sessions.description:
Foldables are the new frontier of mobile form factors. But for cross-platform developers, dynamic screen resizes, physical hinges, and exotic "postures" like Tabletop mode can feel like an architectural nightmare.

In this session, we aren’t just looking at slides—this entire presentation and live demo is running directly from a physical foldable phone.

As we physically bend and unfold the device on stage, we will bridge the gap between native Android hardware mechanics and Flutter widgets in real-time. We’ll dive under the hood to see how Flutter wraps Jetpack WindowManager natively, build a type-safe Kotlin-to-Dart Pigeon bridge to stream hardware telemetry, and prove that complex UI states are completely manageable.

Whether you are an Android engineer skeptical of Flutter’s hardware access, or a Flutter developer intimidated by the "crease," you will leave ready to conquer modern form factors and unfold your app’s true potential.

sessions.title: Douze Points for Flutter! How we built the official Eurovision Song Contest mobile app
sessions.description: When millions of fans tune in for the world's largest live music event, your app can't miss a beat. The official Eurovision Song Contest app hit #1 on both the App Store and Google Play, surpassed 1 million combined downloads, and maintained a 99% crash-free rate during peak global traffic. In this lightning talk, we’ll speedrun the strategies and tools that made this possible - from the essential architectural pillars to the strict tooling that kept our codebase bulletproof. Whether you are building for 100 users or 1 million, you'll leave with a practical checklist for production-grade Flutter apps.

sessions.title: Animating the game - Flutter at Draftkings
sessions.description:
Game Tracker turns raw real-time sports data into an animated, interactive, embeddable game visualization. 

Live plays stream in and come alive as broadcast-quality animations — powered by Flutter, the Flame game engine, and Rive — letting fans feel every moment of football and basketball games as they happen, right inside the sportsbooks and betting sites they already use. 

This talk shows how we married Flutter's UI, Flame's game loop, and Rive's designer-driven motion — all orchestrated by a clean Riverpod architecture that keeps live game state flowing reactively from socket to screen — to transform a live data feed into a smooth, engaging fan experience.

sessions.title: Off the Hook: Simplifying Function Hooking with frooky 1.0
sessions.description:
Function hooking is an important part of mobile application penetration testing. With this technique, it is possible to observe an app's API usage at runtime in order to detect potential risks. Security testers usually do that with the de-facto default tool, Frida.

frooky is a Frida-based tool developed as part of the OWASP Mobile Application Security Project with the goal to simplify this process. It uses YAML to configure hooks and outputs easy-to-parse JSON, allowing testers to quickly intercept functions at runtime.

After an introduction to the basics of function hooking, we use frooky version 1.0 against mobile applications to quickly find various vulnerabilities.

In a second step, we build a simple vulnerability scanner which parses the output generated by frooky for certain patterns in order to automatically generate a report.

sessions.title: AI Doesn't See Your UI: What It Takes to Audit Accessibility with LLMs
sessions.description:
"Check if my app has accessible colors." This was my first prompt to Claude to ensure compliance with the European Accessibility Act. The results were catastrophic: hallucinated colors, incorrect contrast calculations, and no UI interaction.

In this talk, we'll follow the journey from a naive "take a screenshot and ask Claude" prototype to a system capable of performing meaningful accessibility color audits on React Native.

Each failure taught us something new. We'll explore the technical decisions that transformed a toy experiment into a practical auditing system, from understanding color accessibility and the surprising complexity of contrast analysis to extracting information from screenshots and accessibility trees.

Although our case study is accessibility color auditing, it applies whenever we need deterministic result from an AI, including end-to-end testing, UI validation, and automated quality analysis.

sessions.title: Your App's Text Has A Tax
sessions.description:
Every Text in a React Native app pays a small, invisible cost on every render silently eating up your frame budget.

This talk shows what that cost actually is, why your profiler hides it from you, and the measurable performance impact it has on a real-world app. It shows how a clever plugin shifts this issue away from the runtime on the user's device to the compiler, and how such build-time optimizations could shape the next wave of performance improvements for the React ecosystem, starting with the React Compiler.

sessions.title: Build Where Your Customers Are
sessions.description: Scale your apps beyond mobile and the web. Hundreds of millions of customers are watching Fire TV, asking Alexa+ questions, learning with Bee Wearable AI, and integrating computer vision APIs with Ring Cameras. This session walks through the opportunities for Android, Web, and React Native app developers to reach customers around the world through Amazon devices. Learn how other developers are shipping multi-device experiences and how to get started right away. We'll also share our collection of AI builder tools, device SDKs, and open-source samples.

sessions.title: Kill Your Generated Mocks: Compile-Time Mocking with Swift Macros
sessions.description:
For years, our iOS codebase relied on Sourcery to generate mock files for testing. It worked, until we were maintaining over a thousand generated files that bloated the repo. When Apple released Swift Macros, we saw a way out.

This talk is the story of SwiftMockKit, an internal library that generates mocks at compile time with a single annotation, and how we're migrating a large fintech codebase off file-based generation. Our first batch swapped 14 protocols in a single PR; along the way we've deleted nearly 91,000 lines of committed mock boilerplate.

You will learn:
- Why file-based mock generation stops scaling, and the pain signals to watch for in your own codebase
- A migration path from Sourcery
- Where macros fall short: the protocols we couldn't handle and the compile-time costs we measured

If your test suite depends on generated mocks, you'll leave knowing exactly how to delete them.

sessions.title: What AI changed about migrations (and what it didn't)
sessions.description:
AI has us questioning every part of how we build software, and it is tempting to assume it can now do all of it.

So I went back to one migration I led and asked: what would I now hand to AI, and what must stay human?

The migration meant decoupling our frontend from a 15-year-old monolith it had fused into. Think Jenga tower: every dependency load-bearing, a button color change triggering a full-stack redeploy. Untangling it was the technical nightmare, and AI would take most of that off my plate today.

But it never stalled on code. It stalled on the work AI cannot do: aligning people on one direction, cutting scope without losing context, winning buy-in and funding, shipping value in small increments. We broke out only when we dropped the grand plan and shipped one feature on a hard deadline.

An honest reflection on what AI makes effortless in a migration, and the judgment it cannot replace: which one is worth doing, and how you get it funded.

sessions.title: Beyond Optical Tracking: What Wearable Sensors add to XR Hands
sessions.description:
Most XR hand interactions today rely on camera-based tracking or basic controllers, both of which struggle with occlusion, fine motor detail, and grounding a user's actions with any physical feedback.

This talk looks at what changes when you capture hand movement directly from wearable sensors instead of inferring it from cameras: reliable tracking resilient to occlusion, richer gesture data, and the ability to layer in basic haptic feedback. 

Using capacitive-sensing gloves as a working example, I'll walk through how sensor-based hand tracking works, where it outperforms optical solutions, and the practical trade-offs XR developers should weigh when choosing among camera-based, controller-based, and glove-based input for their next project.

sessions.description:

A fast-paced reaction game in a circle,

sessions.title: Break
From Dumb Client to Hybrid Intelligence: Building Production On-Device AI Systems
sessions.description:
On-device AI is moving from concept to production. Modern phones and consumer devices now ship with powerful NPUs, GPUs and accelerators, making local inference practical and fast.

The key question is no longer whether AI should run on-device, but how to intelligently decide what runs locally, what gets routed to the cloud and how to build coordinated hybrid intelligence systems.

In this talk, I’ll share a practical framework for model selection under real constraints like memory, latency, energy, privacy and updates. I’ll also cover proven routing patterns using semantic routing, embeddings, classifiers, rules and lightweight decision layers to handle cloud escalation.

A simple Android demo app shows local AI managing fast, private and low-cost tasks while intelligently escalating complex requests to the cloud.

Attendees will leave with a clear decision framework and reusable patterns for building real-world hybrid AI products.

sessions.title: Beyond the Alt-Tag: Shipping Accessible Web Apps in the Age of AI
sessions.description:
Accessibility is often treated as a final "coat of paint", a checklist applied just before shipping. However, as AI-assisted coding increases development velocity, the risk of scaling inaccessible patterns grows exponentially. This session shifts the perspective from reactive fixing to proactive, AI-enhanced inclusive design.

We will explore why accessibility is the essential infrastructure for the "Agentic Web." Because AI agents navigate the digital world using the same semantic markers as screen readers, an inaccessible site is effectively invisible to future AI users. Attendees will learn to integrate WCAG standards directly into React workflows and discover a "30-minute sprint" strategy to move any site from broken to functional. We’ll move beyond the "Alt-tag" and discuss how to build a machine-readable web that is inclusive of both humans and agents.

sessions.title: HUMAN.md: Are we losing our skills in the SKILL.md era?
sessions.description: Google’s SKILL.md standard teaches agents to navigate our codebases, but our own human skills are throwing a NullPointerException. Historically, the Android developer ladder was built on "productive friction"—debugging crashes, arguing architecture in PRs, and obsessing over UI jank. AI removes this friction, causing a human-skill atrophy. Juniors now prompt stack traces instead of learning to debug. Mid-levels rely on AI scaffolding, completely missing the architectural "blast radius" intuition. And seniors are mutating from master builders into full-time hallucination auditors. This talk breaks down the ledger of what we’ve gained versus what we’ve lost, and how to intentionally inject "synthetic friction" back into our workflows to prevent our engineering teams from becoming technically hollow.

sessions.title: Your offline-first app is not a sync queue.
sessions.description:
Most offline-first apps just queue writes, hope the server agrees, and call it offline by design.

We took the harder path: an event-sourced Kotlin Multiplatform (KMP) architecture where the client records immutable events, not mutable state; a separate engine derives state from them. The client witnesses; it never judges. Each event carries a version snapshot of what it touched, so on sync the server compares those columns against what changed underneath: disjoint edits auto-resolve, only real overlaps reach a human, who "defines reality" forward.

We'll follow one event from tap to server-confirmed — offline-addressable IDs and an optimistic projection that paints the UI instantly, then reconciles with no cleanup code of ours. The kicker: that same Kotlin module runs our backend, compiled to JavaScript, so the rules can't drift.

You'll leave building apps that behave the same on a plane as at a desk: no lost writes, no silent divergence, conflicts as a decision, not a merge bug.

sessions.title: What ExoPlayer Doesn't Tell You: Lessons from Reddit's Full Video Rewrite
sessions.description:
At Reddit, we rewrote our entire video player from scratch — 15+ screens, millions of users, and over a billion playbacks a day across ~16K devices.  

What we discovered along the way is that the hardest problems aren't in the docs.

We'll talk about:
- How we built a feed-first playback engine on top of ExoPlayer for scroll-and-play usage patterns
- How we designed a declarative video API where doing the right thing is the only path
- How we achieved 65% faster load times (P50), 20% faster (P90), and 67% less rebuffering (compared to our previous player)
- How a custom seekbar animation with Choreographer reduced slow frames by 7.3% and frozen frames by 7.7%
- How a playback failure affecting 2 million sessions exposed a blind spot in our architecture — and how we resolved it

If you have any piece of video in your app, this talk will save you a lot of time.

sessions.title: Stop Building the Whole App
sessions.description:
When an engineer is working on a single feature, they only care about changing code, running it, and validating fast.  

At Qonto, our app has 1k+ modules and 300+ features, yet the default workflow still forces engineers to build and install more than they need, so they spend minutes waiting and clicking around to reach the right screen.  

That’s why we changed our approach: instead of building the full app, we generate DevApps, small per-feature apps that build fast, open the right screen, and let engineers validate changes with the same confidence as the main app.

In this talk, you’ll learn how we:  
- Designed an architecture that builds only one feature and its dependencies
- Solved key challenges (DI, navigation, login, data)
- Prevented DevApps from breaking as the codebase evolves
- Built tooling engineers love (skip login, auto-fill forms, mock services)
- Measured and increased adoption and performance

Come learn how to build mini apps and get your feedback loop back.

sessions.title: MCP, Multi-Agents, and "Grill Me": Real-World AI Workflows That Actually Deliver
sessions.description:
Ever feel like using AI is just a glorified game of twenty questions? You ask a chatbot something, get some random code back, and spend ten minutes fixing it. That’s not collaboration; it’s a distraction.

In this talk, we’ll look at how our team moved past basic prompt engineering and turned AI into a true teammate using a simple 4-step framework:

True Collaboration: Changing how we interact with AI daily.

Compounding Assets (MCP): Connecting Figma to Jetpack Compose, auto-generating deep links, and building custom string tools.

Multi-Agent Workflows: Creating an AI assembly line (Planner, Architect, Coder, QA, and Reviewer) to stop model bias and catch bugs before committing.

Our Custom Toolkit: A look at the weird but effective tools we actually use, like the "Grill Me" protocol and handoff sessions.

No hype, just real workflows you can actually use in your Android team.

sessions.title: A Mindful UX for Foldables and Tablets: Real-World Examples
sessions.description:
When people buy a foldable or tablet, they expect more than just a stretched-out phone app — they expect something extra, something more premium. While there are lots of tutorials on building adaptive UIs, very few address building an adaptive UX.

Join this session to explore real-world examples of designing with intention for large screens and unique form factors (remember Surface Duo?). You will walk away from this talk knowing how to:

- Advocate for platform-specific UX best practices within your team.
- Design seamless flows that fully utilise expanded screen real estate.
– Accommodate physical nuances like screen creases, varying input methods, and even left-handed ergonomics.
– Implement proper solutions, both with and without Navigation3.
- Use Android Studio tools to make this job easier.

sessions.title: From Fighter Jets to Flutter: How to Actually Use State Machines
sessions.description:
State machines keep planes, cars, and medical devices from getting confused about what they are doing. The idea was first used to plan the software inside a fighter jet. These industries trust it with people's lives.

In app development, almost no one uses it. We build drag, resize, and gesture-heavy widgets out of a pile of boolean flags that end up fighting each other, and then we wonder why the bugs are so hard to reproduce.

There is already plenty out there about why state machines are good. This talk is not that. I'll show you how to actually use them in a Flutter app, on the kind of tricky interactions every app eventually needs: telling a tap from a drag, handling two gestures at once, and remembering where you were after switching modes. I'll show it all running live, with the tools I built and have leaned on for the past year.

By the end, you'll know how to use state machines to build even the most complex widget interactions.

sessions.title: From Push to Pickup: The Anatomy of a Flutter VoIP Call
sessions.description: What happens, exactly, between someone tapping "call" and your Flutter app ringing on the other side? A lot — and most of it can fail. This talk traces one incoming call from push to pickup, built from a production deployment across a fleet of apps: the push that wakes a sleeping device, the native screen that shows over the lock screen, and the audio that connects over WebRTC. We'll dig into where iOS and Android part ways — PushKit vs. FCM, CallKit vs. Android's full-screen-intent and core-telecom split — and the background limits that kill calls on some phones but never your Pixel. You'll leave with a clear model of the stack and the traps to design around.

sessions.title: Screen-by-Screen Symbiosis: Interleaving Native and Flutter in a Single Stack
sessions.description:
When modernizing a massive application, a full rewrite is rarely an option, but a completely isolated Flutter module isn't enough either. For one of Europe's largest financial institutions serving 100k+ enterprise users, the solution was a deeply integrated hybrid architecture: a single application where native screens and Flutter screens coexist side-by-side in the same navigation flow.
Drawing on my 5 years as a Flutter GDE, this advanced session breaks down the technical realities of orchestrating a hybrid navigation stack. We will explore how to manage seamless transitions between native Activities/ViewControllers and Flutter routes without jarring user experiences. We will dissect the plumbing required for deep state sharing across screen boundaries, handling complex lifecycle synchronization, and optimizing memory when native and Flutter engines tightly interleave at scale.

sessions.title: VGV's AI Ecosystem: Building an Integrated AI-Powered Development Stack for not just Flutter Teams
sessions.description: At Very Good Ventures, we've built a layered AI ecosystem that transforms how teams write, review, and ship production-quality code. This talk introduces three open-source tools that work together: Wingspan, a Claude Code plugin that guides developers through a structured brainstorm-plan-build workflow; the Very Good AI Flutter Plugin, a collection of contextual best-practices skills covering architecture, testing, accessibility, state management, and more; and the Very Good AI Assistant, an internal tool-agnostic CLI that brings VGV standards and skills to any AI coding assistant. We'll learn the full loop: from brainstorming a feature, through planning and building with automated quality review, to shipping a PR — all powered by AI that enforces real engineering standards rather than generating generic boilerplate.

sessions.title: Turn your NPC into a voice agent using LiveKit and Unity
sessions.description:
Voice agents introduce a new interface for interacting with NPCs through natural language. With the advances in voice and language models, conversations finally feel natural. 
By leveraging registered tools, NPC agents can execute actions dynamically when triggered. Without relying on pre-scripted conversations, they also enable procedural character generation.
Combined with the low latency transmission of WebRTC, you can deploy and scale agents in the cloud.

In this session we will build NPCs powered by voice agents using the LiveKit Unity SDK.

sessions.title: How I Hacked React Native DevTools (And Built a Plugin Framework)
sessions.description:
What if React Native DevTools could be extended with your own custom plugins?

That question is what led me to build Rozenite. I started by digging into how React Native DevTools work under the hood, reverse-engineering the architecture, and looking for a way to add custom functionality without forking anything.

In this talk, I'll share that journey: why I built Rozenite, how it hooks into DevTools, and how it turns that idea into a real plugin framework. We'll look at building custom panels with React-based UIs, communicating with the app, running plugin code safely, and what becomes possible when React Native DevTools are no longer a closed box.

sessions.title: From Weights to useModel(): Teaching Agents to Do the Hard Part
sessions.description:
Most on-device AI talks stop at wrapping someone else's model. The real work starts when the model you need doesn't exist yet. You have to adapt it, get it running on a phone, and ship it behind a clean API. And the steps nobody likes to talk about are the ones where projects quietly die: data prep, and export.
Here's the thing. Those steps are fiddly, repetitive, version-sensitive, and unglamorous, which makes them exactly what coding agents are good at.
This talk follows one custom model the whole way: adapted for a real task, exported to run fully on-device, and shipped as a React Native hook you can actually call. At every hard step, I hand the grind to an agent and guide it through the whole process.
You'll walk away knowing how to ship a custom on-device AI feature in React Native, how to direct an agent through the parts that usually break, and how to get it to do the work you've been dreading.

sessions.title: Surviving D-Day
sessions.description:
Building a fast, offline-first, reliable app for ground operations using React Native:

Learn how we built our new "Shotgun Backstage" pro app for event organizers to handle their event on D-day, including selling tickets using Tap to Pay, scanning them fast in the entrance queues, accessing data offline and syncing it between multiple devices using bluetooth mesh, and checking live event data, all without a need for specific hardware, using common iPhones and Android phones.

I will be presenting the stack we chose and why we made those choices.
But also how we architectured the roles and permissions, the data (an event can have tens of thousands of tickets, users etc), how we allow printing physical tickets for some use cases, how we spend time on the UI/UX to make the app as fast and intuitive as possible, etc.

sessions.title: Driving User Engagement
sessions.description: The most important part of any app is its users. If they’re not engaged, your app will be off their phones faster than it got there. In this talk, we’ll cover practical, industry-proven strategies to increase user engagement and ensure your users keep coming back.

sessions.title: Opening Up Open Source
sessions.description: In this talk we'll explore how to build and run a sustainable open source project. We'll cover building and releasing your work to encourage contributors. We'll look at how to build a great community around your project to help it grow. Finally we'll look at how to make the project sustainable, get funding and avoid the dreaded open source burnout! This talk is based upon running Vapor, the most popular framework for Swift on the server that attracts hundreds of contributions, but applies to any open source project.

sessions.title: Product-Oriented Programming: When Shipping Speed Is an Architectural Requirement
sessions.description:
Consumer app architecture is not only about clean code or correctness. For iOS engineers, it is also about how quickly we can change what users experience without waiting for an App Store release.

This talk introduces Product-Oriented Programming: treating product velocity as an architectural requirement. Through a real onboarding flow built in SwiftUI, we will explore how server-driven forms can render fields, handle validation, manage dependencies, and lock behavior from a backend contract instead of hardcoded screens.

Attendees will learn how to decide when server-driven UI is worth the complexity, how feature flags and remote config can become safe product controls, how to design analytics into iOS architecture from the start, and how a shared contract helps iOS, Android, backend, and QA move together. We will also cover the trade-offs for iOS codebases: weaker local reasoning, harder debugging, and the discipline needed to avoid turning flexibility into debt.

sessions.title: The Hardest Problems Weren't Technical
sessions.description:
AI has transformed software development, but the biggest challenges I faced as a Tech Lead weren't technical—they were human. Teams started shipping code faster than ever, yet code quality became inconsistent. Junior developers relied too heavily on AI, code reviews had to evolve, engineering standards became harder to enforce, and balancing speed with maintainability became a daily challenge. 

I'll share real stories from leading engineering teams through this shift, the mistakes we made, what worked, and the leadership principles that emerged. We'll discuss building trust in AI-generated code, redefining code reviews, mentoring in an AI-first world, preventing technical debt, making better architectural decisions, and creating a healthy engineering culture where AI amplifies developers instead of replacing critical thinking. You'll leave with practical strategies you can apply immediately to your own team.

sessions.title: Developing for SPECS: how to ride the see-through AR wave
sessions.description:
Time has finally come for XR devs to design, code and deploy meaningful experiences on a truly spatial computing device that has everything it needs to work "out there": SPECS. 

In this session you will learn about the different options to develop for SPECS at various levels: LensStudio with AI-powered CLAD skills, the optional NDK and WebXR support. We will revise the rich set of device capabilities available on SPECS: world tracking, hand interaction, depth sensing, etc., concluding with a couple of real-world examples of how to bring see-through AR to real projects and customers.

sessions.title: Registration & Check-In
What Shape Are You? Rethinking Engineering in the AI Era
sessions.description:
Somewhere along the way, engineering got defined as the art of excellent execution. Understand the requirements, build the thing well, ship on time. And for a long time, that was enough.

It isn't anymore.

AI has thinned out the layers between technical decisions and commercial outcomes. Smaller teams, faster cycles, fewer people holding customer context upstream of the engineers who need it. The result? Brilliant technical people making expensive decisions in the dark: optimising for depth and accuracy that nobody asked for, in products built for the wrong customer entirely.

This session introduces the flower-shaped professional: a practical model for what senior engineering leadership actually requires right now. We'll look at which petals matter most, what it looks like to test for them in hiring, and how to honestly assess which ones you still need to grow yourself.

Grounded in real experience building AI products from zero, and the hard lessons that come with it.

sessions.title: Hosting the AI Slop party
sessions.description:
Congratulations. You are now the host of the AI Slop Party. You didn't plan it. Nobody RSVP'd. But your codebase is full of guests who don't know why they're there, your docs sound like they were written by a very confident intern who had never seen your product, and someone just merged a PR that works great — for a completely different app.
Your CTO is screaming to go faster, the Platform team is experiencing an existential crisis, Product exploded GitHub Pages into the new MySpace of Internal Dashboards, and Security is burning a new hole in the ozone layer with agents trying to manage the leaks.
The good news: you can actually run this party well. I've built engineering divisions from scratch multiple times, shipped to tens of millions of users, and kept codebases coherent while the tools underneath kept shape-shifting. I've also watched what happens when nobody's minding the door.
This is real-talk on risk frameworks that work, quality gates that don't make your senior engineers want to quit, keeping your codebase from becoming an AI archaeology dig, and turning the chaos into the best thing that ever happened to your junior engineers.

You will get the technical tools to copy-paste into your codebases as well as the techniques to manage scale and growth through rapid change.

sessions.title: An Overview of AAOS SDV
sessions.description:
This session will give an introduction to AAOS SDV, the key features and Design concepts. We will talk about:

- How SDV extends Android to a distributed system: We explore how multiple guest VMs or physical SoCs coordinate and how SDV and IVI systems can communicate.
- How virtualization enables easy deployment: We discuss how VirtIO hardware abstraction decouples software from physical hardware, enabling Cloud Parity through Cuttlefish to run multi-VM testing in the cloud without physical boards.
- A short overview of Display Safety and Telemetry
- SDV's security concepts and Developer Experience
- How to develop a service
- An introduction how to develop services for SDV

sessions.title: Q&A with the Flutter Core Team
sessions.description: Have you ever wondered what goes on behind the scenes of your favorite cross-platform framework? Join members of the Flutter Core Team for an open, interactive Q&A session! This is your unique opportunity to ask the engineers building Flutter directly about the framework's roadmap, deep technical architecture, and best practices for scaling apps. Whether you are curious about Impeller's rendering pipeline, Dart macros, or how to tackle complex state management, bring your hardest questions. We will cover a wide range of topics driven entirely by the audience.

sessions.title: The Future of RASP in an AI-Driven World
sessions.description:
AI is rapidly reshaping the cybersecurity landscape, empowering both defenders and attackers with new capabilities. As organizations increasingly embed AI into their applications and development processes, security teams face a growing challenge: protecting applications against faster, more sophisticated, and highly adaptive threats. For product leaders, security architects, and developers, the question is no longer whether AI will influence application security, but how to leverage it effectively while mitigating the risks it introduces. 
This session explores the evolving role of Runtime Application Self-Protection (RASP) in an AI-driven world and examines how traditional application security approaches must adapt to remain effective.

sessions.title: The React Native Software Factory
sessions.description: In 2026 we barely write React Native code by hand. The work moved from typing to building the system around the agents: what they can see, what they can check, and how far they can go before a human has to step in. We started with one agent in a terminal. Now we run hundreds in the cloud, in parallel, in the background. This talk follows that path one problem at a time: giving agents hands and eyes on real devices, letting them debug the running app, handing them shortcuts past everything that doesn't matter, and paying for all of it without hitting the weekly limit on Tuesday.

sessions.title: What AI Can’t Do: Creating F***ing Awesome User Experiences
sessions.description:
AI can now generate apps in minutes. But if everyone can build something “good enough,” how do we create apps that still stand out?

This talk explores what AI cannot replace: care, creativity and the love for tiny details. Using design choices from apps like our iPad journaling app Bubbles’ Journal, I will show how playful interactions, thoughtful animations and unexpected user experiences can make an app feel alive.

I hope to inspire you to build apps that feel personal and joyful, while feeling less anxious about AI taking over our role, because in the age of AI, “good enough” is no longer enough.

sessions.title: Building a Living Tabletop: Mobile AR, Physical Game Design and AI Characters in Dunkelstein
sessions.description: How do you make a physical board, a handheld device and a digital world feel like one coherent game? Dunkelstein is a cinematic murder mystery that uses mobile AR to bring a 1914 villa, its rooms and its characters to life on the table. This keynote shares lessons from building the game in Unreal Engine: tracking both a flat playfield and a physical wooden villa; designing readable interactions for people moving around a shared table; balancing visual fidelity against mobile performance and thermal limits; and keeping physical, digital and narrative states in sync. It also explores the latest step—an LLM-driven character who can listen, answer in role and react to the investigation without revealing spoilers. Attendees will leave with practical principles for hybrid XR games and an honest look at the prototypes, failures and trade-offs behind turning an ambitious AR concept into a real product.

sessions.title: Energizer "Zip Zap Zop"
sessions.description:
Location: Activity & Networking Area Level 2

A fast-paced reaction game in a circle,

sessions.title: Break
Your AI Wrote the API. Who Wrote the Security?
sessions.description:
We are shipping backend APIs faster than ever because AI coding models make it trivial, but most of those services go to production with no real security: no rate limiting, no security headers, permissive CORS, open prototype pollution, leaking error responses. At the same time, supply-chain attacks are now the cheap way in. No mainstream Node framework ships these protections on by default, and the one stack with great docs ergonomics (FastAPI) is in Python.

This talk introduces DaloyJS, a TypeScript framework that closes those gaps: FastAPI-style auto-generated API docs from a single route definition, a contract-first design where one route powers validation, types, OpenAPI, a typed client, and tests, and security that is genuinely default-on, including a guardrailed core, first-party auth/CORS/CSRF/rate-limit middleware, and a "refuse to boot" mode that stops the app from starting on unsafe config.

sessions.title: Keep It Local: RAG Without the Round Trip
sessions.description:
Retrieval-Augmented Generation usually means a vector database, a server, and a network call. None of that exists on a phone — and for offline-first apps or anything touching private user data, none of it should.
This talk is about building RAG entirely on-device: embedding text locally, storing and querying vectors without a server, and keeping the index fresh without re-downloading your whole knowledge base every time content changes. We'll cover the real constraints — model size vs. APK budget, query latency without a backend to do the heavy lifting, and the storage trade-offs that actually work on a mid-range phone, not just your dev device.
No cloud fallback, no asterisks. Just what it takes to make retrieval-augmented answers work entirely in your user's pocket.

sessions.title: App Distribution, or How to Get Your App Featured and What a Pre-Order Is Good For
sessions.description:
I will show my way to distribute an app while building it and what to expect as well as tricks & tips. We will look into the basics first like ASO, App Store Search Optimization, and a landing page. Followed by more advanced topics like a presskit and doing a pre order campaign.

One of the most common questions I got building and releasing Passable - Wallet Cards was "Why do a Pre Order?" and "Why not release now?" we are gonna look deeply at these questions and will try to figure out why releasing immediately is not always the best choice.

In addition while everyone has probably heard a lot about marketing on TikTok and Instagram etc. we are gonna take a dive into how to get a feature from so called legacy media using a presskit and why this might be easier and more worth it than you expect. 
 
Sharing tips I collected for over 10 years.

sessions.title: Practical Filament - Resheep your UI!
sessions.description:
Let’s take a closer look at Filament, the real-time physically based rendering engine, and learn how to use it to build fun effects in our day -to-day UI.

Using Compose Multiplatform, we will explore the main Filament features, and how to use them to create some particle and material based UI effects and interactions. We will cover how to set up Filament, how to work with its material system, and how to use shaders and lighting to create simple effects that react to touch and animations. All of this rooted in practical examples, without diving too much into low level graphics code.

After this talk, you will have a better understanding of how Filament works, and how you can use it to create expressive and dynamic UI in your own projects.

Keep it fun, keep it animated! :)

sessions.title: What's New in Compose Multiplatform: Better Shared UI for iOS and Beyond
sessions.description:
Compose Multiplatform lets you build beautiful UI with idiomatic Kotlin for Android, iOS, Desktop, and Web apps! It’s stable, production-ready, constantly evolving, and it already powers the experiences of millions of users every day. 

As a framework that can be adopted incrementally rather than requiring a full rewrite, you can start using it risk-free even in existing apps. Your Android skills seamlessly transfer to other platforms, with tools like Navigation 3 already available for Compose Multiplatform.

In this talk, we’ll take a hands-on look at everything that’s new and exciting. iOS improvements like faster rendering, enhanced input handling, and better interop that enables the use of Liquid Glass elements. Web features including accessibility, interop, and other improvements.

And of course, we’ll discuss the developer experience: with a unified @Preview system, a mature Hot Reload solution, and a thriving ecosystem that covers all important areas of modern app development.

sessions.title: From Phone to Vehicle: Bringing Your Android App to the Car with HARMAN Ready Link Marketplace
sessions.description:
Your Android app already reaches millions of users on their phones, and the next opportunity is the car. But bringing a mobile experience into the vehicle is more than another screen adaptation. Automotive-grade UX and safety requirements, certification processes, and OEM-specific ecosystems can make it difficult for developers to scale beyond individual integrations.

In this keynote, HARMAN will show how Ready Link Marketplace helps Android app providers bring their experiences into the car through a Marketplace built for automotive distribution. They will learn how the Marketplace creates value through greater reach across OEM programs, stronger discoverability inside app ecosystems, and extended monetization opportunities.

The session will also highlight what it takes to adapt a mobile Android app for Android Automotive, prepare it for Marketplace onboarding, and move toward certification and deployment without having to start from scratch for every automaker.

sessions.title: The Android Lens: Applying Mobile Forensics to AI Performance
sessions.description:
Modern LLMs like Ollama are technically ground-breaking but suffer from significant thermal and energy inefficiencies on resource-constrained hardware. This is often an overlooked cost of LLM's deterministic nature of token generation along with the heavy, unoptimized CPU operations within the underlying math engines.

With AI data centers, high energy demand translates to high water usage/thermal dissipation needs, and we are seeing it in pushback with American communities. To solve this, we must adopt a more frugal philosophy, the way Android development does.

This talk explores the forensics of loading local AI models to emulate resource constraints. Through the lens of Android and Kotlin CMP, we will audit Ollama's source code and profile how it performs in real time. We will move past the high-level Go wrappers and into the unforgiving C++ threading and memory management, identifying the leaks and bottlenecks leading AI to drown in thermal throttling and hallucinations.

sessions.title: Google SDV: Missed Chance or Game Changer? — An External View on AAOS SDV
sessions.description:
Google has recently released Android 17 and, with it, the AAOS Software-Defined Vehicle (SDV) stack.

We've read all the docs. We've looked at all the source code. We've had many questions.

We're bringing most of the answers — and an external view on SDV's opportunities and shortcomings, from a team that has been working on AAOS since its earliest days.

We will cover:
1.	Getting started with AAOS SDV on Cuttlefish
2.	Vehicle data flows and communication protocols
3.	Requirements for running SDV software

We will demonstrate how to:
1.	Transform Figma designs into working instrument cluster software
2.	Display data from the IVI in the instrument cluster
3.	Write an SDV service
4.	Map data between SOME/IP and SDV services
5.	Consume SDV data in the IVI through the SDV Gateway and VHAL

We will conclude with a summary and our assessment:
•	What does SDV provide out of the box?
•	What is still missing?

sessions.title: Changing tires while still driving - how did we make our development accessible to AI agents?
sessions.description:
When we started building Visible over 4 years ago, we decided to optimize for time to market. Without LLMs it mostly meant cutting corners, building fast and iterating on live features. As we matured, we were introducing new patterns but the old code would still deliver value.

However, in 2026, now with tens of thousands of daily users, when the implementation can be optimized for AI agents, the variety of patterns and legacy code does not make things any easier. Agents get lost in complex logic and often invent new patterns. Skills don’t really help keep it in line. We needed a different approach.

In this talk, I'm going to talk about how we approached making our fairly advanced codebase more accessible to AI, and in turn also to human developers. 

How did we rework our design system to be less verbose, how did we built in-house agent, ported a mobile app to desktop, built all new tools, and where we had to invest more time than we'd like to admit.

sessions.title: Homescreen Widgets - Now in Dart?!
sessions.description:
In the past, adding Homescreen Widgets to a Flutter project meant leaving your comfort zone and diving into a world of native complexity. Developers had to juggle Android Studio infrastructure, click through Xcode, and most frustratingly rewrite UI logic in Kotlin and Swift, shattering the "Write Once, Run Anywhere" promise of Flutter

With recent additions to the home_widget ecosystem, those hurdles are gone.

In this session, we’ll explore a new era of widget development where you can:

Automate Infrastructure: Use the CLI to scaffold native files instantly.

Write Once in Dart: Use a Flutter-like syntax to define your widget UI in Dart and generate full native code with one command.

Cross-Platform Parity: Build iOS widgets without ever needing to touch a Mac.

We will walk through the setup process and look under the hood at how Dart code becomes native components.

sessions.title: Beyond Breakpoints: Flutter Apps for the Foldable Era
sessions.description:
Foldables are an established Android form factor, not a lab experiment. Galaxy Z lineup is in its 8th generation, and the iPhone Duo ships this October. Foldable expectations now land on every team's backlog. Most Flutter apps still aren't ready.

In this session, you'll learn how to:
