1. Read hinges, folds, cutouts, and posture on Android with MediaQuery.displayFeaturesOf and DisplayFeatureState (flat, half-open).
2. Build dual-pane patterns with LayoutBuilder and adaptive navigation, following Material 3 guidelines.
3. Keep navigation, state, and dialogs coherent across fold and split-screen with DisplayFeatureSubScreen and anchorPoint.
4. Prepare for iPhone Duo: side navigation, asymmetric safe areas, and the displayFeatures gap on iOS.
5. Test foldable layouts in CI with widget/golden tests and emulators, without a physical device.

By the end, you'll have a mental model, patterns, and a testing playbook for apps designed for changing screen shapes, not accidentally resized.

sessions.title: The Flutter Enterprise Journey: From Native Apps to AI-Enabled Multi-Platform
sessions.description: This session explores how enterprise teams are navigating the strategic shift from native mobile development to Flutter's unified multi-platform approach, examining the real-world challenges, trade-offs, and wins along the way. We'll dive into why Flutter is uniquely positioned as an AI-era framework - where a single shared codebase dramatically reduces the token overhead of AI-assisted development, meaning fewer redundant prompts, less repeated logic across platforms, and faster iteration cycles when working alongside tools like GitHub Copilot or Claude. Attendees will walk away with a practical roadmap for modernizing their enterprise app strategy with AI at the center, unlocking compounding efficiency gains across iOS, Android, web, and desktop without sacrificing the performance, security, and maintainability that production environments demand.

sessions.title: AI in Live Ops
sessions.description: With downloads and LTVs under pressure while CPIs and development costs continue to rise—especially in the US and Europe—how can live games remain profitable? Join live operators, publishers, and industry leaders as we explore the tools, AI-driven workflows, and LiveOps strategies that help teams reduce costs, improve efficiency, boost retention, and maximize ROI. Learn how smarter production pipelines, automation, data-driven decision-making, and sustainable operations can extend a game's lifecycle and keep live services thriving in an increasingly competitive market.

sessions.title: From Internals to Insights: Reversing React, Flutter and Unity apps with radare2
sessions.description:
Flutter, React Native (Hermes), and Unity applications all produce very different release binaries, extracting valuable information from these modern multiplatform mobile app development frameworks is a real challenge for reverse engineers.
 
The talk will live demo using radare2 and Iaito, showcasing practical techniques for extracting code, metadata, and other useful artifacts from real applications.

sessions.title: Same Destination, Different Roads: Migrating a Live App at Scale
sessions.description:
Rewrites are back on the table. AI can help teams move faster, and more companies will use it to migrate mobile apps: native to React Native, React Native to native, or toward whatever comes next. But in large production systems, code is only one part of migration. When the app is live, business-critical, used by a large audience, and changing every week, every analytics event, edge case, release path, and small behavior matters.

Using a real-world, anonymized case study, this talk compares Greenfield and Brownfield approaches to modernizing a live app without disrupting users or the business. React Native is the concrete example, but the focus is decision-making: continuity, observability, analytics reliability, delivery velocity, organizational constraints, cost, and risk over time.

You’ll see real-world data points, Brownfield architecture, validation through POCs and production reference screens, and a practical mental model for choosing the safest road to the same destination.

sessions.title: Building a React Native App in a Low-Bandwidth Country — How Limitations Made It Universal
sessions.description:
Most React Native developers test on flagship devices with fast WiFi — but most of the world's users are on budget Android phones with variable connectivity and tight data budgets. Shipping a production app in India forced me to rethink every assumption about performance, bundle size, and UX. The solutions didn't just fix my app for constrained users — they made it better for everyone.
A practical blueprint for building React Native apps that are faster, leaner, and more resilient — whether your users are in Mumbai, Manila, or Munich.

sessions.title: How to Structure React Native When You Have Multiple Apps, Multiple Teams, and AI in the Mix
sessions.description:
Monorepos promise elegant code sharing for React Native teams managing iOS, Android, and web apps. The reality? Most teams end up with a complex build system that slows development and obscures best practices.
This talk provides a systematic approach to monorepo adoption for React Native, based on production experience migrating and maintaining multi-app repositories at scale.

We will also learn about how moving to monorepo can bring better experience for Developers and Agents

Technical Topics Covered:

When to monorepo: The specific team structures and codebases
Architecture patterns : How to structure your App
Build optimization : Build optimization best practices 
Tooling evaluation : Hands-on comparison of Turborepo, Nx, and pnpm
Dependency management: Strategies for handling conflicting native modules and platform-specific requirements
Developer experience :  How to improve DX using monorepo
AI advantage : How monorepo can 10x your agentic experience

sessions.title: How to make 2.1 million people feel special - an onboarding story by Yazio
sessions.description:
Yazio’s onboarding is a bit unusual;  It’s extremely long. It takes, on average, around 10 minutes to fully finish it. However, by the time you’ve finished it ,you’ve developed a relationship with Yazio, and with little green yettie that walked you through it all.

This is not by chance - the onboarding at Yazio has been meticulously tested, tweaked, refactored, and tested again, to find what it is that makes users feel the most welcome. 

In this talk we will discuss the plan, pitfalls, successes and failures of having an onboarding that matters, at a very very large scale.

sessions.title: Accessibility Nutrition Labels: How to Test, Evaluate, and Stand Out on the App Store
sessions.description:
Please clone this repo in advance: https://github.com/dadederk/fromZeroToAccessible

Apple’s Accessibility Nutrition Labels bring something new to the App Store: a public way to declare how accessible your app really is, and a chance to differentiate your product.
Nutrition labels aren’t about certifying every detail of every feature. Instead, they focus on the areas that have the greatest impact for users. They’re a meaningful step towards broader accessibility conformance, and deliver real value on their own.
In this workshop, we’ll introduce Apple’s Accessibility Nutrition Labels, what they mean for your users, how they support your business goals, and how they differ from accessibility compliance approaches.
We’ll get hands-on with an example app to explore how to evaluate against Apple’s criteria and make confident decisions about what to declare.
You’ll leave with a clear approach to assessing your app, aligning your team, and publishing Accessibility Nutrition Labels.

sessions.title: Snapshot Testing in Practice: Predictable and Reliable SwiftUI Views
sessions.description:
UI changes can easily introduce regressions, especially in shared SwiftUI components. Snapshot testing helps catch these issues early by verifying your UI across states and device configurations.

But Snapshot Testing does more than prevent regressions. Making UI testable encourages more predictable code, which leads to better architecture and makes it easier to reason about different UI states, resulting in more maintainable SwiftUI views.

In this talk, I’ll share real-world experience using Snapshot Testing in a large codebase: how it improves reliability, how to introduce it into your workflow, and how to run it in CI with Xcode Cloud for your iOS apps.

sessions.title: Your AI Code Reviews Are Missing the Point (And How to Fix It)
sessions.description:
AI code reviews often feel like tossing a coin. Heads - you get endless nitpicks about style. Tails - it finds real issues. And even when the signal is good, are we getting real quality and productivity benefits?

The secret isn't the AI, it's how you deploy it. This talk takes lessons learned from hundreds of teams with thousands of AI code reviews daily to explore what actually drives value in AI-assisted code reviews: rich context, personalization, and measurable impact on developer productivity. 
Learn to transform AI reviews from a compliance checkbox into a strategic advantage for your engineering organization.

Key takeaways:

- Review the criteria for evaluating code review solutions, from basic through advanced to game changer

- Track AI review impact on productivity metrics such as cycle time, code quality metrics and developer satisfaction

- Connect code review with automation flows to curb the new code acceptance bottleneck and unblock productivity for your teams

sessions.title: The Scale Wall: What Breaks When React Native Grows Fast
sessions.description:
Every React Native app is simple at first. Then users multiply, teams multiply, and yesterday's architecture and performance start to crack. 

This roundtable brings together engineers who have pushed React Native to serious production scale across very different environments and very different pressures, to compare what actually held up and what quietly became a liability. Bring your own scaling story, because the sharpest lessons in this room will come from the group, not just the speakers. 

Discuss challenges you have been facing at scale and what could be their best solutions.

sessions.title: Real Ball Tracking in Mixed Reality: How 'Ballee' Turns Physical Balls into Core XR Gameplay
sessions.description:
Most mixed reality experiences rely on standard handheld controllers or bare hand tracking. But physical feedback changes everything. 

In this session, I will take you into the engine room of Ballee, an experimental mixed reality sandbox and arcade experience where a real soccer ball becomes your primary interaction tool.

Building high energy physical games like Attack of the Zombie Elves introduces unique technical hurdles that standard XR tutorials never cover. We will explore how to achieve robust real time color tracking for fast moving balls on standalone hardware without tanking the frame rate. 

Moving from living room sandboxes to location based arcade setups also changes the architecture. I will show how instant spatial calibration using ArUco markers allows multiple players to share a compact physical playing field while keeping virtual targets and physical soccer balls perfectly synced.

sessions.title: ReactCon Gathering
sessions.description:
Location: Activity & Networking Area Level 2

Calling all React Native devs to come by for a quick meet and greet.

sessions.title: Break
Inside the Agent. Under the Hood of Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode.
sessions.description:
AI agents are transforming software development but are often seen as black box.  This talk looks inside the agent at the complex, multi-agent execution loop that gets kicked off by your prompt, and its corresponding context window. 
We will look the back-and-forth LLM interactions, the hidden system prompts, tool schemas, and contexts exchanged every iteration, using real world telemetry to see how tokens accumulate during tasks, how caching helps and when it doesn’t. 
Finally we look at the open source tools available to collate, and analyse histories so you can see what is going on with your own use of these tools.

sessions.title: Why your multi-agent system fails in production (live debugging)
sessions.description: What if the biggest obstacle to your multi-agent system isn't the AI — it's the coordination layer? Most teams spend months building orchestration logic that crumbles when agents behave unpredictably in production. This session diagnoses root causes of multi-agent failure through live coding. You'll see how model-driven approaches let agents reason together and share context without brittle hand-coded workflows. Expect working Python patterns for reliable agent coordination, practical debugging techniques for agent interactions, and monitoring strategies that catch failures before your users do. Stop fighting your agents — start orchestrating them.

sessions.title: We Shipped an AI Feature Users Loved. The A/B Test Told Us to Delete It.
sessions.description:
You built an AI feature. Everyone loved it in the demo. Should you ship it?

At GetYourGuide we added an AI-generated review summary to our Android app's activity page, then A/B tested it in Statsig before rollout. Seven million users later, it had reduced conversion by ~0.8% a statistically significant loss. The reason hid in a secondary metric: people read the reviews ~10% less.

This lightning talk walks one real experiment end-to-end from an Android engineer's seat. You'll learn:
- Why experiments are your safety net on Android, where there's no instant rollback
- How to wire an experiment into a Compose + MVI screen: variation in a reducer, cold-start defaults, exposure on view
- How to read results honestly and why the "mechanism metric" told the real story
- The peeking trap that nearly made us ship the wrong thing
- Why a losing test is your next hypothesis, not a dead end

You'll leave able to run an experiment you trust and to tell a feature that works from one that wins.

sessions.title: Extra Privilege: About System Apps and How to Build Your Own
sessions.description:
System apps are an essential part of our Android devices. Not only do they get the special treatment of coming pre-installed out of the box on your phone, car or smart fridge, they also come with access to much more functionality on the Android OS than your average Play Store app. They get to use special APIs and don’t have to ask for runtime permissions.
But where do you even get started if you ever find yourself in the situation where you get to build a system app yourself? To find out, we will go through the process of building a small privileged system app together.

In this session we’ll go through the steps of:
- Importing a demo app into Android Studio for Platform (ASfP)
- Setting up the Android.bp build files for it
- Pre-approving runtime permissions
- Adding some System API functionality
- And finally, upgrading it to a privileged app

Along the way, we will check out some debugging tricks and helpful tools.

sessions.title: AI in CI/CD: What's Actually Useful vs. Hype for Mobile Teams
sessions.description:
Every CI/CD vendor claims to be "AI-powered" now. But what does that mean for a mobile team shipping real apps — and where's it still marketing over substance?
This talk uses real, aggregate data from millions of mobile CI builds to answer that honestly: how much AI-authored code is flowing through pipelines today, how fast that's growing, and whether AI-authored changes are actually harder to debug when they break (spoiler: it's a wash).
The centerpiece: a live demo building a small Android feature from scratch using Claude in a remote dev environment — no editing tricks, just what the workflow actually looks like today.
You'll leave with a framework for evaluating any "AI-powered" CI claim, and a realistic sense of where to invest your team's attention now vs. later.

sessions.title: Beyond the hype: What user research tells us about agentic Android workflows
sessions.description:
As AI evolves from simple autocomplete to complex agentic partners, Android development is fundamentally shifting. Amidst the industry hype, there is very little hard data on how developers actually interact with these tools day-to-day. What does human-AI collaboration look like in the trenches?

In this 20-minute lightning talk, we move past marketing assumptions to share direct findings from a recent mixed-methods user research study. We’ll decode the realities of AI-assisted building, breaking down the fluid "working modes" that technical and non-technical builders use when partnering with AI. Finally, we’ll uncover the shared aspirations and anxieties of agentic coding.

While these are early insights rather than definitive guidance, examining these behavioral mechanics will give you a framework to evaluate your own workflow and spark vital conversations with your team as you prepare for the next generation of agentic IDEs.

sessions.title: Hands-On: How to bring Your Android App to the Car with Ready Link Marketplace
sessions.description:
This hands-on workshop shows how developers can efficiently bring a mobile Android app to Android Automotive OS (AAOS) and distribute it through Ready Link Marketplace, (HARMAN's in-car app store) to millions of vehicles worldwide.

The session opens by mapping the AAOS application landscape:Media/Audio apps, Car App Library (CAL) templated apps, and Parked apps (Video, Games, Browsers).

The focus then shifts to parked apps and games, and the issues developers hit most often when moving from phone to car: audio focus, landscape support, and edge-to-edge rendering behind system bars.

HARMAN's Ready Link developer tooling are then used to validate real behavior — car screen sizes, audio focus and media session handling, and CaRMA support.

The workshop closes with live AAOS adaptations of several real games in Android Studio — applying the code changes, compiling, and running them on the AAOS to see the improvements take effect.

sessions.title: Playwright for Mobile, in the Age of AI: One API Your Agent Can Drive Across iOS & Android
sessions.description:
We still ship bugs to prod, and AI hasn't fixed that. 

Coding agents write mobile features fast, but they can't reliably prove the app works on a real device, and every platform speaks its own automation dialect: XCUITest, Espresso, Appium, Detox.

This talk shows another way: one Playwright-style API that behaves identically across iOS and Android, on real devices, simulators, and emulators. Live on stage, we connect an open-source CLI and framework to a coding agent, let it explore a running app through the accessibility tree.
 no vision model, no brittle coordinates  catch a real regression, fix it, and re-run to prove the fix. That self-remediation loop wires straight into CI and runs at scale.

You'll leave knowing how to give your agent deterministic device control, standardize test authoring across every mobile stack, and turn agent exploration into tests that guard every commit. All open source.

sessions.title: From Smallest to Biggest Screen: Running Flutter on Apple Watch and Apple TV
sessions.description:
Think Flutter is limited to iOS, Android, and Web? Think again. In this session, we will discover how to stretch Flutter's reach to the absolute extremes of the Apple ecosystem: from the smallest screen on your wrist (watchOS) to the biggest screen in your living room (tvOS).

This is a practical, demo-driven showcase. You will see how Flutter apps can run on these unique form factors and how you can leverage a dedicated, open-source CLI companion to build, deploy, and run your own projects on these platforms with ease.

By the end of this session, you will learn:

The current state of Flutter compatibility on watchOS and tvOS.

How to structure your project to target non-standard Apple screens.

How to use the open-source CLI tool to automate your deployment pipeline.

sessions.title: Code First, Translate Later: Localization at scale with AI
sessions.description:
Managing localization at scale often stalls product releases. The traditional workflow requires manually defining keys, bouncing text between design tools and code, and waiting for translations before a feature can go to production.

In this talk, we’ll share how we flipped this workflow upside down at Holafly, making our engineering localization cycle much faster.

We will walk through the technical architecture of this code-first approach, including:

- How a custom localization skill makes it simple to add new texts.
- How we use the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to give the AI visual layout context.
- How we mitigate layout risks like text expansion.
- How to scale your Flutter app to new languages without overhead through a localization CI/CD pipeline.

You'll leave this session with practical strategies to eliminate manual copy-pasting and automate your localization pipeline using AI development tools.

sessions.title: Turning your App into our Spy - Android App Vulnerabilities in Practice
sessions.description:
Mobile apps often handle highly sensitive data and expose powerful device capabilities - this makes them prime targets for attackers. Even minor flaws can escalate into full compromise, leaking location data or enabling covert camera and microphone access. 

We present a real-world pentest case that uncovered a zero-day vulnerability in the Element X Android application. By exploiting it, we injected malicious web content into the app’s trusted context, demonstrating how subtle weaknesses can have severe impact. 

Building on this case, we share key lessons from targeted mobile penetration testing, highlight recurring vulnerability classes, discuss the unique challenges of securing modern mobile ecosystems and show how taking the attacker's mindset can aid secure app development. 

Fabian and Tobias are experienced mobile pentesters combining academic expertise with extensive project experience across diverse customer environments.

sessions.title: Haptics is like music - how to design haptics that fits perfectly
sessions.description:
Over 65% of users desire haptic feedback tailored to specific activities. Research shows that apps with high-quality haptics receive better reviews and enjoy stronger brand recognition. Haptics are essential because they make apps feel premium; they transfer not only information but emotion - much like music.

Despite this untapped potential, many developers struggle with implementation. Creating custom haptics is a nuanced craft, often likened to composing a melody. In this session, I will explain why quality haptics are vital and outline the key principles of effective haptic design.

I will also introduce Pulsar - Haptics Ecosystem, a new library with a rich collection of haptic presets and haptics toolset . Pulsar simplifies the design process, allowing developers to easily integrate and harvest the benefits of great haptics in their applications.

sessions.title: Build Once, Watch Everywhere
sessions.description:
In this hands-on session, we'll show you how to build a React Native app for TVs. You'll learn how to share a single codebase across Vega OS, Android TV, Web, and Apple TV, then layer in platform-specific dependencies for Fire TV to optimize for the Amazon Appstore, which reaches hundreds of millions of devices.

We'll also share starter samples with the essentials built in: D-pad focus, ten-foot layouts, and our recommended libraries. Then we'll dig into our latest AI builder tools and the workflows we use to migrate existing apps. You'll leave with your app running on TVs and a clear path to keep going.

Note:
 - Please download the Vega SDK before the workshop: https://developer.amazon.com/docs/vega/0.24/install-vega-sdk 
 - Prior TV app experience is not required

sessions.title: Fail fast, build faster - feedback loops in feature driven monorepos
sessions.description:
In massive monorepos, slow feedback loops can make even the smallest changes expensive and time-consuming. A simple feature update can trigger long CI pipelines, unrelated test failures, unclear ownership problems, or unexpected breakages among many other issues. As teams and systems grow, the “fail fast” mindset has to be applied to more than just the testing strategy.

This talk explores how feature driven architecture can help teams create faster and more meaningful feedback loops in large monorepos. It will discuss how to create clear feature boundaries, dependency-aware CI, affected builds, caching, architecture checks, and public API rules in order to support the developers catch problems earlier without validating the entire repository on every change.

sessions.title: Designing for Laziness: Apps for Effortless Users
sessions.description: We have entered the age of the passive user. Modern users do not want to search or type. They want magic to happen while they scroll. This session is a discovery of how we can stop fighting this behavior and use it to our advantage. We will explore how to move beyond the main app icon and build an orbit of features that live exactly where the user already is. We will look at how Share Extensions and Safari Extensions can make your app feel like a native part of Safari, TikTok, or Instagram. You will see how App Clips provide instant value without a long download and how App Intents and Shortcuts bring users back with a quick search or a voice command. By the end, you will see why these features are the secret to keeping an app active and indispensable by making it as lazy friendly as the people using it.

sessions.title: There is no (other) AppSec person: 5 things Swift developers can do against the Vulnpocalypse
sessions.description:
We live in interesting times. Who hasn't read the posts: nation-state supply chain exploits, ClickFix, Mythos and friends, agentic sandbox escapes, security releases with over 100 fixes credited to far more than 100 researchers. Not only are Swift developers not exempt, but the popularity of macOS as a development platform has it moving up the target list disproportionate to its absolute installs, while iOS has always been a juicy target.

Even though we're experiencing a rare case of the future arriving on time, we aren't helpless, and not every countermeasure is difficult. This lightning talk will go over the 5 most consequential steps you can take to shift to a defensive mindset, without getting overwhelmed.

sessions.title: What I Got Wrong About AI Adoption
sessions.description:
Everyone is talking about the productivity gains from AI in software development. Almost nobody talks honestly about what breaks along the way, and it is rarely the code. As Head of Mobile Development, I spent a year rolling out agentic coding across a ten person team building mobile apps. This is the talk I wish someone had given me at the start.

I will walk through the assumptions I got wrong when adopting agentic coding, why they were wrong, and what I would do differently. Expect stories about people and expectations rather than tools, prompts and benchmarks.

sessions.title: 5 years and going - how we built a sustainable live service VR game
sessions.description:
Puzzling Places launched as a small, meditative VR puzzle game - and quietly turned into a live service title that's still shipping new content and expanding to new platforms years later. This talk is a practical look at running a VR live service game told from the perspective of a small, independent team without a big publisher behind it.
I’ll share with why we chose to go live service in the first place and what it means to ship monthly content as a small team. I’ll outline the processes and infrastructure we had to built to make this sustainable (content curation & sourcing, processing pipeline, cross platform CI/CD). I’ll close with which features, updates and ports moved the needle, which didn’t, and how our business model evolved over time to keep it all sustainable.
A hands on retrospective of 5+ years of live service from a team still in the middle of it, for other builders who want to have a plan for what can come after launch day.

sessions.title: Break
Clean Code Revisited in the Age of AI
sessions.description:
For a generation of developers, Uncle Bob’s Clean Code wasn’t just a book—it was a manifesto. While "Effective [Add Language here]" books guide us in syntax, Clean Code taught us our coding standards. A set of rules so strict that many criticized it, such as the number of lines per method.

But the game has changed. The hands on the keyboard are often no longer human, and the code our LLMs write is far from what traditional “Clean Code” is. AI favors verbosity over abstraction and completion over long-term maintainability; it even adds “evil” comments everywhere because that’s how its completion works.
Are these rules still valid when refactorings happen in the blink of an eye?
But humans will still review the code, won't they?
Let’s revisit the rules!

sessions.title: AI Agent as a Function
sessions.description:
This is a live coding session in which you'll see how to build an AI agent from scratch using Kotlin and the http4k toolkit. No frameworks, no magic!

Starting with a simple API call, we'll add the core building blocks of modern AI agents: prompts, conversation memory, and tools ("translating" them from other open-source projects). Along the way, we'll explore what an agent is actually sending over the network and how LLMs interact with external systems. 

By the end of the session, you'll understand how AI agents work under the hood and how they can be represented as nothing more than a function.

sessions.title: Bringing Your Canvas Creations to Life with Jetpack Compose
sessions.description:
Take your Android UI development to the next level with the power of Canvas and Jetpack Compose! This session dives deep into crafting astonishing custom graphics, from beginner-friendly shapes to expert-level effects.

What you'll learn:
 - Explore production examples showcasing the versatility of Canvas in Jetpack Compose.
- Delve into algorithms and mathematical calculations for precise pixel positioning
- Embrace Blend Modes: Gain a comprehensive understanding of Blend Modes and their impact on canvas rendering.
- Bring it to Life: Discover powerful functions and APIs to seamlessly animate your custom graphics within Jetpack Compose.

This session is perfect for:
Android developers curious about pushing the boundaries of UI design.  Anyone looking to create visually stunning and interactive experiences.

Join me and learn the secrets to animation and breathe life into your custom graphics.

sessions.title: Going Beyond Obfuscation: Advanced Techniques for Protecting Android Apps
sessions.description:
Protecting intellectual property and preventing app manipulation is a significant concern for many businesses, and sometimes obfuscation just won't cut it. In this talk, we'll discuss how mobile devs can go beyond basic code obfuscation by exploring techniques like anti-tampering, anti-debugging, root detection, and other runtime application self-protection (RASP) methods to protect an app's code and data from reverse engineering and exploitation.

You will leave this talk with practical steps on how to make some significant steps in improving your app's security, and the pros/cons of doing so

sessions.title: Breaking Frozen Frames: Phased Rendering for Feature Rich UIs
sessions.description:
Feature-rich Compose screens often produce frozen frames when multiple heavy UI sections are composed in a single pass. Users are forced to wait for the entire screen to finish composing before seeing anything meaningful, creating slow and unresponsive first-load moments.

This talk presents Phased Compose, a phased rendering technique that splits a large composition into deterministic steps. Instead of generating one long frozen frame, each major section renders in its own phase, allowing meaningful content to appear immediately while remaining parts compose progressively. This approach reduced frozen frames by over 30% on complex screens, without delays or timers.

I will explain why existing APIs like PausableComposition and lazy layouts don’t solve first-frame jank, and how Phased Compose provides a general, predictable solution. Attendees will learn how to apply phased rendering to ship smoother startup experiences and eliminate long UI stalls in real apps.

sessions.title: Shark Dive: building a tool for expert human-agent investigations
sessions.description:
When I released LeakCanary in 2015, a whole class of Android bugs became visible, but they still weren't easy to fix. Over the next decade, LeakCanary got better UX and better traces, and I spent years teaching engineers how to read them.

Then AI agents arrived: anyone can paste a leak trace into a chat and get back a confident, plausible, wrong root cause. Ten years of effort, handed to a "stochastic parrot". Do experts still matter?

Of course they do! We've been dumping data at agents, hoping for the best, trusting the writeup. Instead, we need tools that enforce the expert's methodology, give humans and agents the same capabilities, and let them show you their progress & reasoning inside the tool itself.

I'll share what I learnt building Shark Dive, and the design choices behind it. The result is an agent that investigates with you, to dive even deeper than you could alone.

sessions.title: Tree-Shaking Native Code and Assets with Link Hooks
sessions.description:
Flutter is famous for its aggressive tree-shaking, but why stop at Dart code? Imagine a world where every single byte in your app is strictly necessary, from assets and translations to native binaries. In this session, we will dive into Link Hooks, the @RecordUse annotation, and the experimental data assets to discover how you can strip away unused native code and ship the leanest app possible.

In this session you'll learn

* how to use the @RecordUse() annotation to record uses of functions and classes in the Dart ahead-of-time compiler,
* how to use the recorded uses in a link hook to tree-shake native code with the native linker,
* how to use the data assets experiment to declare data assets in build hooks and tree shake them in link hooks, and
* some pirate language! Yarr!

sessions.title: GenUI in Production: How GenUI and A2UI Change Mobile Apps
sessions.description:
AI has made it easier to ship apps but not easier to make apps people keep using. The apps that matter will be the ones that fit the person opening them. GenUI is a key enabler in this direction: the design system stays stable while the UI adapts to the user.

We will go from idea to architecture: what GenUI actually is (and is not), how the A2UI protocol makes it provider agnostic, and the four ideas that make it possible: surfaces, the catalog, the data model, and the transport.

Then we will dive into learnings from the genui features in production. I will share what production taught me about cost and performance when composing surfaces with GenUI.

I will close with a vision: not static screens for everyone, but screens shaped by what your backend knows about this user, at this moment.

sessions.title: Self-Healing Flutter UI with Widgetbook: Teaching Coding Agents to Judge Their Own Work
sessions.description:
Coding agents generate Flutter UI faster than ever. The hard problem isn't speed anymore, it's quality. How can we ensure that coding agents create high-quality PRs that don't accidentally introduce UI bugs, like design system or accessibility violations? And how do we as humans not only review the code but also visual changes made by coding agents easily?

Walk away with a complete UI agent-assisted development workflow for Flutter: how to give your design system to an agent as context, how to build self-healing test loops with Widgetbook and flutter test, and how to review your agent's work in Widgetbook Cloud.

Selected Widgetbook customers will join the stage to showcase how they have been using Widgetbook.

sessions.title: Best Practices on Autopilot: How the Very Good AI Flutter Plugin Makes AI Write Code Your Way
sessions.description:
AI coding assistants are powerful, but they don't know your team's conventions — until you teach them.
The Very Good AI Flutter Plugin is a Claude Code plugin that injects production-grade Flutter and Dart best practices directly into the AI's context. Covering 12 skill areas — from BLoC state management and layered architecture to accessibility, Material 3 theming, GoRouter navigation, testing, and security — it ensures every line of AI-generated code follows VGV standards out of the box. This talk explores how each skill provides architecture patterns, code examples, testing strategies, and anti-patterns to avoid.
We'll also cover MCP integration with Very Good CLI for project scaffolding and license auditing, and the automatic hooks that run dart analyze and dart format on every file edit.

sessions.title: Level Design - The key to unlocking the true potential of casual puzzle games!
sessions.description:
In the day and age of mobile gaming companies looking to crack the next big casual/hyper-casual game, the answer might lie in the most overlooked element of game development - level design. 
The session will explore:
- Role of Level Design in mobile games.
- How Level Design can break or make your game.
- Level Design and related variables in casual games.
- Outcome driven vs Experience driven Level Design.
- Data informed vs Data driven decision making.
- The right amount of casual to succeed in a market where we compete with Tik Tok and Netflix.

sessions.title: ANOM: The Android That Took Down 1,000 Criminals
sessions.description:
Here's the true and fascinating story of a global law enforcement operation that unfolded entirely within the Android ecosystem.

For three years, the FBI and the Australian Federal Police secretly operated ANOM, an encrypted communication platform marketed to criminals as “ultra-secure.” In this session, we’ll break down the unprecedented technical setup that enabled the interception of over 27 million messages—ultimately leading to thousands of arrests worldwide.

We’ll dive deep into the inner workings of ANOM (a modified Android OS, intentionally flawed encryption mechanisms implemented by the agencies, and clever tricks like the “fake calculator” used to hide the app...) to discover how one of the largest digital infiltration operations in history was executed—right at the heart of our Android world.

sessions.title: React Native Chat Apps in 2026: Should You Build One?
sessions.description: Chat apps look simple—but they are one of the most demanding UI problems in modern mobile development. In 2026, React Native has matured significantly, yet building a production-grade chat still pushes its limits across lists, real-time updates, keyboard handling, gestures, and animations. This talk provides a practical, experience-based breakdown of what actually works, what still requires native solutions, and where tools like Skia and modern databases fit in. If you're deciding between React Native and fully native apps, this session will help you understand the real cost, trade-offs, and whether React Native is the right choice for your next chat product.

sessions.title: Zero to First Frame: Inside Your React Native App's Startup Flow
sessions.description:
Your app's slowest 500 milliseconds happen before you write a single line of render logic. In 2026, sub-second cold starts on mid-range devices are achievable, and the New Architecture has eliminated most obvious bottlenecks. So where do the remaining milliseconds hide?
This talk walks through the complete modern React Native cold start: native process launch, JS engine initialisation, JSI setup, module registration, bundle loading, and the handoff to first render.
You'll learn what Hermes V1 actually changed, and what's still ahead. Why native module initialisation remains a hidden cost post-migration. How bundle strategy and load order impact Time to First Render. Real production profiling data on where teams still lose time. And practical, high-leverage defaults that deliver consistent wins.
Walk away with a clear mental model of the startup path and a checklist to hit sub-1.2s iOS, sub-2s TTI Android in 2026.

sessions.title: 1 Billion Rows - Optimizing Swift for the Billion Row Challenge
sessions.description: Processing a billion rows is different than most day-to-day tasks we do as Swift developers. .Small inefficiencies in your algorithms can expand to massively increase the runtime performance of your program. The Billion Row Challenge was originally created for Java developers and has gained in popularity in other communities as well. Recently Ben completed the Billion Row Challenge in Swift to see how the traditional methods of developing in Swift and using the standard library change when you're processing vast amounts of data. We'll talk about memory-mapped files, scanning the file searching for particular characters, parsing floats, SIMD, and of course Swift Concurrency.

sessions.title: SwiftUI Is One Graph: Reverse Engineering Apple’s UI Engine
sessions.description: SwiftUI is often explained as a tree of views that gets diffed every time state changes. After reverse engineering the framework’s behavior and comparing it with Apple’s granted patents, I arrived at a different mental model: SwiftUI is a single demand-driven attribute graph. In this session we’ll follow the data from @State through dependency tracking, invalidation, layout, rendering, and animation to understand why SwiftUI behaves the way it does. Instead of focusing on API usage, we’ll examine the underlying architecture and connect it to Core Animation and the rendering pipeline. The goal is to leave with a coherent mental model that explains many of SwiftUI’s seemingly mysterious behaviors.

sessions.title: Swift API Design for Developers Who Don't Read The Manual
sessions.description:
When working in teams we often find ourselves writing code that will ultimately be used by others. In an effort to reduce potential bugs we should strive to write code that's impossible to misuse. One of Swift's greatest assets is its compile-time safety which prevents entire classes of bugs, but only when APIs are designed to leverage it. This talk demonstrates how to design your APIs to be fundamentally safer, catching errors at compile time rather than in production. These techniques apply to any Swift code, from single types to full SDKs.

We'll transform URLSession's unsafe imperative patterns into a type-safe, declarative networking library where the compiler becomes your documentation, actively telling you what you must, can and cannot do. You'll see how to apply modern Swift features such as macros, typed throws for exhaustive error handling, actor isolation for thread safety and more to make your APIs misuse-resistant.

sessions.title: Building for the (digital) Illiterate users
sessions.description:
For more than a decade I am building in-house software in a center for people with cognitive disabilities. People who are not able to read and write, people who are not able to understand complex information aren't able to use a computer in a normal way.

Although those people don't use apps and computers in the same way as most people do, in a digital world it is important that they can perform some digital tasks if they want to participate in a inclusive society. This is the way to go to give them the same quality of life as most people have.

In this talk I teach you how I build software to include those people. I will guide you to principles of color-by-function, images and iconography, text simplification, text-to-speech and tangibility. You'll learn how to use those methodologies to build software that helps to include those wonderful people with cognitive disabilities.

sessions.title: Migrating to the React Compiler: Share Your War Stories and Roadblocks
sessions.description:
The React Compiler promises to eliminate manual memoization, but migrating an existing React Native codebase to an automated build step is rarely a friction-free process. 

This roundtable is an open, peer-to-peer exchange for developers who are actively testing, deploying, or blocked by the React Compiler in real-world apps.

Instead of architectural theories, we will trade actual war stories from the trenches. Bring your real-world experiences with strict mode violations, third-party library incompatibilities, linting headaches, and unexpected debugging loops. We will map out where the compiler delivers immediate wins, where it introduces new breaking behaviors, and how different teams are managing the cultural shift from manual useMemo to automated compilation. Come ready to share what broke, what worked, and how you fixed it.

sessions.title: Human Augmentation with XR and AI
sessions.description:
Human-Centered XR: Where are we with actually enhancing human capabilities with XR and AI? Are we there yet with hardware, software, platforms, and social acceptance? What is holding us back from this future vision? Are we keeping a conscious and human-centric approach to design and business?

Join this panel discussion featuring many decades of combined experience:
Kelly Vero, NAK3D: Creative Badass | Award-Winning Female Founder |  Author “How Video Games Made The Metaverse” and “Breaking Through Bytes”
Binh Minh (Nguyễn Thị Bình Minh) Herbst, Telekom MMS: “Design For Happiness” as XR Creative Director, Female Founder in Tech, Professor, Speaker, Consultant, Diversity Advocate, Migrant Mom, Human
Kanzul Fatima Arif, Headraft: Head of Innovation | AI + XR Strategy | Human-First Tech Futures | Obsessed with Future Interfaces
Thomas Bedenk: Tech Strategist & Advisor | Bridging Human Psychology, Business & Emerging Tech

sessions.title: Lunch
Flutteristas meet & Greet
sessions.description:
Location: Activity & Networking Area Level 2

Join the Flutteristas for a little get-together and some networking time

sessions.title: Harness Engineering or How to Keep Agents on Track
sessions.description:
AI coding agents move the bottleneck in software teams. Once a model can produce a decent patch in minutes, the scarce work is steering: giving it the right context, catching drift early, preserving architecture, and making failure easy to catch and cheap to fix.

This talk makes Harness Engineering concrete: the platform work around agentic coding. A useful harness turns the repository into an environment agents can operate inside safely. That means project commands, task-specific skills, architecture maps, coding rules, tests the agent can run and understand, feedback loops, and guardrails that keep changes observable and contained.

You will leave with a practical checklist for building your own harness: making your codebase more agent-ready, reducing drift and cognitive debt, while keeping accountability where it belongs: with humans.

sessions.title: Power to Business: Business-Owned AI — What It Takes to Build and Why It Matters
sessions.description:
Everyone is talking about AI agents, but the biggest challenge isn't the agent—it's ownership.

When an AI assistant serves real customers, who controls its behaviour? Who decides what it can do? And how do developers build systems that remain safe, observable, and adaptable?

In this session, we'll explore what it takes to build and operate business-owned AI. Through the real-world example of Moi ApulAInen, an AI-powered customer assistant for Finnish mobile operator Moi, we'll discuss how business teams and developers can work together to create AI-powered services where business owns the outcomes and developers provide the guardrails.

We'll share the technical, organisational, and operational decisions required to move from prototype to production—and why ownership is often the missing link between AI capability and business value.

sessions.title: Flutter Developers Meetup
sessions.description:
Location: Activity & Networking Area Level 2

All Flutter Communities and Meetup groups and organizers are welcome to attend this meetup

sessions.title: Securing EUDI Wallets - What App Devs need to know
sessions.description:
EUDI Wallets are mandated by member states of EU by the end of 2026. There are many question marks about its functionality, security and certification. As the digital identity ecosystem grows, the requirements of banking, payments, insurance, healthcare and other services will require interoperability with the wallet through government issued wallets. For the upcoming EUDI wallets, this talk will help developers, product managers and tech leaders obtain clarity on:

1. Wallet's components and architecture patterns
2. Security requirements

sessions.title: currentTime, upTime, clocks, timers and the bugs nobody talks about
sessions.description:
Ah the classic System.currentTimeMillis and the SystemClock.upTimeMillis dilemma. What are they for and why can’t I just have one clock to rule them all?  Which one is affected by time zones and which one is affected by system sleep? 

See how we make using clocks painless at Sentry and the journey we took to get us there. We’ll cover when to use which clock in Android/Java/Kotlin. And how to set up a proper abstraction so humans and LLMs do the right thing™ in your codebase.

Trigger warning: time zones are discussed

sessions.title: Pushing Kotlin Beyond the Limits of Sanity
sessions.description:
Kotlin grants us incredible expressiveness: elegant DSLs, extension functions, overloaded operators, and reified types. It’s a developer's paradise. But in our quest for "clever" code, it’s dangerously easy to cross the line, leaving behind features nobody else dares to touch.

We'll share a real-world retrospective on Kotlin design choices that seemed brilliant on Day 1 but turned into nightmares on Day 100. From over-engineered DSLs to unreadable extension chains, we will analyze how high expressiveness can silently hurt onboarding, velocity, and maintainability.

Don't get us wrong, we love Kotlin. This session isn’t about bashing the language; it’s about evaluating the true cost of cleverness. We will provide concrete code smells, decision frameworks, and pragmatic rules to find the sweet spot between individual elegance and collective readability.

A talk for Android devs who might have been a bit too clever... and are now staring at their own code wondering what it actually does.

sessions.title: Unlock Multiplatform: Port your Compose Design System to Web
Composable Preview Driven Development with AI: TDD-fying your UI pAInlessly!
sessions.description:
So you're already familiar with Compose UI… but have you considered using Test-Driven Development (TDD) alongside Composable Previews to build and refactor UI faster, with fewer bugs, and without fear or pain?

Allow me to introduce you to “Composable Preview Driven Development”, a modern workflow where Previews, screenshot tests and TDD work hand in hand, and I’ll show you how to amplify it with AI.

In this tech talk, you will learn…

- Practical AI and non‑AI tricks to implement UIs with Compose faster and with fewer bugs

- Why designing @Preview APIs before AI code generation leads to more maintainable, higher-quality UI code

- How to turn @Previews into automated screenshot tests

- How to use those @Preview tests, plus TDD and AI, to generate, refine, and evolve UI confidently

Make sure not to miss this opportunity to explore the powerful combination of AI, Test-Driven Development, and Composable Previews!

No previous TDD knowledge is required!

sessions.title: Driving engagement while parked: get more mileage from your adaptive app with Android for Cars
sessions.description:
In this session, you'll learn how you can extend your existing adaptive app to support Android Auto and Android Automotive OS to reach your users on millions of additional devices.

I cover everything about Android for Cars, from the fundamentals of designing apps for use in cars, criteria for which types of apps can be used while driving versus while parked, to the newest developments for building and testing them.

You'll leave inspired and with everything you need to know to get your app on the road!

sessions.title: Don’t Break the Brand: Maintaining a Design System in Flutter
sessions.description:
Building reusable widgets in Flutter is easy. Building a design system that scales and stays consistent over time is not.

As applications grow, design systems often turn into “widget dumping grounds”: inconsistent APIs, duplicated styles, and components that slowly drift away from the original design intent. Without clear boundaries, a solid theming foundation, and proper validation workflows, even well-intentioned systems become hard to use and harder to trust.

Drawing from our experience building and evolving the design system behind the Holafly app, we’ll share real-world challenges, trade-offs, and lessons learned while scaling a production UI system.

Whether you’re starting a design system from scratch or trying to regain control of an existing one, joining us in this talk will give you practical tools to ensure your code remains a source of truth rather than a source of frustration.

sessions.title: The Reverse Flutter Journey: Taking a Production Flutter Web App to iOS and Android
sessions.description:
Most Flutter stories start with building first for mobile, then maybe shipping to web as a bonus. We had a chance of doing it the other way round - taking a production Flutter healthcare logistics app that was heavily optimized for web workflows and releasing it for iOS and Android.

In this talk, we'll dig into the two parts. First, getting a web app to compile and run natively: web-only packages and dart:html code that won't work on mobile, and the patterns that keep platform branching out of your feature code. Then the bigger challenge - making it feel native in terms of UX: gestures, navigation, dialogs, file handling, and assumptions the browser used to handle for free.

sessions.title: Flutter is an amazing video source. Here is why and how!
sessions.description:
What if you could use your existing React, Angular, Vue, Flutter or any other frontend framework skills to not only build UIs on screens, but to create visual stories ... and export them as real mp4 videos? 

From Spotify-Wrapped like summaries, instructional content that evolves with your codebase, to personalized videos ... all generated programmatically.

No video editor app, no ui clicking ... just beautiful code and open source! <3
Along the way, we’ll discuss architectural decisions, performance considerations, and why UI rendering engines turn out to be a surprisingly powerful foundation for video.

And yes, although optional, we will also discuss what unbelievable potential vibe coding videos has. 
Just think about telling Claude Code "take all images and information form this folder and turn it into a video". 

This talk is  a technical deep dive into how frontend frameworks work under the hood and how coding videos might actually even be better than using traditional tools.

sessions.title: One Codebase, Two Platforms: How ING Wholesale Banking Unified Mobile Development with Flutter
sessions.description:
ING Wholesale Banking migrated its mobile application from native Android and iOS to Flutter — this session shares the real story: strategic decisions, technical challenges, and honest results.
 
We'll cover why we chose Flutter for enterprise banking, how we approached the migration, and the challenges of security and compliance review in a regulated environment. We'll also dig into a question every enterprise team hits: what do you do when Flutter alone isn't enough? We rely on platform channels and platform views to keep certain native UI and logic in place. You'll see where and why we drew that line, and how we integrated Flutter with existing native infrastructure. We'll close with team transformation — what changed for Android/iOS specialists — and what worked (and what didn't).

sessions.title: From UnCrackable to Uncrackable: Rebuilding the Android Crackme for 2026
sessions.description:
The OWASP MAS Crackmes are how a lot of us learned mobile RE, they are how I learned it. So when I was asked to run an Android reversing workshop for my team, I wanted to build something of my own rather than borrow: three apps, each forcing a single discipline (static, then dynamic, then network) by closing off the shortcuts to the other two. RASP, R8 obfuscation, native certificate pinning, instrumentation detection and encrypted storage, every defence in them taken from something I had already met on a pentest, including the weak ones. It mirrors a real engagement and maps onto the MASVS Resilience and Network categories.

By the end you'll be able to:

- read and beat layered tamper, root and instrumentation detection
- judge what a control actually costs an attacker, and say so honestly in a report
- bypass both managed and native certificate pinning to intercept live traffic
- design crackmes and internal CTFs that force real skill rather than pattern matching

sessions.title: React Native at Scale: Real Decisions, Trade-offs, and Hard Lessons
sessions.description:
Every company runs React Native differently. Some rewrote an application from scratch, others integrated it in a brownfield scenario. Some tried other cross-platform solutions first and migrated to React Native, or vice versa.

In this panel we bring together engineering leaders from companies running React Native at scale: millions of users, complex use cases, and real-world constraints.

We'll dive into the decisions that actually mattered when shipping in production. How did React Native land in the organization in the first place? What did the first twelve months look like? What did they migrate to, or from, and why? And what would each team do differently today?

This is the panel where the polished conference talks meet the production trade-offs nobody blogs about.

sessions.title: The cost of JavaScript in React Native apps
sessions.description:
React Native is a complex web of dependencies and environments that interact in ways often hidden from the developer. We happily build our components and native modules, but rarely see what actually happens under the hood when data crosses between worlds.

In this talk, I want to explore the overhead, missed optimizations, and boilerplate we generate every time our app is translated from JavaScript to native.

I'll cover the JavaScript Interface (JSI) and Java Native Interface (JNI), and share measurements such as how expensive it really is to pass a single integer from JavaScript into a native component.

I'll also look at related types like folly::dynamic and the new (still unstable) jsi::ISerialized fast serialization interface in Hermes.

Time permitting, I'll touch on the performance of native modules and discuss when it's actually better to keep something in JavaScript rather than handing it off to native.

sessions.title: Building a React Native Super App
sessions.description:
Building a Super App sounds exciting until you have to make the first architectural decision.

Unlike traditional mobile apps, Super Apps introduce a completely different set of engineering challenges. How do you organize dozens of features? Where do you draw module boundaries? What should be shared, and what should remain independent? How do you prepare for multiple teams working in the same codebase without slowing each other down?

In this talk, I’ll share our experience designing our first React Native Super App. I’ll walk through the architectural decisions we’re making, the trade-offs we’ve faced, and how we’re approaching modularization, navigation, shared UI, dependency management, feature flags, and release strategy. Rather than presenting a finished success story, this is an honest look at the engineering decisions that shape a large React Native application from day one.

sessions.title: Effect Systems: a powerful alternative to Dependency Injection
sessions.description:
Swift apps depend on side effects such as disk I/O, networking, randomness, and concurrency. While essential, side effects make code harder to extend, customise, and test.

Today, they are managed with DI frameworks and opinionated architectures. This often requires invasive scaffolding and sometimes forces procedural code into unidirectional data flow.

This talk presents Swift Effect, an architecture-agnostic effect system that makes side effects controllable, composable, and testable while keeping the code linear.

The talk introduces Algebraic Effects and Effect Handlers, and demonstrates how they unlock:
- Natural composition of behaviour
- Deterministic Swift Concurrency testing
- Mock-less testing of complex programs

Effect handlers can intercept, suspend, and resume side effects at runtime, enabling step-by-step execution of application code. This enables writing tests for observable behaviour and state changes, mirroring a human tester interacting with a running program.

sessions.title: The iOS Decisions You Can't Take Back
sessions.description:
Some engineering decisions are easy to change. Others become part of our app’s future.

This talk explores the one-way doors of iOS development. The decisions that are easy to make early on but can be surprisingly difficult to undo later. From architecture and data persistence to API contracts, platform decisions, and app state, these choices can shape how an app evolves for years.

We’ll look at what makes a decision difficult to reverse, why these decisions are often underestimated, and what can happen when they meet a growing codebase, team, and user base.

sessions.title: The Tale of Logging
sessions.description: Every tale hides a truth. Logging is one of the least glamorous parts of software development, until your app misbehaves in a way nobody can explain. In this talk, a fox leads us through Console, SwiftLog, and os_log to uncover what Apple's native tools can, and can't, tell you about your running app. By default, AI coding assistants reason from static code, the same way we do when we only stare at files, so without real runtime context, even AI ends up guessing. We'll watch human and AI try to fix real bugs, first without proper logging, then with it, and see how differently that story unfolds.

sessions.title: We broke QA twice before it worked
sessions.description:
Salmon is a fast-growing mobile bank. As the product accelerated, our regression load grew faster than the team could test — and release fear set in. We tried to fix it by rebuilding the QA process. We broke it twice before anything held.
This is the honest version, not a polished case study. Both rebuilds looked reasonable on paper: we hired, we changed how the team worked, we reshaped the workflow. Both times the classic approach collapsed under a product that changes faster than tests can keep up. We'll show exactly where it broke, what it cost us, and what we missed each time.
The third attempt started working. We have E2E infrastructure on mobile, devs automating against it. We don't chase a full pyramid or pure E2E — we split each story into layers, from cheap snapshots to long E2E flows. We test stories end to end, mobile through backend, not each side alone, learning not to duplicate checks. It's not perfect, but for the first time in four years we see how to scale this.

sessions.title: Building an Accessibility Culture, One Step at a Time
sessions.description:
Accessibility is an interesting part of building a project. Arguably easy in some areas, and incredibly difficult in others. Touching product, design, engineering and testing. Everyone can play their part — or not.

Play your part by understanding what you don’t know, advocating for organizational buy-in, and having enormous impact on your users.

In this roundtable, I'd love to discuss overcoming these challenges at various companies, from iOS to Android & web, and how you can be set up to be successful at your company — and beyond. How can you clarify impact of accessibility? How can you constructively encourage various parts of the company to embrace accessibility? How can you deal with hitting (inevitable) roadblocks?

sessions.title: Museums and Exhibitions in the Age of AI and Immersive Technology
sessions.description: Cultural spaces have become one of the toughest testbeds for XR and on-device AI. You get unpredictable lighting, untrained users, all-day uptime, and no tolerance for a headset that needs rebooting mid-tour. This session looks at real installations built for museums and expos, drawing on projects from across the field as well as our own work. We'll cover the architecture, the tracking and rendering trade-offs, and where AI runs on the device to personalize or translate an experience in real time. The takeaways apply well beyond a gallery wall, to any app facing harsh conditions and non-technical users.

sessions.title: Break
Self-Correcting SDKs: Keeping Specs and Implementations in Sync with Agents
sessions.description:
AI agents make it easy to change code across many SDKs and packages. The harder problem is keeping all of them aligned on the same behavior.

At PostHog, we use shared SDK specs as a control plane, conformance tests as the safety net, and agent-powered Loop workflows connected to GitHub to continuously detect and fix drift.

Spec changes can fan out into guarded SDK PRs, SDK changes can trigger spec updates, and GitHub issues can be triaged into draft fixes automatically.

The goal is not autonomous code changes. It is a system where agents handle the repetitive alignment work while humans stay in control of review and decisions.

sessions.title: Crafting Intelligent Agents with Context Engineering
sessions.description:
We've all heard about prompt engineering. But now with the emergence of context engineering you may be scratching your head about what the difference is. The reality is that to build reliable agents, we need to use all tools in our context toolbox to ensure they provide accurate responses in the correct format.

Let's dive into the world of context engineering. I'll explain what it is, why it is important and the elements of context that we can tune and tweak to build more reliable AI agents and associated systems.

sessions.title: You Are Being Nudged
sessions.description:
Every default setting, every notification, every empty state screen — these are nudges. And if you build digital products, you're already designing them, whether you know it or not.

This talk explores the psychology behind persuasive technology: how digital products use cognitive biases, reward loops, social mechanics, and friction reduction to shape human behavior. We'll look beyond TikTok and Instagram to see how the same mechanisms operate in fintech, productivity tools, and everyday apps.

You'll leave with:
• A vocabulary for design decisions you currently make on instinct
• The core psychological models behind habit-forming products (Fogg, Kahneman, Eyal)
• The ability to spot the line between helpful nudging and dark patterns
• Awareness of how small UX choices create real behavioral change in your users

sessions.title: Design and build desktop-class Android experiences
sessions.description:
The ecosystem of Android devices is rapidly growing. Explore the essential quality and design guidelines to ensure your applications deliver a polished, productive experience on connected displays, googlebooks and other desktop setups. 

Discover the latest tools, APIs, and best practices to build desktop-class experiences with optimized layouts, enhanced input support, and powerful window management capabilities.

In this talk we will explore what it takes to build a desktop-first Android app, by looking at:
- The new desktop design guidelines
- The new desktop quality guidelines
- The new APIs and tools to support your development journey 
- The best practices around managing multiple instances
- What's new in input support

sessions.title: Android Open Accessory - Make Apps talk via cable
sessions.description:
This session shows you how to make apps on two Android devices talk to each other via USB. While not a common use case, it provides low-latency, high-bitrate communication that is more reliable for local communication than P2P Wi-Fi or Bluetooth could ever be.

This is enabled by Android Open Accessory, a standard that allows setting up high-level communication over a USB cable.

While I will touch on OS-level and hardware topics, the core of this talk will focus on the app implementation for Android Open Accessory and the architectural decisions you can make. As a practical example, I will also share an approach to sharing the same login session across both devices, requiring only one login to your online infrastructure — without giving your identity team a headache.

sessions.title: We are all Fucked: An Android Developer’s Guide to the Post-AI Apocalypse
sessions.description:
The illusion of Artificial Intelligence is dominating Android development, driven by hype over reality. As companies rush to embrace AI to save hypothetical costs, we are left cleaning up a dumpster fire of unscalable slop. 

Real engineering relies on the pains and learnings that we as engineers have accumulated over the years, it takes experience of failure and learnings not to figure out what to build, but what not to build. I'm not going to tell you how to use AI for your advantage, I'm not going to tell you how best to use AI tools.

Mostly, we can try to temper our relationship with AI, sometimes we can use it to our advantage, sometimes we can even manage upwards (though rarely). sometimes, we can even distract our managers by giving them safe arenas to play with, like a child with an adult colouring book.

But perhaps, we can just laugh and make a joke about the collective hell we've found ourselves in.

sessions.title: Fundamentals of Mobile System Design
sessions.description:
Mobile apps are no longer just thin clients that passively render API responses. Modern apps are expected to cache, sync, stream, retry, paginate, prefetch, observe, and recover. They must seamlessly adapt to unreliable networks, strict background execution limits, and volatile device resources.

In this talk, we’ll break down the foundations of mobile system design and the critical questions senior engineers must answer before writing code: What data survives offline? How do we balance data freshness against battery and memory constraints?

Using a concrete example, we’ll explore the real-world trade-offs behind feed orchestration, infinite pagination, client caching, state synchronization, etc. without spoiling the full blueprint.

You’ll walk away with a practical mental model for approaching complex mobile architecture, whether you’re prepping for senior/staff interviews, mentoring your team, or making critical design choices in production iOS and Android apps.

sessions.title: Building Vehicle-Aware Apps with VHAL, VSS, and Runtime Permissions
sessions.description:
Modern automotive software development must balance broad access to vehicle data and functions with OEM governance, safety, privacy, and compatibility across fragmented ecosystems.
This work, developed within COVESA’s AOSP Group, extends Android by combining Android’s VHAL and CarAPI framework with its runtime permission model, optionally enhanced with a standardized semantic model such as VSS. These components create a unified, cross-OEM vehicle capability layer that enables secure and backward-compatible access to vehicle data and functions.
Using Android’s runtime permission model, OEMs can dynamically govern access to vehicle capabilities without requiring application redeployment. Applications become capability-aware and adapt gracefully as permissions, policies, or hardware availability evolve over time.
The result is a scalable and future-ready platform for software-defined vehicles that enables richer applications while preserving OEM control, safety, and compliance.

sessions.title: Bringing hot reload to your full Dart stack: backend, website, and database
sessions.description:
Hot reload is a defining feature of Flutter, but what if it extended through your backend and database? How much faster could you ship?

In this session, we explore bringing true hot reload to the Dart server. From updating business logic on the fly to applying database migrations while the server runs, we’ll demonstrate a workflow where nothing stops, and everything stays in sync.

We’ll dive into the technical details: code reloading strategies, state preservation, and safely evolving schemas without downtime to create a cohesive, full-stack experience powered entirely by Dart.

We’ll also explore how this unlocks massive productivity when combined with AI agents. By integrating an MCP server, agents can generate and apply database migrations and backend logic in real time, all while your app keeps running.

Whether building prototypes or production systems, this talk will fundamentally change how you think about building full-stack apps.

sessions.title: Let’s Build a Nano Banana App with Flutter
sessions.description:
In this hands-on workshop, we’ll build a fun, creative mobile app using Flutter powered by Nano Banana.

We’ll focus on turning simple prompts into rich visual experiences and shaping an interface that feels fast, interactive, and intuitive. Using Firebase, we’ll connect everything into a smooth, real-time flow so users can generate and refine results instantly.

By the end of the workshop, you will:

- Build a Flutter app that generates and edits images
- Turn user input into dynamic visual results
- Design a clean, responsive UI around generative features
- Explore how AI reshapes modern app experiences

This session is practical, with a strong focus on building something real. You’ll leave with a new Flutter app added to your developer portfolio and a clear sense of how to bring AI-driven creativity into your own projects.

No special prerequisites are required, just Flutter set up on your machine and an existing Firebase account.

sessions.title: Learning Embedded Flutter from a Fortune Telling Fish
sessions.description:
Captain Reef is a pirate fish who lives in a cabinet and tells your fortune. She's also a Flutter app.

Over ten months, a Zoltar-inspired side project turned into a full-blown arcade machine: a Raspberry Pi 5 and an ESP32, a Pepper's Ghost display, a thermal printer that hands you your, custom PCBs, and more than half a million fortunes stored in SQLite so the whole thing runs offline. 

This talk is the story of that build and everything it taught me about running Flutter on real hardware. You'll learn how flutter-pi works and how to get it running, how to get your Pi talking to a microcontroller, and how to tune your system for reliable embedded deployment in a machine that has to survive a conference floor.

Then we'll go beyond the breadboard: designing custom PCBs and a Pi HAT that take your project from "wires everywhere" to "actually shippable." 

Fair warning: Captain Reef foresees a Raspberry Pi in your future.

sessions.title: The Cost of a Character: Scaling Rich Text Parsing and Caching
sessions.description:
Text rendering is one of the most deceptively heavy operations in the Flutter framework. When processing formatted strings inside high-velocity scrolling feeds like chat interfaces or real-time dashboards, continuously parsing tokens and rebuilding nested RichText components creates massive layout overhead, spikes heap allocations, and causes noticeable UI micro-stutter.

This session breaks down the journey of building an open-source text-formatting utility from the ground up for its v3 architecture. We will analyse the trade-offs of moving away from expensive cascading regular expressions toward a highly efficient, single-pass linear scanner operating at O(N) scale. More importantly, we will dissect how implementing an internal token and layout memoization cache layer allows your application to bypass the rendering pipeline entirely during widget lifecycle updates.

sessions.title: From Board Games to AI Agents: Engineering Behavioral Loops in B2B Workflows
sessions.description:
Gaming isn't dying; it is being absorbed into B2B SaaS and enterprise platforms. However, to build successful apps, we must move past superficial "gamification" (points and badges) and architect structural "Serious Games" that drive behavioral change and measurable ROI.

In this session, we will explore how to engineer deep game mechanics into non-gaming applications. Drawing from over 60 serious game designs, including "Meteorite" (a B2B knowledge management platform) and "DealIQ" (a multi-agent AI sales simulator), I will bridge game design theory with practical app engineering.

We will cover how to act as an "AI NPC Psychologist" when designing multi-agent architectures, state management for behavioral loops, and how to engineer safe failure states that increase user retention. Attendees will leave with a practical blueprint for turning dry enterprise workflows into engaging, game-driven architectures.

sessions.title: Luma: A Moldable Workspace for Dynamic Instrumentation
sessions.description:
What if your Frida workspace could remember everything, turn results into interactive tools—and investigate alongside you?

Luma is the official open-source Frida GUI: a persistent, moldable environment for exploring live processes across macOS, iOS, Linux, and Windows. Sessions survive crashes and restarts, while hooks, traces, captures, notes, scripts, and results stay together in a project you can reopen and continue.

We’ll demo tracing and capture diffing, plus integrated scripting where code and results are persisted, visualized, transformed, and exported through custom presentations inspired by moldable development.

We’ll also explore Missions: give an LLM a goal, choose a provider such as Anthropic or OpenAI, and let it work inside the environment. A built-in MCP server can expose the same capabilities to external tools.

Frida gives you access to a running process. Luma turns it into a living laboratory—for humans, scripts, and agents.

sessions.title: The Fourth Platform: How Vega got us surprisingly close to “Write Once, Run Everywhere”.
sessions.description:
"Write once, run everywhere" is a promise that often breaks down under real-world constraints. At Zattoo, building streaming apps across Android, Apple, and Web meant years of separate native stacks that didn't align and didn't scale. This talk is a case study on how Vega, a React Native-first platform from Amazon, brought us surprisingly close to that goal.

The multiplatform landscape is shifting fast. Vega lets React Native run natively on the OS without translation layers. For teams struggling with fragmented codebases and duplicated effort, understanding what's now possible can reshape their platform strategy.

Key takeaways:
1. Designing a scalable multiplatform architecture with React Native and Vega
2. Managing platform-specific boundaries
3. How a shared codebase shifts team topology from OS silos to feature-focused teams
