4. Practical lessons from shipping a production streaming app across all major ecosystems

sessions.title: The Feature That Didn't Need to Be Smart
sessions.description:
A more and more common story: you're asked to add AI to a product. Not a chatbot. Not an AI platform. Just one small feature that needed to be smarter. 

In this talk, I'll share practical lessons from shipping a small LLM feature in production, including in React Native: how to keep the architecture simple, how to set guardrails, how to communicate your values ethically, and how to decide when AI is actually the right tool.

This isn't the first time a big technology hype has caught up with us and might creep us out at first, and this talk will look at that history, too.

sessions.title: Why React Native apps monetize better
sessions.description:
Subscription monetization is one of the hardest—and most important—problems in modern app businesses, directly impacting growth, sustainability, and valuation. Understanding why React Native apps outperform in key revenue metrics helps developers make better product and technology decisions, not just engineering ones.

Major takeaways for the audience:
- React Native apps show significantly higher conversion, early revenue per user, and lifetime value compared to other frameworks
- Faster iteration cycles in React Native enable tighter feedback loops on paywalls, onboarding, and pricing
- Cross-platform consistency can improve user experience and reduce friction in monetization funnels
- Data suggests advantages persist beyond early lifecycle, indicating stronger long-term retention and value extraction
- There are still areas (e.g., performance edge cases, platform-specific UX polish) where native approaches may outperform

sessions.title: App Adaptivity: Opening your UI to new screen sizes
sessions.description: At my company I am the pioneer of trying to move our macOS and iOS codebase closer together, by creating a unified UI layer, which can be used on both platforms. On the 2 recent WWDC Apple made big steps into that direction, in 2025 we got the iPad Windowing System, which makes the iPadOS closer to macOS. This year we have the App Adaptivity, where our iOS app can support different screen sizes, even going to sneak into the macOS area (except the EU :P), where iPhone Mirroring can translate our app into a(n almost) macOS app. In September 2026 we finally had the iPhone Duo, where we finally connected the dots. I will hop through what changes are required for support this transition, and also on what can go easily wrong and how to fix it.

sessions.title: Async/Await at Scale: Designing High-Throughput iOS Architectures
sessions.description:
Swift's async/await made concurrency look simple, but shipping it at scale is still a boss-level problem. Swift 6's strict concurrency can expose issues in existing codebases: hidden race conditions, cancellation that is not handled correctly, and background work that outlives user intent.

This workshop breaks down how to design an iOS architecture that coordinates 10,000+ logical async operations without melting CPUs or spiraling into Task-hierarchy spaghetti. We'll go deep into structured concurrency, task lifetimes, cancellation propagation, actor re-entrancy traps, and the most underrated weapon in Swift concurrency: backpressure the technique that keeps your app smooth when work arrives faster than it can be processed.

sessions.title: App Performance Monitoring at Scale
sessions.description: There are lots of ways to track an app’s performance—Apple and Google tools, plus plenty of third-party options. I’ll share how we ended up building our own performance monitoring suite at Booking.com, and why we went down that path. I’ll talk through the metrics we started with, what didn’t really work, and what turned out to be more useful. I’ll also cover what our current setup can do, how it’s been holding up after 4 years in production, and finish with a story from our two-year journey to track down and fix a really annoying fatal hang in our iOS app.

sessions.title: How to do AI when your team hates AI
sessions.description:
The hardest part of AI adoption isn’t the tooling, or the cost, or even the legal bits. It’s the same thing it’s always been: people. And it’s hardly surprising that a number of engineers are so reluctant to innovate with the tool they’re constantly told will take their jobs.

In this talk we'll go through our learnings and successes as engineering managers navigating the hopes and fears of our team members in this strange and uncertain new world.

Some areas we’ll cover include:
- How nurturing a safe space that respects boundaries whilst encouraging people to leave their comfort zones turbocharged AI learning and usage.
- How having senior developers as advocates can alleviate fears and skepticism far better than AI-enthusiastic managers ever can.
- How to respond when a team member is steadfastly against using AI at all.

This is a talk for leaders who know engineers do their best work when leadership is driven by understanding, not fear.

sessions.title: Why Design Systems Break in React Native, and How Teams Fix Them
sessions.description:
Most design systems start as a collection of buttons, inputs, tokens, and reusable patterns, but teams quickly discover that components alone do not solve the real friction between design and engineering. Figma drifts from code, documentation gets outdated, ownership becomes unclear, and the system slowly turns into either a bottleneck or a forgotten asset. 

This roundtable brings together React Native developers, designers, and product-minded engineers to talk about what makes a design system sustainable in practice: governance, contribution models, release processes, quality checks, and the day-to-day habits that keep adoption easy. The goal is to compare what has worked, what has failed, and what makes a design system feel like product infrastructure instead of just a shared UI kit.

sessions.title: Phones Away, Glasses On! The Making of DUMBO Spatial Guide
sessions.description:
DUMBO Spatial Guide is a hands-free, narrated tour experience built for the iconic streets of Dumbo, Brooklyn. It recognises real-world landmarks through Meta AI glasses and guides you with contextual audio, all while your phone stays in your pocket.

This talk walks through our journey, from prototyping computer vision approaches to understand when someone "looks" at a point of interest for indoor and outdoor spaces, to the user experience challenges of guiding someone without a screen. You'll hear about the technical decisions, the dead ends, and what it takes to ship an XR product when there's no existing playbook to follow.

sessions.title: Game 'App Ideas Battle'
sessions.description:
Location: Activity & Networking Area Level 2

Come play a fund game where teams develop an absurd app in 10 minutes and pitch it.

sessions.title: Break
Developers Now Have a Second Brain: Learning to Think With AI
sessions.description:
AI tools are often positioned as a way to write code faster — but their biggest impact is in how developers think, reason, and make decisions.

This talk reframes the conversation: instead of chasing prompt tricks or the latest tooling, it centres on the mental models and workflows that make AI genuinely useful in day-to-day engineering.

You'll leave with:

A repeatable approach for debugging complex issues using AI — without outsourcing your thinking.
Practical strategies for navigating unfamiliar codebases with more confidence and speed.
A clearer way to structure technical decisions and pressure-test your assumptions using AI as a thinking tool.
A framework for staying in control of your craft — regardless of which AI tools dominate next quarter.

Mental models outlast tools. This talk gives you ones worth keeping.

sessions.title: Stop Shipping Slop: Practical Tips for AI-Assisted Development
sessions.description:
AI coding agents can create pull requests faster than ever and the real bottleneck is no longer writing code. But we don't want to ship slop as fast as the agent can produce it.

At Wolt, a DoorDash company, we have been exploring how to move quality checks closer to the agent workflow, so AI does not just produce more code, but helps raise the bar for what reaches production. This talk shares practical patterns for closing the loop between agents, CI, code review, production monitoring, and team knowledge.

The talk will include concrete examples from Wolt-style engineering workflows. In particular, we will look at how AI-assisted development changes quality practices before, during, and after shipping: using agents for full-stack and cross-repository changes; improving PR reviews with project-specific context; and feeding production errors, logs, analytics, and rollout data back into future fixes.

sessions.title: Beyond the Map: Why Android Navigation Is Harder Than Rendering a Route
sessions.description:
Putting a map into an Android app is easy. Building a usable navigation experience is not.

This lightning talk focuses on one practical lesson from working with map-heavy Android apps: a map SDK and a navigation product are very different things. Using MapLibre-Compose and Ferrostar as reference points, we will look at the hidden work behind route rendering, camera behavior, location state, rerouting, offline expectations, Compose integration, and UX recovery.

The goal is to give Android developers a quick decision framework for evaluating open-source map and navigation stacks before they commit to building on top of them.

sessions.title: Compose Styles in a Real Codebase: Did It Actually Get Faster?
sessions.description:
Compose Styles look promising on paper: cleaner styling APIs, better state-based visuals, and potential performance wins. But official benchmarks are not the same as a real app with an existing design system, complex screens, and production constraints.

I’ll show what happened after migrating our application design system to Compose Styles: what changed, what became cleaner, what became awkward, and whether the performance gains showed up in practice.

You’ll learn what to migrate first, how to benchmark complex screens and layouts, what to measure beyond recompositions, and how to decide whether Styles are worth adopting at scale.

sessions.title: How We Cut Android CI Costs by 80%
sessions.description:
Most teams treat CI as a fixed cost — you pay for the machine, you wait for the pipeline, that's just how it is. It isn't. In this talk I'll share how we cut CI credits by 80% and pipeline duration nearly in half on a real production Android app.

I'll walk through the handful of decisions that made the biggest difference — some obvious in hindsight, some counterintuitive — and the actual dashboards showing before and after. These patterns aren't Android-specific: if your CI runs the same expensive steps on every PR regardless of what changed, this talk is for you.

Real numbers, nothing theoretical.

sessions.title: Flutter + KMP: Complementary architecture
sessions.description:
Flutter and Kotlin Multiplatform are often presented as competing choices. In this talk, I'll share a real production case where using both together turned out to be the better architecture.

While building a real-time flight simulator in Flutter, I needed to keep a simulation engine and a native 3D map in sync at 60 FPS. Every frame had to cross the Flutter ↔ native bridge, and the platform channel became the bottleneck.

So instead of optimizing the bridge, I took it out of the hot path:

- Flutter for UI and product experience
- Kotlin Multiplatform for the real-time simulation engine
- Native plugins for per-frame map rendering

In this session, you'll learn:

- Why platform channels struggle with real-time, per-frame updates
- Why common optimizations fall short
- How to split responsibilities between Flutter, KMP and native code

A practical case study on real-time performance, architectural boundaries, and how Flutter and KMP can complement each other rather than compete.

sessions.title: Almost Self-Improving Agentic Flows in Flutter
sessions.description:
We all want our Flutter projects to enforce their own standards, but manually writing custom lints, comprehensive tests, and maintenance scripts is a tedious chore. What if your development workflow could learn to do the heavy lifting for you?

In this lightning talk, we’ll explore how to build "almost" self-improving agentic flows tailored for the Flutter ecosystem. By integrating AI retrospective skills with automated feedback loops, we can shift from writing rigid, manual rules to creating dynamic systems that evaluate their own outputs, learn from analyzer errors, and adapt to your specific project conventions over time.

sessions.title: The new store in town: Let users access your app without leaving their AI Chat
sessions.description:
Nowadays, users often find it easier to stay in their AI chat instead of navigating to other apps. This means that the app you built might have better UX or functionality, but it's too far from the user's attention. 
The MCP Apps protocol that was shipped in Jan 2026, lets servers render interactive UIs inside Claude.ai, ChatGPT and others. This means that your app can live directly inside the user's AI chat. In this talk I'll show you how to transfer your app's widgets and functionality into an MCP App, without leaving the Flutter ecosystem. We'll walk through how MCP Apps work and their current limitations, as well as use Flutter Web to ship your Flutter code directly into Claude. We will also touch on how Gemini decided to structure their own solution.

sessions.title: Testing Mobile App Resilience: A Hands-On OWASP MASTG Workshop
sessions.description:
An 80-minute hands-on workshop where participants test and learn about mobile application resilience mechanisms, like root and emulator detection, anti-debugging, runtime instrumentation detection, integrity checks, and obfuscation in a purpose-built Android application. Every exercise is mapped to OWASP MASVS-RESILIENCE and MASTG v2, with equivalent iOS patterns and practical remediation guidance.

This workshop gives developers and security professionals an opportunity to learn mobile resilience testing directly from contributors who helped turn these mechanisms into focused, reproducible tests and runnable demos for OWASP MASTG v2.

The workshop setup guide for students can be found here: https://github.com/vulnit/mastg/releases/tag/v0.1.0. It is needed to perform the setup before the workshop.

sessions.title: The Defect-Driven Way to Migrate a 3M-User Android App to React Native
sessions.description:
In 2 months, we went from 3 weeks to 3 days per screen migrating a 3 million users app from native Android to React Native with AI. To achieve both high-quality code generation and sufficient velocity, my team and I drew inspiration from other engineering domains, notably systemic defect analysis.

As the Tech Lead for this project, in this talk I will:

- Describe our overall quality process: our aggressive definition of a defect, how we map weak points, and how we measure the improvements they bring.
- Provide concrete examples of issues encountered during the Android to React Native transformation and how this process helped us fix them.
- Show how it reshaped the developer's role — shifting them from coders to true engineers.

You'll leave with: a defect-driven framework you can apply, a methodology for measuring AI code quality at scale and a new lens on how AI changes what "senior engineer" means in 2026.

sessions.title: Offline First Mobile Apps with React Native & LegendState
sessions.description:
Your users don't care about your internet connection. They just want the app to work.

Offline-first is no longer a nice-to-have, it's a baseline expectation for any serious mobile product. But most React Native apps still crash, freeze, or show errors the moment connectivity drops.

In this talk, I'll show you how to build truly offline-first apps using React Native + LegendState v3, a blazing-fast state and sync library that makes local-first architecture surprisingly simple to implement.

You'll learn how to structure your data layer so your app works on day 1, with or without connectivity, and understand the real trade-offs I hit building production apps with this stack.

No more spinners. No more error screens. Just apps that work.

sessions.title: The bottleneck shift - why does the speed of CI/CD matter even more?
sessions.description:
AI agents now write iOS code directly, not just autocomplete it. That shifts the bottleneck: generating changes is no longer the constraint, validating them fast enough is. Most CI/CD pipelines were built for human commit cadence, not an agent proposing a new commit every few minutes. Mobile builds in particular were never designed to be hit dozens of times an hour by an autonomous loop.
This session covers what agentic coding demands from mobile infrastructure: near-instant build feedback, aggressive caching, and validation fast enough for an agent to act before context is lost. It looks at where traditional mobile CI/CD breaks down under this load, and what has to change to keep pace.
You'll see how Bitrise is addressing this with Build Hub, mobile-specific build infrastructure built to cut the time between an AI-generated change and a trustworthy result. A live demo walks through a real migration to Build Hub, including how fast and low-friction the move is.

sessions.title: How to enable everyone (including non-Engineers) to contribute code.
sessions.description:
This is the story on how we enabled more people to contribute to our Flutter App. This includes Backend Engineers, Designers and Product Managers.

This talk will cover our progress from going from 0 non-Flutter Contributors to having 30% of monthly contributors not be Flutter-First Contributors.

We will explain our Team Setups with a Platform Team and various Feature Teams contributing and will shine a light on this topic from engineering and management angles.

The talk will cover:

Codebase Architecture:
How to successfully structure code so getting started takes minutes, not days.

Psychological Safety:
How to build guardrails so beginners feel safe committing code and existing developers don't fear for their job.

The AI Enabler:
How we leverage AI tools to onboard people who have never coded before.

Metrics that Matter:
How to measure the success of cross-functional enablement.

sessions.title: Building an Immersive Concert Experience on Meta Quest
sessions.description:
What does it actually take for a mobile developer to build for Meta Quest?

I'm a mobile developer. Global Citizen XR is the first headset app I built from scratch, on my own: an immersive concert viewer on Quest, connected to a mobile product with millions of users.

This is the honest version of that process. How you actually get started with the Meta Spatial SDK. The tools that made it possible: Meta Spatial Editor, the Quest Simulator, ShapesXR, Nano Banana, MCP. And how far AI can carry a mobile developer into an unfamiliar platform.

sessions.title: swiftCon Community Meetup
sessions.description:
Location: Activity & Networking Area Level 2

Calling all iOS / Swift developers. Come by for a community meetup and get to know some new people in the community.

sessions.title: Break
Ditch Markdown. Build a Living Graph.
sessions.description:
Most teams I see are teaching their AI agents with Markdown files. `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, architecture notes, prompt snippets, rules in prose. I do it too. It works better than nothing. But it still feels like handing the agent a pile of notes and hoping it reads the right paragraph at the right time.

I spent the last months researching and prototyping a different substrate: a living graph where capabilities, use cases, tickets, decisions, scenarios, runtime facts and code are connected. Not docs about the project. Project knowledge as something queryable.

This talk is a field report from that research. I will show the direction that looks promising to me: a small Flutter app read through a living graph, with use cases opened as playable scenarios that also runs as tests. The question is not "how do we write better Markdown for agents?" The question is what changes when we stop using Markdown as the source of project memory.

sessions.title: From AI Features to AI employees: Designing Systems That Act
sessions.description:
Most valuable knowledge inside organizations is never documented. It lives in meetings, chats, and informal conversations, making it invisible and unusable. As a result, teams often end up solving the same problems multiple times without knowing it.

This fragmentation creates constant coordination work — and much of that knowledge is lost as people change roles or leave organizations.

In parallel, AI is moving beyond features into systems that can execute workflows — what we can think of as “AI employees”.

This shift changes how work happens, as systems start handling parts of workflows instead of just supporting them.

In this talk, I’ll explore what that means in practice — where it works, where it breaks, and what changes when integrating AI into real workflows.

Takeaways:

- Why fragmented knowledge creates hidden inefficiencies
- How AI employees change how workflows are executed
- What changes when systems start acting instead of waiting for input

sessions.title: Your Career GPS Has No Signal - What Happens After You Hit the Peak?
sessions.description:
In tech, we’re told that learning is everything. Learn fast. Learn continuously. Learn forever. But after a few years in the industry, many engineers discover something unexpected: You can learn constantly and still stay exactly where you are.

You switch technologies, adopt new patterns, fill gaps in your knowledge — and yet you feel like you’re moving in circles. Different tools. Same ceiling. This talk introduces the concept of the Skill Loop Trap — a subtle career plateau where your effort is enormous, your progress is visible, but your trajectory is flat.

We’ll explore why this happens even to strong performers:
1) when learning becomes a safety zone,
2) when “upskilling” replaces real growth,-
3) when career direction is missing,
4) and when you accidentally build a version of yourself that’s always improving… but never evolving.

sessions.title: Getting the Hole picture. Visualising maths in a fun way.
sessions.description: Mathematically, we are fascinated by the shape hidden within data—how points connect, form clusters, and create holes. In this talk, I will show how we can bring these abstract ideas to life visually using Kotlin. By interactively adjusting the connectivity radius, we can watch points merge into components, loops appear, and topological features emerge and disappear. Using Multik for computations, Kotlin DataFrame for handling CSV data, Kotlin Statistics for analysis, and Jetpack Compose for interactive visualizations, we can see the mathematics of connectedness unfold in real time. This talk focuses not just on the data itself but on the story of its shape, making topology tangible and interactive on mobile devices.

sessions.title: I Put Android in Charge of My Fish Tank (What Could Go Wrong?)
sessions.description:
Keeping fish alive is stressful, but what if Android handled the life support?

This session dives into a smart aquarium that collects sensor data, manages climate control, identifies fish via computer vision, and evaluates water toxicity using an on-device LLM, all driven by a native Android app.

Maintaining optimal aquatic conditions is high-stakes.
Tracking temperature, pH, conductivity, and turbidity lays the foundation for hardware automation. It’s a practical case study bridging raw hardware, scalable architecture, Edge AI, and delightful UI.

This session covers:
• Architecture: Interfacing sensors via MQTT and a Firebase backend.
• UI Polish: Pushing Jetpack Compose Canvas to build an interactive 2D digital twin.
• Climate Control: Securely managing high-voltage heaters and DC fans.
• ML & Edge AI: Deploying live fish identification and a compact Gemma 3 LLM via Google's LiteRT-LM for real-time telemetry analysis.

And voilà, the fish keep swimming!

sessions.title: Paths, Polygons, and Donuts - Building a Freehand Drawing Tool for Maps
sessions.description:
At Spoke, we build last-mile delivery tools for drivers, dispatchers, and retailers. One of our features lets drivers guide our route optimizer by grouping and ordering their stops with freehand lassoing. The first drawing tool only supported creating and undoing groups. Our users needed more control, so we built them a proper polygon editor.

In this talk, I'll share how finger-drags can become polygons on a map, and we'll dive into the tricky bits of editing them: self-intersecting loops, polygons with holes, and the machinery that decides which stops belong to a group. I'll cover finicky edge cases we caught, fixed, and screenshot-tested before release. There will be donuts!

By the end of the talk, you'll have a better grasp on:

- Turning freehand drawings into map polygons with Path and Path.Op
- How fill rules make or break boolean path operations
- Verifying drawing and grouping logic with screenshot tests

sessions.title: Debugging Android ANRs at Scale: Lessons from Building a Mobile Profiler
sessions.description:
Every Android developer knows the frustration: Your launch times are trending up, your ANR rate is spiking, and your Play Store rating is at risk. Your observability tools tell you what broke but not why.
Android’s ProfilingManager API opens the door to collecting production profiling data like stack samples, traces, and heap dumps directly on user devices. But raw Perfetto traces alone aren’t enough. The real challenge is turning that data into actionable insights.
In this talk, we’ll share how Datadog built a production profiling pipeline on top of the ProfilingManager API in collaboration with Google’s Android team. From collecting traces at scale to linking profiling data with real user sessions, surfacing flame graphs and call stacks, and pinpointing the methods behind slow launches or ANR spikes. We’ll walk through real debugging examples, preview what’s next for Android profiling, and show how these techniques can fit into your own debugging workflow.

sessions.title: Marionette MCP: Give AI control of your Flutter app
sessions.description:
What if your AI didn't just write your code, but actually used your Flutter app?

In this talk, I’ll show Marionette MCP, an open-source MCP server that lets AI agents connect to a running Flutter app and actually use it. The agent can understand the current UI, decide what to do next, and execute complete user flows, adjusting its actions as the app responds, rather than following predefined scripts.

This will be a demo-first session: less theory, more real world uses. We’ll start with simple interactions, move to a realistic user journey, and then show how Marionette can be extended to expose hidden runtime capabilities. By the end, you’ll have a clear mental model for when Marionette is useful, how it differs from code-focused tooling, and where it fits in a Flutter workflow.

sessions.title: Spatial Awareness with Flutter and UWB
sessions.description:
Ultra-Wideband is the technology behind experiences like precision finding, digital car keys, and keyless building access. It allows devices to understand not just that something is nearby, but roughly how far away it is and in which direction.

In this talk, I'll explore what spatial awareness means for Flutter apps and how UWB can move us beyond simple proximity. We'll look at real-world use cases like digital car keys, item tracking, and nearby device interaction, then walk through flutter_uwb, an open-source plugin I built to bring these capabilities to Flutter.

The session is built around a live demo using Flutter, two phones, and a UWB chip, showing distance and direction as first-class inputs and walking through the Dart code that produces them.

If you've ever wanted your app to know where a user actually is in physical space, not just whether they're nearby, this talk gives you the mental model, the API, and the code to start.

sessions.title: From Review Bottleneck to Auto-Merge: AI Code Review for Flutter Teams
sessions.description:
AI coding tools helped our team produce Flutter code faster, but pull requests started waiting longer for review. The bottleneck had moved from implementation to the PR queue.

In this talk, I'll show how we built an AI reviewer for our production Flutter app with GitHub Actions. I'll compare Cursor CLI, Copilot CLI and Claude routines explain why we chose our current setup, and show how it helps us review changes faster.

You'll see how we moved beyond generic comments by teaching the reviewer our Flutter architecture, conventions, best practices, Effective Dart rules, and team standards. I'll also show how a code graph gives it the context to review a change beyond the diff while reducing noise and token usage.

You'll leave knowing:

* Why AI coding moves the bottleneck to review
* How to teach it your Flutter and Dart practices
* How code graphs improve context and review quality
* Which PRs can be auto-approved, and when a human should stay involved

sessions.title: Why so serious? Fun, Action and Humor in Educational XR Games.
sessions.description:
Director & Game Designer Christoph Rasulis showcases the ideas, philosophy, and thought processes behind combining games and narratives with culture and education, as seen in his XR games "Green Guardians VR," "Carbon Dream$ Land," "Blautopf VR," and "Midnight Theater."

Discover how and why you can fight climate change in the future or even in your dreams, experience mysterious adventures in Germany's deepest cave system, or find yourself locked inside one of the most beautiful Baroque palaces at midnight.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M9tFbGEqGGg

sessions.title: New Architecture Without the Hype: What Fabric, TurboModules, JSI, and Hermes Mean for Developers
sessions.description:
React Native’s New Architecture is often explained with big words: Fabric, TurboModules, JSI, Hermes, concurrent rendering, synchronous layout, codegen. For many app developers, that can make the topic feel like something only native-module authors or C++ engineers need to understand.

This talk takes the opposite approach. It explains the New Architecture from the point of view of an application developer who wants to ship better React Native apps, make better technical decisions, and avoid misunderstanding where performance problems actually come from.

We will look at what the old bridge did, why it became a limitation, what JSI changes, how TurboModules affect native module access, what Fabric changes in rendering, and where Hermes fits into the runtime story. The goal is not to turn every React Native developer into a native internals expert. The goal is to give app developers a practical mental model so they know what matters, what does not, and when they need to care.

sessions.title: React Native is the best way to build desktop apps
sessions.description:
React Native is not a compromise, it's actually the best.

This will be a detailed exploration and discussion of benchmarks that show that React Native is faster than other desktop frameworks, the importance of native UI, and how to run mobile and desktop apps in Expo. 

I'll show you how to get started building React native desktop apps, the current status of React Native macOS and React Native Windows, and the latest developments in the RN desktop ecosystem

Plus at least two Legend announcements!

sessions.title: Make Your Apps Move! Awesome Animations with React Native ⚡️
sessions.description:
Get ready for some serious app magic! Animations, those delightful little touches that make things slide, bounce, and swirl, are often treated like an afterthought. We're usually too busy obsessing over “core features” or wringing our hands over performance and complexity, but we’re here to flip the script!

We’ll embark on a journey that starts from an explanation about what an animation really is and why they add so much value to our product, we’ll pass through the real world physics lying under the hood, and finally we’ll get our hands dirty building an Apple Wallet-inspired component — sleek, smooth and powered by react-native-reanimated!

By the end, you’ll see just how simple it is to breathe life into your app. So, grab your laptop, because we’re about to make your app move, and it’s going to be epic! 🌀🚀

sessions.title: Swift Beyond iOS: Sharing Product Logic with Android Without Sharing UI
sessions.description: Swift 6.3 made Swift on Android official, which changes the question for mobile teams. It is no longer "can this run?" but "what is worth sharing?" In this session I will walk through a pragmatic architecture: native SwiftUI on iOS, native Compose on Android, and Swift used for the product logic that should not be written twice. We will look at boundaries, async APIs, generated interop, local persistence, and team ergonomics. This is not about replacing Kotlin or forcing one architecture onto two platforms. It is about using Swift where it creates leverage, while keeping each app feeling native. You will leave with a practical model for deciding what to share, what to keep platform-specific, and what tradeoffs to expect.

sessions.title: DRI Your Career
sessions.description:
Tech workers: we used to be pampered Instagram raccoons — living for the aesthetic, optimising for comfort. Now we live in Toronto. And Toronto raccoons don't wait for someone to leave the lid off.
Your career is yours. It always was — you just didn't need to think about it. This talk is about thinking about it: taking stock of the power you have to shape your own trajectory, building yourself when no one's offering to do it for you, getting coachable enough to actually grow from hard moments, and knowing when it's time to move on before the job makes that decision for you.

sessions.title: Building a Native visionOS App with a Live Physiology Engine for Medical Training
sessions.description:
Most medical simulation VR runs pre-scripted scenarios on mobile chips with handheld controllers. This talk covers how I built a fully native visionOS app for a major health system that runs a real-time physiology engine, where patient vitals respond dynamically to every trainee action.

The physiology engine powering the simulation is a C++ library, which meant bridging native Swift and visionOS code with C++ in a clean, performant way. Every Swift developer working with legacy systems, game engines, scientific libraries, or any third-party C++ dependency will be able to take this knowledge and apply it directly to their own projects.

The app uses native hand tracking and speech recognition that validates verbal announcements at each step to enforce AHA ACLS protocol compliance in real time. With limited documentation and few people who had tackled anything like this before, the Swift and visionOS community was one of the most important resources throughout the entire build.

sessions.title: Between Hype and Hate: AI Without Deskilling the Team
sessions.description: "Use AI for everything or you're finished" versus "AI is just autocomplete for cheaters" — both positions are tiring, and both are wrong. This talk is the pragmatic middle: how a real engineering team produces code with AI day to day. I'll walk through everyday AI-assisted coding (where it earns its keep, and where we keep humans firmly driving), generative tooling we built (plain English to live BigQuery charts that replaced one-off dashboards), and an agentic pipeline that triages Sentry errors and drafts a fix but deliberately stops at a pull request, never a merge. The throughline is AI proposes, humans dispose — but the part most talks skip is the 'without deskilling the team' bit: avoiding review fatigue, over-trust, and the morale hit of feeling replaceable. You'll leave with a practical way to adopt AI on your team without the FOMO and without eroding the craft or the people, plus a checklist for where to draw your own automate-versus-gate line.

sessions.title: “Can’t Reproduce”: Reconstructing an iOS Bug After the Screenshot
sessions.description:
“Can’t reproduce” is the most expensive phrase in mobile development. Every team has lost days chasing a bug where the screenshot lacked the logs, the logs lacked the network request and nobody remembers which build it happened on.

In this roundtable, we’ll explore how mobile teams reconstruct the context around a bug from signals scattered across an application. What information should we capture when something goes wrong? How can we correlate UI state, logs and network activity into a consistent snapshot? How do we do this without affecting performance? And where is the line between useful diagnostic data and user privacy?

We’ll share approaches, tools, production lessons and failures, with the goal of leaving with practical ideas for making the next “can’t reproduce” bug easier to diagnose.

sessions.title: GamesCapitalBerlin Reception - get your invitation at Level 2 booth 54
sessions.description: GamesCapitalBerlin Reception hosted by the Berlin Senate Department for Economic Affairs, Energy and Public Enterprises, Thurs. 5pm to 6:30pm - get your invitation at Level 2 booth 54

sessions.title: Registration & Check-In
Just One More Prompt: Why Agentic Coding Hooks Us
sessions.description:
Coding agents have made starting things almost effortless. 

Finishing them has not got any easier. 

While one agent thinks, we open another, then another, and the phone brings the next session to dinner, to the weekend and to bed. 
Many of us now have more projects underway than ever, and fewer of them done.

This talk looks at why. 

Drawing on Natasha Dow Schüll's research with machine gamblers in Las Vegas, it maps the mechanics that keep people playing (unpredictable rewards, near misses, the bonus round, betting on every line) onto the everyday experience of agentic coding, and examines what that pull costs us in fulfilment, energy and attention.

Then it turns to what works. 
Three practical techniques, adapted from gambling harm-reduction and social-media research, help developers and teams set limits before a session starts, keep the agents out of their pocket, and decide which w tools deserve their time. 
Less spinning, more finishing.

sessions.title: The Lord of Collection Functions - The Fellowship of Kotlin
sessions.description:
A darkness has awoken in Center-earth, an ancient evil is reaching out of the shadows of every corrupt codebase, intent on bringing destruction & algorithmic oppression to all that call this world home. That my dear friends, is where you come in…

Join the Kotlin fellowship & Together, we will explore the expansive array of Kotlin Collection Functions; these allow us to perform useful tasks on collections, like Set, Map, & List. Enabling us to transform, check, analyse, & aggregate the contents of the collection.

If we survive, you will take with you a deep comprehension of all of these functions (and many more), expanding your technical repertoire, to help you overcome any complex coding challenge (even the treacherous Advent of Code trials).

So, are you ready to fight the sinister Lord For-ron & trade imperative code for the elegant power of functional programming? Prepare for a perilous adventure—join the fellowship…

The fate of Center-earth is in your hands…

sessions.title: Burn down the bridges!
sessions.description:
Over 5 years of iterating, research and development have led to what Nitro is today: a fundamental building block for modern Margelo- and community open-source projects which powers thousands of apps worldwide.

VisionCamera's latest release (V5) took Nitro to a new level and demonstrates what's possible: full type-safety, close-to-zero overhead, instance-based APIs, and full testability with Harness.

In this talk, I'll go over the past 5 years in react-native, the current state, as well as the future in the Nitroverse.

sessions.title: We Have the Tech, Now What? Foundation Models, Siri, and the Reality of Enterprise AI
sessions.description:
The arrival of foundation models and next-generation system intelligence has changed the conversation across the Apple ecosystem. Yet, for commercial engineering teams and product leaders, the immediate question remains: we have this remarkable technology, but how do we turn it into real, sustainable value?

In this Friday keynote panel, industry leaders and platform specialists come together to cut through the hype. We will debate the practical realities of adopting foundation models and Siri-driven capabilities inside commercially focused organisations. From architectural trade-offs and privacy considerations to user experience design, this session examines how teams are moving past simple novelty features to build tools that genuinely move the needle.

sessions.title: A Decade of Lessons: Wins, Fails, and What They Taught Me
sessions.description:
I've led teams and built products used by millions and spent all of my career learning — often the hard way — what it actually takes to scale engineering teams and lead people. I'm still learning and would love for others to also learn from my mistakes and capitalise on my wins fuelled by this sincere and hopefully practical talk.
I'll try to interactively showcase how to make better leadership decisions, scale teams, hire effectively, give meaningful feedback, execute strategy, and turn failures into practical lessons.

sessions.title: Human Bingo (without cards)
sessions.description:
Location: Activity & Networking Area Level 2

Human Bingo (without cards) – facilitator calls out statements (e.g. 'has had an app featured in the App Store', 'uses Flutter', 'hates push notifications'); participants find matching people

sessions.title: Break
Practical On-Device Al: Turning Edge Al into Real Features
sessions.description:
​Building a solid mental model of Edge AI and hybrid patterns is the first step toward transforming UI state and structured data into reliable AI inputs. This session moves past the hype to show how on-device AI can power actual user-facing features while maintaining low latency, privacy, and predictable behavior by keeping sensitive data off the cloud.

​We will break down the engineering trade-offs, context design, and safety mechanisms required to close the agentic loop. You’ll leave with practical proof-of-concepts for building AI features that are useful, stable, and ready for production.

sessions.title: Inside a Real-Time Voice Agent: The Sub-Second Latency Budget and How to Defend It
sessions.description:
Most AI features can hide a slow response behind a spinner. A voice agent cannot: a reply that arrives a beat late feels broken, so the whole pipeline must fit inside a roughly one-second budget. 

This session opens up a self-hosted voice agent on a provider-swappable pipeline (speech-to-text, an LLM, text-to-speech, over LiveKit and Twilio) and treats latency as the design problem it is. 

Where the time goes: STT finalization, LLM time-to-first-token, TTS time-to-first-audio, network and telephony. The three techniques that bought back the most time without changing the model: pre-warming STT and TTS connections, routing predictable turns down static paths that skip the LLM, and caching the stable prompt prefix. 

And the decisions that outlast any model: keeping each layer swappable, and knowing when to drop the cascaded pipeline for a speech-to-speech model. 

You leave able to budget, measure, and defend the latency of a real-time AI feature.

sessions.title: Native vs. Cross-Platform: The Future of Mobile App Development
sessions.description: The mobile landscape is evolving faster than ever. From native Android and iOS to cross-platform powerhouses like Flutter and React Native, developers are faced with an abundance of choices and unprecedented fragmentation. In this cross-framework panel discussion, experts from Android, Flutter, Swift, and React Native will debate the future of mobile app development. We'll explore the trade-offs between native performance and cross-platform efficiency, the rise of AI in coding, and how emerging tech like XR is reshaping user expectations.

sessions.title: The Next Software Crisis Won't Be About Writing Code
sessions.description:
AI generates code faster than ever. But thirty years of software crises tell the same story: every time we confuse producing with building, we lose meaning, and every time, a movement brings it back. Agile restored the why, Craftsmanship and XP the how (TDD, clean code), DDD and Clean Architecture the what (modeling the domain, not stacking features). Each time, we rediscovered that the real value of our craft lies beyond code production.
Today, AI pushes us toward a new crisis: not technical, but architectural. When code is nearly free, "good enough" becomes invisible and technical debt compounds at the speed of light.
Drawing from 20 years of building software, creating the Koin Kotlin Framework, and running Kotzilla, I'll show why architecture and domain modeling have never mattered more. Then, using dependency injection as an example, I'll walk you through architecture observability to give both developers and AI agents the context to make decisions that hold up.

sessions.title: OpenTelemetry on Android: From black box to X‑Ray
sessions.description:
On the backend, OpenTelemetry is quickly becoming the default for observability but on Android, it’s still uncommon to see something else than Firebase or any vendor-locked solution. Many teams don’t know where to start or whether it’s “ready” for mobile use. The result: a production app that behaves like a black box, with only crash reports and a few logs to rely on when things go wrong.

In this talk, we’ll turn a typical Android app into an “X‑ray friendly” client using OpenTelemetry. We’ll explore the available OpenTelemetry SDKs, wire them into a simple observability stack, and instrument a realistic user flow end‑to‑end. Along the way, we’ll discuss maturity of the tooling, and how it compares to popular mobile APM solutions. Attendees will learn concrete patterns and pitfalls so they can evaluate and adopt OpenTelemetry on Android with confidence.

sessions.title: Build a Coding Agent to Understand Coding Agents
sessions.description:
Coding agents can search a repository, modify files, run commands, inspect failures, and repeat until a task is complete. But what is actually happening between your prompt and the resulting code?

In this talk, we will build a small coding agent from the ground up and use it to examine the core pieces behind tools such as Claude Code or your coding agent tool of choice. We will look at how an agent constructs context, exposes tools to a model, runs an agent loop, handles tool results, and decides what information should remain in the conversation.

The goal is not to replace mature coding agents. It is to develop a practical mental model for evaluating them. By understanding their underlying architecture, Android developers can better diagnose poor results, configure their workflows, and decide whether a features of their favorite coding agents is essential, useful, or unnecessary complexity.

sessions.title: Prompting for Performance: Writing Butter-Smooth Jetpack Compose in the AI Era
sessions.description:
AI assistants can easily spit out 200 lines of flawless, compiling Jetpack Compose UI from a single prompt. It feels like magic—until you run it on a mid-range device, start scrolling, and hit massive jank.

The open secret of 2026? AI models are great at writing code that works, but notoriously bad at understanding the Jetpack Compose rendering pipeline. They pass raw state instead of lambdas and miss optimization tropes. Our jobs are shifting: we are no longer just code writers; we are performance auditors.

This talk shatters old optimization mindsets to view Compose performance through an AI-assisted lens. You'll learn:

AI Blindspots: How to spot LLM-generated recomposition traps in code reviews.

Bypassing Phases: Forcing AI to defer state reads using lambda modifiers to skip straight to the Drawing phase.

The Prompt Audit Loop: Feeding Perfetto traces and Macrobenchmark data back into AI for surgical fixes.

Stop fighting AI—learn how to audit it for butter-smooth UI.

sessions.title: AI Observability for LLM-Powered Flutter Apps
sessions.description:
Most Flutter apps today are LLM-powered, and it's often just a few steps to bring an agent into the mix. But once your app starts calling models like Gemini or OpenAI, debugging becomes fundamentally different. Unlike traditional APIs, LLMs are non-deterministic, making it difficult to understand why responses change or costs increase.

This talk explores practical ways to add telemetry and observability to AI-powered Flutter apps (that is using cloud backends like Supabase). 

Some of the things we'll cover:
- Which AI metrics matter: cost, latency (and why percentiles beat averages), token usage, errors, and output quality
- How telemetry helps you monitor, debug, and improve LLM-powered features
- Hosted AI observability platforms like Langfuse: tracing, evaluations, dashboards, pricing, and alternatives

By the end, you'll have a practical framework for monitoring, debugging, and improving your LLM-powered features.

sessions.title: Evolution of flutter_gemma: From a Simple Wrapper to a Cross-Platform AI Engine
sessions.description:
flutter_gemma started as a thin MediaPipe wrapper for running Gemma on Android and iOS. Today it's a full on-device AI platform: 6 platforms, 2 inference engines, multimodal support, function calling for local agents, and on-device RAG with vector search — featured by Google at I/O 2026.
This talk walks through that evolution via real engineering decisions. How adding Web forced sealed classes over string URLs. How desktop went from a Kotlin/JVM gRPC server to running LiteRT-LM directly via dart:ffi — dropping a bundled JRE and cutting engine startup from ~15s to ~2s. How the Strategy and Adapter patterns let us add a second engine without a rewrite. How we built on-device RAG on a Qdrant vector store that runs identically on mobile and in-browser via WASM. Plus real bugs and fixes, from Web hot-restart crashes to iOS Simulator vision-model limits.
Minimum theory, maximum code, diagrams, and stories of how it broke and why it looks like this now.

sessions.title: Flutter and Architecting Multi-Windows and Adaptive Apps for present and Next Gen OSes
sessions.description:
Multi-window experiences are no longer a niche feature — they're becoming the standard on Android with desktop windowing, foldables, and external displays, and on iPadOS with Stage Manager and its new windowing engine. Flutter developers who still architect around a single, fixed-size screen are already falling behind.

This session introduces the core concepts behind building multi-instance, adaptive Flutter apps. We'll cover how Flutter engine groups enable lightweight parallel instances, how to manage state across windows, and how to design layouts that respond gracefully across all displays — from split-screen panes to a tablet paired with an external monitor.

This is a practical primer: what multi-window and adaptive layout really mean today, why they matter for Flutter apps, and where to start when architecting for this new reality. You'll leave with a clear mental model and a concrete starting point.

sessions.title: Stability, Performance and Optimization in (Unity) Mobile Games
sessions.description:
Building a great mobile game is hard—keeping it stable, fast, and scalable throughout its lifecycle is another challenge entirely. In this Unity-focused session, we’ll share practical strategies across three key areas:

Profiling & Optimization: Use Unity’s CPU, GPU, and Memory Profilers alongside native tools to enforce FPS budgets and manage assets effectively with Addressables.

Technical Health: Discover why proactive maintenance — like staying ahead of engine and Gradle dependencies — is crucial. We'll discuss balancing technical debt with feature development to prevent future dependency nightmares.

Monitoring & Response: Track real-world crashes and ANRs using Crashlytics custom logs and Google Play Console. We’ll also introduce our “geo release” strategy: a targeted, low-risk Android rollout for validating risky SDK updates before launching globally.

Developers will leave with actionable processes for delivering consistently smooth mobile experiences.

sessions.title: When "Encrypted" Isn't: Protecting On-Device ML Models in Mobile Apps
sessions.description:
Ship a model to a phone and you've shipped it to whoever owns the phone. Teams know this, so they encrypt the model on disk and move on. That's not protection. It's a speed bump.

I'll show why, with an SDK I took apart and disclosed: Cambridge Mobile Telematics' SensorFlow, which rides inside insurance apps. Inside is an encrypted PyTorch crash classifier. Its verdict feeds premium pricing and claims, so the model is worth hiding, and the encryption is the whole defense.

I pulled the cleartext model out without rooting a device and without Frida. The method is almost dull, which is the point: emulate the SDK's own native library, libsensorflow.so, in software with a Unicorn harness, and let the app's decryption routine hand me the plaintext in emulator memory. The app unlocks its own secret.

sessions.title: React Native Brownfield deep dive: how RN moves in to native applications
sessions.description:
Many mobile teams reach a point where maintaining duplicate implementations across iOS and Android becomes unsustainable. React Native promises a unified approach, but a full rewrite is rarely an option - in practice, most migration efforts are discarded as infeasible. RN Brownfield is the solution - a set of tools for embedding RN apps in native apps as self-contained libraries, which allows for a gradual adoption of React Native in native applications.

In this talk, we will do a deep dive into the internals of Brownfield: how RN apps are packaged, what tooling is needed (nav, state), why we had to implement a custom Gradle Plugin, a few things about real-life problems with transitive dependency handling, SO stripping, how Hermes V1 is handled on Android, how prebuilt RN core on iOS (0.81+) is handled with backwards compatibility, SPM support, and how integration of this complex library with Expo is handled using just 1 line of code for the end user, thanks to an Expo config plugin.

sessions.title: React Native: Performance Analysis & Optimization
sessions.description:
Performance can become a serious challenge as React Native applications grow. But before you optimize the code, you need to understand what causes the problem.

Based on the engineering patterns we use at Software Mansion for large-scale products, this hands-on workshop teaches you how to diagnose performance problems in React Native applications. We will use tools such as Flashlight, the React Native Performance panel, and the Profiler to identify the root causes of UI lag and understand where performance issues come from.

Key Takeaways:
- Use the React Native Profiler to identify unnecessary re-renders and expensive component work.
- Use the Performance panel to find heavy JavaScript operations.
- Use Flashlight to measure CPU and memory use.
- Compare FlatList, FlashList, and Legend List using real performance data.
- Build a clear process for diagnosing performance problems before deciding how to fix them.

sessions.title: Compiling a real-world CLI tool to native with Static Hermes
sessions.description: Most solutions that "compile" JavaScript actually package an application together with a JavaScript engine. The code is still interpreted or JIT-compiled at runtime. Static Hermes takes a different approach: it ahead-of-time compiles the application itself into native machine code. Using the Flow bundler as a case study—a substantial Node.js application that relies on Node APIs, Babel, and even a WebAssembly module—we'll explore how a real-world JavaScript application can be transformed into a single native executable. Along the way, we'll discuss the technical challenges, the tradeoffs, and what this means for the future of JavaScript tooling and deployment.

sessions.title: Building a Real-Time Video Synthesizer in Swift & Metal
sessions.description:
What else can an iOS app be? Chromatose is my answer: a real-time, modular video synthesizer that turns an iPhone into a GPU-driven instrument, running custom Metal shaders at 60fps, even on a five-year-old device. It's a genuinely new category of app, and building it meant taking Swift somewhere it rarely goes.

I designed, built, and shipped it solo. This session is a candid tour: a performance-critical render loop, a custom Metal pipeline, and a deeply custom UI where the usual frameworks stop helping. I'll share the architecture that held up, the parts I rewrote more than once, and the platform realities (Apple API black boxes, SwiftUI/UIKit gaps, GPU performance) that tutorials skip.

The bigger idea: the techniques that make a video synth fast and maintainable (custom rendering, value-type architecture, document versioning) are what let you invent something new on a platform millions already carry. You don't need to care about graphics to use them.

sessions.title: Designing a design system for the future
sessions.description:
A design system is the organized set of components, constants, and layout structures behind your app. Building one early speeds up feature work, keeps your UI consistent across every target you ship, and gets real components into stakeholders' hands long before the features around them exist.

We'll package your components as a SwiftUI package and version it into your CI flow, then get into the parts that make it feel effortless: typography and color that live in one place, styles that let a component say what it is instead of how it looks, and previews good enough that a designer can review in them. Then we package it into an app to put right into their hands.

sessions.title: Think Local: Magic at your fingertips
sessions.description:
The original iPhone felt magical because it made software feel physical, immediate and personal. For many of us, that was the moment we wanted to build for mobile.

Today AI has the potential to create that same kind of magic again but only if it feels native: fast, private, available, and close to the user.

In this talk, I’ll explore how on-device AI is becoming practical on Apple platforms: from Apple Intelligence and Foundation Models to Core ML, Core AI, Accelerate, and others. I’ll share lessons from deploying an actual on-device text-to-speech model in the ElevenReader app, including model packaging, performance optimization, latency, memory, battery, and model IP protection.

Just as personal computers moved computing away from mainframes, increasingly powerful devices and increasingly optimized models may move many AI experiences away from server-side inference. The cloud will not disappear but the most magical mobile AI experiences may be the ones that run right in your hand.

sessions.title: Data vs. Gut in React Native: Shipping Features When Metrics and Instincts Clash
sessions.description:
Every team says they want to be data-driven, but most product decisions still happen somewhere between a dashboard and a gut feeling. We ship features because a metric looked promising, or we ignore the metric entirely because we believed in the idea anyway. Neither approach is wrong all the time, but almost nobody talks honestly about how these decisions actually get made in real React Native teams.

This roundtable brings together developers and product-minded engineers to compare real experiences with A/B testing, feature flags, and rollout decisions in React Native apps. We will talk about the experiments that clearly worked, the ones that quietly failed, and the moments when data pointed one way but the team shipped the other anyway. We will also get honest about the hidden cost of experimentation itself: the extra engineering overhead, the slower release cycles, and the times testing infrastructure created more confusion than clarity.

sessions.title: Making XR multiuser simple: from turn-key helpers components, to smartglasses emerging communication
sessions.description:
This session will provide an overview of how to quickly bootstrap a multi-user XR application, while also exploring the unique smart glasses capabilities that can enhance shared experiences. 
It will cover:
- Multiplayer capabilities that can be easily deployed using Photon SDKs  and helper add-ons
- How to architect your XR application to seamlessly integrate multiplayer features  and to build cross-platform applications for XR headset, smartphones, webGL, or smartglasses
- A focus on new communication capabilities offered by smartglasses, such as streaming a user's view to any device, from a WebGL page to a full-fledged XR application

sessions.title: Break
Teaching My AI to Remember: Building an AI Wiki for Coding Agents
sessions.description:
AI coding agents are becoming increasingly powerful, but writing better prompts is only one part of working effectively with them. As projects grow, the bigger challenge becomes helping agents understand context: past decisions, debugging history, architecture choices, and lessons learned over time.

Inspired by Andrej Karpathy’s llm-wiki concept, I experimented with building my own AI wiki for coding agents using automation, hooks, and documentation workflows. I wanted to explore a question many developers are starting to face: how can we help AI assistants build on accumulated knowledge instead of starting from scratch?

In this talk, I will share what worked, what broke, and what I learned from building this workflow — from capturing useful context to understanding the limitations of relying on AI-generated knowledge.

As AI changes how we build software, managing context might become one of the most important skills in collaborating effectively with coding agents.

sessions.title: The AI Knowledge Cliff: What happens when your stack is newer than the training data
sessions.description: Everyone is shipping faster with AI, but there's a hidden failure mode: what happens when your framework is newer than the AI's data? Based on my experience shipping a production app on .NET MAUI 9, I'll show you how AI confidently generates perfect-looking code that’s subtly wrong for new APIs. This is a structural problem every developer will face, whether on SwiftUI, Jetpack Compose, or any new tech. The model's confidence doesn't drop when its knowledge does. Join this session to learn how to detect the "knowledge cliff" and the specific workflow changes that let you keep the AI benefits without the hidden tech debt.

sessions.title: Waking Up Safely: Reducing Background Wake Locks with Android 17
sessions.description:
How many times have you checked your app's battery telemetry and winced at background wake locks? For over a decade, exact background timing meant pairing AlarmManager with a PendingIntent. It works, but it brings a messy tail of heavy-handed intents and battery blame. Shouldn't there be a lighter way?

Android 17 introduces a platform shift: a variant of setExactAndAllowWhileIdle() that accepts a direct OnAlarmListener. But what about Doze mode? And more importantly, how do you architect a unified dispatch engine that leverages this optimization on Android 17 while gracefully falling back to traditional broadcast lifecycles on older Android versions?

In this talk, we’ll move past the basic method signature and dive into the mechanics of low-power background execution. We will look at how to safely bridge the cross-version architectural gap, handle edge-case process terminations, and restructure your sync engines to keep both operating system and batteries happy.

sessions.title: From Open Hardware to Open App: Building a Kotlin Multiplatform Device Companion
sessions.description:
As apps increasingly interact with physical devices, developers need to understand systems beyond APIs, including firmware constraints, unreliable connections, and cross-platform integration challenges. Fully open ecosystems are still rare, which makes it difficult to learn how these layers truly interact in practice. This session offers a real-world example of how mobile, embedded, and open-source development can work together in a maintainable and scalable way.

In this session, we explore the complete stack behind the Teufel MYND speaker: 
open hardware
https://github.com/teufelaudio/mynd-hardware
open firmware
https://github.com/teufelaudio/mynd-firmware
and an open-source Kotlin Multiplatform app
https://github.com/teufelaudio/mynd-app

We’ll walk through how these layers connect, from firmware capabilities to Bluetooth communication to reactive UI—and how we structured the app to stay maintainable across platforms and devices.

sessions.title: Who killed my app? - An Android murder mystery
sessions.description:
Diagnosing a sudden stoppage of your app is complicated. The circumstances surrounding a lifecycle-related race condition or a process death can be mysterious. What are the prime suspects that can kill an Android app? There are important differences between things like force-stopping an app and swiping it out from the Recents, and simulating each termination during debugging is not straightforward. Configuration changes after sunset are strangely more likely, and you need to prepare for the user revoking permissions. Do you know who the dreaded Viking Killer is?

In this lightning talk, we will unravel the tangled web of misconceptions and investigate the eight primary ways your app can be terminated. I will show survival techniques and share my most trusted debugging practices. We won’t stop at low-memory situations, and the takeaway won’t just be to use ViewModels.

sessions.title: Adapt or Outdated: Flutter is the Ultimate Engine for the Agentic Era
sessions.description:
We are moving beyond apps that just display data to apps that act as host environments for AI Agents. In this high-intensity session, I will explain why Flutter is uniquely positioned to lead the "Agentic Era."

Forget the hype; let’s look at the technical reality. Flutter’s architecture allows for seamless integration of agentic workflows without the need for overly complex tooling. We will explore how to leverage existing packages to build A2A (Agent-to-Agent) communication and dynamic A2UI (Agent-to-UI) updates that feel native and responsive.

I will demonstrate a clean architectural pattern that connects Gemini logic with Flutter’s reactive UI, proving that you can deploy a sophisticated agentic system faster than in any other framework.

Key Takeaways:

The A2UI Pattern: How to let agents manipulate the UI directly and safely.

Lightweight Integration: Using the Flutter ecosystem to handle Agent-to-Agent orchestration.

sessions.title: Quiet on set… rolling... action! From eco-volunteering to promoting my side project in Australia!
sessions.description:
How can an eco-volunteering mission on a paradise atoll transform a mobile developer and spark a project that travels the world?

From the beaches of Tetiaroa, where I monitored sea turtle nesting sites, to Australia, where my app “We Spot Turtles!” was featured in #WeArePlay by Google, this talk tells an unexpected journey.

It’s above all a human story: a side project born from passion, built between freelance missions, and growing into a concrete tool for marine conservation.

I’ll share how to turn technical skills into impact, the doubts along the way, and the importance of community.

If you’re a developer seeking purpose, or curious how a side project can take you further than expected, this talk is for you.

sessions.title: Semantics in, nothing out: Flutter's hidden accessibility regression
sessions.description:
Your Flutter semantics are correct. Your iOS app works. Your tests pass. Then TalkBack on Android says nothing. Same code. Different reality.

In November 2025, Flutter 3.38.0 broke the Android accessibility bridge. The bridge translating Flutter semantics into native Android accessibility changed its behavior. No errors. No warnings. Just broken accessibility.

This talk is for senior developers learning Flutter's accessibility internals:

1. How the accessibility bridge works between Flutter semantics and Android/iOS trees
2. Where it broke: The specific change that silently removed backward compatibility
3. Why you didn't catch it: Tests verified semantics while the platform layer ignored them
4. The invisibility trap: Platform parity hides obvious regressions
5. What you need to know: Your Flutter semantics might be broken

You'll understand more about cross-platform accessibility and why your test coverage may have a blind spot.

Based on a real production post-mortem.

sessions.title: Shell Is All You Need: Predictable Flutter Dev Environments with Nushell
sessions.description:
As Flutter projects grow, the development environment often becomes part of the problem: different tool versions, scattered scripts no one knows how to use, CI-only commands, undocumented setup steps, together leading to "works on my machine" bugs.

The more flavors, tests, generators, secrets, and release pipelines you add, the harder it becomes to keep local development and CI aligned.

Why attend:

This talk explores how Nushell and Nix/Devbox can create a shared, predictable automation layer for developers, CI runners, and AI coding agents.

You’ll learn:

- How to make tool versions and setup more reproducible & speed up the onboarding process
- How to turn complex workflows into readable commands
- How to reduce gaps between local and CI execution
- How to enable humans and AI agents run the same project tasks

Best for teams with growing automation needs.

sessions.title: Reconstructing Telegram: Time Travel Debugging Meets AI on Android
sessions.description:
Telegram is one of the world's most security-sensitive Android applications, which makes it an ideal case study. In this talk, we show how the combination of full-system Time Travel Debugging (TTD) and AI reconstructed Telegram's processing from a real 7 billion-instruction execution trace, without source code, hooks, or prior instrumentation.
We explain how full-system TTD records an application's complete execution, including its interactions with Android internals, turning transient runtime behavior into persistent data that both humans and AI can explore. We then show how this static representation lets AI overcome the context-window limitations that normally constrain debugger-driven analysis. Through the Telegram investigation, attendees will see how this approach exposes transitions, framework interactions, and low-level system behavior that conventional debugging often misses. Following that, they will see how this method extends to QEMU-based full-system emulation on iOS.

sessions.title: Catching up on Node-API for React Native
sessions.description:
Node-API for React Native is an alternative to JavaScript Interface (JSI) to call JavaScript from native code as well as a new auto-linked native module system, comparable to TurboModules.

In this talk I want to briefly introduce the project again (to frame why I feel it's important to our community) and then catch up on the progress the project has made since then (internal changes as well as advancements in Hermes and the Node.js project) and provide a couple of technical deep dives into key pieces of the architecture.

sessions.title: Crafting Fluid Animations Across Apple Platforms
sessions.description:
Great motion design doesn’t just make an app look good. It guides users, provides contextual feedback, and turns your product into a memorable experience.

In this talk, we’ll explore the fundamental principles of effective motion design and how you can apply them to your apps. We’ll peek under the hood of animations, learn why they sometimes don't do what you’d expect, and how to use the framework to precisely express your intent. We’ll also explore how Swift’s powerful language features let you push the boundaries of what’s possible. Whether you're fixing a janky transition or building delightful interactions from scratch, you’ll leave equipped with new tools and a deeper understanding of animation craft in Swift.

sessions.title: Your Idle Game Economy Is a Dependency Graph. Treat It Like One.
sessions.description: In an idle game, everything derives from everything: turret level feeds DPS, DPS affects enemy HP, kills feed income, income feeds upgrade costs, and all should consider the desired progression speed. One tap ripples through dozens of derived values, and both common fixes (recompute everything, or hand-wired update calls) fall apart as the economy grows. The third option: model your stats as an explicit dependency graph. Declare base properties and calculators; when an input changes, only the affected subgraph recomputes, exposed as reactive properties. One idea, a working open-source Unity package, 20 minutes.

sessions.title: Break
Securing Agentic AI with PyTorch: Threat Modeling & LLM Red Teaming in Practice
sessions.description:
Agentic AI systems are evolving from single-model assistants into distributed multi-agent ecosystems. These architectures introduce risks that traditional threat modeling often misses, including privilege escalation across agents, trust-boundary collapse, cascading failures, and resource starvation.

This session presents a practical methodology for threat modeling Multi-Agent Systems (MAS) using the MAESTRO framework (Multi-Agent Environment, Security, Threat, Risk, and Outcome). Rather than focusing only on prompt injection or model misuse, the talk shows how to analyze cross-layer risks created by agent autonomy, non-deterministic behavior, inter-agent communication, tool use, and chained authorization.

The session is aimed at application security engineers, security architects, AI engineers, and threat modelers who want a repeatable approach to securing next-generation autonomous systems.

sessions.title: The End of "Good Enough": How AI Forces Us to Rethink Sprints, MVPs, and Engineering Prioritisation
sessions.description:
Modern software delivery practices such as the two-week sprint, the Minimum Viable Product, and strict backlog prioritisation were built on one assumption: software is slow and expensive to build. AI is rapidly eroding that constraint.

In this talk, Vahid Panjganj, a software engineer, and Nadav Mordechai, a product leader, challenge delivery practices the industry has treated as gospel for decades. From the engineering side, AI-assisted development is compressing work that once took weeks into hours, raising questions about velocity, estimation, and prioritisation. If building is no longer the bottleneck, why deprioritise features?

From the product side, this shift challenges the idea of the Minimum Viable Product. MVPs were designed for a world of scarcity. When products can be built and tested in days, “minimum viable” may no longer be the right strategy.

Together, they explore what still matters and what product and engineering leaders need to rethink now.

sessions.title: Laugh Session / Laughter Yoga
sessions.description:
Location: Activity & Networking Area Level 2

Laugh Session / Laughter yoga – guided laughter, usually awkward at first, then liberating

sessions.title: Oh, that UI looks dope … wish it wasn’t so hard to read tho
sessions.description:
Did you ever struggle with reading a piece of text in a game? Typography is still a crucial mediator for information in digital media—be it a text log, an item description or just a menu option.  In this seminar I want to explore interface design from a typographic angle: What makes your typography shine, how to optimize for readability, what are the unique challenges text faces in gaming environments, and what to consider when adapting to mobile devices.

The seminar is suitable for people already interested in typography, as well as those who have not considered type as a possible obsession yet.

sessions.title: Building a Multiplatform Window Manager for Fun
sessions.description:
Window managers are the default way of interfacing with desktop computers, giving users freedom in how they work and multitask, letting them lay out apps in ways most comfortable for them. Wouldn’t it be fun to bring that paradigm into Compose Multiplatform apps?

In this talk, we’ll build a prototype for window management inside a Compose Multiplatform app together, adapting key ideas from window managers and replicating some iconic late-2000s aesthetic along the way.

We’ll explore architectural challenges relevant to broader development tasks: ViewModelStoreOwners, lifecycle events, coroutine scopes and their lifetimes, navigation patterns, and building UI for resizable surfaces, among others.

Through the power of CMP & KMP, we’ll see it all in action across platforms, from Android tablets to iPads to Desktop.

By the end, you’ll understand how flexible Compose Multiplatform lets you be when building UIs, and gain a deeper grasp of key framework-level architecture concepts.

sessions.title: Before Compose: A Case Study in Building Fast Android UI Preview
sessions.description:
Meta’s Android codebase works as a monorepo. Before our area was ready for Compose, teams still had to solve the same daily problem: slow builds made UI iteration painful.

This talk is a case study in building fast preview tooling for Litho, Meta’s declarative Android UI framework. During 2023, we started from a single goal — “change UI code and see the result quickly inside Android Studio” — and split one big problem into a chain of technical challenges: compiling changed Java/Kotlin code, spinning up a dedicated local server, sending payloads to a sandboxed mobile activity, and rendering the result back through an IDE plugin. The resulting solution reduced preview time from minutes to seconds.

Attendees will learn how web-stack development techniques can be adapted for mobile tooling, and how to stitch compiler, server, app, and IDE pieces into one practical developer workflow.

sessions.title: Crafting delightful apps your users will love
sessions.description:
Jetpack Compose gives us powerful APIs to craft interfaces, but standard implementations often miss opportunities to create truly delightful user experiences. I will demonstrate how thoughtful animation layering transforms a basic gesture into something that feels polished and intuitive.
We'll build a complete slide-to-dismiss component, exploring:

- Tap animations using spring physics for natural, responsive feedback
- Drag gestures with fluid but interruptible motion
