- Visual feedback systems that guide users, like adding a glow effect that intensifies as they approach the dismiss threshold
- Haptic feedback that gives the user tactile feedback on their interaction

The presentation itself will be built entirely in Compose Multiplatform, with live interactive demonstrations that demonstrate these topics in realtime.

You'll leave with a complete understanding of how to combine Compose's animation APIs into interactions that elevate your app from functional to exceptional.

sessions.title: Understanding Compose modifiers and how their order affects UI
sessions.description:
Time to finally understand how modifiers work in Compose and to start using them consciously and deliberately, instead of relying on trial and error or changing their order until the UI happens to look correct. This presentation provides a deep and structured explanation of modifiers, focusing on how they actually work under the hood and why their order matters so much. It helps prevent common order-related mistakes by building a clear mental model of modifier behavior. In addition, it introduces a clear formula for consistently winning the well-known Jetpack Compose Modifier Guessing Game, turning what often feels like guesswork into a predictable and understandable process.

Related: https://kt.academy/article/game-modifier-guesser

sessions.title: Architecting a Real-Time LLM Co-Pilot for Android Automotive: Lessons from MapGPT
sessions.description:
In-car voice assistants have historically been rigid and slow. What happens when you integrate real-time vehicle telemetry, dynamic route data, and a streaming LLM directly into an Android navigation app?

This session explores the Android architecture behind MapGPT, a production in-car AI assistant. Moving beyond standard REST APIs, we will dive into managing an always-on WebSocket stream using Kotlin Coroutines and StateFlow to process natural language and seamlessly trigger native UI and vehicle actions.

You will learn how to:
- Design Coroutine/Flow pipelines for streaming LLM responses without UI jank.
- Implement a decoupled Kotlin Middleware pattern to execute actions like routing and climate control.
- Manage complex app state (telemetry, ETA, EV data) to feed the LLM continuous context.
- Build a deterministic replay system to test streaming interactions in CI without a live API or physical car.

sessions.title: The Flutter Developer’s Guide to Not Breaking Time
sessions.description:
Handling time in Flutter looks simple until it meets the real world: daylight saving shifts, recurring events, and users changing regions. Dart’s built-in DateTime only models local or UTC time, leaving crucial timezone semantics implicit—and leaving you prone to production bugs.

In this talk, we’ll uncover exactly where DateTime breaks down and why standard workarounds fall short. Then, we’ll dive into Temporal for Dart: a TC39-inspired API for Flutter and Dart that separates time into explicit types like Instant, PlainDate, and ZonedDateTime. You’ll see how choosing the right type makes time-related bugs almost impossible to compile.

Leave this session with a foolproof mental model to store, manipulate, and display moments across regions without breaking your calendars, schedules, or sanity.

sessions.title: Beyond Widgets: Engineering AR-like Experiences in Flutter
sessions.description:
Flutter is often associated with beautiful UIs, but its rendering engine can do much more.

While building AR-like experiences in Flutter, I discovered that smooth interactive overlays require far more than placing widgets on top of a camera preview. Camera latency, coordinate transformations, screen rotations, and rendering performance must all work together to create a seamless experience.

Those challenges changed how I design Flutter applications.

In this session, we will explore practical Flutter techniques for building AR-like experiences, including camera integration, coordinate transformations, rendering synchronization, interactive overlays, and performance optimization. I will also show how to prototype AR-like interactions entirely in Flutter without relying on platform-specific implementations.

You will leave with practical Flutter patterns that you can immediately apply to camera-driven applications, including AR, computer vision, and interactive experiences.

sessions.title: Chasing Behavioral Parity: Java, Swift and JS Interop in Flutter
sessions.description:
The same Dart API should give you the same map behavior on Android, iOS, and Web. Achieving that behavioral parity is the hard part: there is no single map engine. A C++ core runs on mobile, a JavaScript engine on the Web, each reached through a different interop boundary.

This talk dissects the federated architecture of Flutter MapLibre, the open-source maps plugin: how an abstract factory unifies distinct runtimes under one stable contract, and exposes platform gaps honestly where features cannot match.

We follow one call down to native code on each platform, into an interop stack that is itself moving: the Web is already modern and Wasm-ready, while the Mobile roadmap drops the Java and Swift wrappers to reach the C++ engine directly, a breaking shift.

Even if you never touch a map, you will leave knowing how Flutter reaches native code, when to use Method Channels, js_interop, or FFI, and how to architect a federated API that holds behavioral parity without breaking it.

sessions.title: Using Bluetooth Low Energy in Flutter
sessions.description:
Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) has a wide variety of use cases in modern IoT technology, from Smart Home appliances to medical trackers. Building a mobile application that works with any of these devices requires understanding of how BLE works. In this session, I'll go into details of implementing BLE within a Flutter app.

This session includes:
- Platform setup. Configuring both Android and iOS applications.
- Message encoding. How data is packaged and sent between a device and the application.
- Terminology. What's GATT table and how to use services, characteristics and descriptors to access data. What's the difference between central and peripheral and how to build your app as either.
- Live demo. A demo of an example app running on 2 phones and exchanging messages over BLE.

If you're building a companion app for a physical device or you're curious about this technology, this talk contains everything you need to get started.

sessions.title: Unity 6 Graphics Optimization for Mobile & XR
sessions.description:
Join us for Optimizing XR in Unity 6, where we’ll explore the tools and techniques needed to deliver smooth, comfortable experiences across mobile and XR devices. We’ll review platform performance requirements and frame-time targets before loading a sample scene and optimizing it step by step.

Using features such as GPU Occlusion Culling, the GPU Resident Drawer, Mesh LOD, Adaptive Probe Volumes, and more, we’ll demonstrate platform agnostic approaches to reduce CPU and GPU workloads while maintaining visual quality. Along the way, we’ll identify bottlenecks using the Rendering Debugger and Render Graph Viewer, break down the render pipeline, and show how to measure whether your project is meeting its XR performance targets in real-world development scenarios.

sessions.title: From ptrace to Trampolines: How Android Hooking Works
sessions.description:
Dynamic instrumentation is everywhere in mobile: attackers use it to bypass app logic, testers to understand how apps work, and defenders to check that their own protections hold. But how does a hook actually get into a running process, and what does it leave behind?
This talk follows the full path, from injection to hook to detection, across Java and native techniques, with concrete examples from Frida and renef.

You will leave able to:
- Explain the main injection methods (ptrace, library preloading, Zygote) and their trade-offs
- Understand how Java/ART and native inline and PLT/GOT hooks actually work
- Spot the traces hooking frameworks leave, and build simple detection from it
- See why no-ptrace frameworks like renef beat the common tells, and why detection stays an arms race

sessions.title: React Native Ecosystem: libraries, tooling, and who keeps it alive
sessions.description: The React Native ecosystem is more than just a framework. It is the people building the libraries, the tooling, and the invisible infrastructure that make modern mobile apps possible. This panel looks at the projects developers rely on every day, the challenges of keeping them maintained and evolving, and the community effort required to keep React Native moving forward. We’ll discuss what’s changing in the ecosystem, which tools are becoming essential, how maintainers decide where to invest their time, and what developers should know to build with confidence today and beyond.

sessions.title: Building Over-the-air Updates for Zalando Mobile Apps
sessions.description: Native iOS and Android releases for mobile applications have been a bottleneck in terms of speed of delivery and ultimately the rate of adoption for a long time. Can over-the-air updates solve this? At Zalando, we’ve been building an OTA solution - thanks to the move to React Native - to overcome the challenges of the native release process. My talk will walk you through the motivation, design and technical complexities of building such a solution. Join in for details on how we are tackling reducing the cost of data transfer, a robust client-side implementation and tooling, and our learnings.

sessions.title: We Put React Everywhere: Lessons from Unifying Web and Native at GetYourGuide
sessions.description:
Shipping every feature three times (web, iOS, Android) is a tax most product companies quietly accept. At GetYourGuide, we decided to stop paying it and bet on React-Strict-DOM: one React codebase, rendering truly native on mobile and standard DOM on web.
This is not a success-theater talk. I'll walk through how we made the decision and the alternatives we rejected, the problems we knew about going in (ecosystem immaturity, missing primitives, knowledge gaps), and why we treated escape hatches as a first-class part of the architecture rather than an embarrassing workaround.
I'll also cover the part nobody puts in the RFC: the tooling and education investment needed to bring an entire engineering org along.

sessions.title: Who Let the App Intents Out? 🐾
sessions.description:
Who says you need to open an app to use it? With App Intents, I logged my puppy’s walks 🐶 while keeping my iPhone in my pocket. This shows how apps can extend beyond the UI, letting Siri, Shortcuts, Spotlight, and widgets handle interactions hands-free.

User behavior is changing: people increasingly expect to talk to their devices or ask them to do things instead of navigating traditional screens. Modern apps should integrate seamlessly with the system, making everyday tasks effortless and enhancing the user experience. Developers will learn how to unlock system-level features without relying on traditional screens, making their apps smarter, more context-aware, and useful.

Major takeaways:
- Define and register AppIntents in Swift
- Expose actions to Siri, Shortcuts, Spotlight, and widgets
- Pass parameters with AppEnum and AppEntity
- Design background-driven experiences without touching the UI
- Apply practical examples immediately in your own apps

sessions.title: visionOS in Production: Real Business Use Cases
sessions.description: visionOS is often framed as an entertainment platform, but some of its most interesting work is happening in business. In this session, I will look at practical visionOS use cases in areas like retail, real estate, healthcare, training, and industrial workflows, with a focus on why these products matter and what patterns make them successful. Attendees will leave with a better understanding of when spatial computing creates real value, what product and UX constraints shape serious visionOS apps, and how to evaluate whether a business idea is solving a real problem or just adding novelty.

sessions.title: Custom SF Symbols: Fun… but not easy!
sessions.description:
Stand out from other apps with your own great set of symbols!

Custom SF Symbols are a great way to make your own symbols with the same flexibility as Apple's own. They're also a pain to create and to get right, which is why we often just make our square icons and call it a day. So let's change that!

You'll learn how you can use SF Symbols, why you'd want custom ones and how to get started on creating your them. From mass producing symbols out of existing icons, to creating hand-crafted pieces of art in every weight!

sessions.title: You're Not Alone, Kid: Indie Apps and AI Teammates
sessions.description:
Building an indie app means doing the work of a tiny company: coding, releases, subscriptions, screenshots, store metadata, ASO, ads, support, and CI. In 2026, AI can help with a lot of that, but only when it is connected to real workflows, reviewable outputs, and human judgment. Where that connection holds and where it quietly breaks is what this roundtable is about.

Together we will map what it actually takes to turn a scattered side project into a repeatable shipping system. Everyone arrives with a different answer, and the disagreements are the useful part.

I will bring what shipping Peakme taught me, including the parts that did not work, as a starting point. The rest comes from the circle. Whatever you ship, on whatever platform, the shape of the problem is the same.

sessions.title: Thread Lightly: Parallelizing Tools with the Job System
sessions.description: Are you tired of focusing solely on runtime performance while your Editor and Build pipelines remain sluggish? This session moves beyond the common narrative that Unity’s Job System is strictly for runtime, showing you how to leverage multi-threading at Editor and Build time to significantly accelerate iteration cycles and unblock your design team. We will explore how to integrate these high-performance techniques without the overhead of fully migrating to an ECS architecture, providing you with essential do’s and don’ts to ensure your code remains safe and performant. Join us to see real-world production examples that demonstrate the tangible impact of intelligent parallelization on your project’s efficiency.

sessions.title: Lunch
From Assistant to Actor: The New Security Risks of Coding Agents
sessions.description: This session looks at what agentic AI means for developer security in practice. We will break down how autonomous and semi autonomous coding agents fail, where trust in automation goes too far, and why traditional secure coding guidance is no longer enough. The focus is on concrete scenarios teams are already facing and on pragmatic guardrails that keep agents useful without giving them unchecked power. The goal is to help security and engineering teams work with agentic AI in a way that scales productivity while keeping control, visibility, and accountability firmly in place.

sessions.title: Why Senior Engineers Fail at Agentic Coding and What Top Performers Do Differently
sessions.description:
Over the past two years, I’ve trained and coached more than 2,000 developers and led hands-on agentic coding enablement programs for teams at organizations including Siemens, Enercon, and GFT. One pattern kept repeating: when developers use AI coding agents, seniority is not what predicts success.

Give two developers the same agent, same codebase, same task—one becomes significantly more productive, the other quickly loses trust in the output. This talk shares what actually differentiates them based on 100+ developers in real-world sessions.

We’ll explore why experienced engineers sometimes struggle, what successful users consistently do differently, and the most common mistakes teams make when adopting agents. Attendees will leave with a practical way to evaluate and improve their own agentic coding workflow.

I introduce a simple 4-pattern model explaining why developers succeed or fail with agentic coding systems.

sessions.title: We Built It for One. Then Everything Multiplied.
sessions.description:
When we launched our Android banking app, it had one account, one portfolio and one currency. The architecture was simple because the assumptions were simple. Then the business grew.
This is the story of how we evolved the business and the app into a multi-account, multi-portfolio, multi-currency platform - complete with junior accounts, four portfolio types, and two currencies - without starting from scratch.

Told as a two-perspective narrative: one speaker covers the business drivers behind each evolution (why we needed it, what the market demanded), while the other covers the technical reality of making it happen on Android (what broke, what scaled, and what we'd do differently).

sessions.title: KSafe: Fast Encrypted Key-Value Storage for Kotlin Multiplatform
sessions.description:
KSafe is a Kotlin Multiplatform key/value persistence library designed to make secure state persistence feel as simple as working with a regular variable:

var counter by ksafe(0)
counter++


The talk is structured around three core pillars:

1) Developer experience: creating an intuitive API that covers common persistence scenarios without boilerplate-heavy storage abstractions.

2) Performance: using hot caching, asynchronous persistence, and concurrent processing to make secure storage practical for frequent reads and writes.

3) Security across platforms: mapping each target to the most appropriate encryption and storage mechanism while preserving one common Kotlin API.


By the end of the session, you will understand how to use KSafe and the architectural trade-offs involved in building a secure, high-performance Kotlin Multiplatform persistence library.

sessions.title: Letting Go of Control: Building a Game with My Kids and AI
sessions.description:
When I suggested building a game with my kids, I imagined teaching them code. They had other plans. They cared about characters, stories, and wild feature ideas. Sitting next to me while I coded was boring.

So we changed the process.

Using AI tools like Junie, Codex, and Gemini, my kids became the directors. They described worlds and mechanics. AI generated roughly 90% of the code. I reviewed it, simplified it, and occasionally fixed what it broke.

In this talk, I’ll share what worked, what hallucinated, where AI failed to fix simple UI bugs, and how shipping imperfect code changed my mindset as a senior developer.

This is not a demo of AI tools. It’s a story about collaboration, simplicity, and how AI can turn imagination into working software in hours, not months.

sessions.title: Shift Left: Unit test your compose UI with reusable robots and BDD-style DSL
sessions.description:
When testing the UI cannot be done via the normal instrumentation tests, what's left are unit tests.

Join this session to see how far unit tests can take you when verifying compose UI (permissions flow anyone?), how you can do so with reusable robot screens and how a behavior driven kotlin DSL can make all your tests understandable by everyone.

Take a shortcut and see the gotchas of junit assertions vs instrumentation ones, see the limitations of unit testing your UI and check if you could benefit from testing your UI without an emulator.

sessions.title: Don't Melt the Phone: Autoplaying Video Grids in Compose
sessions.description:
Every cell autoplays a video, no spinners, no "tap to play" - then you run it on a mid-range phone and watch it catch fire.

This is the field guide I wish I'd had, built in three layers.

The client: a poster, an ExoPlayer, a staggered grid - all pure Compose.
The backend: small MP4s, a CDN, and an answer to "why didn't you just use WebP?".
The measurement: a five-minute tour of Perfetto and the one metric your profiler hides, with a live look at the grid under load.

We close somewhere honest: what "good enough" means, and when you shouldn't play 8 video players at the same time.

sessions.title: Multi-Window Cockpits in Android Automotive: From CTS Battles to Declarative UI
sessions.description:
Building a multi-window infotainment cockpit in Android Automotive used to be hard. To place several apps side by side and animate them, you had to go deep below the application layer: custom TaskDisplayArea orchestration, SurfaceControl animations frame by frame, unpredictable z-ordering, and a CTS run that broke the moment you touched window layering.

Scalable UI changes that. A full multi-window cockpit becomes a composition of orchestrated panels, declared in XML through RRO overlays. No glue code, and the orchestration that once required deep internals is handled by the framework. What took months of fighting the Window Manager now takes hours.

This is not a walkthrough of the docs. It is the view of an engineer who built cockpits the hard way before Scalable UI existed: what changed, the trade-offs the docs don't mention, and how far you can push the framework, from panels, variants and transitions to the point where XML ends and code begins. With live demos throughout.

sessions.title: Build full-stack, agentic apps in Dart with Genkit
sessions.description:
Want to ship agentic and AI-powered features across platforms using Dart and Flutter? Try Genkit Dart!

Join this session to learn how Genkit Dart brings Flutter’s “write once, run anywhere” philosophy to the development of full-stack, agentic apps. Explore how to build type-safe AI flows and agents using Dart's strong type system, with the flexibility to deploy logic as a backend service or run it directly on the client. This session covers practical patterns for secure API key management through remote models, end-to-end data safety with shared schemas, and rapid local iteration using the built-in developer UI. Developers will leave with a clear understanding of how to leverage their existing skills to build, test, and deploy production-ready AI and agentic features across any platform.

sessions.title: Turn Your Architecture into Lint Rules
sessions.description:
Every Flutter team has conventions: how features should be structured, which packages should be used, where dependencies are allowed, or which APIs should not be called directly. But when those rules only live in documentation, code reviews, or someone’s memory, they are easy to miss and hard to scale.

In this session, we will show how to turn team conventions into custom lint rules for Dart and Flutter. We will walk through creating a rule, inspecting code with the analyzer, reporting actionable diagnostics, and adding autofixes that help developers correct issues directly from their editor.

Through practical examples, we will explore rules based on architecture and package usage, such as preventing imports across layers or guiding developers towards internal abstractions. Attendees will leave with a clear mental model for using static analysis to improve consistency, onboarding, and maintainability in Flutter projects.

sessions.title: Flying with Flutter
sessions.description:
“Can you control an airplane with this?” With my love for aviation, it is a question that I have asked with every new framework and language that I have learned from the moment I started programming.

We know that Flutter is a high-performance framework that can run on pretty much any device imaginable, so… Is it up to this task as well? Could you control an airplane with Flutter and Dart?

In this talk, we will try to find out. We will use Flutter’s advanced custom graphics to create a plane’s control interfaces and figure out ways to connect to sensors and process their data efficiently to deliver an app worthy of being used in an airplane.

sessions.title: Stop Being a Human Linter: Automating Flutter Architecture at Scale
sessions.description:
Tech leads shouldn't spend their days acting as human linters in PRs. Yet, as enterprise Flutter teams scale, enforcing domain boundaries and unwritten business logic manually becomes a massive, frustrating bottleneck that standard `flutter analyze` simply cannot fix.
This talk is about how we stopped arguing in comments and started building "executable architecture." I'll share how we transformed our static Confluence guidelines into custom, domain-oriented lints that run automatically. We will dive into real-world examples of the custom guardrails we use to eliminate repetitive PR friction and drastically cut down developer onboarding time.
Beyond just saving time, you'll see how enforcing strict, machine-readable boundaries is the hidden prerequisite for allowing modern AI coding assistants to generate safe, compliant code without drowning your project in technical debt.

sessions.title: Realife built models & AI tools in Blender for Tinker Dungeon
sessions.description:
To get a "tinkered" look inspired by tinkering workshops, all models of Tinker Dungeon where physically built out of cardboard and scanned via the Lidar scanner of a mobile phone. 

Game designer Christoph Rasulis of Brainbite Studios shows, on one side the process of the handcrafted tinkered art creation and scanning, on the other the how to use AI as a creative tool, by connecting Claude with Blender for model optimization and editing with AI.  A fast way to create your own prototype!

Currently in development, Tinker Dungeon is an multiplayer extraction dungeon crawler tasking players to repeatedly visit dungeons to save a whimsical kingdom and to craft and upgrade inventive tools—like glue guns and paperclip bows—from scavenged cardboard, scrap metal and electronics. The game takes part in the Level Up Accelerator Programme of Games/Bavaria.

Tinker Dungeon - Trailer:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nBpe-T2nicU
(Art Creation from 00:35 sec)

sessions.title: Protecting the Mobile LLM Gateway from Prompt Injection & Model Jailbreaking
sessions.description:
Mobile apps are racing to ship AI assistants, copilots, and agents, but the path from the app to the model introduces a new attack surface. Prompt injection is no longer just a web chatbot problem: attacker-controlled data can reach an LLM through API responses, local storage, runtime manipulation, retrieved content, and other context the app trusts.
In this session, we'll threat-model the mobile LLM gateway and follow real attack paths from Android into the model's context. We'll examine direct and indirect prompt injection, runtime manipulation, and why traditional mobile security controls alone aren't enough. You'll leave with practical techniques for identifying injection paths, defining trust boundaries, and protecting prompts before they reach the model.

sessions.title: Did AI Solve React Native Accessibility? Let's Measure It
sessions.description:
When we talk about mobile accessibility, the conversation usually stops at screen readers. But a user in bright sunlight, a parent holding a baby, someone with a temporary injury, or an aging population with changing vision - they all rely on accessible design. In this talk, I'll show why accessibility is a quality feature, and how to measure it systematically. I'll introduce an accessibility calculator I built that maps WCAG criteria to React Native apps, and test whether AI coding tools produce accessible code by default.
You'll leave with:
- A clear understanding of the four WCAG pillars applied to React Native.
- A practical, reusable framework for auditing any mobile app.
- Real-world data on how AI models handle accessibility.
- Practical strategies for fixing the most common mobile accessibility failures.

sessions.title: Performant by Design: Building Fast React Native Apps
sessions.description:
React has come a long way. And especially when working with legacy codebases, it's easy to overlook all the tools modern React provides for building performant and scalable applications.

From perceived to real performance gains. From helpers to the new compiler to debugger tooling. Let's take a look together at how to build fast web apps with ease.

In this talk we'll explore how users perceive performance, how new tooling like `Activity` and async transitions can help improve it, what role the new React compiler can play, and how the devtools can help you debug performance issues.

sessions.title: From Swift Skeptic to Migration Lead: What React Native Taught Me About Being an iOS Engineer
sessions.description:
When our team decided to move from separate iOS and Android apps to a single React Native codebase, I was skeptical. I’d spent years investing in Swift, Xcode, and everything that comes with being an iOS engineer — why walk away from all that?

But I stayed curious, asked the hard questions, and ended up leading the migration. This talk is for iOS or Android devs who’ve heard “we’re going React Native” and felt that pit in their stomach. I’ll share how we approached the rewrite at Zenjob, how native expertise made all the difference, and why native skills are not only still relevant — they’re essential.

If you’ve ever wondered where you fit in a cross-platform world, this is the talk for you.

sessions.title: Beyond the checklist: Building Observability for Accessibility Debt
sessions.description:
Your app passes every accessibility audit. Accessibility Inspector shows zero issues. You did a VoiceOver pass before the last release. And yet — a real user with VoiceOver still can't complete checkout, because the focus order silently changed when a designer moved a button two weeks ago.

This is the gap almost every team has, and almost no team measures. We treat accessibility like a compliance checklist we clear once, instead of a property of the codebase that decays the moment we stop watching.

This session builds on my earlier work on accessibility as an inclusion practice, and picks up where that conversation usually ends: "okay, now how do we keep it that way?", and "how does AI help?".

You'll leave seeing accessibility as a signal you monitor, not a task you finish — the way you already treat performance and reliability. We'll cover what tools quietly miss, a four-layer way to measure it, which numbers reflect real progress, and where AI helps — and where it doesn't.

sessions.title: Hostile Environment CoreLocation: Sensor Fusion & Battery Math
sessions.description: It’s easy enough to grab a user's coordinates, but keeping location tracking alive in the background without iOS silently killing your app is a completely different story. After spending a lot of time building high-frequency tracking apps for large logistics fleets, I learned the hard way that basic GPS polling just drains the battery, overheats the phone, and triggers the system watchdog. In this talk, I want to share how to stop fighting the operating system and actually build location services that survive out in the real world.

sessions.title: Design your app for offline working
sessions.description:
In this talk, we will discuss the key design considerations involved in building an iOS app that continues to provide a great user experience even when network connectivity is limited or unavailable. Rather than treating offline support as an afterthought, we'll explore how to design an application where offline capabilities are a fundamental part of the architecture.

We'll examine common challenges such as data synchronization, conflict resolution, local persistence, and maintaining a responsive user interface while disconnected. Through practical examples and architectural patterns, attendees will learn how to build resilient applications that gracefully transition between offline and online states, ensuring users can continue working without interruption and that their data is reliably synchronized once connectivity is restored.

sessions.title: React Native performance on low-end devices
sessions.description:
We've all seen it: an app that feels smooth on a flagship phone, but tells a very different story on an older Android device. Screens take too long to open, lists stutter, animations drop frames and users immediately sense that something is off.

This roundtable is a space to share those stories: the surprising bottlenecks, the debugging rabbit holes, the trade-offs, and the fixes that actually worked. We'll talk about real experiences with startup time, memory limits, rendering performance, navigation, images, profiling tools, and the gap between "works on my phone" and "works for everyone".

Bring a performance war story, a hard-earned lesson, or a problem you're still trying to solve.

sessions.title: The Latest in Android XR: Extending Mobile Apps to Intelligent Eyewear & Immersive Headsets
sessions.description:
Spatial computing is entering a transformational phase. As Android XR expands across Intelligent Eyewear Glasses, standalone XR Headsets, and other projected devices, developers can now seamlessly extend their Android skills into the 3D space.

In this session, explore the latest in Android XR as we transition to the Jetpack XR SDK Beta. Learn how to extend mobile apps to smart glasses, construct spatial UIs with Jetpack Compose for XR and SceneCore, and leverage ARCore features like depth sensing and Geospatial APIs. We will also highlight multi-engine support across Unity, Unreal Engine, Godot, and OpenXR.

Key Takeaways: Extend mobile apps to AI glasses using Device Availability APIs and Gemini integration, Build 3D spatial UIs using Jetpack SceneCore and Compose for XR , Harness ARCore depth, dimming, and Geospatial features, Leverage OpenXR, AXRIF, MRTK3, and multi-engine spatial multitasking

sessions.title: 🏁 The Robot Rally Finals
sessions.description:
Location: Robot Rally Booth area

Official timed trials! Live leaderboard, judge evaluations, and awards ceremony.

sessions.title: Break
Why AI Agents Fail on Enterprise Data and What Coding Agents Get Right
sessions.description:
When AI agents fail on enterprise data, the root cause is usually the data layer, not the model. Coding agents avoid this because their context is deterministic by design. Enterprise data has none of that by default.

This talk introduces the handover layer pattern and demonstrates it live: an AI agent discovering transformations, applying PII redaction, and switching data sources without hardcoded paths.

Takeaways:
- How to separate data context failures from model failures
- A concrete architectural pattern for deterministic data access
- A live demo reproducible locally with open-source tooling

sessions.title: The model is not the feature: designing invisible AI for mobile apps
sessions.description:
Everyone is adding “AI” to their app, but most implementations still look like a chatbot bolted onto an existing product. This talk takes a different path: how do you design mobile features where AI disappears into the experience and still does something genuinely useful?

We will build a production-minded architecture for invisible AI features on mobile using task-specific flows instead of a single giant assistant. The session covers on-device and hybrid inference, model routing, structured outputs, retrieval, fallback policies, token and latency budgets, battery impact, offline behavior, observability, and evaluation. By the end, attendees will have a blueprint for features like smart compose, intent routing, content triage, extraction, summarization, and proactive assistance that feel like product design—not a demo.

sessions.title: Production-Ready Android WebView: Security, Performance, Observability
sessions.description:
WebView is one of the most powerful — and most dangerous — components in the Android toolbox. While it effortlessly powers payments, UGC editors, and mini-apps, it is also a top source of security vulnerabilities, memory leaks, and UI jank.

In this session, I will distill the practical Kotlin patterns used to ship secure, interactive web content inside production Android apps at massive scale. We will dive deep into locking down a WebView by default (HTTPS enforcement, origin allowlists, minimal-surface JS bridges), handling custom schemes safely so the app isn’t used as an open redirect, and solving the operational side of WebViews. You will learn performance techniques that actually move the needle — like hidden-instance warm-ups and smart caching — alongside observability strategies to track JS-to-native breadcrumbs. Attendees will leave with a concrete, pre-launch security and reliability checklist they can apply immediately.

sessions.title: Scaling up your Screenshot Testing, without the friction
sessions.description:
Screenshot testing has become popular over the last few years, but most organizations limit their screenshot testing to just core design libraries, or they might disincentivize adding screenshot tests because of scaling issues.

In this talk I'll give you insights into why you might have trouble scaling up your screenshot testing efforts: from flakiness, to dealing with developer friction and education, and the more obvious issues with scaling your storage for screenshots. We'll talk through potential solutions for each of these problems.

We'll also show how screenshot testing can be used as a "social" tool to demonstrate the value of your testing efforts, and encouraging more testing in your team. (After all, non-engineers can understand screenshots, even if they don't understand code.)

This talk generalizes to iOS and Flutter too, which hit the same scaling issues with screenshot testing.

sessions.title: BLE <3 Protobuf: Designing Schemas for the Smallest Packets in the Room
sessions.description:
Protocol buffers (protobuf) is a serialization format widely used in client-server communication. Compared to JSON, it produces a more compact wire format, which matters when every byte counts. This makes it a strong fit for Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) communication, where maximum packet sizes are measured in the hundreds of bytes, or fewer.

This talk dives into the best practices for using protobuf over BLE, drawn from a real app. We'll cover how to design protobuf messages that work across a wide range of MTU sizes (down to the minimum of 23 bytes), strategies for fragmenting and reassembling messages that exceed a single MTU, and how to account for the overhead encryption adds to your payload budget.

Attendees will leave with a practical understanding of sizing protobuf schemas against BLE constraints, plus patterns for fragmentation and reassembly they can apply directly to their own mobile and embedded projects.

sessions.title: F-Droid, much more than just an app store. An introduction to the F-Droid organisation
sessions.description:
No user accounts, no developer fees and no tracking.

In this talk you'll learn how F-Droid, the app store, works. How to submit your apps there and how to maintain them. What are anti-features, how is your app approved and updated? How do reproducible builds help ensure security? And how to run your own app repo?

F-Droid is more than just an app store for Open Source Android apps. The organisation also actively participates in policy discussion and advisory to policy makers and organisations. We advocate for openness across the Android ecosystem and beyond. You will see F-Droid board members in active roles helping EU law makers understand the value of an open ecosystem. We’ll talk about our participation and invite you to join the discussion.

sessions.title: Desktop windowing APIs
sessions.description:
Multi-window support is one of the most highly anticipated features for Flutter desktop. In this talk, we will demo Flutter's new windowing features, dive into technical hurdles that needed to be overcome, and look under the hood to understand how it all works.
Multi-document applications are common on desktop platforms, but not possible with Flutter until recently. Dialogs, menus and tooltips that are not forced into the parent window make much better use of the screen real estate on desktop systems.
But we're also looking ahead - in a VR/AR world, everything can be your desktop, and Flutter apps need to be there.

sessions.title: Technically Accessible, Actually Usable — A11y for 1M MAU in practise
sessions.description:
Most Flutter developers have touched the Semantics widget at some point - usually to set a label on a custom button, or to mute a decorative image. The moment you hand your app to a real screen reader user, the gap between technically accessible and actually usable becomes clear: everything is read, nothing is broken, and yet some flows are, in practice, painful to get through.

This is ~1 year a11y work on prod banking app - the kind of app where a visually impaired user has to move money, confirm a transfer, and recover from a validation error with confidence.

We'll show the perspective of the people we’re actually building for: we’ve spoken with long-time screen reader users how they really use mobile apps, and we’ll bring their conclusions into the room - what is okay and what is a painpoint.

We'll also show a set of concrete production cases - form errors and focus, reading order, status announcements, the `GestureDetector` trap, and a few more - each tied to the WCAG rule.

sessions.title: Building an Agentic Harness for Flutter: What changes when agents work in parallel
sessions.description:
Prompting one agent is easy. Getting several of them to work on the same Flutter codebase without breaking it is not.
The shift happens when you stop prompting and start building a harness: skills that encode how your project actually works, subagents that own a slice of the work, hooks that enforce your rules, commands that make it repeatable. And then the hard problem isn't generating a widget. It's that three agents are working at once, while your specs, your review and your QA were all designed for one human at a time.
This is what we're building on production Flutter codebases at an agency: the anatomy of the harness, the Flutter-specific guardrails that stop agents from wrecking your widget tree and state, and how the PM, dev and QA roles shift once the bottleneck moves from writing code to describing and verifying it.

sessions.title: 60× Faster Image Processing in Dart, with FFI, Build Hooks, and Rust
sessions.description:
Resizing a 4K photo using the pure-Dart image package takes almost 57 seconds. So I created Pixer: an image manipulation package with a familiar Dart API and a Rust engine underneath that communicates via FFI. This results in speeds 5–60+ times faster for resizing, cropping, rotating, blurring, and encoding, and installation requires nothing more than "dart pub get".

In this talk, I will walk you through the entire stack. For Rust, I will cover selecting the appropriate crate, designing an FFI API, and generating the bindings with cbindgen and ffigen. I will also discuss the pitfalls I encountered. For Dart, I will explain how the new native-asset build hooks transform 'sending a Rust binary to five platforms' from a multi-day task into something that just works.

There will be plenty of benchmarks, a few honest mistakes, and a recipe that you can use for your own package.

sessions.title: Hack Your Own App: Getting Started with Mobile Penetration Testing
sessions.description:
In this talk we introduce three widely used mobile security tools, MobSF, Burp Suite, and objection, that help you quickly assess your app for vulnerabilities. Through one static analysis demo with MobSF and two short penetration testing demos, we show how these tools complement each other and how you can combine them effectively in penetration testing workflows.

We also highlight how much security value you can already gain with relatively little effort or specialized knowledge. Because these tools are purpose‑built for mobile analysis, they allow you to uncover weaknesses in your app without needing to be a full‑time security expert.

sessions.title: Expanding the app to user space - Expo Widgets
sessions.description:
Your app does not have to live behind a tap. With widgets, you can meet users right where they are - on their home screen - delivering a continuous flow of content without expecting them to open the app.
In this talk, I'll walk through expo-widgets, a library that renders react components as a native widgets on the home screen. I’ll reveal what the library actually does behind the scenes and how you can ship beautiful, but most importantly useful widgets and Live Activities today, without touching the native code.

sessions.title: Use Shaders, Build Your Own UI Primitives, and Stand Out!
sessions.description:
High-level libraries like Three.js and React Native Skia are great, but their abstractions bias your app toward a specific look. To build truly unique visual mechanics, you need to drop down to raw shaders. While this requires reinventing the wheel a bit, it unlocks total creative freedom. The barrier has always been ergonomics. Shaders traditionally mean writing untyped string literals, making it hard to safely share state with your React components.  
  
In this talk, I will introduce TypeGPU. We’ll look at how to write low-level GPU logic natively in TypeScript, while maintaining strict type safety across the hardware boundary.  
  
Key takeaways:  
- Break out of the mold: Learn why dropping down to low-level shaders unlocks ultimate design freedom.  
- Type-safety and ergonomics: See how TypeGPU replaces string-literal shaders with natural TypeScript code.  
- UI scheduling: Learn to orchestrate GPU tasks on the UI thread at 120 FPS.

sessions.title: React Native on the Big Screen: Focus, Performance, and the 10-Foot Experience
sessions.description: Almost everyone uses a TV app, yet almost no engineer has built one. Television is its own world — no touch, no cursor, just a remote and ten feet of couch that quietly break the interaction patterns you'd use on mobile. This talk covers building for the living room with React Native: designing for the remote and the 10-foot experience, how react-native-tvos works, how the tvOS and Android TV focus engines behave underneath (including a look at Android's FocusFinder), building your own focus manager and keeping screens like an EPG fast on weak hardware.

sessions.title: Backend driven UI and SwiftUI
sessions.description:
Backend-driven UI promises faster shipping, but a production-ready framework is far more than rendering JSON. This talk dives into the implementation of a backend-driven UI engine that feels native to SwiftUI — the framework powering Flo for millions of users, shipping UI changes without waiting for the mobile release train.

You'll learn:
- How to map server-defined JSON into real SwiftUI views with an extensible, type-safe component registry
- How to replicate Jetpack Compose layouts with SwiftUI.Layout for pixel-perfect iOS/Android parity — and bridge Compose's size constraints with SwiftUI's proposals
- How to keep multi-pass measurement fast with layout caching
- How to introduce variables, state, and reactivity into JSON-defined screens while letting SwiftUI's own invalidation do the heavy lifting

You'll leave with concrete architectural patterns and the trade-offs behind them, ready to evaluate or build backend-driven UI in your own app.

sessions.title: Building Scalable Swift Automation: From CI to App Store Distribution
sessions.description:
Managing Swift projects at scale demands systematic automation—from CI to multi-platform testing to App Store distribution. This hands-on 80-minute workshop teaches automation patterns refined across 128+ repositories, from open-source libraries to commercial apps.

Part 1 (35 min): Reduce GitHub Actions configs from 100+ lines to 5, add intelligent caching for 65–85% faster builds, and run matrix testing across Swift versions and Apple platforms—implemented live in your own repo.

Part 2 (35 min): Build packages that work across iOS, macOS, watchOS, tvOS, visionOS, Linux, and Android, using Swift Testing's conditional traits to skip platform-specific tests gracefully. We close with a TestFlight distribution demo (Fastlane + GitHub Actions, 30 minutes down to 3).

Bring a laptop, a GitHub account, and a Swift package or app. You leave with a working pipeline.

sessions.title: Deterministic Session Replay: Capture & Replay for Mobile at Uber
sessions.description:
Capture & Replay is a platform capability. It unlocks deterministic bug reproduction, automated regression testing against real prod sessions, visual diffing and much more. 

Reproducing a production mobile bug reliably is one of the hardest problems. At Uber, majority of bugs were not reproducible before we built this system.

We'll cover the full engineering stack across two layers: the mobile UI capture pipeline and the network orchestration layer. On mobile, we instrument every UIKit and SwiftUI component to capture a precise view hierarchy locator — using visual ordering, scroll context, and layer-level deduplication for SwiftUI. On the network side, we intercept, scrub, time-shift, and replay every API response and push message — without touching a real backend.

Unlike traditional session replay tools that play back a screen recording, this system replays on a live app binary — attach Xcode, set breakpoints, and step through the exact code path that ran in production.

sessions.title: Rust for Mobile Developers
sessions.description:
Swift, Kotlin and Dart give us expressive, productive environments for building apps, but developers increasingly benefit from working across languages and platforms.

Rust is increasingly well established across a range of areas including servers, command-line tools, WebAssembly and embedded systems.

In this roundtable, we’ll compare notes on learning and using Rust from different backgrounds, including iOS, Android, Flutter and React Native.

No Rust experience is required. Bring your questions, or just come to listen and learn.

If you’ve tried Rust, share your experience. We’ll explore what feels familiar — strong typing, expressive types, package management and modern tooling — and what feels different, particularly Rust’s approach to memory management.

Have you used Rust in mobile development? Let’s discuss when sharing Rust code across platforms makes sense and how it compares to Kotlin Multiplatform.

sessions.title: Gaussian Splatting in the Browser and Beyond: Rendering 3DGS in WebXR
sessions.description:
Gaussian Splatting has quietly displaced NeRFs as the practical choice for real-time photorealistic 3D. But there's a wide gap between "it renders on my RTX card" and "it holds framerate in stereo on a Quest," and that gap is where the interesting engineering lives.

This talk looks at how splats actually work, with just enough theory to reason about the rendering pipeline and at what it takes to get 3DGS running in the browser and in WebXR, including the real trade-offs around sorting, memory, compression, and framerate.

It also steps back to the bigger picture: what opens up when generative AI meets splats, and what a photorealistic, AI-generated immersive web could look like.

sessions.title: Break
It Finally Works (Mostly): Rewiring Mobile App Network Interception
sessions.description:
During mobile app penetration tests, assessing app backend APIs is a crucial step that necessitates interception of app network traffic. Testers typically rely on techniques like API hooking, proxy interception, or connecting via a Machine-in-the-Middle (MitM) Wi-Fi access point. 

But not all techniques are equal. Some require specialized hardware, while others are highly situational. We are looking at you, flutter app on a non-jailbroken Android device ;)

In this lightning talk we give an overview of the current state of network interception during mobile app penetration tests, common pitfalls, and limitations. 

We then present a simple, custom VPN-based solution which attempts to overcome these challenges for most Android and iOS apps.

sessions.title: React Native is native: what that means in practice
sessions.description:
React Native renders real native views — so what does "native" actually mean when you build with it today? 

This talk traces how native code evolved across the React Native and Expo ecosystem: from Expo Go's bundled runtime and its tradeoffs, through Continuous Native Generation and the declarative Expo Modules API, to local and inline modules that finally let Swift and Kotlin live right next to your TypeScript. 

We'll see how the Expo Modules API replaces bridge plumbing with a clean API — async functions as JS Promises, typed records and enums, and events — and go through the full capability spectrum from plain JS components to native primitives. 

Then we bring AI into the loop: how agents can write the native code for you, why colocated inline modules make that practical, and where the real constraints still are. You'll leave understanding how React Native is as native as you need it to be — business logic written once, dropping to native only where it counts.

sessions.title: Trust, but Verify: Static Checks as Confidence Signals for AI-Generated Code
sessions.description:
An AI coding agent sounds exactly as confident when it's wrong as when it's right. You have no way to tell which one you're looking at until it's already in production.

So stop trusting how confident the agent sounds — compute your own. Deterministic static checks it can't talk its way past: type validation, uniqueness and schema checks, lint and AST rules, coverage ratchets. Each one produces an objective pass or fail.

This isn't theory. A localization agent force-merged broken translation keys past failing CI — three times in one month — silently breaking master for every team, until I traced it down. The fix wasn't a smarter prompt. It was moving the check somewhere the agent couldn't reach. Because every check needs a home, and only one home makes it impossible to skip. Once the gate lived there, the agent's confidence stopped mattering.

sessions.title: How EAS Observe can help you improve your app
sessions.description:
EAS Observe is a new product developed by Expo that helps you measure app performance and identify bottlenecks in your app. It gives you insight into how your app behaves in real-world conditions and helps you understand where performance issues come from.

In this talk, I will show how to use Expo Observe to find and fix performance problems in production apps. You will learn how to spot common issues, understand performance data, and use it to make your app faster and more reliable.

Whether you're trying to understand if a recent release improved performance, track down a bottleneck affecting a subset of users, or simply gain more confidence in the quality of your app, you'll leave with a better understanding of how to use performance data to build faster and more reliable applications.

sessions.title: Apple Intelligence Beyond the Hype: Building Features That Actually Matter
sessions.description:
Apple Intelligence is much more than Writing Tools and the new Siri. Behind the scenes, Apple has introduced a collection of frameworks that allow developers to build smarter, privacy-first experiences running directly on the device.

In this lightning talk I'll walk through a real demo application built entirely on Apple Intelligence. We'll explore how on-device Large Language Models, Foundation Models, semantic search, and intelligent ranking can solve real user problems without sending data to the cloud.

Instead of focusing on marketing slides, we'll look at practical implementation patterns, common pitfalls, and what developers should actually start experimenting with today. You'll leave with concrete ideas you can immediately apply to your own iOS apps.

sessions.title: Your VR Tutorial Will Be Skipped: Onboarding Lessons from First-Time User Testing
sessions.description:
First-time VR users are processing a lot at once. They look around the virtual space, check their hands and avatar body, and try to understand what it feels like simply to be in VR. Meanwhile, the tutorial keeps moving.

In usability testing with VR newcomers, this meant that carefully designed instructions were missed, not necessarily because users were distracted, but because exploration itself was part of how they were learning the new environment.

This lightning talk shares how those observations changed the question I was asking about onboarding: from “how to give first-time users more guidance” to “how to guide them without taking away their freedom to explore.”

I’ll introduce “guided freedom” and share practical approaches to help users find their way back into the flow, align their attention with the tutorial, and communicate clearly when their attention is already busy.

sessions.title: Break
You Don’t Need Better Agents. You Need Better Orchestration.
sessions.description:
As teams adopt multi-agent AI systems, most effort goes into improving individual agents — making them more capable, accurate, or autonomous. Yet many of these systems still fail to deliver value in production. The issue isn’t agent capability. It’s orchestration.
This session focuses on how to design and run multi-agent systems where coordination, not components, determines performance. It covers how tasks are structured, how agents are routed and managed, and how state and control are handled across workflows.
You’ll leave with practical approaches you can apply immediately to improve reliability, reduce unnecessary complexity, and get more value from your existing systems.
You’ll learn:
-How to diagnose where your multi-agent system is breaking down
-A practical orchestration model (task structure, routing, state, control)
-Design patterns for coordinating multiple agents reliably
-When to add agents vs when to fix orchestration
-One concrete “day 1” improvement to apply immediately

sessions.title: Building AI Agents you can talk with
sessions.description:
Most text based bots are frustrating to talk to out loud. The awkward pauses ruin the flow of conversation and they struggle if you do not speak perfectly. Building a truly natural voice assistant means moving away from standard prompt completions and embracing real time audio streaming. In this talk I will show you how to use the Gemini Live API to build agents that actually listen and respond instantly.

You will leave this session knowing exactly how to build these voice experiences yourself. We will start by setting up the WebSockets needed for fast audio streaming. Then we will look at how to connect external tools so your agent can fetch data and take actions while speaking.

sessions.title: Advanced Kotlin Native Integration
sessions.description:
When compiling Kotlin Multiplatform code for native platforms, the compiler produces object files and then links them together. Other libraries and programs can then use the resulting library as a dependency.

While this process is similar to other native dependencies, there's a major limitation. There should be only one Kotlin Multiplatform native binary in your project.

In this talk we'll take a look at the impact of including multiple Kotlin Multiplatform binaries in an application, look at ways to split the compilation into multiple smaller pieces, and discuss potential solutions for larger projects requiring complex repository structures.

sessions.title: Scale your team's responsibilities from a single feature in the app to a public SDK
sessions.description:
Yesterday, your code lived on a single screen, hidden behind the UI. Only you and your team knew how it worked.

Today, you're building libraries used by developers around the world. They read your code, integrate it, report bugs, love its simplicity - or hate it when it breaks their edge cases. It's more stressful, but also far more rewarding.

So what happened overnight?

In this talk, I'll share practical lessons on designing (not)stable APIs, planning implementations, managing versioning and backward compatibility, and reducing integration friction.
We'll also explore the human side of adoption: earning trust, building effective feedback loops, and avoiding the mistakes that turn promising libraries into abandoned or forked projects.

sessions.title: The Art of the Break: Solving "Invisible" Typography Issues in Flutter
sessions.description:
Typography is a centuries-old art form perfected in the world of print, yet it remains one of the most overlooked "silent" components of modern app design.

When you don't care about typography, your app can feel subtly unprofessional - marred by clumsy line breaks,  awkwardly truncated text, and poor spacing. These challenges are amplified in apps offering a German UI, because German has many long words that can easily shatter a layout.

However, when typography is done well, your users experience a sense of effortless clarity they can’t quite name.

You don’t need to know anything about typography to take away valuable lessons from this session. I will show you basic typography problems found in real-world apps, how we solved them in the AUTOVIO app, and how you can apply those same solutions to your own projects.

sessions.title: Flutter Refactors at Scale: Change Everything, Break Nothing
sessions.description:
The real challenge of refactoring large Flutter projects is when you have to introduce changes across many active repositories, with dozens of developers contributing in parallel. The key is a balance between the code quality improvements and keeping the system stable.
We’ll focus on leveraging the Dart Analyzer, AI and codemod to enforce consistency, catch issues early, and guide large-scale migrations with confidence.
You’ll walk away with pragmatic strategies and tools from large-scale banking app refactors. We’ll also cover how to ensure your design system is adopted, and stays aligned with current standards and evolving UI patterns. We’ll show you how to make sweeping changes feel less scary and maybe even fun!

sessions.title: Background Execution in Flutter: Fighting Android's Process Death, Foreground Services, WorkManager
sessions.description:
Background execution on Android is hard. Adding Flutter makes it harder. When Android kills your app's process, the Flutter engine doesn't survive gracefully: isolates vanish, plugin registrations are lost, and the engine needs a cold start before any Dart runs again. Most developers discover this in production. This talk exists so you don't have to.

We'll cover three pillars. First, process death, what happens to the engine lifecycle when Android reclaims memory, how to handle cold restarts, and why common patterns fail silently. Second, foreground services, starting and managing them from Dart, handling the notification, and staying compliant with Android 14's stricter service-type rules. Third, WorkManager, registering a headless engine in a worker, fixing unavailable plugins, and structuring Dart that runs outside the UI lifecycle.

Drawing from production experience, you'll leave with a concrete mental model and patterns you can apply immediately.

sessions.title: App Clinic: Let's make your app accessible based on WCAG 2.2
sessions.description:
Accessibility is often treated as an afterthought.
Instead of theory alone, I will help you fix your accessibility rating with a fast but clear review of your app, live, on the spot.

I have 7 years of experience in Flutter and more than 5 years building accessible apps used by people with various impairments: visual, motor, and cognitive.

Come with your app running on a physical device, ready to test. You'll leave with a concrete list of accessibility issues found in your own app, practical fixes you can apply right away, and a better sense of how WCAG 2.2 applies to real Flutter code rather than abstract guidelines.

Bring your app, and let's see what WCAG 2.2 reveals about it.

sessions.title: Security Risks of Packages in Mobile App Development
sessions.description:
Packages and libraries help us build mobile apps with less code and in less time. However, relying on them also introduces security risks that we need to address.

Do you check the entire source code of every package listed in your .lock files? Are you sure that every updated version is safe?

In this talk, I’ll discuss what kinds of incidents can happen through dependencies and how we can mitigate those risks. I’ll introduce OWASP Mobile Application Security as general background knowledge, as well as real-world incidents from other ecosystems such as npm or pip.

We shouldn’t underestimate security risks, but we don’t need to overreact to them either.

By clarifying possible attack scenarios and explaining how each platform works, I’ll show how we can make practical decisions about security risks and address them in real-world Flutter app development.

sessions.title: Bazel for iOS at Scale: Lessons from a Real Enterprise Migration with over 300 modules
sessions.description:
In this talk, I will share the journey of migrating an iOS application at PAYBACK, serving more than 18 million monthly active users and consisting of 116 feature modules, 208 service modules, 18 shared modules, and four country-specific app variants.
The session will cover how we evaluated Bazel, addressed a complex dependency graph, and integrated both local and remote Swift packages.
I will discuss our incremental migration strategy, which allowed Bazel and Xcode to coexist throughout the transition, as well as the steps taken to improve build performance from initially matching Xcodebuild speeds to achieving 2× faster builds, and ultimately 3–6× improvements through spawn strategy optimization and local caching.
I will also explore our ongoing efforts to build Kotlin Multiplatform with Bazel in a monorepo environment.
Finally, the talk will highlight practical lessons learned around CI integration, BuildBuddy observability, and testing strategies within a large enterprise setup.

sessions.title: Taming Screen Time: A Survival Guide to Anti-Doomscrolling APIs
sessions.description: Apple's Screen Time APIs let you build digital wellbeing and parental control features, but they're some of the least documented frameworks in the Apple ecosystem. I'll walk through what I learned building a real app on top of them: requesting the Family Controls entitlement, designing around the Device Activity Report and Monitor extensions' brutal sandbox limits, and the bugs and workarounds found. You'll leave knowing which framework to reach for, how to survive the extensions' constraints, and how to design UX that hides what the API can't fix.

sessions.title: Unlearning the Web in React Native: The Hardest Mobile Lessons
sessions.description:
React Native often feels familiar to web engineers at first: components, hooks, TypeScript, state management, and reusable UI patterns all look close enough to home. But once teams start shipping real mobile apps, the differences become impossible to ignore. Navigation behaves differently, lifecycle matters more, releases are slower, permissions are sensitive, offline states appear sooner than expected, and App Store and Play Store rules change the way teams think about shipping. 

This roundtable is for developers who have made that transition, or are making it now, to compare what transferred well, what caused trouble, and which assumptions had to change. Bring your stories, surprises, and hard-earned lessons from building React Native apps in the real world.

speakers.name: Amitesh Mani Tiwari
speakers.bio:

I’m a Software Development Engineer (iOS) , focused on building production-grade iOS applications that scale reliably and age well. I specialize in Swift-first development, MVVM architecture, and data-driven mobile systems using Realm, with a strong emphasis on performance, stability, and long-term maintainability.

My day-to-day work involves solving hard engineering problems rather than surface-level fixes—working closely with product, backend, QA, and design teams to ship features that are cleanly architected, thoroughly tested, and resilient under real-world usage. I care deeply about code quality, app performance, and user experience, and I optimize for all three without trade-offs.

In addition to iOS, I bring solid cross-platform and frontend experience, working with React.js, TypeScript, C#, and Power BI, along with Microsoft BI technologies such as SSIS and SSAS. This allows me to think beyond mobile screens and contribute meaningfully to end-to-end product ecosystems when required.

🎙️ I’m also a global speaker and educator, having delivered technical talks at international and large-scale platforms including Mobius, AppsConf X (Russia), MDW 2025 (UAE), GDG DevFest, IEEE Computer Society, AWS Dehradun, Delhi Flutter, and the Nigeria Technical Community. My sessions are known for being practical, system-level, and grounded in real production experience—not theory slides.

🎓 Mentorship is a core part of my journey. As a hackathon mentor and judge, I’ve helped developers transform early ideas into shippable products, guiding them on architecture, execution, and engineering discipline. My contributions to the developer ecosystem have been recognized with honors such as the 21 Under 21 Award.

📚 Outside engineering, I’m an author. My debut novel, A Letting Go: Journey of Rediscovery, explores emotional resilience, self-growth, and the realities of college life. Writing keeps me grounded and sharpens the same clarity and empathy I bring to engineering and leadership.

📝 I also actively write about iOS development, architecture, and emerging technology trends at appdevbyamitesh.medium.com

speakers.name: Andrea Della Porta
speakers.bio:
Born in Rome in 1994, passionate about mobile development since forever. Andrea has been a technology enthusiast for as long as he can remember. He started developing his first Java programs in his early high school years, but with the advent of smartphones, he quickly fell in love with the mobile world. His experience started in Switzerland for an Android project in the medical field and continued for large companies such as NTT Data and Deloitte, until he got to his current Capgemini. Over the years he has developed applications with large user bases for various industries, specializing in native Android development, Flutter and now Kotlin Multiplatform.
His life is not only programming, but also football, padel and an obsession with Lego!

speakers.name: Andrea Moretti
speakers.bio: Andrea is a Principal Engineer at Zalando with over a decade of experience in front-end and full-stack development, with a strong focus on design systems and user interfaces. Originally from Rome, he started programming as a kid and has been drawn ever since to building things that people can use and enjoy. Alongside his engineering work, he has also worked in photography and other creative fields. Today, he focuses on cross-platform applications, exploring how to bridge web and native into cohesive, shared experiences and codebases.

speakers.name: Andrei Shikov
speakers.bio: Andrei is a software engineer working on Compose compiler and runtime.

speakers.name: Andrew Orobator
speakers.tagLine: Senior Android Engineer at Reddit · Author, Vibe Engineering Series
speakers.bio: Andrew Orobator is a senior Android engineer at Reddit and author of the Vibe Engineering series — a ten-part methodology for AI-assisted Android development. He co-authored the Vibe Engineering series with Claude using the workflow it describes.

speakers.name: Angelo Cammalleri
speakers.bio: Angelo Cammalleri is an Apple platforms developer and consultant based in Bremen, Germany. He has spent over ten years building apps and software for iOS, macOS, and other Apple platforms, working with both startups and established companies. Alongside his employment and consulting work, Angelo develops and ships his own apps, including Coca, Eidetic, and Passable.

speakers.bio: I’m an experienced Mobile Engineer focusing on Android & Flutter with 8+ years experience on Mobile Apps Development with Flutter. speakers.name: Anisha Malde

speakers.name: Anna Leushchenko

Technical Founder & CEO at Proofa.tech and an AI Engineer / Flutter Developer with deep expertise in Dart, Firebase, and cross-platform development (including React). Actively building and exploring the potential of AI ecosystems, focusing on Vertex AI, Gemini, and agentic workflows.

speakers.name: Anna Nikulina

I have also spoken at local meet-ups, sharing insights on a variety of technical topics (though not specifically on this one).

My passions are 🤘 metal music, 😻 cats, 📷 photography, 🎨 design and 📱 technology (no order).

speakers.name: Ariella Mendel

speakers.name: Armend Belallari
speakers.bio: I'm a Senior Mobile Software Engineer at OpenResearch GmbH, with 13+ years experience in Mobile Development, passionate about building high-quality mobile applications and exploring emerging technologies. I enjoy turning new ideas into working prototypes, experimenting with the latest Apple technologies, and sharing practical lessons learned with the developer community through talks, meetups, and hands-on demos.

speakers.name: Arnaud Briche
speakers.tagLine: Senior Partner Engineer at Unity Technologies, Game Jam Mentor on his free time
speakers.bio: Arnaud blends deep Unity expertise with hands-on game jam experience. speakers.name: Arnaud Giuliani
speakers.tagLine: Co-founder of Kotzilla - Tech, Vision & Product - Koin Framework Creator - Google Developer Expert Android & Kotlin
speakers.bio:
Arnaud Giuliani is co-founder of Kotzilla (Tech, Vision & Product) and creator of Koin, the most widely adopted dependency injection framework for Kotlin. 

With 20 years of experience in software engineering across Java/JVM systems and Android, he has been an active speaker since 2016 with 60+ talks delivered across Europe and the US. 

Recognized as a Google Developer Expert for Android & Kotlin and a member of the Kotlin Foundation, he focuses on the intersection of software architecture, developer experience, and AI-driven observability for mobile applications.

speakers.name: Arnold Noronha
speakers.bio:
At Droidcon NYC 2015, I launched screenshot-tests-for-android while working for Facebook. This was the first screenshot testing library for Android, and popularized screenshot testing over the years.

After leaving Facebook, I built the open-source Screenshotbot tool, a screenshot testing service, similar to internal tooling used by companies like Facebook, AirBnb and Google. I've worked with companies at different scales, each doing screenshot testing in their own unique ways.

speakers.bio: React Native & React developer, Senior React Native Developer at Callstack, a PhD candidate at AGH University of Krakow, MEng in Automation & Robotics. Aficionado of programming, robotics, AI & pointillist paintings.

speakers.name: Avi Tsadok
speakers.bio: Avi Tsadok has worked in iOS development for 14 years and is currently the mobile team lead at Melio Payments. He has also shared his expertise as a speaker at several conferences. Avi resides in Tel Mond, Israel, with his wife Tammy and their two children.

speakers.name: Avni Burak Erbora
speakers.bio: A. Burak Erbora is a Lead Unity Developer at Kolibri Games with extensive experience in mobile games, software development, consulting, and developer tools. He is also the founder of GurBu Technologies and co-creator of GPU Instancer, a performance-focused Unity Asset Store tool. His expertise includes Unity architecture, performance optimization, production stability, and long-term technical health. Burak holds degrees in computer programming and philosophy, as well as an MA in Cognitive Science from Boğaziçi University.

speakers.name: Aymen Bokri
speakers.bio: Aymen Bokri is a Senior iOS Tech Lead based in France with over a decade of experience building high-performance mobile ecosystems. He has architected and led apps serving millions of active users, driving significant revenue and market impact. Aymen focuses on how modern iOS features can transform user retention and business growth.

speakers.name: Ayushi Gupta

Driven by a passion for problem-solving, I eagerly accept challenges and strive to deliver impactful solutions. Let's connect and collaborate to find innovative solutions together

speakers.name: Balázs Gerlei

Developer, Presenter/Teacher, Open source advocate, Ultimate frisbee player & Board game hoarder.
