speakers.name: Benedict Pregler
speakers.bio: Benedict Pregler is a Staff Software Engineer at GetYourGuide in Zurich, leading the technical side of its migration from three separate stacks (Vue web, native iOS, native Android) to a single React + React Strict DOM codebase. A former Android engineer and Android Guild Lead, he crossed over to the web side and lived to tell the tale.

speakers.name: Benedikt Löbbecke
speakers.bio: I am a freelance software developer from Munich working with android for about 10 years for customers including Daimler, Allianz and ING. In my last project I supported the apps Team of the Otto shopping app, one of the best known shopping apps in Germany. Currently I am working on a private KMP project related to app security.

speakers.name: Benjamin Faller
speakers.bio: After graduating with a Bachelor of Science in Applied Computer Science from HTWG Konstanz in 2022 I chose to pursue my career in information security. Currently, I work at Redguard as a Security Tester analyzing various applications and infrastructure for security vulnerabilities.

speakers.name: Bettina Carrizo
speakers.tagLine: Flutter Engineer at Holafly | Flutter & Dart GDE | WTM Ambassador
speakers.bio: I'm a Software Engineer from Montevideo, Uruguay, passionate about building thoughtful mobile experiences and empowering the dev community. I work as a Flutter Engineer at Holafly e-SIM, and I love sharing my learnings through talks at events like FlutterConf LATAM and FlutterCon EU. In 2025, I became the first woman Flutter & Dart GDE in LATAM, and at present, the only active one across the Americas. As a Women Techmakers Ambassador and co-organizer of FlutterConf LATAM, I love bringing people together to grow and learn. When I’m not coding, you’ll find me out walking with my dog or diving into personal growth content.

speakers.name: Binh Minh Herbst
speakers.tagLine: Lead Experience Director, Deutsche Telekom MMS
speakers.bio:
Minh is Lead Experience Director at Deutsche Telekom MMS, driven by a deep passion for creating meaningful experiences in life and at work. Her guiding principle is 'Design for Happiness': the idea that technology should not only be functional, but also human, empowering and emotionally resonant.

She explores how cutting-edge technologies shape everyday routines and transform the way we live and work, from XR and AI glasses to generative AI in content, design or code. In her role, she advises, inspires and supports people and organizations in adopting new technologies, always with a human-centred mindset and a clear eye for innovation.

Before joining Deutsche Telekom MMS, Minh worked on AR-technologies in Silicon Valley and was later appointed Professor of Game Art & Design at the University of Fine Arts Essen. As co-founder of A.MUSE – Interactive Design Studio, she creates impactful experiences across interactive installations, XR, AI, edutainment and games.

Her work moves playfully between art, design, technology and social entrepreneurship. She advocates for cultural diversity, digital equity and more inclusive access to future technologies. Her projects have received international recognition, including awards from Unity for Humanity, Games for Change, MIT XR Hack and Kultur- und Kreativpiloten Deutschland.

speakers.name: Blend Hamiti
speakers.bio: Compiler Engineer at Guardsquare, working on the DexGuard R&D team, where we implement code obfuscation techniques and runtime checks to protect Android apps against both static and dynamic analysis.

speakers.name: Bogdan Hobeanu
speakers.bio:
Building apps for 15 years. Loving design + code + @FlutterDev - author of bitsdojo_window - http://github.com/bitsdojo/bitsdojo_window

Find me on Twitter: https://twitter.com/callmebit

speakers.name: Bogdan Plieshka
speakers.bio:
Engineer with over a decade of Frontend development experience, passionate about automation, accessibility, and scaling complex systems.

Working at Zattoo as a Principal Engineer, focusing on delivering frontend solutions across Web, React, and React Native for streaming media content.

Organizer of the React Berlin Meetup, actively contributing to the development community.

speakers.name: Boris Denisenko
speakers.bio:
Hi, I'm Boris. I’ve been passionate about software engineering for over 17 years. Throughout my career, my path has taken me across diverse domains: from building widely used mobile applications to working closely with embedded systems and advanced automotive technologies. Today, I'm based in Munich, working as a Technical Lead and Senior Software Engineer at Mapbox, where I architect complex navigation solutions for leading global car manufacturers.

My professional journey is driven by the challenge of bridging the gap between raw hardware signals and seamless user experiences. A significant milestone for me was my time working for Jaguar Land Rover project, where I served as the Lead Mobile Developer for their vehicle remote control platform. I also spent time pushing the boundaries of mobile tech as a core engineer on the Mapbox Vision SDK, developing real-time computer vision systems for edge computing—a project recognized for its technical excellence by the Qualcomm Developer Network. While my past projects heavily involved machine learning and computer vision, my core focus today lies in conquering the architectural challenges of Android Automotive OS (AAOS).

My technical foundation is rooted in a Master’s degree in Applied Mathematics and Informatics. In my day-to-day practice, I leverage Kotlin, C++, and robust Android architectures to build high-performance, hardware-integrated systems. Ultimately, I believe that truly great automotive products are born when we translate noisy, complex vehicle data into a reliable and inspiring experience for the person behind the wheel.

speakers.name: Bradley Wilson
speakers.tagLine: Head of Client Platform, Trade Republic
speakers.bio:
Bradley Wilson is Head of Client Platform at Trade Republic, where he leads the teams responsible for building Trade Republic's Mobile & Web foundations - crafting secure, user-friendly Fintech products that navigate the complexity of user needs, business goals and regulatory requirements.

A seasoned Android engineer turned engineering leader, Bradley has spent years solving hard technical and regulatory problems across banking, digital health and privacy & security. He has led teams of all sizes, shipping products in some of the most demanding and compliance-heavy environments in the industry.

Beyond the code, Bradley co-founded a mental health startup and is a passionate advocate for mental health in the workplace, accessibility and equity in tech. A servant leader grounded in empathy, trust and transparency, he believes the best products are built by psychologically safe, high-performing teams with a clear sense of purpose.

He speaks on topics including Android platform engineering, leading in regulated industries, mental health in tech, and building high-performing engineering cultures.

speakers.name: Braedon Schmidt
speakers.bio: Braedon is a Software Engineer at Google who's been working in Dart since 2022, and on Dart since March.

speakers.name: Bruno Scheele

His interest in making software that can be used by anyone and everyone, leads him to consider inclusivity in all aspects of development. Accessibility especially has captured his imagination and he now strives to keep learning more about this whole new world and help companies and organizations make truly usable apps for everyone.

speakers.name: Cagatay Ulusoy

speakers.bio: Cagatay is a Google Developer Expert for Flutter and Dart. After working as a native Android developer in different sizes of companies for a long time, he decided to continue his application development journey with Flutter. He is an active member of the Flutter community and enjoys sharing his knowledge with sample apps, articles, and talks.

speakers.name: Calvin Chestnut
speakers.bio: Calvin Chestnut has been an Apple enthusiast for twenty years and an Apple Platform developer for twelve. Originally from Texas, after three countries and six states they've settled in Salem, MA to raise their child and snake. They can usually be found building apps from a local coffee shop and chatting with tourists.

speakers.name: Carlos Holguera
speakers.tagLine: OWASP Mobile Application Security Project Lead / NowSecure, Distinguished Mobile Security Research Engineer
speakers.bio:
Carlos is a distinguished mobile security research engineer working with NowSecure and one of the core project leaders and authors of the OWASP Mobile Security Testing Guide (MASTG) and OWASP Mobile Application Security Verification Standard (MASVS), the industry standard for mobile app security.

He collaborates closely with the Android security leadership at Google and the teams behind the "Mitigate security risks in your app" pages in the Android Developer Docs and MASA for Google Play.

Carlos is passionate about reverse engineering and dynamic instrumentation of mobile apps and is continuously learning and sharing his knowledge.

speakers.name: Carlos Mendonça
speakers.bio: Carlos is a Product Manager for Flutter at Google NYC. He is passionate about languages, compilers, operating systems, AI, and many other computer science fundamentals. He is always open to connecting in English, Portuguese or broken Spanish to learn what others are building.

speakers.name: Carly Richmond
speakers.bio:
Carly is Developer Advocate Lead at Elastic, based in London, UK. Before joining Elastic in 2022, she spent over 10 years working as a technologist at a large investment bank, specialising in front-end web development and agility. She is a UI developer, who occasionally dabbles in writing backend services, a speaker and a regular blogger.

She enjoys cooking, photography, drinking tea, and chasing after her young son in her spare time.

speakers.name: Carmen Huidobro
speakers.bio: Carmen Huidobro is a developer advocate and deved enthusiast. She thrives on lifting others up in their tech careers and loves a good CSS challenge. Always excited to talk about teaching tech, especialmente en Español, oder auf Deutsch.

speakers.name: Catalin Miron

speakers.bio: I love giving life to UI through animations and so, creator of AnimateReactNative.com and Keyframer.dev. I'm a speaker, YouTuber, father of 2, React & React Native enthusiast, Open Source contributor and coffee nerd. In my free time I help others to succeed.

speakers.name: Cate Huston
speakers.bio: Cate is the author of The Engineering Leader, fractional CTO at Twill and engineering leadership coach. She was previously in leadership roles at DuckDuckGo and Automattic, and an advisor at Glowforge. She started her career as a software engineer at Google.

speakers.name: Chittipolu Jayakrishna
speakers.tagLine: Expert IT Development, REWE International AG
speakers.bio: With over 15 years of experience in Android development, has worked across a diverse range of domains including mobile games, home automation consoles, security systems, licensing modules, custom-engineered devices, and e-commerce applications and currently focused on cutting-edge research and development in Augmented & Virtual Reality, building innovative solutions through my startup, particularly in the aviation and industrial training sectors. Also an active member of the developer community and organizer of GDG Wien, and empowering fellow developers.

speakers.name: Chris Gill
speakers.bio: Chris has spent his career working on products to make developer’s lives better. Currently, he is a product manager at Google, focused on helping developers more easily integrate AI capabilities into their applications.

speakers.name: Chris Ward
speakers.tagLine: Head of Mobile Development - Personal Content @ 1&1 Mail & Media
speakers.bio: Chris started coding life as a full-stack developer and moved between all sorts of weird and wonderful disciplines and industries before he settled on Android. In more recent years he moved into management, as both an EM and head of engineering for mobile teams. In addition to coding life, he's been an elected official in the UK, had a key role in legalising same-sex marriage in the UK through his LobbyALord app, and addressed the UN Human Rights Council in Geneva on atrocities against LGBT+ people abroad. He writes and speaks about his experience of being diagnosed with ADHD late in life and how he deals with the unique challenges neurodivergency brings to an individual working in tech. He lives in Berlin with his cat and his husband and has a mid-life-crisis friendship with crows.

speakers.name: Christoph Rasulis

Christoph Rasulis develops award-winning educational games and experiences, often in collaboration with partners such as the film production company Tellux and pixelcloud, for television broadcasters like SWR and Kika, and for cultural institutions like the Bayerische Staatsoper, or Schlösser und Gärten Baden-Württemberg. The products I've been involved with have won numerous awards and generated international reach, which I'm very proud of. I also experiment a lot with AI, computer vision and sound design.

speakers.name: Chrystian Vieyra Cortes
speakers.bio: Chrystian Vieyra Cortes is Director of Engineering at Thomson Reuters, where he leads mobile teams building cross-platform news experiences. A longtime Android and iOS developer, Chrystian specializes in sensor data visualization and has published several popular educational apps. Originally from Celaya, Mexico, he came to the United States as a student to earn a B.S. in Computer Science from Western Illinois University and later made the U.S. his permanent home.

speakers.name: Claire Sivadier
speakers.bio: Claire Sivadier is a freelance iOS developer who almost became a dog breeder, until an unexpected career twist brought her into tech. She’s worked on meaningful iOS products, from helping people develop healthier habits at Kiplin to shaping the listening experience at Deezer. Claire is also deeply involved in the community as a co‑organizer of CocoaHeads Nantes.

speakers.name: Corrie Green
speakers.bio: Corrie is a Senior Developer Advocate at Unity Technologies, from Scotland. With a PhD focused around Virtual Reality Optimization & 3D Interaction with over a decade of experience as a software engineer in the simulation sector, they bring end-to-end research and development expertise across technical domains. As an indie developer, Corrie has released apps and contributed to over 18 game titles, including several independently published across desktop and mobile storefronts. Corrie now focuses on helping developers on their  development journey — whether you're just getting started with the Unity game engine or tackling XR design challenges.

speakers.name: Cory Cook

He is dedicated to exploring how mobile apps can be extended into intelligent eyewear and XR headsets, leveraging tools like Jetpack Compose for XR to build the next generation of immersive user interfaces.

He explores Scalable UI and platform internals through technical deep-dives (@passenger6 on Medium / ProAndroidDev).

speakers.name: Daniel Sproll
speakers.bio: A trained cognitive scientist, Daniel has been working with XR technologies for over a decade: as researcher studying human navigational behavior and as UX designer laying groundwork in early VR interaction design. As co-founder of realities.io he produced multiple award winning VR experiences, the latest being the indie VR hit Puzzling Places. His work is driven by the hope that if we get spatial computing right, it holds the chance to make computing less abstract, more explorable, more embodied and ultimately more human.

speakers.name: Daniel Zloczower
speakers.bio:
Daniel Zloczower is Director of Partnerships at HARMAN Automotive, leading content and strategic partnerships for the Ready Link Marketplace (formerly Ignite Store), HARMAN's automotive app store platform for Android Automotive and a key component of HARMAN's Software-Defined Vehicle (SDV) vision. Since the early stages of the product, he has helped shape the marketplace ecosystem, working closely with OEMs, app developers, content providers, and technology partners worldwide.
With more than 10 years of experience in automotive and smart mobility technologies, Daniel focuses on expanding connected vehicle ecosystems, automotive app platforms, and digital cockpit experiences, helping bring innovative content and services to vehicles around the globe.

speakers.name: Danny Preussler
speakers.bio: Danny built mobile applications for companies like Viacom, Groupon, eBay and Alcatel. He is a Google Developer Expert for Android. Before there was Android he was already active in the Blackberry development community.

speakers.name: Daria Orlova
speakers.tagLine: Co-founder of bbapps.dev. GDE Flutter & Dart. Flutterista.
speakers.bio: Flutter GDE 💙 Co-founder BBapps - apps that care for you and the planet 🌍🫶🏽 Author “Flutter Design Patterns and Best Practices” 📚 Flutterista 💜 WTM 💚 I also love to read 📖, dance 💃🏽, travel ✈ and learn languages 🇪🇸 Mother of Cats 😻

speakers.name: David Anthony
speakers.tagLine: XR Software Enginer @ Studio Tim Deussen
speakers.bio: I'm a software engineer who loves bringing innovative solutions to life at the intersection of science and technology. At Studio-Deussen in Berlin I build mixed reality training tools for healthcare professionals, and previously worked on collaborative digital twin systems at Fraunhofer HHI. Four years of shipping XR across Unity, OpenXR, and WebGL.

speakers.name: David Blanc
speakers.bio: After 8 years as a java engineer in various French IT companies, I moved to iOS and Android development in 2012. In 2015, I decided to focus more on Android as I joined the French banking group BPCE, before moving to the cybersecurity team, in charge of our mobile applications.

speakers.name: David Castaño
speakers.tagLine: Senior Mobile Engineer at Very Good Ventures
speakers.bio: David Castaño is an Electronics and Software Engineer whose foundational work on a Mobile System for water measurements via Bluetooth now fuels his career as a specialist iOS Native and Flutter Developer. He is an expert in architecting high-performance. David excels in developing complex solutions for IoT/BLE health monitoring, geospatial applications, and large-scale financial SuperApps, focusing on robust, cross-platform, user-centric experiences.

speakers.name: David Khourshid
speakers.bio: David is a software engineer who loves playing piano and is passionate about animations, state machines, cutting-edge user interfaces, and open-source. Previously at Microsoft, he is now the founder of Stately, a startup focused on making even the most complex application logic visual and accessible to developers and non-developers alike.

speakers.name: David Leuliette
speakers.bio:
David Leuliette is a French freelance React Native developer helping companies ship universal apps for iOS, Android, and the web since 2016.

He hosts the Cross Platform Show, the #1 French-speaking React Native podcast with 10K+ listens, and has delivered 50+ talks at conferences and meetups across Europe.

When he's not shipping production apps, he's sharing hard-won lessons about mobile architecture, Expo workflows, and the tools that actually  work in the real world.

speakers.name: David Mařák
speakers.bio: David Mařák is co-founder and CTO of Yord and has spent over a decade building XR and AI applications, from museum installations and brand experiences to hardware experiments and advanced training centers.

speakers.name: Dawid Matyjasik
speakers.bio:
I'm a Software Engineer at Software Mansion with over six years of experience, acting as a go-to expert for React Native performance and the New Architecture. I specialize in solving complex bottlenecks, and most of my day-to-day work is dedicated to helping large-scale commercial clients optimize, stabilize, and scale applications that handle millions of active users under heavy load.

Beyond my core work and past contributions to the open-source ecosystem, I am deeply involved in the developer community. Recently, I run performance workshops at App.js Conf 2026 alongside my coworkers. I am also a regular participant at major industry conferences, including React Universe 2025 and previous editions of App.js. Whether I am mentoring developers at local hackathons, exploring emerging tech at AI meet-ups, or joining discussions at Cursor Cafe, I am passionate about sharing knowledge and connecting with the tech community.

speakers.name: Dennie Declercq
speakers.bio: Dennie is Microsoft MVP Developer Technologies and has experience in accessibility with Microsoft technologies. In daily life Dennie is president and developer at DDSoft, a nonprofit that connects IT to People who are less tech-savvy. Dennie invented technical solutions and systems to help people with disabilities to participate in their daily life. Thanks to his autism he's the right man at the right spot to contribute as a volunteer in function of people with disabilities.

speakers.name: Devlin Duldulao
speakers.tagLine: Creator of DaloyJS, speaker, published book author
speakers.bio: Devlin Duldulao is the creator of DaloyJS, a software engineer, educator, and published author with 12+ years of experience building and teaching modern web development. Originally from the Philippines and based in Norway since 2019, he writes books and courses for developers who want to ship real, secure systems and takes his Asian home cooking about as seriously as his TypeScript.

speakers.name: Dhiraj Sriram
speakers.bio: I'm a Staff Software Engineer at HelloFresh in Berlin, building the shared React Native modules behind our iOS and Android apps. I care deeply about usability, accessibility, and performance the parts of software people feel but don't notice. I'm currently focused on helping teams adopt AI coding agents safely with the right guardrails to ensure stability.

speakers.name: Dionysis Lorentzos
speakers.tagLine: Mobile Engineering Manager · CISSP · OWASP MAS Lead Author
speakers.bio:
Dio is an Engineering Manager on the Mobile team at Enpal, a Berlin-based solar energy company, where he leads Flutter, Android, and iOS development. His focus spans mobile infrastructure, customer data, and security. A practitioner turned leader, Dio combines native mobile experience with a track record in engineering management.

He holds a CISSP certification and is a lead author of the OWASP Mobile Application Security (MAS) project. Previously EM Mobile at ShareNow, he also maintains open source Android libraries with over 6,000 combined GitHub stars.

speakers.name: Dmitrii Ivanov
speakers.tagLine: Senior iOS Developer, Platform team, ING
speakers.bio: Dmitrii started iOS development in times when screen size was fixed, UI was skeuomorphic and you were not able to develop for iOS without using tons of square brackets. Since then he worked on various projects in healthcare, tourism, dating services, and e-commerce. Currently, Dmitrii mostly struggles with scalability issues while helping one of the biggest banks in the Netherlands to move its banking app to the next level.

speakers.name: Dmitry Kandalov
speakers.bio: Dmitry has been writing software since DOS times. He spent the last 20 years or so in Java lands, working with server-side Kotlin using Extreme programming practices for the last few years.

speakers.name: Dmytro Polianskyi
speakers.bio:
I’m Dmytro Polianskyi, an E2E Lead / iOS Developer at Salmon, focused on building consumer apps that are flexible, fast to ship, and actually useful to people.

I originally started as a product designer, but taught myself how to code because I wanted to get closer to how products are really built. That path shaped the way I think about engineering: not just as writing clean code, but as designing systems that help teams learn, adapt, and ship better product experiences.

I lived and studied in China, where I studied applied computer science and big data analysis before leaving the country and continuing my career in iOS. My first iOS app was Chinese With Laowai, a language-learning app where I worked on everything from custom UI to NLP, pronunciation practice, and performance-heavy text rendering.

Today, my work sits at the intersection of iOS engineering, product thinking, and cross-functional delivery. I’m especially interested in how SwiftUI architecture, backend contracts, analytics, and team structure can help mobile teams move faster without turning their codebase into chaos.

speakers.name: Dominik Roszkowski
speakers.bio: Dominik is a Google Developer Expert in Flutter, eager to create beautiful apps for mobile and desktop platforms. He’s a Head of Engineering at Visible - a health startup helping people manage complex chronic illnesses using wearable tech. He is an active speaker at local meetups and writes Flutter-related articles on his blog, roszkowski.dev.

speakers.name: Dominik Šimoník
speakers.tagLine: Technical Delivery Lead @ Very Good Ventures | Firebase, Flutter GDE
speakers.bio: Technical Delivery Lead at Very Good Ventures who sets a high bar, pairing clean architecture and strong Flutter skills with AI to build smarter and faster. Working in mobile since 2016, he loves helping startups turn a rough idea into a production-ready product. As a GDE for Firebase and Flutter and a GDG organizer, he mentors, speaks, and organizes events. Outside work, he's into gaming, volleyball, and a good beer.

speakers.name: Douglas Hill
speakers.bio: Douglas spent many years as the iOS team lead at Nutrient (previously known as PSPDFKit) and recently switched to work across a wider range of technologies at Nutrient. He’s a long-time organiser of NSLondon.

speakers.name: Ed Holloway-George
speakers.tagLine: Lead Android Developer @ Kraken Field | Android GDE
speakers.bio:
Ed Holloway-George is an Android Developer and Google Developer Expert originally from Oxford, UK but now currently residing in Nottingham, UK.

An Android developer for over 10 years; Ed now works for Kraken Field as a Mobile Tech Lead having previously worked on well-known applications such as ASOS, National Trust, My Oxfam, Snoop, Carling Tap and many more.

In his spare time, Ed can be found playing trading card games and posting pictures of his dog.

speakers.name: Ed Rooth
speakers.bio: Ed Rooth (aka Hekuli) is a solo developer and visual artist with over 20 years in software. He's the creator of Chromatose, a real-time, shader-based video synthesizer for iOS that he designs, engineers, and ships entirely on his own. A longtime DJ and electronic-music hobbyist, he fell down the real-time-graphics rabbit hole, taught himself Metal, and set out to put a GPU instrument in everyone's pocket.

speakers.name: Eduard Loginov
speakers.bio: Mobile QA Engineer with over 5 years of experience delivering quality for iOS and Android applications. Throughout my career, I've tested products ranging from logistics marketplaces and crypto solutions to banking applications, working with diverse testing frameworks and development teams. I enjoy solving complex quality challenges and sharing practical insights from hands-on experience.

speakers.name: Edward Harker
speakers.bio: Edward is a software engineer formerly at Deliveroo and Shazam. He is passionate about building high-quality mobile apps with a focus on quality, testing and performance.

speakers.name: Eeva-Jonna Panula
speakers.bio: Eeva-Jonna, or Eevis, is an accessibility specialist and senior Android developer. They are also Android GDE. Their passion is to share knowledge, and they speak and write a blog. When they're not doing that, they explore the beautiful Finnish nature either by foot or kayak.

speakers.name: Ekaterina Volkova
speakers.bio: I started as a PMO at Deutsche Telekom before deciding to become an engineer from scratch. Before graduating from Metropolia University, I joined Zalando as an iOS developer — and soon found myself shipping features to millions of users… while quietly wondering if I really belonged. Now, I talk about the parts of tech we don’t always put on LinkedIn.

speakers.name: Eliza Camber
speakers.bio: Eliza is a Staff Android Engineer and GDE alumni with 15+ years of experience building and modernising large-scale Android ecosystems. She began her Android journey in 2013 and has been actively involved in the tech community as a volunteer, organiser, lead, and speaker ever since. In her spare time, she loves travelling, reading, solving puzzles, and taking long walks with her dog.

speakers.name: Ellen Shapiro
speakers.bio: Ellen Shapiro is an iOS and Android developer who's been building native apps since late 2010. She works for Figma on their iOS app. She lives in Rochester, New York. When not coding or talking about coding, Ellen can generally be found traveling, biking and kayaking all over the place, playing sous-chef to her wife Lilia, and relentlessly Instagramming their cats.

speakers.name: Elvira Leveque
speakers.bio:
Elvira is a mobile software engineer, currently working at ING Netherlands. 
She is a true passionate about mobile app development and its power of crafting meaningful experiences, which led her to transition from a design role to a software development one. 
After exploring different stacks, she is now a Flutter enthusiast.

speakers.name: Emil Schoenawa
speakers.tagLine: Android Developer @ SumUp, Free-Time AR Enthusiast
speakers.bio: Android Developer for a Fintech by day, AR Developer refusing to use Unity by night. At SumUp I'm developing for the POS Lite and Android Payment Terminals. In my free time, I enjoy exploring the capabilities of mobile AR and the potential of VR.

speakers.name: Emīls Pļavenieks
speakers.bio:
Self-taught lead full-stack software engineer with focus on building systems that can scale. Coding since early years and keeping the passion of code strong.
Explored the vanilla JavaScript deeply with code golf. Working mainly with Node.js and React since the early releases and have dived into performance depths. I know my PHP, SQL and Go.
Also a husband, father of 2 daughters, motorcycle track racer, coffeeshop owner, multiple hackathon winner. Featured on Times Square billboard for World Paywal Speedbuilding Championship in 2025.

speakers.name: Emma Twersky
speakers.bio: Emma is a DRE at Google. She is passionate about good user experience and design.

speakers.name: Engin Deniz Usta
speakers.bio: I’m a Senior Mobile Engineer at Wolt and the solo founder of Havira (havira.app), a breezy AI video generator for casual users. I love building products end-to-end, experimenting with AI, and occasionally turning those experiments into things people can actually use.

speakers.name: Enzo Conty
speakers.tagLine: Flutter & Dart GDE. Flutter Bordeaux Organizer. CTO at Ezymob
speakers.bio:
Enzo Conty currently serves as the CTO of Ezymob, applying his extensive skills as a Sr. Mobile SWE honed over seven years of freelancing. Renowned for his expertise in Flutter, he has developed numerous innovative applications exploring new platforms such as Steam Deck, embeddable systems, drink distributors and even Steam games.
Enzo also enriches the tech community being a Google Developer Expert (GDE) and organizing the GDG Bordeaux and Flutter Meetup Group Bordeaux.

speakers.name: Erik Hellman
speakers.bio: Erik Hellman has been engineering scalable software systems since 1995. Through his independent consultancy, Hellsoft, his track record includes shaping critical features for Spotify, scaling Husqvarna Automower applications, architecting ICA’s self-scanning platform, and consulting for Google’s WebRTC team. Currently working with Eyedentity AI, Erik also maintains an active role in personal software projects, including indie games and developer tools. He is a regular speaker at international technical conferences, delivering practical insights and battle-tested engineering practices.

speakers.name: Erwin Soekianto
speakers.tagLine: Maps, location, Flutter. Developer Evangelist at Mapbox.
speakers.bio:
Erwin is a Developer Evangelist at Mapbox. He's spent his career shipping location systems across multiple platforms and ecosystem —in-vehicle, mobile, web, and everything in between.

He brings deep experience in location features, navigation systems, and building ecosystems that developers love. At Mapbox, he helps developers bring maps and location to their apps 
with minimal friction.

speakers.name: Esra Kadah
speakers.tagLine: Senior Flutter & AI Engineer, Google Developer Expert, Author, Co-Lead (Flutteristas, Flutter Berlin, Flutter Community AI Circle, GDG Cloud Berlin)
speakers.bio:
Esra Kadah is a Senior Flutter & AI Engineer at Antigua Mobile in Berlin and a Google Developer Expert for Flutter and Dart. She builds production Flutter apps with AI inside them, and shows how on stage.

With more than eight years in app development, she works on large-scale enterprise Flutter apps: architecture, CI/CD automation, automated UI testing and code quality. Her current work brings Gemini, Firebase and on-device models into real apps, from voice features to SoundStage, a six-track audio and video editor built entirely in Flutter.

She is co-author of Flutter Design Patterns & Best Practices (Packt, 2024) with Daria Orlova and Jaime Blasco, and co-leads Flutteristas, Flutter Berlin, the Flutter Community AI Circle and GDG Cloud Berlin. She has spoken at events from Istanbul to Berlin, Paris, Kenya and the U.S.

speakers.name: Evghenii Beriozchin
speakers.bio:
I am Evghenii, a software engineer who worked across web, mobile and XR. As of late, I opened a tiny indie game studio in my home country of Moldova, where we work on our first PC title - Absurdocracy!
I teach CS at the Technical University of Moldova and develop other apps in my free time, mostly in Flutter. Minútes is a collection of mini-games for Android and iOS, which you can check out during your coffee break.
I also like playing games - digital and analogue, learning about social choice and painting while being bad at it!

speakers.name: Fabian Brenner
speakers.bio: Fabian Brenner is a penetration tester at usd AG, where he is responsible for Mobile App Penetration Testing services and plays a key role in advancing this area. During his studies, he focused on secure Android app development and contributed to the development of a vulnerability scanner for mobile apps.

speakers.name: Fabio Giubilo
speakers.tagLine: Android Mobile Apps Reverse Engineer @ BT
speakers.bio: Fabio Giubilo is a security consultant at BT specialising in web and mobile application security, with a strong focus on Android testing and reverse engineering. His work spans practical mobile penetration testing, static and dynamic analysis, and building tooling — and hands-on training challenges — that make assessments more efficient, structured, and evidence-driven. He has a particular interest in Android internals, Frida-based instrumentation, and AI-assisted engineering workflows that turn tester experience into practical offensive-security tools.

speakers.name: Fahim Uddin
speakers.tagLine: iOS/visionOS Developer, MSU Apple Developer Academy. Building spatial computing apps for healthcare.
speakers.bio: I am an iOS developer at the MSU Apple Developer Academy, where I built a production Vision Pro cardiac emergency training simulator in partnership with Henry Ford Health. The app integrates a real-time C++ physiology engine, AHA ACLS-compliant scenarios, and is the only app of its kind on visionOS.

speakers.name: Fatima Khan
speakers.bio: Fatima has spent the last 10+ years working in the SaaS domain through developing solutions, consulting for Mobile Application Security for Fortune 500 companies in Finance, Banking, Healthcare, Mobility and Government domains. She has extensive experience in Mobile Application Security and is currently leading the Mobile AppSec product line.

speakers.name: Felipe Espinoza
speakers.bio:
Chilean developer based in Norway. Felipe started his career working on the backend, mainly with Ruby on Rails. Later, in 2017, he turned his focus to Apple platforms, developing for iOS at work and macOS in his spare time.

Felipe has worked at well-known Norwegian companies such as Hyper, Schibsted, and Finn.no. He is currently the Tech Lead for the iOS app at SATS, the largest fitness chain in the Nordics.

In 2024, he started a YouTube channel called [@CraftingSwift](https://www.youtube.com/@CraftingSwift), where he shares his knowledge and passion for Swift development.

speakers.name: Filip Dolník
speakers.bio: Filip is a Founding Engineer at Ntive Labs, specializing in the development of custom AI agents, the Kotlin compiler and Gradle. His work revolves around improving the Kotlin Multiplatform developer experience. He is best known as a co-author of SKIE, a compiler plugin that generates a Swift-friendly API for Kotlin Native. With a deep passion for compilers, programming languages, and technology in general, Filip is dedicated to pushing the boundaries of what's possible in the Kotlin ecosystem.

speakers.name: Florian Mierzejewski
speakers.bio: Software engineer with 15+ YoE and a strong mobile background. I’ve worked in agencies and startups for widely different clients from various countries, on an even wider range of projects. From greenfield to enormous untested legacy codebases, I’ve seen horror and glory while repeatedly managing to have a positive impact. Eternal learner, you’ll always find me with a book, listening to a podcast, or at a local meetup to improve what I know or discover something I don’t. I aim to always write simple and readable code, apply best practices, share knowledge, pair program, and mentor with a good dose of empathy and compromise.

speakers.name: Francesco Romano
speakers.bio: Developer Relations Engineer for Android @ Google.

speakers.name: Francesco Tamagni
speakers.bio: "Seasoned" software engineer and reverse engineer, focusing mostly on iOS. Sporadic contributor of Frida and radare2.

speakers.name: Francis Ma
speakers.tagLine: Founder @ JoyCrew.ai | AI engineer | Startup builder | ex-Google Sr. Director of Product & Engineering
speakers.bio:
Francis Ma is the founder of JoyCrew, an AI-native startup focused on helping businesses succeed with agentic AI.

Prior to this, he spent nearly 15 years at Google, leading product and engineering teams, including Firebase, a platform beloved by app developers. Before Google, he was a startup founder and engineering lead at Amazon.

He grew up in Canada and holds an engineering degree from the University of Waterloo.  Outside of tech, he loves the craft of making coffee.

speakers.name: Francisco Aguilera
speakers.bio:
Hi there, 

I'm Fran, I've been working on Android for a bit now. I've been focused on performance, shipping reliable apps with massive scale and mobile observability

speakers.name: Franz Nkemaka
speakers.tagLine: CEO Nextise GmbH | Kodschul.com | AI & Automation für den Mittelstand
speakers.bio:
Franz Nkemaka is the CEO & Founder of Nextise GmbH, a Stuttgart-based AI implementation company helping industrial and mid-sized enterprises build and deploy sovereign AI systems, intelligent knowledge platforms, process automation, and modern software solutions.

As an entrepreneur, AI strategist, and technology leader, Franz works at the intersection of artificial intelligence, automation, and software engineering. Through Nextise and its education platform Kodschul, he and his team have trained more than 3,000 professionals—from software developers and IT specialists to department leaders and C-level executives. His work has included training and consulting engagements with organizations such as Deutsche Bahn, TÜV Nord, Deutsche Telekom, Bundeswehr, Big Dutchman, LMV Versicherung, and Austria's Bundesrechenzentrum.

Franz is known for translating complex technologies into practical business outcomes. Drawing from real-world implementation experience, he helps organizations move beyond AI experimentation toward scalable, production-ready solutions. He has also spoken at the Embedded Software Engineering (ESE) Congress, where he presented on Rust for Embedded Systems to industry professionals and decision-makers.

Today, he leads a growing international team of AI specialists, software engineers, and trainers, helping companies apply emerging technologies in ways that create measurable operational and competitive advantages.

His story began in Dschang, Cameroon, where curiosity became the foundation of a lifelong passion for technology. Long before reliable internet access was available, Franz taught himself computer skills through relentless experimentation and self-directed learning. A pivotal breakthrough in 2016 accelerated his journey into software development and entrepreneurship, laying the foundation for the international company he leads today.

Having moved to Germany as a teenager without speaking German and building his career without a formal degree, Franz represents a new generation of technology entrepreneurs who combine technical depth, business execution, and a global perspective.

His mission is simple: empowering businesses and professionals to build scalable, future-proof solutions with AI, automation, and software engineering.

speakers.name: Gabriel Palmisano
speakers.bio:
I am a Mobile Developer at EBWorld and maintainer of the Flutter MapLibre package (maplibre_gl), specialized in building mobile apps with advanced mapping. My mission is to bring geospatial data out of the office: I build Flutter apps that turn complex infrastructure, such as telecom networks or aqueducts, into essential operational tools for the people working out in the field.

I have been writing code since I was very young, driven by a curiosity to explore the limits of the technologies I use. Beyond my work at EBWorld, I actively contribute to open source to improve the tools developers rely on every day. 
As a speaker, I love bringing real-world use cases to the stage, translating complex architectural challenges into practical solutions for the community.

speakers.name: Gabriel Volpi
speakers.bio:
I am an Android Software Engineer with over 5 years of experience building large-scale mobile applications, currently working at iFood, one of the largest food delivery platforms in the world. As part of the Order Delivery team, I work on critical flows that impact millions of users, with a strong focus on performance, scalability, monitoring, reliability, and product-driven engineering.

My recent work has focused on Edge AI and on-device machine learning, exploring how Android’s ML Kit Prompt APIs, AICore, and generative models can be used to turn AI capabilities into real product experiences. I am especially interested in the trade-offs between cloud and on-device AI, including latency, privacy, cost, scalability, and user value.

I hold a degree in Control and Automation Engineering from UNICAMP and I am currently pursuing a postgraduate degree in Software Engineering. I am also actively involved in the Android community, sharing practical experiences about mobile architecture, production monitoring, and on-device AI. Most recently, I presented at AndroidMakers by Droidcon Paris, discussing practical approaches to bringing Edge AI into production-grade Android applications.

speakers.name: Gabriele Romagnoli
speakers.bio: Gabriele Romagnoli is the founder of XR AI Spotlight, a platform with the mission of bringing focus, depth, and perspective to XR and AI. He Gabriele began his VR journey in 2015 and built a professional reputation in the XR world as an expert in design and UX for immersive experiences. Since then he has been sharing daily his findings and hands-on experiences about the latest tech for creatives and professionals and helping founders identify and communicate the value their experiences provide to clients, users, and the general public. He gathered an engaged community of over 50K followers across various social media platforms and keeps learning, researching, and sharing about how 3D, XR, AI and Gaussian Splatting will impact creatives and professionals. His passion for the intersection between creativity and technology brought him to several international stages to inspire audiences and share his vision of how technology will a meaningful impact on creativity and productivity RIGHT NOW.

speakers.name: Gautier de Lataillade
speakers.bio: Flutter developer with 7+ years building mobile apps, and maintainer of several open-source Flutter packages. At L+R, I work on spatial and wearables experiences: Meta Ray-Ban smart glasses and Meta Quest with the Meta Spatial SDK.

speakers.name: Georgie Steele
speakers.bio:
Georgie Steele is a second-time founder and engineering leader building AI products for high-stakes, regulated environments. She is currently founding a new venture in fintech and wealth management, building agents that behave reliably in production and tackling problems few have solved: long-horizon memory under tight context budgets, low-latency systems, and earning trust in a heavily regulated space.

Previously, Georgie was Co-Founder and CTO of Maiven, a climate tech startup making complex regulation actionable with AI, where she raised £1.5M pre-seed in two weeks and shipped the MVP two months later.

An award-winning engineer recognised by Forbes 30 Under 30, she has led high-impact technical teams across McLaren, Tractable, and Sylvera, scaling backend platforms tenfold and contributing to a unicorn valuation.

She is also a committed advocate for diversity in tech, having mentored over 100 underrepresented technologists and represented UN Women UK at the UN Commission on the Status of Women.

Georgie speaks on building trustworthy AI products, agents in production, and what engineering leadership actually requires in the AI era.

speakers.name: Gerard Paligot
speakers.bio: Father and husband · Google Developer Expert for Android · Senior Android Engineer at DuckDuckGo · DevLille organizer · Disney Fan!

speakers.name: Ghasem Bakhtiari
speakers.tagLine: Senior Principal Software Engineer at Zalando
speakers.bio: Based in Berlin, Ghasem Bakhtiari is a Senior Principal Software Engineer at Zalando. He is currently spearheading the company's React Native migration, driving a robust, cross-platform client foundation across web, Android, and iOS at scale, with a focus on integrating Zalando’s custom "Rendering Engine" React framework into mobile ecosystems. Ghasem is deeply passionate about platform engineering and building intuitive, reusable solutions that empower massive engineering teams.

speakers.name: Gian Sandoval
speakers.tagLine: Software Architect | Flutter & React Native Expert | AI Agent Systems | Founder of Flutter Piura
speakers.bio:
Gian Sandoval is a Software Architect with over 9 years of experience designing and delivering scalable mobile, web, and backend solutions across industries including banking, fintech, transportation, tourism, healthcare, and startups.

He specializes in Flutter, React Native, React, Node.js, Firebase, and Google Cloud, applying Clean Architecture, modular design, and engineering best practices to build high-quality products used by thousands of users.

Currently, Gian leads frontend initiatives in one of the largest banking environments in Latin America, focusing on large-scale mobile architectures, enterprise design systems, performance, and team scalability.

Beyond his professional work, he is the Founder of Flutter Piura, a Google-recognized developer community dedicated to empowering developers through education, mentorship, and technology events.

His current areas of interest include AI-powered applications, Agentic Systems, Software Architecture, Mobile Engineering, and building the next generation of intelligent digital platforms.

speakers.name: Gianfranco Papa
speakers.bio:
I’m a Flutter Developer, Passionate Software Engineer, and Football Fanatic in my spare time. I’m CTO & Co-Founder of Somnio Software, a 100% specialized Flutter Company based in Uruguay. 

I’m really passionate about technology in general but Flutter & Dart are my top choices. I’ve focused on becoming an expert in these technologies to have the best tools to help our partners with their projects!

I’m also co-organizer of Flutter Uruguay Meetup to help grow the community of this tech both in our country and also in the world. This group has helped me unite with other developers and Flutter fanatics to exchange experiences and ideas!

speakers.name: Gianluca Veschi
speakers.bio:
I’ve been working as an Android Developer since late 2019, witnessing the evolution of the platform from the final days of Java to the latest wave of AI-driven features. 

My journey has started in Shanghai and has later led me to work in Paris and Berlin, where I currently work.  I’ve built products in diverse sectors, from ecommerce (Douglas) to fintech (Qonto, Trade Republic). This broad international experience has given me a unique perspective on both the technical and cultural aspects of mobile development.

I now work in a hybrid role at GetYourGuide where I work both on the Android Platform and the Backend one, which is fully written in Typescript.

speakers.name: Gil Megidish
speakers.bio:
Founder at Mobile Next
Former Co-founder and CTO of TestFairy
Former Architect of Mobile Device Cloud at Sauce Labs
Hacker by heart
https://github.com/gmegidish

speakers.name: Gio Scalzo
speakers.bio: Gio Scalzo is a London-based AI and engineering lead at NewDay and CTO of a set of consumer AI apps, including Pocket Sommelier (AI wine pairing) and the AI-driven wellness apps Neurona and Selena. A published author of seven books, he spends much of his time exploring what happens when AI meets real engineering work. He speaks regularly at communities such as NSLondon and Londroid and, more recently, at the LDX3 New York conference, ships AI products, and is especially interested in the gap between impressive demos and messy production reality.

speakers.name: Giovanni Laquidara
speakers.bio:
Giovanni Laquidara is a Senior Dev Advocate at Amazon, where he works on supporting developers around the world using the Amazon Appstore across many devices. Previously, Giovanni worked as a software engineer building mobile apps, real-time defense systems, and VR/AR experiences. For fun, Giovanni enjoys low level programming, IoT hacking and Dancing Bachata around the world 🕺

You can connect with Giovanni on Twitter, Linkedin, and giolaq.dev.

speakers.name: Giuseppe Franco
speakers.tagLine: Software Engineer & AI Startup Founder @ HGB Solutions Oy
speakers.bio:
Giuseppe Franco is an engineering leader with over 10 years of experience building enterprise mobile security platforms and leading distributed teams in cybersecurity environments.

He has led platform development and engineering initiatives focused on reliability, scalability, and long-term product ownership. In parallel, he co-founded HGB Solutions Oy, where he is building Palautus AI — applying the same principles in a startup environment.

His current work focuses on integrating AI into real-world workflows and understanding how it changes the way software systems and organizations operate.

speakers.name: Gleb Tarasov
speakers.bio: iOS engineer with 15 years of experience, including 7 years at Booking.com. Working across Mobile Platforms, leading and shaping the core app foundation and infrastructure that supports over 200 mobile developers and powers an app used by millions of users worldwide.

speakers.name: Grace Yan
speakers.tagLine: Head of Mobile Development - Growth/Activation at 1&1 Mail and Media
speakers.bio: Grace Yan leads Mobile Development for Growth/Activation at 1&1. She's been shipping mobile apps — iOS, Android, all of it — for years, and cares a lot about building teams that actually enjoy the work.

speakers.name: Grant Douglas
speakers.bio:
Grant has over 15 years of mobile security specialism and has built and contributed to open source mobile security tooling. Grant has worked in both engineering and red team roles and has worked on multiple SAST & DAST mobile security products. 

Grant now spends most of his time reversing advanced mobile anti-tamper, and building robust mobile anti-tamper defences.

speakers.name: Gustavo Gomes
speakers.bio:
I am an Android developer for over a decade now, having worked  in both consultancy and product companies. I love to learn new things and also thinker around outside of just my domains.

Currently I have jumped on the AI wave, but mainly focused on how to run models locally for efficiency and data privacy.

speakers.name: Gustavo Guzman
speakers.tagLine: Freelance Software Developer | Operations & Technology lead @ DDB EXPRESS
speakers.bio:
I’m a Freelance Software Developer with experience across very different environments, from early-stage startups to large corporate projects with teams of more than 30 developers.

I’ve worked on products at different stages of maturity, from building new ideas from scratch to contributing to complex systems already used at scale. Today, I work independently with companies on software products while also building my own projects.

I’m especially interested in open source, simple architectures, and developer experience. I enjoy experimenting with new ideas, building tools, and understanding how software can be made simpler, clearer, and easier to maintain.

speakers.name: Halle Winkler
speakers.bio: Halle Winkler is a veteran indie software engineer and end-user privacy advocate, who became an offensive security researcher and a consulting application security engineer for Apple platforms. She is a Certified Ethical Hacker, with 12 Apple Security credits spanning all Apple devices, and publishes the [Berlin Bassline Brief](https://buttondown.com/Halle/archive/) security newsletter. Previously, she brought offline speech recognition to iOS with OpenEars. She lives in Kreuzberg, Berlin and secretly adores it, but don't let it get around.

speakers.name: Hannah Downey
speakers.tagLine: Software Engineering Team Lead @ BBC | International Tech Conference Speaker | App Store Entrepreneur
speakers.bio: Hannah is a mobile engineer turned team lead, with experience ranging from iOS and Android to large-scale backend systems. As a software engineering team lead, she's currently focused on mobile BFFs and bridging the gap between client and server for the BBC Sounds product. Her native apps are available on the App Store and the Play Store and she is an international tech conference speaker.

speakers.name: Hanno Gödecke
speakers.bio:
- I've been an app developer by heart ever since
- Build my first mobile apps when I was 11 y.o to cheat in mobile games
- Police was ringing at my door when I was 14 y.o. because of an illegal movie streaming app I built
- 1 year later I built an app that gained over 2 million downloads (it was basically Spotify's UI but with music from YouTube ... also slightly illegal but it survived longer).
- React Native enthusiast for over a decade now, building the best mobile apps @margelo

speakers.name: Harny Otuoniyo
speakers.bio:
Harny has a knack for solving high technical problems and currently enjoys doing this in the mobile domain, he is passionate about automation, architecture at scale, state that stays predictable, and the observability and experimentation that reveal what production is really doing. 
Beyond his technical expertise, he loves the thrills of traveling, enjoys cooking and is always up for dancing.

speakers.name: Hasan Hosgel
speakers.bio:
Hasan Hoşgel is a dedicated Android developer with professional programming experience since 2003. Since 2010 doing all-day Android application development and was from 2016 to 2019 a Google Developer Expert for Android.
Continuous improvement of the architecture, performance, and quality is his dedication.
He works for T-Systems. Beforehand, he worked for companies like MHP - A Porsche Company, LAB1886 - The Incubator of Daimler AG, ImmobilienScout24 & Kitchen Stories.
As a former co-organizer of the "GDG Berlin Android" and as a speaker, he attended many conferences and several Google Developer Groups across Europe. As well being in program committees and organized conferences.

speakers.name: Håvard Sørbø
speakers.bio: Håvard Sørbø is an iOS Security Researcher at NowSecure and an active Frida contributor, focusing on low-level iOS dynamic analysis and custom runtime instrumentation.

speakers.name: Haydar Sahin
speakers.bio: Haydar Sahin is a Technology Consultant at Netlight with a passion for building digital products that users enjoy using. Combining strategic consulting, hands-on software engineering, and technical leadership, he has helped organizations across e-commerce, automotive, and media deliver high-quality user experiences. He is particularly interested in AI-assisted engineering and the practical application of emerging technologies to create smarter products and empower development teams.

speakers.name: Hemal Bodasing
speakers.bio:
Hemal Bodasing is an award-winning XR developer and creative technologist with over 20 years of experience across the creative, corporate, and defence sectors. He currently works hands-on with glove hardware and firmware integration at StretchSense, building on a career that spans VR, AR and mixed reality development for a variety of platforms.

Earlier in his career, Hemal worked in R&D at Sony Computer Entertainment Europe, and as a games developer at various studios before moving into XR. Since then, he has delivered projects for the defence, healthcare, energy, and creative industries, including a mixed-reality collaboration system for defence applications and award-winning interactive installations featured at festivals and museums.

Hemal has extensive experience interfacing hardware such as motion sensors and depth cameras with real-time software systems and is also an experienced mentor.

speakers.name: Henni Wiesner
speakers.tagLine: Graphic Designer, Web Developer, Composer, Solo Developer @ It’s just Letters
speakers.bio:
I love typography, games, and music—so I make my own. My name is Henni and I’m a professional graphic designer and hobbyist game dev, running my own type foundry.

The games I made or were part of making can be found here:
https://riekay.itch.io

speakers.name: Himanshu Singh
speakers.bio: Himanshu is a Full Stack Kotlin Engineer specializing in Android development. Recognized as a Google Developer Expert (GDE) for Android, he is an active speaker and content creator. Passionate about community building, Himanshu loves mentoring aspiring developers and helping them transition into the tech world.

speakers.name: Hugo Drumond Jacob
speakers.bio: Hugo is a Software Engineer at Google, where he led the release engineering team behind the successful launch of the AAOS SDV architecture. In his current role, he partners with OEMs and SoC vendors to streamline the AAOS platform integration, optimizing for performance, quality, and time-to-market. He brings extensive prior engineering experience from both the automotive and medical sectors.

speakers.name: Hugo Guillaume
speakers.bio: Hugo Guillaume is a security engineer and researcher. He spent close to three years on offensive and defensive security research in a government national-defense setting, doing vulnerability research and reverse engineering and building automated bug-discovery systems (fuzzing, concolic execution, and reinforcement learning). His work includes published CVEs and open-source releases. He also teaches cybersecurity at a university in France. He currently works on application security at Konvu.

speakers.name: Ian Leshan
speakers.tagLine: Creating delightful UI in Compose @ sinasamaki
speakers.bio: Android developer with a passion for building creative UI

speakers.name: Ido Priel
speakers.bio: Ido drives HARMAN’s Ready Link Marketplace (in‑vehicle experiences) in the automotive software space. A senior product professional with over 10 years at HARMAN, he has worked across multiple automotive software domains and now focuses on building scalable app ecosystems for software‑defined vehicles, collaborating closely with global OEMs and cross‑functional teams.

speakers.name: Ilya Savin
speakers.bio: Engineering Manager with 10+ years in mobile and product engineering. I started as an Android engineer, still care deeply about the craft, and now spend a lot of my time helping teams use AI in practical ways: speeding up delivery, cutting busywork, and making room for better product thinking. I like building things that are useful, polished, and actually make it into customers’ hands.

speakers.name: Ioannis Anifantakis
speakers.bio:
Hi, I am Ioannis, a Google Developer Expert for Android and a Software Engineer whose 25-year industry journey began in Windows Desktop Development and Database Design, and it has evolved into mobile engineering, where I developed a strong passion for Android, Kotlin Multiplatform, and modern software architecture.

Since 2016, I have been an active Technology Events Speaker, frequently speaking at developer conferences in Greece and internationally. My talks focus on Android, Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, Google technologies, and software engineering.

I am also a dedicated Computer Science Educator and content creator, committed to lifelong learning and knowledge sharing. Through my YouTube channel and Medium.com articles, I create educational content that helps developers better understand Android, Machine Learning, and programming concepts.

speakers.name: Ipek Erten
speakers.bio: Ipek is a product designer and creative coder from Istanbul, blending a background in Architecture and Communication Design. She is passionate about motion design and app development. She began her iOS journey at the Apple Developer Academy in Naples and has since been building apps across Apple platforms. When she's not crafting, she enjoys travelling and chasing down the best sfogliatella in Naples.

speakers.name: Irmela Göhl
speakers.bio:
Irmela is a Berlin-based engineering leader with 13+ years across the stack, from Rails, Go, and TypeScript backends to Flutter mobile apps. She has led teams in healthcare integrations and home energy management, and worked as a senior engineer at Shopify.

For most of the last seven years she has worked in leadership while staying close to the code. She cares about diverse teams, clean code, performance, and user experience.

speakers.name: Isabelle Andreani
speakers.tagLine: Awarded Writer-Director and Lecturer, XR narratives, UX, real-time 3D Animation @ ANIMA concepting
speakers.bio:
As a Writer and Director for new media and immersive technologies, I write and design narrative experiences such as Nana Lou, awarded animated and interactive film for virtual reality produced by SMALL Creative / Skill Lab / France Télévisions.
A specialist in new media, I also support creators, producers and institutions in the production of their digital formats, and I teach XR storytelling at university.
Trained as an engineer and researcher in Physics, followed by a Master's degree in New Technology Management, I built my career around the Digital Tech between the United States and Europe, successively developing skills in software development, marketing, entrepreneurship, and production. I have been innovating in the creation of interactive content and digital experiences for over 25 years .

Latest Works
>> Nana Lou 2024 - VR animated and interactive tale - Duration : 35 minutes
*European XR Award 2024 - Best User Experience
*Selections in competition - 2024 : Annecy Festival, Venice Biennale, Animateka, Thessaloniki, Stereopsia - 2025 : Lux Film Fest, Kaboom, Anifilm, Anibar, Animest, Clermont Ferrand, Fivars, Guanajato, Kaohsiung, Lëtzebuerger Filmprais

>>Last Night - 2019/2021/2022/2024 - A comics series for Instagram about the neuroscience of addiction

speakers.name: Isak van der Walt
speakers.bio:
I've been taking things apart for as long as I can remember and only later learned how to put them back together. 
Previously did R&D, CAD draughting, basic electronics, software development and linux sysadmin work. 
I have been working at Orange Cyberdefense for the last 3+ years, with a particular interest in mobile and embedded security.
Recently I mostly worked on red/purple team, laptop and other specialised assessments.

speakers.name: István Juhos
speakers.bio: Staff Android Engineer @ Spoke; Co-organizer of Android Budapest

speakers.name: Iulia Stana
speakers.bio:
First computer owned: Intel running Windows 3.1.
First programming language: Pascal.
First time I realised being a [good] programmer is (way) more about being able to work well with other people than writing code: late 2010,  aprox. 3 years after starting to work as a programmer.
Since then I've made "Learn. Develop. Teach." my mantra and tried my best to live up to it.

speakers.name: Iury Souza
speakers.bio:
I'm a GDE for Android with over 10 years of hands-on experience with most of the mobile tech stack.
Curiosity driven, tinkering with computers and building things.

speakers.name: Ivan Leider
speakers.tagLine: Software Engineering, Teaching and Managing @ L+R
speakers.bio: Ivan Leider is the Director of Engineering at L+R, where he leads the engineering teams responsible for L+R's spatial computing, mobile, and emerging technology practices. With a career in mobile development stretching back to the launch of the App Store in 2008, Leider has overseen the development of cross-functional applications used by millions of people worldwide. He was selected to represent L+R at Apple's invitation-only Vision Pro Developer Labs in London and has been featured by Meta in coverage of L+R's spatial computing work, including the Media View project launched at Meta Connect. He has spoken publicly on XR readiness, the future of human-computer interaction, and the role of pragmatic engineering in bringing emerging technology to mainstream adoption.

speakers.name: Ivanna Kaceviča
speakers.tagLine: GDE in Flutter and Dart, Lead Software Engineer (Mobile, IoT)
speakers.bio: Ivanna is a Google Developer Expert in Flutter and Dart and a Lead Software Engineer at LMT (Latvijas Mobilais Telefons), Latvia's first and largest mobile telecommunications operator, where she contributes her expertise to building mobile apps in the field of innovations and IoT. Over the past couple of years, she has won three coding scholarship competitions and several contests, ranging from small community-organized events to large hackathons hosted by companies like Google, securing the Grand Prize in both the Flutter Global Gamers Challenge and the Google Cloud NCAA March Madness Competition. She got into Flutter during the global pandemic in 2020 and released her first indie app that same year. Outside of coding, Ivanna enjoys cinema, travel, and cappuccinos.

speakers.name: Iwo Plaza
speakers.tagLine: Lead Developer of TypeGPU @ Software Mansion
speakers.bio:
Iwo Plaza is a software engineer & artist, trying to incorporate art into every project he gets his hands on. He's passionate about graphics programming and softening the learning curve for future developers trying to get into it.

He is currently working at Software Mansion on an experimental graphics utility library called TypeGPU that promises advanced TypeScript and WebGPU interoperability.

speakers.name: Jackson Hardaker
speakers.bio: Jackson is a Founding Engineer at bitdrift, building high-performance observability and crash reporting systems. A frontend specialist at heart, Jackson managed to successfully dodge the complexities of Android development—right up until he was voluntold to start thinking about WebView instrumentation. Based in Beacon, NY, he spends his downtime quietly plotting a future rotisserie chicken empire.

speakers.name: Jacob Ras
speakers.bio: I'm an Android/Kotlin Multiplatform engineer with almost fifteen years of experience in native Android development. Next to my full-time job I work on my own apps, which have over a million downloads.

speakers.name: Jacobo Casado de Gracia
speakers.bio:
Jacobo Casado de Gracia is a Senior Security Evaluator with experience on vulnerability research and penetration testing on a wide variety of software and hardware appliances. Regarding Mobile Security, he has participated in EMVCo projects to evaluate SBMP (Software-Based Mobile Payment) applications.

As part of its work, he contributes to the OWASP Mobile Application Security project, with a particular focus on the evolution of MASTG v2 and MASVS-RESILIENCE. Their work includes tests, techniques, best practices, and runnable demonstrations covering anti-debugging, emulator and virtual-device detection, runtime instrumentation detection, obfuscation, and application integrity controls.

speakers.name: Jade Emmanuel
speakers.tagLine: Senior Data & AI Consultant | Data & Insights Advisor
speakers.bio:
Jade Emmanuel works at the intersection of data, AI systems, engineering, and business strategy focusing on how organisations turn AI capability into systems that actually deliver value.

She partners with teams to design and scale AI systems in production, combining technical depth with a strong focus on how systems and people behave in real organisational contexts and decisions are made, from navigating complex architectures and driving transformation through emerging AI capabilities, to how teams learn, experiment and operate at scale.

Her work is grounded in a simple observation: most AI initiatives don’t fail because of the technology, but because of how systems and organisations are designed around it. 

She focuses on closing that gap with practical, system-level approaches that engineering and leadership teams can apply directly to achieve meaningful outcomes.

speakers.name: Jaewoong Eum
speakers.bio: A Google Developer Expert (GDE) for Android and Firebase. He has created over 100 open-source libraries and projects, which collectively achieve more than 40 million downloads annually by developers worldwide. An author of the Manifest Android Interview book.

speakers.name: Jaime Blasco
speakers.bio: Jaime is a Google Developer Expert focused on Flutter. He has created and currently maintains some useful and popular packages related to this toolkit. He is a very active member of the community and co-leads the Spaniard Flutter Community.

speakers.name: Jakub Fijałkowski
speakers.bio: Head of Backend at LeanCode, but he sometimes dresses up as a Flutter Developer to support mobile teams. He brings backend architectural best practices into the mobile world, helping teams tackle complex challenges with a fresh perspective. In his free time, he enjoys watching golf and balancing it out by headbanging at metal gigs.

speakers.name: Jakub Grzywacz
speakers.bio: Jakub is a Software Developer on the Expo SDK team and a maintainer of react-native-svg in React Native Open Source team. He contributes to the Expo and React Native ecosystem by maintaining libraries and working with the community.

speakers.name: Jakub Tkacz
speakers.bio: Jakub is a software engineer at Expo, where he maintains Expo Router and works on Expo Observe. Before joining Expo, he worked on several React Native projects and helped maintain React Native Screens.

speakers.name: James Cullimore
speakers.tagLine: Freelance Android Developer @ James Cullimore - Software Engineering
speakers.bio:
● Software / Application / Mobile Developer with experience in Java, Kotlin, Android, Web & Fullstack Development
● Creator of open source projects such as StreamingYorkie, blackforest-woodburnings.de & Lazy Shortcuts
● Developer of hansgrohe home, hansgrohe SmartExpert, farmerJoe & lexoffice
● Software development freelancer & technology hobbyist
● Android Instructor & Independent Writer
● Extensive knowledge in new technologies with keenness to learn more

● Married with 2 children
● MMA enthusiast

speakers.name: James Gatt
speakers.bio: James Gatt is an AOSP Engineer based in Malta, currently pursuing an MSc in Microelectronics and Microsystems. He is the founder of the PixelBuilds custom ROM distribution and has recently expanded his expertise into Android app development using Kotlin and Jetpack Compose. With a BSc in Computer Engineering from the University of Malta, James also specializes in Embedded systems and practical IoT applications.

speakers.name: James Seconde
speakers.bio: A trained actor with a curious background: from Theatre Studies, to Q/A, to Business Intelligence development, to full stack web development, I am the resident specialist PHP Developer Advocate at Global Cloud Communications giant Vonage. I founded Birmingham, UK's current PHP usergroup BrumPHP, as well as being on the Fusion Meetup team. I mentor, write and speak on PHP, Javascript, DevOps, DevRel and tech culture. I pretended to be a DJ on the way.

speakers.name: Jan Kubovy
speakers.bio: Jan is a research and development engineer and Android expert focused on software-defined vehicles, vehicle data platforms, and cross-OEM interoperability. His work centers on extending Android Automotive, standardization of vehicle interfaces and enabling scalable, secure, and developer-friendly vehicle ecosystems.

speakers.name: Jan Rabe
speakers.bio: I lead native app development at CHECK24 Profis in Berlin. 15 years of mobile development across Android and iOS, 30+ app projects, and enough opinions to fill a conference talk, although hopefully wise enough to know when to let them go. I build tools, lead teams, and raise a toddler who is teaching me more about graceful failure recovery than any production incident ever did.

speakers.name: Jan Jaap de Groot
speakers.bio: Jan Jaap has been developing (accessible) apps for 10 years. Since 2018, Jan Jaap has specialized in making apps accessible by supporting accessibility features and assistive technologies. He leads the W3C Mobile Accessibility Task Force, is a chair of the Appt Foundation, and is co-founder of Abra; where he builds software to automatically detect accessibility issues in apps.

speakers.name: Janina Kutyn
speakers.bio: Janina Kutyn has worked across the tech spectrum: from scrappy startups to global brands like adidas and ING, and she even spent six years at Apple building products like Apple Music and the TV App. Now as an indie developer, she’s interested in creating apps that are not only beautiful and high-performing, but also make a positive social impact. When she’s not writing software, she’s writing children’s books.

speakers.name: Jason Davenport
speakers.bio:
Jason is an Area Technical Lead at Google Cloud. He is the overall Tech Lead for information experience, developer relations, and frameworks and languages. He focuses on applied generative AI in coding and software development, including AI in the SDLC, integration with AI in business transformation, and forward-looking trends in AI. His background is in data engineering, software engineering, and DevOps.

Prior to his current role at Google, Jason held various roles in technical leadership and management, including serving as a practice director for a regional consultancy.

speakers.name: Jay Meistrich
speakers.bio: He builds Legend State and Legend List to make React and React Native apps faster and easier. Previously at EA Games and Microsoft he's now a performance obsessed web and mobile developer. He's been a digital nomad since 2012, and enjoys photography and long walks through interesting places.

speakers.name: Jens Gyselinck
speakers.tagLine: freelance software engineer at diskwriter and spectrum22, organizer of the Flutter Belgium Meetups
speakers.bio:
Started working with Flutter in 2018 when I attended a Flutter Belgium meetup. Working full-time with Flutter since 2019. Co-organising the Flutter Belgium meetups.
In my spare time I enjoy bouldering, rock climbing and playing music.

speakers.name: Jesper Bellenbaum
speakers.bio: As a UX engineer and researcher, he combines hands-on development with deep insights into user behaviour to create transformative digital experiences.

speakers.name: Jessica Randall
speakers.bio:
Jessica Randall is a Master's graduate in Mathematics, an Android developer Co-lead at Mentorlst, and a Zindi Ambassador. Deeply immersed in the world of Android development, she is passionate about Kotlin and Jetpack Compose, thriving in the collaborative environment of Android Studio.

She applies her background in data science and Topological Data Analysis to address complex societal issues. As a Zindi Ambassador, she advocates for data science and machine learning, empowering others to solve real-world problems through technology.

As an organizer for GDG Cape Town, she fosters local developer communities and shapes impactful tech events in South Africa. Her journey as a Google Crowdsource Influencer sparked her interest in AI and Machine Learning, fueling her continuous learning. A forward-thinker, she is an inspiring figure in the ever-evolving tech landscape.

speakers.name: Joaquin Fernandez
speakers.tagLine: OneSpan, Sr Director Product Manager AppSec
speakers.bio:
I've spent more than a decade protecting mobile apps from threats that live on the device itself. I co-founded Build38, a company focused on mobile application protection, and ran it as COO until OneSpan acquired it. 
At OneSpan I now lead Product Management for AppSec. I work on how apps can defend themselves against tampering, reverse engineering and runtime attacks, and on what comes next in application security.

speakers.name: Jonas Jensen
speakers.bio: Jonas has been works on pub.dev and Dart package eco-system.

speakers.name: Jonas Menesklou
speakers.bio: Jonas Menesklou is the co-founder and CEO of AskUI, an innovative tech startup specializing in AI-powered automation solutions. With a background in software development and entrepreneurship, he is driven by the vision of creating a new generation of QA agents that can visually understand and control applications—regardless of the operating system. His passion lies in combining technology and efficiency to radically simplify the use of digital tools.

speakers.name: Jonas Uekötter
speakers.bio:
Jonas is a passionate senior engineer, working at Wolt/DoorDash.
Next to his work as an engineer, he also enjoys sharing knowledge through talks, blogs and as a guest in podcast.

speakers.name: Joo hyun Lee
speakers.bio: Joo hyun Lee is an independent product designer and UX engineer based in Berlin, working from product questions through research, design and implementation. Joo hyun's recent work centers on conversational avatar-based VR, exploring how effects demonstrated in research can be translated into lightweight implementations that work on commercial standalone headsets. Joo hyun focuses on turning insight into practical design and technical decisions that hold up in real-world products, with a background in communication design, UX research, and software engineering.

speakers.name: Jorge Coca
speakers.tagLine: Head of Engineering, Very Good Ventures | Google Developer Expert in Flutter
speakers.bio:
