He is a Google Developer Expert for Cloud, AI, Firebase, Flutter, and Dart, co-organizes the Flutter Berlin Community, and is a recognized international speaker and writer, having presented at 30+ conferences worldwide.

speakers.name: Satyajit Sahoo
speakers.tagLine: Software Engineer @ Callstack | Open Source Maintainer
speakers.bio: Satya is the creator and maintainer of numerous open-source libraries, including React Navigation, React Native Paper, React Native Builder Bob, and Linaria. When not coding, Satya enjoys cooking and playing video games.

speakers.name: Saverio Labella
speakers.bio:
Systems Architect and Team Leader with 15+ years experience in Systems Architecture, Requirements Management,
Software Design & Development for Telecom and Real-Time Embedded Systems.
Broad experience in Android from framework and Android Automotive OS application development.

speakers.name: Sebastian Aigner
speakers.bio: As a Kotlin and Compose Multiplatform Developer Advocate at JetBrains, Sebastian spends a lot of time thinking about how technology can advance and inspire people. When he first tried Kotlin, it was love at first sight. He is one of the hosts of the Talking Kotlin podcast, and creates videos for the official Kotlin YouTube channel. Sebastian loves to develop networked applications, uses Kotlin on a variety of platforms, and passionately tinkers on his programs until late into the night.

speakers.name: Sébastien Poivre
speakers.bio:
Sébastien Poivre is an XR and multiplayer developer working for Photon Engine. He’s always focused on merging a software craftmanship approach, with a strong attention on user experience. First for end-user, on iOS technologies during 8 years, and then on immersive technologies for 9 years. 

Recently, this focus turned to the immersive developers’ user experience, preparing simple tools and samples for Photon’s developer customers, while supporting them in their more advanced requests.

speakers.name: Sepehr Ghasemi
speakers.bio: Sepehr Ghasemi is a Unity software engineer based in Germany, hands-on with the engine since 2018, with 4 years of professional experience across XR and mobile games. He started at an early-stage startup, where he shipped XR mobile games on iOS, Android, and Meta Quest. Since then his work has spanned the range of the Unity ecosystem: multiplayer VR on Quest, an AI-driven app on Apple Vision Pro, and multiplayer mobile projects, usually with end-to-end ownership, from client architecture to backend. He cares a lot about architecture that survives team growth, code you can actually test, and systems that keep working when the network doesn't.

speakers.name: Sergey Yamshchikov
speakers.bio: Sergey Yamshchikov is a Senior Android Engineer at League with 9+ years of experience building consumer apps at companies including Scout24, Oviva, and Quandoo. Currently leading his team's adoption of coding agents and AI-assisted development workflows. He is the author of DTA (Development Tools for Android), an open-source MCP server that gives AI agents direct access to Android device internals — UI hierarchy, network traffic, and mocking. Sergey previously open-sourced Rikki (a BDD verification framework presented at Berlin GDG 2019) and the platform_proxy Flutter plugin.

speakers.name: Sergi Alvarez
speakers.tagLine: Mobile Security Research Engineer at NowSecure
speakers.bio: Pancake has more than 25 years of experience in the reverse engineering and security fields. Author and maintainer of radare2, r2frida and other plugins around the radare ecosystem, he began working as a forensic analyst, but moved to other roles as embedded system developer, software developer, optimizing codecs in assembly for a variety of architectures.

speakers.name: Sergio Garcia Cabrera
speakers.bio:
Sergio García is a security researcher specializing in reverse engineering, low-level security, and mobile application security. His work focuses on analyzing and evaluating complex software using static and dynamic analysis techniques, with extensive experience across tools and frameworks such as Binary Ninja, JADX, Frida, Qiling, and AFL++.

In recent years, he has focused primarily on mobile security, working extensively with Android and iOS as well as specialized commercial platforms. His areas of expertise include reverse engineering, dynamic instrumentation, and the analysis and bypass of advanced software protection mechanisms.

speakers.name: Sergio Sastre Flórez
speakers.bio:
Google Developer Expert for Android with 11+ years of experience, currently consulting for Deutsche Bahn Systel. He's worked for other well-known companies such as Check24, Liferando, AutoScout24, and Hermes Germany.

He is a passionate advocate for software testing and has authored numerous blog posts on the matter.

He has also contributed to open-source libraries on Android UI testing like KasperskyLab/Kaspresso and authored others, like Android Screenshot Testing Playground, which won a Google Open Source Peer Bonus award in 2024.

When not coding, he enjoys playing sports like football, running, rollerblading or snowboarding in the mountains.

He  loves challenges and making things happen.

speakers.name: Serhii Buvaka
speakers.tagLine: Head of Android Development @ Salmon Bank Inc.
speakers.bio: I’m the Head of Android Development at Salmon, a digital bank in Southeast Asia. Over the past four years, I’ve built and scaled the Android team while leading the development of mobile banking products used by hundreds of thousands of customers. Before Salmon, I worked on payment and banking products at Yandex and Tinkoff, and co-authored the Android course at Yandex Practicum. My interests include engineering leadership, software architecture, testing strategies, and applying AI to software development.

speakers.name: Seth Webster
speakers.tagLine: Executive Director, React Foundation | Chief Developer Advocate, Expo
speakers.bio:
Seth Webster is a technology executive, software architect, and community leader best known for his work advancing the modern React ecosystem and helping shape the future of cross-platform application development. He currently serves as Executive Director of the React Foundation and Chief Developer Evangelist at Expo, where he focuses on the intersection of AI, developer tooling, and the future of native software experiences.

Over the course of more than two decades in engineering leadership, Seth has built a reputation as a deeply technical leader with a people-first philosophy. He previously led React at Meta, helping steward one of the most widely used UI technologies in the world. His work has centered on enabling developers to move faster, build better products, and bring ambitious ideas to life at global scale.

Seth is known for his ability to bridge technology, product vision, and storytelling. He has led initiatives spanning open source governance, platform strategy, developer experience, AI-native tooling, and large-scale organizational leadership. Through his work with the React Foundation, he has championed the idea of React as critical digital infrastructure — something larger than any one company, deserving of long-term stewardship and community investment.

Beyond engineering, Seth is also an accomplished photographer, writer, and creative technologist. His interests span adventure and wildlife photography, design systems, human-centered leadership, language immersion, aviation, and the future of AI-assisted creativity. Whether speaking on stage, mentoring engineers, building products, or crafting narratives around emerging technology, he brings a mix of pragmatism, empathy, and relentless curiosity.

At the core of Seth’s work is a simple belief: technology is ultimately about people — and the best tools don’t just increase productivity, they expand human potential.

speakers.name: Shahbaz Kaladiya
speakers.tagLine: Senior Software Engineer - iOS Engineer @ Uber
speakers.bio: I am the Founding Mobile Engineer of the Edge Platform team in Bangalore. In the last Five years, I have established myself as the Domain expert for Ramen protocol and gRPC stack and ModelGen for both Proto and Thrift - providing constant support across timezones to various product team use cases. I have led some key initiatives aligned with our goal of building the most efficient and reliable Uber Client <> Backend communication platform.

speakers.name: Shilpa Bansal
speakers.bio:
Shilpa Bansal is a Staff iOS Engineer at Delivery Hero, one of the world’s largest food delivery platforms. She has over 14 years of software development experience, with a Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology from India. Throughout her career, she has worked with a wide range of companies, from global enterprises like Walmart, Bank of America, and EA Games, to fast-paced startups, giving her a unique blend of large-scale systems expertise and agile product innovation.

At Delivery Hero, she focuses on performance, observability, and architecture improvements for Rider apps used across 70+ countries. She is an active contributor in mobile engineering leadership, shaping best practices, and driving cross-platform collaboration across multiple teams and brands.

Outside of work, she has a keen interest in developer communities and knowledge sharing, and is excited about contributing to the iOS ecosystem through talks, workshops, and mentoring the next generation of mobile engineers.

speakers.name: Shree Bhagwat
speakers.tagLine: Founder Codeaamy | GDE Flutter and Dart
speakers.bio:
Shrihriday Bhagwat (Shree) is a Flutter Google Developer Expert (GDE), founder of Codeaamy Pvt. Ltd., and an international speaker known for his deep work on scalable Flutter architectures, AI-integrated mobile experiences.

He has delivered impactful sessions at conferences like Droidcon London, FlutterCon Berlin, and Google Cloud Community Days, Devfest, inspiring developers to think beyond UI and explore what’s next for Flutter in the AI era.

Through Codeaamy and the Flutter Pune community, he has trained engineers from companies, blending real-world production learnings with community spirit.

His current focus is on building the next generation of AI-assisted developer tools, super app architectures, and Edge-function-driven platforms that make Flutter shine at scale.

speakers.name: Simon Auer
speakers.tagLine: Organizer of flutter vienna meetup and CEO of marqably
speakers.bio:
With more than 15 years in development and the experience of building and working on over 200 projects for startups and multinational companies Simon has worked professionally with almost every major modern framework. From React, Angular, Vue, Ember and Svelte to Flutter, and has discovered their pros and cons.

This experience is used to teach at multiple universities/fhs and to consult companies on frameworks and solutions for their specific needs, as well as train whole tech teams on them in leading companies in Austria, Germany and Switzerland.

speakers.name: Simon Binder
speakers.tagLine: Creator of Drift, engineer working on PowerSync
speakers.bio: Simon is a software engineer with passion for databases and developer tooling in the Dart ecosystem. He maintains and contributes to widely-used open source libraries like Drift,  helping developers build reliable and scalable applications. Recently, he joined the PowerSync team, building tools for offline-first architectures and real-time data synchronization.

speakers.name: Sinan Kozak
speakers.bio: Sinan is an Android GDE and he works as Staff Engineer at Delivery Hero, food delivery company. He has been working with Android since 2011 and has 13 years of professional experience with software development. He is passionate about Kotlin and loves to contribute open-source.

speakers.name: Slobodan Nikolic
speakers.tagLine: Engineering leader, who loves tech, games, people and building all sorts of things
speakers.bio: Built and led teams in Two Desperados, Nordeus, King, Scopely. Started as an engineer, working on client and backend in Unity and native mobile apps trough roles of Senior Engineering Manager, Head of Development, Senior Director of Engineering.

speakers.name: Sofía Rey
speakers.bio: Sofía Rey is a Software Engineer at Very Good Ventures, based in Uruguay, with a background in Multimedia Design and over four years of experience with Flutter. She combines design, product, and technology to create high-quality experiences. She is an international speaker, having presented at FlutterConf Latam, Fluttercon USA, and Fluttercon Europe, and is actively involved in the Flutter community.

speakers.name: Sohrab Mostaghim
speakers.tagLine: Product & Serious Game Designer @ Game is Serious
speakers.bio: Sohrab Mostaghim is a Product and Serious Game Designer and the founder of the Berlin-based studio GameIsSerious.co. With over a decade of experience, he has published 5 physical board games and designed over 60 serious games focused on behavioral change and ROI as the CEO and Lead Game Designer at Farbood.games. Previously serving as CPO for the AI-training startup WiseWorld, Sohrab specialized as an "AI NPC Psychologist," designing complex behavioral architectures. Today, his work bridges game mechanics and enterprise software through B2B platforms like DealIQ (a multi-agent AI simulator) and Meteorite (a knowledge management game).

speakers.name: Sophia Roetker
speakers.bio: I am a mobile developer with over 5 years of experience building applications for Android, Flutter, and .NET MAUI. My work across various industries has focused on shipping robust, production-grade apps on modern, fast-moving platforms. I'm passionate about leveraging new tools like AI to accelerate development, but I'm also deeply interested in navigating their real-world risks and limitations. This talk is a direct result of my hands-on experience staying on the cutting edge of cross-platform development.

speakers.name: Sreeram Gollangi
speakers.bio:
I am Sreeram Gollangi. Born and brought up in India. I graduated as an Architect where I fell in love with Design. For Masters I chose to combine my love for Design with my love for video games. After my post graduation in Game Design Development and Management at Rubika, I started my career at Zynga. After working at Zynga for two years, I moved to Rovio in 2019 and I have been here since.
I am now the Lead Gameplay Designer and Team Manager of Angry Birds Match at Rovio.

speakers.name: Stacy Devino
speakers.bio: Stacy leads the Fanatics App and client platforms in the Fanatics Ecosystem. She is a multifaceted, international keynote speaker noted for her work in diversity advocacy, tech democracy, and "real-talk" leadership development. She has been a mobile specialist her whole career and worked on nearly every aspect of the ecosystem, currently specializing in engaging, fan-first Sports experiences for Fanatics. Her work has been featured on sites like Wired, Gizmodo, and Geek.com in addition to being mentioned directly in published books and being named to WWC's "100 Technologists to Watch". You can catch Stacy posting advice on LinkedIn, traveling to conferences, or working in her local DFW community as an educator and mentor for all career stages.

speakers.name: Stanislav Sydorenko
speakers.tagLine: Mobile Engineer & Indie Developer @ Allica Bank
speakers.bio:
Stanislav Sydorenko is a mobile engineer with 12+ years of experience in Android and Flutter, including several years leading & scaling mobile teams. He is also a co-organizer of Flutter meetups and an active member of the Flutter community.

Alongside his professional work, Stanislav builds independent apps and experiments with Flutter, maps, aviation data and AI. His projects include Flymap, an offline flight map for travellers, and ZenGlide, a relaxing flight simulator built with Flutter. He enjoys pushing Flutter beyond traditional mobile apps and sharing the practical lessons learned along the way.

speakers.name: Stefan Bernhardsgrütter
speakers.bio:
As Security Tester at Redguard AG, Stefan conducts penetration tests in various fields such as web applications, networking, embedded devices, and cloud environments. His primary expertise lies in mobile security, a specialized area he leads at Redguard. In this role, he is responsible for advancing mobile application security testing within Redguard but also to contribute to the broader security community.

Stefan has been working in information security since 2012 and joined Redguard AG in 2017. He holds an M.Sc. in Engineering with a focus on IT security and part-time teaches an IT security course at a higher technical college in Switzerland.

speakers.name: Stefan Hoth
speakers.bio: Stefan Hoth is an engineering leader based near Dresden, Germany, with over fifteen years building and shipping software across startups and scale-ups. Most of his professional experience he spent leading platform teams, enabling product teams to ship high quality results. He is currently between roles and working hands-on with AI tools, figuring out what they genuinely change about how we build software, and what they do not.

speakers.name: Stelios Frantzeskakis
speakers.bio:
Stelios is a Staff Engineer at Perry Street Software, publisher of the LGBTQ+ dating apps SCRUFF and Jack'd, serving a community of over 40 million members worldwide.

He enjoys speaking at technical conferences and writing about architecture, testing, and developer experience.

speakers.name: Stepan Mirskiy
speakers.tagLine: iOS Engineer @ Flo Health UK Limited
speakers.bio: With over 10 years of experience in mobile engineering, I have worked as an iOS Engineer and Engineering Manager across a wide range of products. For the past 3.5 years, I've been at Flo Health, helping build and scale the world's leading femtech app, serving more than 80 million monthly active users. My current focus is iOS architecture and developer experience, with a particular interest in building backend-driven UI systems with SwiftUI.

speakers.name: Stephan Arenswald
speakers.bio: Stephan is the founder of LeanBytes, a Germany-based indie software studio building macOS apps for a productivity boost, and the maintainer of the open source project MacPacker. Before going independent, he spent a decade in the automotive industry, as a Senior Product Owner and Agile Coach at Mercedes-Benz, where he worked on user experience and voice interfaces, including Hey Mercedes. With around 20 years of experience across engineering, product, and business, he now runs LeanBytes, handling everything from code to pricing to positioning. He spends a lot of time thinking about what it takes to run a lean, independent software business, and how new tools like AI change that equation without changing the fundamentals.

speakers.name: Stephen Lee
speakers.bio: Stephen Lee is VP of Partnerships at DECA Games, known for their Live Ops expertise and as the mobile unit of the Embracer Group. With over 16 years of free-to-play publishing experience across three continents, Stephen also advises companies and works with non-profits in the games industry.

speakers.name: Stephen Said
speakers.bio: Stephen is a Sr. Solutions Architect with AWS and concentrates on Data Analytics and Data Platforms. With over a decade of experience in software engineering and DevOps, he is committed to enhancing data engineering productivity and architecting resilient data platforms. Building on engineering best practices like automation or iterative software development, Stephen is passionate to create efficient solutions that empower organisations to deliver analytical workloads of high quality.

speakers.name: Steven Moyes
speakers.bio:
Steven Moyes is a Senior Technical Product Manager at Amazon, where he leads React Native for Vega OS - Amazon’s purpose-built operating system for devices including Echo and Fire TV. He works directly with media application developers to help them build and deliver React Native experiences for Fire TV and other Vega OS-powered devices.

Steven is also a member of the React Foundation, focusing on Platform Expertise. Previously, he led platform initiatives for React Native for Windows at Microsoft, shaping APIs, native-module support, and developer experiences across desktop platforms.

speakers.name: Suraj Giri
speakers.bio:
- Currently working as a Senior Mobile Engineer (L6) at GetYourGuide, the largest travel experience company, crafting seamless user experiences.
- Previously a Senior Android Engineer at SixFlags, the world’s largest theme park company, led mobile innovation during their merger with CedarFair another giant in the same domain.
- Spearheaded Swipe's fintech revolution in billing software category, contributed to its status as a top-tier startup as an Android Engineer.
- Developed for Doubtnut (India's largest educational app) for 2.5 years , actively implemented solutions for 80+ million users.
- Orchestrated 30+ freelance projects, showcasing adaptability and technical prowess.

speakers.name: Szymon Chmal
speakers.bio: Creator of Rozenite, Harness and Voltra. The kind of person who dives into code and somehow makes the "impossible" happen. Focused on building the next generation of developer tools so you can ship your apps even faster.

speakers.name: Taaha Rauf
speakers.tagLine: Engineer III at Very Good Ventures
speakers.bio: Taaha Rauf is an Engineer III at Very Good Ventures with five years of experience in Flutter development. His background includes contributions to both early-stage ventures and established enterprises. He has experience across the full lifecycle of app development, from initial creation to integration within cross-functional teams. His work on numerous production-scale applications has emphasized the critical importance of performance and optimization. This presentation will synthesize his practical experiences in identifying and resolving memory leaks in complex Flutter environments.

speakers.name: Tadeas Kriz
speakers.bio: Tadeas is a Senior Mobile Developer at Touchlab, experimenting with Kotlin compiler plugins. Began as a PHP developer, moving to .NET desktop apps later on. Finally landing in mobile development with Android first and then falling in love with iOS. Fortunately, Kotlin Multiplatform happened, opening the path to doing both mobile platforms.

speakers.name: Tamás Bazsonyi
speakers.bio: Tamas Bazsonyi is a member of the Solutions Engineering team at Bitrise working with customers in the EMEA region to implement CI/CD pipelines successfully that help them during their day-to-day jobs. During his career he’s been working as a Full Stack Developer, QA Engineer and also jumping into mobile app development. Some of his favourite topics are Test Automation and Automation in general.

speakers.name: Tatiana Kondratyeva
speakers.bio: Tatiana Kondratyeva is the CEO and Co-Founder of PlayPack, a Berlin-based mobile games studio, founded in 2021, focused on creating and scaling casual free-to-play games. The studio combines rapid product development, data-driven iteration, and strong publishing partnerships to build games for global audiences. PlayPack is best known for Merge Away, which has reached millions of players worldwide.

speakers.name: Tatiana Sherbul
speakers.bio: UI/UX designer and Unity developer based in Berlin with over a decade in mobile games, including work on hits like June's Journey and Asphalt 8. She's currently at StarBerry Games, supporting development of a new game. Straddling both the visual and technical sides of UI, she brings a grounded, production-tested view of where AI genuinely speeds up game design work today — and where it doesn't.

speakers.name: Thomas Bedenk
speakers.tagLine: Tech Strategist & Advisor | Bridging Human Psychology, Business & Emerging Tech
speakers.bio: Thomas Bedenk is a freelance advisor and tech strategist with 30 years of experience in emerging technologies. He is also the co-host of the Spatial Realities podcast. His focus areas are Strategy, UX, Innovation, and Emerging Technologies (XR/AI) across industries. He is a keynote speaker and founding member of XRBB and the German Games Association. He was an interim Professor of Creative Producing and Digital Strategies for XR at Hochschule Darmstadt. From 2015 until 2024, he was VP Extended Reality at Endava and Director Immersive Media at Exozet. In 2008, he founded the game studio Brightside Games. He has degrees in Media Design and Human Factors. Prior to that, he was an interactive designer and developer since 1996, when he published his first games and websites online.

speakers.name: Thomas Hanning
speakers.tagLine: Head of Mobile at Arvato Systems
speakers.bio: Thomas is Head of Mobile at Arvato Systems, leading mobile development initiatives and driving technical excellence. With over a decade of experience in mobile engineering, he has transitioned from a hands-on mobile developer and architect to a leadership role, guiding teams in building scalable and high-quality mobile applications.

speakers.name: Thomas Künneth
speakers.tagLine: Google Developer Expert for Android with a previous life in the Java Enterprise. Speaker. Mentor. Wrote a couple of books along the way.
speakers.bio: Thomas fell in love with Android in 2009. He has been constantly contributing to the community since then. Thomas loves writing books (four titles, 15 editions) and articles. He enjoys speaking at conferences and meetups. Thomas' first encounter with programming was in the era of home computers during the early 1980s. Later came C, Perl and a few more. During the 90s he wrote a bunch of programs for the Atari ST series. The first decade of Thomas' professional career centered around Java Enterprise. Today it’s all things Android and Kotlin.

speakers.name: Tim Condon
speakers.bio: Tim is a Swift developer from Manchester, UK and one half of the Vapor Core Team. He sits on the Swift Server Workgroup and delivers talks and workshops on Vapor and server-side Swift around the world. He runs Broken Hands, a server-side Swift consultancy and works with clients around the world to help them deploy Swift on their backends. He also co-organises the ServerSide.swift conference - the world’s first and only conference focused on server-side Swift.

speakers.name: Tim Lehmann
speakers.tagLine: Product Engineer that loves to think about the human factor.
speakers.bio: I discovered Flutter when it was still in alpha, while I was doing my bachelor's degree in my student dorm, and jumped in head first. Today, I have a Master's degree in Human Computer Interaction and have worked with Flutter professionally for years in various jobs, from start-ups to Volkswagen Future Center Europe. I am currently a Staff Engineer at ClickUp and love experimenting and maintaining open-source projects for "whynotmake.it" in my free time.

speakers.name: Tobias Hamann
speakers.tagLine: Penetration Tester/IT-Security Consultant at usd AG
speakers.bio:
Tobias Hamann is a security researcher and penetration tester at usd AG, an information security company based in Germany with the mission #moresecurity.

As part of the SAP penetration testing team at the usd HeroLab, Tobias is contributing mainly to the development of new analysis tools and the research of new attack vectors. Beyond that, he is interested in reverse engineering and vulnerability research in general.

Outside the SAP domain, Tobias has a strong interest on mobile security. He has published several research papers in security-focused scientific conferences.

speakers.name: Tom Colvin
speakers.tagLine: Android GDE, freelancer, co-founder of Apptaura
speakers.bio:
I'm a Google Developer Expert in Android, available either as a freelancer or through Apptaura, the mobile app development agency I co-founded. I build great apps for people, helping them to build great app businesses. I have a commercial focus and a wide knowledge of many technologies (both back- and front-end).

I'm a regular conference speaker on topics related to Android, and app startups more generally. I also provide mentorship to those looking to start app businesses.

I have a proven entrepreneurial capability and enjoy the energy of startup culture.

speakers.name: Tom Kaltofen
speakers.tagLine: Striving to make data and algorithmic pipelines robust, reliable, and finally painless
speakers.bio: Tom Kaltofen is a Berlin-based data and AI engineer and the creator of mloda, an open-source (Apache-2.0) Python framework for declarative, plugin-based data access in AI workflows. After years of building in-house feature stores, ML pipelines, and RAG systems, he kept seeing "model" failures that were really data-context failures, and built mloda to close that gap: the layer between raw sources and the feature stores, RAG frameworks, and agent orchestrators that consume them. His work on open government data is currently funded by the Prototype Fund.

speakers.name: Tom Quercia
speakers.tagLine: Principal Software Engineer at Universal Destinations and Experiences
speakers.bio: I am a mobile engineer with 15 years of experience, with a focus on enterprise scale applications. Nowadays I make Flutter mobile apps, websites, and desktop applications for Universal's suite of parks and experiences.

speakers.name: Tomasz Żelawski
speakers.bio: I'm Tomasz Żelawski, a software engineer working at Software Mansion, working in the React Native Open Source team for over two years. I utilize my deep love for low-level programming and academic aspects of code to manipulate abstract syntax trees, chase race conditions and basically hack whatever I can.

speakers.name: Tomek Czajecki
speakers.bio: Tomek is an Engineering Manager at Expo, where he leads the Web Services team. He has been working in the React ecosystem for close to a decade, shipped large React Native apps for several years as a mobile consultant, built backends in various technologies, and spent countless hours writing React code. He hasn’t written a full line of code in 2026, yet he has shipped more than in any year when writing code was his full-time job. He strongly believes agents can be used to ship more code and raise the quality bar if used right.

speakers.name: Tris Bates
speakers.bio:
Engineering leadership is more than a job to me. I’m passionate about engineering excellence at scale, building high-performing teams, and transforming technology! Over the last decade, I have scaled and built teams to deliver award-winning apps and services to over 15 million users.

I enjoy all facets of software engineering, from debating and selling solutions to senior stakeholders to recruiting and mentoring engineers. My leadership style is empathetic; I listen to my team’s problems, remain calm and work towards solutions. I believe automation is essential, and wherever possible, I’ve led my team in automating processes to shorten development cycles.

Outside of work, I am a recognised technology thought leader and have featured on various podcasts, webinars and panels discussing Mobile apps and engineering leadership. Also, I'm a key part of Europe’s largest Apple engineering group, NSLondon. We have over 3,000 members and have held regular events at many of the UK’s largest tech giants, including Google, Revolut, Monzo, JustEat, AWS, Ford, Deloitte and Bumble. This year, we were showcased by Apple at their WWDC25 conference and were also the first engineering event to be hosted at their new Battersea HQ

speakers.name: Tsuyoshi Chujo
speakers.bio:
He is a freelance mobile app developer in Japan. He is also a developer of crop_your_image, the most popular Flutter package that provides a widget that enables Flutter developers to embed the cropping images feature in their apps, and also a developer of animated_to, a handy widget that enables you to animate whatever widgets when their position is updated.

He is very passionate about sharing insights and knowledge about the internal mechanisms of Flutter and packages by publishing articles or providing talks at conferences.

speakers.name: Tzvetan Mikov
speakers.bio: Tzvetan Mikov is the architect of the Hermes JavaScript engine and leads the development of Static Hermes, an ahead-of-time compiler for JavaScript. He has spent too many years building compilers, virtual machines, and systems software in C and C++, and remains fascinated by making dynamic languages faster, smaller, and easier to deploy.

speakers.name: Ulli Hinze
speakers.bio: Ulli Hinze is a Solutions Architect at AWS, where he helps software companies build cloud- and AI-native SaaS products. He optimizes for shipping fast, as the worst product is the one that never ships. In agentic AI he focuses on two things: context and retrieval engineering, because an agent is only as good as its context; and observability, because agent quality has to be measurable before it can be improved. Ulli has spent 13+ years architecting and engineering software across multiple industries and has spoken at conferences globally, including AWS re:Invent. He is dad to two small kids, so specializations outside work include airplanes that talk and competitive dishwasher loading.

speakers.name: Vadym Pinchuk
speakers.bio:
Vadym is a Software Development Engineer and Google Developer Expert (GDE) in Flutter & Dart, driven by a dual passion: engineering world-class mobile solutions and elevating the developers around him. His deep expertise and active contributions to the tech ecosystem were formally recognized by Google with the GDE award in 2025.

With a rich background spanning over 8 years in native Android and more than 4 years in cross-platform development with Flutter, Vadym has a proven track record of building high-quality applications. He has partnered with industry giants such as Samsung, Volvo, Instagram, and Sky, as well as numerous dynamic startups, to deliver cutting-edge mobile solutions across a diverse range of sectors.

A true believer in the power of sharing knowledge, Vadym is a powerhouse in the community and a familiar face on the international conference circuit. He is known for bringing vibrant energy to the stage at major events including Droidcon, Fluttercon, FlutterHeroes, and Appdevcon. But his commitment doesn't stop at the podium; he also actively supports events as an MC and stage manager, dedicating his energy to ensuring a smooth and engaging experience for speakers and attendees alike.

At his core, Vadym is on a mission to empower the tech community. He is deeply passionate about developer education and channels this into dedicated mentoring, fostering growth, and helping to build the next generation of tech leaders.

speakers.name: Vahid Panjganj
speakers.tagLine: Senior Principal for AI Engineering at Elsewhen
speakers.bio:
I have more than 20 years of rebust experience in software engineering. At Elsewhen, I lead the generative AI initiatives, focusing on embedding cutting-edge AI technologies into real-world business applications. 

My role involves aligning technology with business strategy, enabling clients to automate complex processes and achieve a competitive edge through AI.

My leadership focuses on upskilling, creating autonomous teams and implementing high-performance practices. I advocate for continuous learning and improvement.

speakers.name: Valentina Llavayol
speakers.bio: Hi! I'm Valentina Llavayol, a Software Engineer from Uruguay and currently a Senior Flutter Engineer at GlobalComix, a Flutter-powered comic reader application. Before diving into the world of digital comics, I was part of the fantastic team at Very Good Ventures. I genuinely enjoy being a part of the Flutter community and am always eager to help others and share what I've learned. I have previously presented at community events, such as FlutterCon USA 2024 and 2025. Excited to connect with fellow developers and learn together!

speakers.name: Valeri Milke
speakers.tagLine: Founder & Principal AI Security Consultant @ VamiSec | AI Threat Modeling, LLM Security & Agentic AI
speakers.bio:
Valeri Milke is CEO of VamiSec GmbH and an information security and compliance expert focused on helping organizations translate European cyber and digital regulations into practical operating models. His work spans information security management, AI governance, secure development, and regulatory implementation across frameworks such as the EU AI Act, NIS2, DORA, CRA, and ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO/IEC 42001.

He advises organizations on how to operationalize regulatory requirements in real environments by connecting governance, engineering, risk management, and security architecture. His focus includes secure-by-design approaches, product and software security, AI risk management, third-party risk, and resilience requirements in regulated industries.

Valeri regularly works at the intersection of policy, technology, and implementation, with a particular interest in how European regulation affects software development, open technology ecosystems, and digital sovereignty.

speakers.name: Vasyl Dytsiak
speakers.bio:
I have 10+ years in software development for complex web and mobile applications. 
Through my career I went from backend developer on PHP through React/ReactNative frontend developer and now I'm full time flutter developer. Managing local community of flutter developers called ArtFlutter.

speakers.name: Vedran Vidakovic
speakers.bio: Vedran Vidakovic is an Android Engineer who, after early years at small startups, has spent almost a decade at Super, where he built its high-traffic sports-betting and casino apps from the ground up - products now used by people around the world. Based in Zagreb, and still as excited about mobile as on day one.

speakers.name: Venkata Padma Kumar Vemuri
speakers.bio:
I’m Venkata Vemuri, a front-end engineer with a relentless passion for crafting digital experiences that don’t just look great—but feel extraordinary. With a keen eye for intuitive interfaces and a deep understanding of the intersection between design and development, I thrive on pushing the boundaries of what’s possible in UI engineering.

As a lead engineer on multiple projects, I’ve mastered the art of transforming complex requirements into seamless, scalable, and high-performing applications. I don’t just write code—I create experiences that delight users, drive engagement, and set new standards for excellence. Whether it’s harnessing the power of modern frameworks, optimizing performance, or pioneering design systems, I believe that a pixel-perfect UI isn’t just about aesthetics—it’s about engineering precision.

At Dev Conference, I’d love to share my insights on elevating front-end development  with AI —whether through cutting-edge performance techniques, streamlined developer workflows, or design-driven engineering. Let’s talk AI, code, creativity, and crafting the future of web experiences!

speakers.name: Viktor Lidholt
speakers.bio: With a master’s in computer science and more than 20 years of industry experience, Viktor has a solid background in software engineering. Before starting his own venture, he worked at Google’s Flutter team in Silicon Valley. He has held talks and taught guest lectures on programming, app creation, and computer graphics at international conferences and universities such as MIT, Carnegie Mellon, and UC Berkeley.

speakers.name: Viktor Mukha
speakers.tagLine: Paradox Cat GmbH, Principal Software Architect
speakers.bio: Viktor Mukha has spent years deep in the Android Open Source Project (AOSP), specializing in Automotive — shipping BMW and MINI head-units built on AAOS. He contributes to COVESA's Automotive AOSP App Framework standardization and sits on the steering committee at aosp-devs.org. Off the clock, he plays guitar in an award-winning melodic death metal band and quietly conspires with Home Assistant and ESPHome to outsmart his own house.

speakers.name: Ville Lindfors
speakers.bio:
Ville Lindfors leads Codemate's AI, Data & Cloud practice and helps organisations turn AI from experimentation into production-ready services. His work focuses on AI-powered products, cloud-native architectures, and the organisational challenges that emerge when AI becomes part of real customer experiences.

Before joining Codemate, Ville held leadership roles at Aiven and F-Secure, building and operating mission-critical systems at scale. Today, he works with companies that are looking to adopt AI safely, create business value from data, and build systems that can evolve alongside rapidly changing technologies.

speakers.name: Violina Popova
speakers.tagLine: Software Developer at ClipMyHorse.TV, Co-lead and Co-founder of Frontend Queens
speakers.bio:
With a passion for creating seamless cross-platform experiences, my journey in tech started not with programming, but as a consultant in the tech industry. The desire to build and innovate led to a shift in focus towards software development, particularly mobile app development, where the thrill of solving complex problems and crafting user-friendly applications became a calling.
Co-founding Frontend Queens was a natural extension of this journey, inspired by a commitment to inclusivity in tech. This community was born from the belief that everyone, especially women, should have the opportunity to thrive in technology. By fostering a supportive environment, we aim to empower women to break barriers and pursue fulfilling careers in this ever-evolving field.

speakers.name: Vipul Shah
speakers.tagLine: Senior Flutter Engineer turning 14 years of Android expertise into next-gen banking experiences at ING
speakers.bio: Senior Flutter Engineer at ING with 14 years of mobile development experience, evolving from native Android specialist to cross-platform expert. Deep background in Android Jetpack and Kotlin Coroutines gives a native-first edge to Flutter development. Currently building wholesale banking mobile experiences, focused on the intersection of security, intuitive design, and performance in fintech.

speakers.name: Vladimir Jovanović
speakers.bio: Vladimir Jovanović is a passionate Android developer and a LinkedIn Learning author. Since Android 2.2, he has been helping companies have clean and stable Android applications. He currently lives in Berlin and is an active member of the Android community.

speakers.name: Vladislav Markov
speakers.bio: I am an iOS Engineer with 7 years of hands-on experience. In recent years, I have focused on graphics-intensive projects: I played a key role in developing a photo and video editor with millions of users, and I am now working at a startup Medida AI specializing in Computer Vision and AI.

speakers.name: Weiyin He
speakers.bio: Weiyin He is the CTO of Appetize.io, where he leads the team building cloud-based mobile app infrastructure for development teams across the industry. Appetize.io makes native Android and iOS apps accessible from a browser via a URL, which opens the door to preview environments, CI/CD integration, and cross-functional review workflows that do not require a physical device or any installation.

speakers.name: Yauheni Slizh
speakers.bio:
I'm Yauheni Slizh, an Android/Flutter/KMM developer, writer, and speaker. I love to investigate the world of technology and translate my vision into practical solutions. I thrive on new opportunities and enjoy tackling complex problems.

I have more than 8 years of commercial experience in Android development. During this time I worked in different components and products, from small startup applications to large big-tech products used by millions of people around the world.

Now I am living in Stockholm, Sweden, and not only learning new things but also trying to build local communities to make developer life more interesting.

speakers.name: Yessine Mahdouani
speakers.tagLine: Paradox Cat GmbH, Senior Software Developer
speakers.bio: Yessine has over 10 years of Android expertise, with experience designing, developing, and architecting Android software. He has worked extensively within the Android Open Source Project codebase; working on BMW and MINI head units built on AOSP; including native platform development and system-level components.

speakers.name: Yishai Beeri
speakers.bio:
Yishai Beeri likes to solve problems, and that’s why he was so fascinated with programming when first encountered Logo back in the 80s, where the possibilities seemed endless.

He has made it a focus of his career to solve complex programming problems, as a consultant and entrepreneur. Between 2013 and 2020, Yishai worked in the CTO office of a fast moving cloud security startup, and after its acquisition in the Cloud Security unit of a networking giant. In 2020 Yishai joined LinearB to focus on Developer Productivity and Experience. As CTO he engages with hundreds of engineering leaders and helps build products that answer the industry's core questions about AI & Productivity for software engineering.

speakers.name: Yoni Newman
speakers.bio:
Yoni is a mobile software engineer and team lead at Appdome, specializing in mobile application security. His work focuses on Android and iOS runtime protection, reverse engineering, anti-tampering, anti-debugging, and runtime threat detection.

With hands-on experience analyzing mobile applications and the techniques used to attack and protect them, Yoni enjoys diving deep into the lower levels of mobile platforms and understanding how things work behind the scenes.

speakers.name: Yuhao Feng
speakers.bio: Senior Software Engineer at DraftKings

speakers.name: Zahed Heidari
speakers.bio:
I'm a Senior Software Engineer specialising in AI integration and intelligent tooling. At Blue Beck, I'm a core developer on SMARTY's React Native app, serving 500k+ users, and I champion the team's adoption of AI-assisted engineering practices.

Outside of client work, I build web and mobile products with React Native and Next.js, and explore how AI can act as a reasoning partner for developers rather than just a code generator - externalising what you know, what you suspect, and what constraints you're working within.

I speak on helping developers adopt AI deliberately, so they stay sharp and ship faster without losing the thinking that makes them good engineers in the first place.

speakers.name: Zhanibek Marshal
speakers.bio: 12+ years shipping production Android. At Trade Republic building payment rails, design systems, and more. Active speaker at Droidcon Berlin. Advocate for testable code and automation.

speakers.name: Zoltan Ferenczi
speakers.tagLine: Founder & XR/Game Developer @ Make a Break Berlin UG
speakers.bio: Zoltan Ferenczi is an XR developer, immersive game designer and founder of Make a Break in Berlin. For more than a decade, he has created technology-driven escape-room and interactive experiences enjoyed by over 150,000 players. He is the creator and lead developer of Dunkelstein, a crowdfunded AR tabletop murder mystery built in Unreal Engine that blends a physical villa, cinematic characters and mobile augmented reality. Alongside independent game development, Zoltan works as an XR developer at Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin on the CUBES Circle digital-twin research project. His work focuses on turning ambitious spatial-computing ideas into accessible, social experiences.
